196		if current == nil {
197			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
198		}
199		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, buildAgentMessages(e)...)
200		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp

217	func mergeToolResult(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) {

287	// buildAgentMessages maps a pi assistant message entry to one or more schema
288	// Messages: one Message holds the text+thinking content parts; each toolCall
289	// block becomes its own agent Message carrying a ToolInfo.
290	func buildAgentMessages(e rawEntry) []schema.Message {
291		var am assistantMessage
292		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &am); err != nil {
293			return nil

296		var messages []schema.Message

303			case schema.ContentTypeThinking:
304				if b.Thinking != "" {

341	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
342		return schema.Message{

344			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
345			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
346			Model:     am.Model,
347			Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{

359	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {

1	package piagent
2	
3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"log/slog"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"strings"
13	)
14	
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// Skip entries missing the envelope fields the tree walk and exchange
91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}
104	
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
187	
188	// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
189	// if not found.
190	func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
191		for i, e := range path {
192			if e.ID == keptID {
193				return i
194			}
195		}
196		return -1
197	}

114			switch v := val.(type) {
115			case float64:

147	// Validate checks the SessionData against schema constraints and logs warnings for any issues.
148	// Returns true if validation passed, false if there were any issues.
149	func (s *SessionData) Validate() bool {
150		valid := true
151	
152		// Check schema version
153		if s.SchemaVersion != "1.0" {
154			slog.Warn("schema validation: schemaVersion must be '1.0'", "got", s.SchemaVersion)

164			slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.name is required")
165			valid = false
166		}
167		if s.Provider.Version == "" {
168			slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.version is required")
169			valid = false
170		}
171		if s.SessionID == "" {
172			slog.Warn("schema validation: sessionId is required")
173			valid = false
174		}
175		if s.CreatedAt == "" {
176			slog.Warn("schema validation: createdAt is required")
177			valid = false
178		}
179		if s.WorkspaceRoot == "" {
180			slog.Warn("schema validation: workspaceRoot is required")
181			valid = false
182		}

184		// Validate each exchange
185		for i, exchange := range s.Exchanges {

187				slog.Warn("schema validation: exchange.exchangeId is required", "exchangeIndex", i)
188				valid = false
189			}

191			// Validate each message in the exchange
192			for j, msg := range exchange.Messages {
193				if !msg.validate(i, j) {
194					valid = false
195				}
196			}
197		}
198	
199		return valid
200	}

202	// validate checks a single message against schema constraints.
203	func (m *Message) validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex int) bool {
204		valid := true
205		logCtx := []any{"exchangeIndex", exchangeIndex, "messageIndex", messageIndex}
206	
207		// Check role is valid
208		if m.Role != RoleUser && m.Role != RoleAgent {
209			slog.Warn("schema validation: message.role must be 'user' or 'agent'",
210				append(logCtx, "got", m.Role)...)
211			valid = false
212		}
213	
214		// User message constraints
215		if m.Role == RoleUser {
216			if len(m.Content) == 0 {
217				slog.Warn("schema validation: user message must have non-empty content", logCtx...)
218				valid = false
219			}
220			if m.Tool != nil {
221				slog.Warn("schema validation: user message cannot have tool", logCtx...)
222				valid = false
223			}
224			if m.Model != "" {
225				slog.Warn("schema validation: user message cannot have model", logCtx...)
226				valid = false
227			}
228		}
229	
230		// Agent message constraints: must have at least one of content, tool, or pathHints
231		if m.Role == RoleAgent {

233			hasTool := m.Tool != nil
234			hasPathHints := len(m.PathHints) > 0
235			if !hasContent && !hasTool && !hasPathHints {
236				slog.Warn("schema validation: agent message must have content, tool, or pathHints", logCtx...)
237				valid = false
238			}
239		}
240	
241		// Validate content parts
242		for k, part := range m.Content {
243			if !part.validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex, k) {
244				valid = false
245			}
246		}
247	
248		// Validate tool if present
249		if m.Tool != nil {
250			if !m.Tool.validate(exchangeIndex, messageIndex) {
251				valid = false
252			}
253		}

30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// Skip entries missing the envelope fields the tree walk and exchange
91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}
104	
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
187	
188	// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
189	// if not found.
190	func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
191		for i, e := range path {
192			if e.ID == keptID {
193				return i
194			}
195		}
196		return -1
197	}

13	// writeDebugRaw writes numbered JSON files (one per non-header entry) plus the
14	// central session-data.json via the shared spi helper. This matches the
15	// --debug-raw contract used by every provider.
16	func writeDebugRaw(sessionPath string, data *schema.SessionData) error {
17		if err := spi.WriteDebugSessionData(data.SessionID, data); err != nil {
18			return err
19		}
20		dir := spi.GetDebugDir(data.SessionID)
21		entries, err := readRawEntries(sessionPath)
22		if err != nil {
23			return err
24		}
25		return writeNumberedEntries(dir, entries)
26	}
27	
28	// writeNumberedEntries writes each raw entry as 1.json, 2.json, ... in dir.
29	func writeNumberedEntries(dir string, entries []json.RawMessage) error {
30		for i, raw := range entries {
31			filePath := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", i+1))
32			payload, mErr := json.MarshalIndent(raw, "", "  ")
33			if mErr != nil {
34				continue
35			}
36			if wErr := os.WriteFile(filePath, payload, 0o644); wErr != nil {
37				return wErr
38			}
39		}
40		return nil
41	}
42	
43	// readRawEntries returns each non-header line of a session file as a raw JSON
44	// value, for debug-raw burst output. Uses bufio.Reader (via readLines) so
45	// arbitrarily large lines are captured without the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap.
46	func readRawEntries(path string) ([]json.RawMessage, error) {
47		var out []json.RawMessage
48		first := true
49		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
50			if first {
51				first = false // skip the session header line
52				return nil
53			}
54			out = append(out, json.RawMessage(line))
55			return nil
56		})
57		return out, err
58	}

1	package piagent
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// piSessionsRoot returns ~/.pi/agent/sessions, the directory under which pi
11	// stores one subdirectory per working directory (each named with the encoded
12	// cwd, see EncodeCwd). It does not require the directory to exist.
13	func piSessionsRoot() (string, error) {
14		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
15		if err != nil {
16			return "", fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot resolve home dir: %w", err)
17		}
18		return filepath.Join(home, ".pi", "agent", "sessions"), nil
19	}
20	
21	// EncodeCwd maps a working directory to pi's session-subdirectory name.
22	// pi replaces every '/' in the absolute path with '-' and wraps the result with
23	// a leading '-' and a trailing '--', producing e.g. "/Users/jane/proj" ->
24	// "--Users-jane-proj--". The encoding is derived from real session dirs:
25	// "/Users/jakelevirne" -> "--Users-jakelevirne--" and
26	// "/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory" -> "--Users-jakelevirne-dev-getspecstory--".
27	func EncodeCwd(cwd string) string {
28		encoded := strings.ReplaceAll(cwd, "/", "-")
29		return "-" + encoded + "--"
30	}
31	
32	// ProjectSessionDir returns the absolute path to pi's session subdirectory for
33	// the given project, WITHOUT requiring it to exist. Callers (DetectAgent, sync)
34	// check existence separately. The path is symlink-resolved before encoding so
35	// it matches the directory pi actually wrote to (pi encodes the real cwd); a
36	// relative or symlinked projectPath would otherwise produce a different name.
37	func ProjectSessionDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
38		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
39		if err != nil {
40			return "", err
41		}
42		cwd := strings.TrimSpace(projectPath)
43		if cwd == "" {
44			cwd, err = os.Getwd()
45			if err != nil {
46				return "", fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot get working dir: %w", err)
47			}
48		}
49		realPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cwd)
50		if err != nil {
51			realPath = cwd // fall back to the raw path if resolution fails
52		}
53		return filepath.Join(root, EncodeCwd(realPath)), nil
54	}
55	
56	// SessionFilesInProject lists the *.jsonl files in the project's pi session
57	// directory. Returns an empty slice (no error) if the directory does not exist.
58	func SessionFilesInProject(projectPath string) ([]string, error) {
59		dir, err := ProjectSessionDir(projectPath)
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
64		if err != nil {
65			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
66				return nil, nil
67			}
68			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading session dir %s: %w", dir, err)
69		}
70		var files []string
71		for _, e := range entries {
72			if e.IsDir() {
73				continue
74			}
75			if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".jsonl") {
76				continue
77			}
78			files = append(files, filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
79		}
80		return files, nil
81	}

107	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path
108	// branch into the unified schema.SessionData. It honors compaction entries:
109	// when a compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId
110	// are dropped from the conversation (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
112		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		if header == nil {
117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
118		}
119		if header.Type != entrySession {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
121		}
122		if header.ID == "" {
123			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
124		}
125		if len(entries) == 0 {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
127		}
128		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
129		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
130	}

132	// piProviderVersion derives the provider version string recorded on SessionData
133	// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
134	// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
135	func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
136		if header.Version > 0 {
137			return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
138		}
139		return "v1"
140	}
141	
142	// buildSessionData maps the ordered leaf-path entries into schema.SessionData.
143	func buildSessionData(header *sessionHeader, ordered []rawEntry) *schema.SessionData {
144		return &schema.SessionData{
145			SchemaVersion: "1.0",
146			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{
147				ID:      providerID,
148				Name:    providerName,
149				Version: piProviderVersion(header),
150			},
151			SessionID:     header.ID,
152			CreatedAt:     header.Timestamp,
153			WorkspaceRoot: header.Cwd,
154			Exchanges:     buildExchanges(ordered),
155		}
156	}
157	
158	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
159	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
160	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo. Control entries
161	// (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the conversation body.
162	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
163		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
164		var current *schema.Exchange
165		commit := func() {
166			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
167				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
168			}
169		}
170		for _, e := range ordered {
171			if e.Type != entryMessage {
172				continue
173			}
174			switch messageRole(e) {
175			case roleUser:
176				commit()
177				current = &schema.Exchange{
178					ExchangeID: e.ID,
179					StartTime:  e.Timestamp,
180					EndTime:    e.Timestamp,
181					Messages:   []schema.Message{buildUserMessage(e)},
182				}
183			case roleAssistant:
184				current = appendAssistant(current, e)
185			case roleToolResult:
186				mergeToolResult(current, e)
187			}
188		}
189		commit()
190		return exchanges
191	}
192	
193	// appendAssistant appends an assistant message to the current exchange, creating
194	// one if none exists yet.
195	func appendAssistant(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) *schema.Exchange {
196		if current == nil {
197			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
198		}
199		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, buildAgentMessages(e)...)
200		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
201		return current
202	}

213	// mergeToolResult folds a toolResult entry into the matching agent ToolInfo in
214	// the current exchange, keyed by toolCallId == ToolInfo.UseID. It also advances
215	// the exchange EndTime to the toolResult's timestamp so downstream stats that
216	// read the last exchange's EndTime report the real final-event time.
217	func mergeToolResult(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) {
218		if current == nil {
219			return
220		}
221		var tr toolResultMessage
222		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &tr); err != nil {
223			return
224		}
225		content := toolResultContent(tr)
226		for i := range current.Messages {
227			msg := &current.Messages[i]
228			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.UseID == tr.ToolCallID {
229				msg.Tool.Output = buildToolOutput(content, tr)
230				msg.Timestamp = e.Timestamp
231				current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
232				return
233			}
234		}
235	}

237	// toolResultContent joins the text blocks of a toolResult message.
238	func toolResultContent(tr toolResultMessage) string {
239		var parts []string
240		for _, b := range tr.Content {
241			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
242				parts = append(parts, b.Text)
243			}
244		}
245		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
246	}

248	// buildUserMessage maps a pi user message entry to a schema user Message.
249	// pi user content is either a plain string or an array of {type:text|image}.
250	func buildUserMessage(e rawEntry) schema.Message {
251		var um userMessage
252		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &um)
253		parts := userContentParts(um.Content)
254		return schema.Message{
255			ID:        e.ID,
256			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,

258			Content:   parts,

262	// userContentParts decodes a pi user message's content (string or array) into
263	// schema ContentParts. Image blocks are dropped in v1 (recorded as a gap).
264	func userContentParts(raw json.RawMessage) []schema.ContentPart {
265		if len(raw) == 0 {
266			return nil
267		}
268		if raw[0] == '"' {
269			var s string
270			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
271				return []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: s}}
272			}
273		}
274		var blocks []contentBlock
275		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
276			return nil
277		}
278		var parts []schema.ContentPart
279		for _, b := range blocks {
280			if b.Type == schema.ContentTypeText && b.Text != "" {
281				parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
282			}
283		}
284		return parts
285	}
286	
287	// buildAgentMessages maps a pi assistant message entry to one or more schema
288	// Messages: one Message holds the text+thinking content parts; each toolCall
289	// block becomes its own agent Message carrying a ToolInfo.
290	func buildAgentMessages(e rawEntry) []schema.Message {
291		var am assistantMessage
292		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &am); err != nil {
293			return nil
294		}
295		var parts []schema.ContentPart
296		var messages []schema.Message
297		for _, b := range am.Content {
298			switch b.Type {
299			case schema.ContentTypeText:
300				if b.Text != "" {
301					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
302				}
303			case schema.ContentTypeThinking:
304				if b.Thinking != "" {
305					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: b.Thinking})
306				}
307			case "toolCall":
308				messages = append(messages, buildToolMessage(e, b, am))
309			}
310		}
311		if len(parts) > 0 {
312			head := schema.Message{
313				ID:        e.ID,
314				Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
315				Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
316				Model:     am.Model,
317				Content:   parts,
318				Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
319			}
320			return append([]schema.Message{head}, messages...)
321		}
322		if len(messages) == 0 {
323			return buildErrorMessage(e, am)
324		}
325		// Tool-call-only assistant message: carry model+usage once on the first
326		// tool message so no metadata is lost and no schema-invalid empty message
327		// is emitted.
328		messages[0].Model = am.Model
329		if messages[0].Usage == nil {
330			messages[0].Usage = mapUsage(am.Usage)
331		}
332		return messages
333	}
334	
335	// buildToolMessage builds an agent Message wrapping a ToolInfo from a toolCall.
336	// The parent assistant message's model is passed through so tool messages carry
337	// the same model metadata as text/thinking messages. The Message ID is derived
338	// from the parent entry id + the toolCall id, so multiple toolCalls in one
339	// assistant message get distinct Message IDs (downstream provenance keys use
340	// msg.ID as a deterministic component).
341	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
342		return schema.Message{
343			ID:        toolMessageID(e.ID, b.ID),
344			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
345			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
346			Model:     am.Model,
347			Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{
348				Name:  b.Name,
349				Type:  classifyToolType(b.Name),
350				UseID: b.ID,
351				Input: b.Args,
352			},
353		}
354	}
355	
356	// toolMessageID builds a unique Message ID for a tool-call message from the
357	// parent entry id and the toolCall id. This avoids duplicate Message IDs when a
358	// single assistant entry contains multiple toolCall blocks.
359	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {
360		if callID != "" {
361			return entryID + ":" + callID
362		}
363		return entryID
364	}
365	
366	// buildToolOutput constructs the ToolInfo.Output map from a toolResult's
367	// content, error flag, and optional details blob. details (e.g. exitCode) is
368	// decoded into a generic value so downstream consumers (markdown rendering,
369	// cloud) can surface structured tool metadata without re-parsing raw JSON.
370	func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
371		out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
372		if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
373			var details any
374			if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {
375				out["details"] = details
376			}
377		}
378		return out
379	}
380	
381	// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map
382	// to InputTokens/OutputTokens; cacheRead/cacheWrite map to the Claude-style
383	// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics).
384	func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
385		if u == nil {
386			return nil
387		}
388		return &schema.Usage{
389			InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
390			OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
391			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
392			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
393		}
394	}
395	
396	// buildErrorMessage surfaces an assistant entry with stopReason=error and an
397	// empty content array (no text/thinking/toolCalls) as an agent text message so
398	// the error event is not dropped from the transcript (and compaction boundaries
399	// stay interpretable). Returns nil if there is no errorMessage to surface.
400	func buildErrorMessage(e rawEntry, am assistantMessage) []schema.Message {
401		if strings.TrimSpace(am.ErrorMessage) == "" {
402			return nil
403		}
404		return []schema.Message{{
405			ID:        e.ID,
406			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
407			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
408			Model:     am.Model,
409			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "[error] " + am.ErrorMessage}},
410			Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
411		}}
412	}
413	
414	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
415	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
416	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
417	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
418		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
419			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
420				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
421					continue
422				}
423				for _, part := range msg.Content {
424					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {
425						return spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(t)
426					}
427				}
428			}
429		}
430		return ""
431	}
432	
433	// classifyToolType maps pi tool names to the schema tool-type taxonomy.
434	func classifyToolType(name string) string {
435		switch strings.ToLower(name) {
436		case "read":
437			return schema.ToolTypeRead
438		case "edit", "write":
439			return schema.ToolTypeWrite
440		case "bash", "ls":
441			return schema.ToolTypeShell
442		case "grep", "find", "web_search", "fetch_content":
443			return schema.ToolTypeSearch
444		case "until_done_set", "until_done_plan", "until_done_task_update",
445			"until_done_progress", "until_done_complete", "until_done_block",
446			"until_done_replan", "until_done_distill":
447			return schema.ToolTypeTask
448		default:
449			return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
450		}
451	}
452	
453	// firstUserText extracts the first user message text from a message entry, if
454	// its role is "user". Returns "" for non-user messages or empty content.
455	func firstUserText(e rawEntry) string {
456		var m struct {
457			Role    string          `json:"role"`
458			Content json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
459		}
460		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m); err != nil {
461			return ""
462		}
463		if m.Role != roleUser {
464			return ""
465		}
466		return userContentString(m.Content)
467	}
468	
469	// userContentString extracts a plain string from a pi user message content
470	// field (either a string or an array of {type:text} blocks). The result is
471	// trimmed so the scan path produces the same Slug/Name as the full-parse path
472	// (deriveSlug trims too).
473	func userContentString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
474		if len(raw) == 0 {
475			return ""
476		}
477		var s string
478		if raw[0] == '"' {
479			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
480				return strings.TrimSpace(s)
481			}
482		}
483		var blocks []contentBlock
484		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
485			return ""
486		}
487		for _, b := range blocks {
488			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
489				return strings.TrimSpace(b.Text)
490			}
491		}
492		return ""
493	}

1	package piagent

3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"log/slog"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"strings"
13	)
14	
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// Skip entries missing the envelope fields the tree walk and exchange
91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}
104	
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
187	
188	// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
189	// if not found.
190	func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
191		for i, e := range path {
192			if e.ID == keptID {
193				return i
194			}
195		}
196		return -1
197	}

1	package piagent
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// piSessionsRoot returns ~/.pi/agent/sessions, the directory under which pi
11	// stores one subdirectory per working directory (each named with the encoded
12	// cwd, see EncodeCwd). It does not require the directory to exist.
13	func piSessionsRoot() (string, error) {
14		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
15		if err != nil {
16			return "", fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot resolve home dir: %w", err)
17		}
18		return filepath.Join(home, ".pi", "agent", "sessions"), nil
19	}
20	
21	// EncodeCwd maps a working directory to pi's session-subdirectory name.
22	// pi replaces every '/' in the absolute path with '-' and wraps the result with
23	// a leading '-' and a trailing '--', producing e.g. "/Users/jane/proj" ->
24	// "--Users-jane-proj--". The encoding is derived from real session dirs:
25	// "/Users/jakelevirne" -> "--Users-jakelevirne--" and
26	// "/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory" -> "--Users-jakelevirne-dev-getspecstory--".
27	func EncodeCwd(cwd string) string {
28		encoded := strings.ReplaceAll(cwd, "/", "-")
29		return "-" + encoded + "--"
30	}
31	
32	// ProjectSessionDir returns the absolute path to pi's session subdirectory for
33	// the given project, WITHOUT requiring it to exist. Callers (DetectAgent, sync)
34	// check existence separately. The path is symlink-resolved before encoding so
35	// it matches the directory pi actually wrote to (pi encodes the real cwd); a
36	// relative or symlinked projectPath would otherwise produce a different name.
37	func ProjectSessionDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
38		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
39		if err != nil {
40			return "", err
41		}
42		cwd := strings.TrimSpace(projectPath)
43		if cwd == "" {
44			cwd, err = os.Getwd()
45			if err != nil {
46				return "", fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot get working dir: %w", err)
47			}
48		}
49		realPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cwd)
50		if err != nil {
51			realPath = cwd // fall back to the raw path if resolution fails
52		}
53		return filepath.Join(root, EncodeCwd(realPath)), nil
54	}
55	
56	// SessionFilesInProject lists the *.jsonl files in the project's pi session
57	// directory. Returns an empty slice (no error) if the directory does not exist.
58	func SessionFilesInProject(projectPath string) ([]string, error) {
59		dir, err := ProjectSessionDir(projectPath)
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
64		if err != nil {
65			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
66				return nil, nil
67			}
68			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading session dir %s: %w", dir, err)
69		}
70		var files []string
71		for _, e := range entries {
72			if e.IsDir() {
73				continue
74			}
75			if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".jsonl") {
76				continue
77			}
78			files = append(files, filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
79		}
80		return files, nil
81	}

13	// writeDebugRaw writes numbered JSON files (one per non-header entry) plus the
14	// central session-data.json via the shared spi helper. This matches the
15	// --debug-raw contract used by every provider.
16	func writeDebugRaw(sessionPath string, data *schema.SessionData) error {
17		if err := spi.WriteDebugSessionData(data.SessionID, data); err != nil {
18			return err
19		}
20		dir := spi.GetDebugDir(data.SessionID)
21		entries, err := readRawEntries(sessionPath)
22		if err != nil {
23			return err
24		}
25		return writeNumberedEntries(dir, entries)
26	}
27	
28	// writeNumberedEntries writes each raw entry as 1.json, 2.json, ... in dir.
29	func writeNumberedEntries(dir string, entries []json.RawMessage) error {
30		for i, raw := range entries {
31			filePath := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", i+1))
32			payload, mErr := json.MarshalIndent(raw, "", "  ")
33			if mErr != nil {
34				continue
35			}
36			if wErr := os.WriteFile(filePath, payload, 0o644); wErr != nil {
37				return wErr
38			}
39		}
40		return nil
41	}
42	
43	// readRawEntries returns each non-header line of a session file as a raw JSON
44	// value, for debug-raw burst output. Uses bufio.Reader (via readLines) so
45	// arbitrarily large lines are captured without the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap.
46	func readRawEntries(path string) ([]json.RawMessage, error) {
47		var out []json.RawMessage
48		first := true
49		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
50			if first {
51				first = false // skip the session header line
52				return nil
53			}
54			out = append(out, json.RawMessage(line))
55			return nil
56		})
57		return out, err
58	}

22	// Provider implements the SPI Provider interface for Claude Code
23	type Provider struct{}

25	// NewProvider creates a new Claude Code provider instance
26	func NewProvider() *Provider {

28	}

30	// filterWarmupMessages removes warmup messages (sidechain messages before first real message)
31	func filterWarmupMessages(records []JSONLRecord) []JSONLRecord {
32		// Find first non-sidechain message
33		firstRealMessageIndex := -1
34		for i, record := range records {
35			if isSidechain, ok := record.Data["isSidechain"].(bool); !ok || !isSidechain {
36				firstRealMessageIndex = i
37				break
38			}
39		}
40	
41		// No real messages found
42		if firstRealMessageIndex == -1 {
43			return []JSONLRecord{}
44		}
45	
46		// Return records starting from first real message
47		return records[firstRealMessageIndex:]
48	}
49	
50	// processSession filters warmup messages and converts a Session to an AgentChatSession
51	// Returns nil if the session is warmup-only (no real messages)
52	func processSession(session Session, workspaceRoot string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
53		// Write debug files first (even for warmup-only sessions)
54		if debugRaw {
55			// Write debug files and get the record-to-file mapping
56			_ = writeDebugRawFiles(session) // Unused but needed for side effect
57		}
58	
59		// Filter warmup messages
60		filteredRecords := filterWarmupMessages(session.Records)
61	
62		// Skip if no real messages remain after filtering warmup
63		if len(filteredRecords) == 0 {
64			slog.Debug("Skipping warmup-only session", "sessionId", session.SessionUuid)
65			return nil
66		}
67	
68		// Create session with filtered records
69		filteredSession := Session{
70			SessionUuid: session.SessionUuid,
71			Records:     filteredRecords,
72		}
73	
74		// Get timestamp from root record
75		rootRecord := filteredSession.Records[0]
76		timestamp := rootRecord.Data["timestamp"].(string)
77	
78		// Get the slug
79		slug := FileSlugFromRootRecord(filteredSession)
80	
81		// Generate SessionData from filtered session
82		sessionData, err := GenerateAgentSession(filteredSession, workspaceRoot)
83		if err != nil {
84			slog.Error("Failed to generate SessionData", "sessionId", session.SessionUuid, "error", err)
85			return nil
86		}
87	
88		// Convert session records to JSONL format for raw data
89		// Note: Uses unfiltered session.Records (not filteredSession.Records) to preserve
90		// all records including warmup messages in the raw data for complete audit trail
91		var rawDataBuilder strings.Builder
92		for _, record := range session.Records {
93			jsonBytes, _ := json.Marshal(record.Data)
94			rawDataBuilder.Write(jsonBytes)
95			rawDataBuilder.WriteString("\n")
96		}
97	
98		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
99			SessionID:   session.SessionUuid,
100			CreatedAt:   timestamp, // ISO 8601 timestamp
101			Slug:        slug,
102			SessionData: sessionData,
103			RawData:     rawDataBuilder.String(),
104		}
105	}

112	// buildCheckErrorMessage creates a user-facing error message tailored to the failure type.
113	func buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType string, claudeCmd string, isCustom bool, stderrOutput string) string {
114		var errorMsg strings.Builder
115	
116		switch errorType {
117		case "not_found":
118			fmt.Fprintf(&errorMsg, "  🔍 Could not find Claude Code at: %s\n", claudeCmd)
119			errorMsg.WriteString("\n")
120			errorMsg.WriteString("  💡 Here's how to fix this:\n")
121			errorMsg.WriteString("\n")
122			if isCustom {
123				errorMsg.WriteString("     The specified path doesn't exist. Please check:\n")
124				fmt.Fprintf(&errorMsg, "     • Is Claude Code installed at %s?\n", claudeCmd)
125				errorMsg.WriteString("     • Did you type the path correctly?")
126			} else {
127				errorMsg.WriteString("     1. Make sure Claude Code is installed:\n")
128				errorMsg.WriteString("        • Visit https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/quickstart\n")
129				errorMsg.WriteString("\n")
130				errorMsg.WriteString("     2. If it's already installed, try:\n")
131				errorMsg.WriteString("        • Check if 'claude' is in your PATH\n")
132				errorMsg.WriteString("        • Use -c flag to specify the full path\n")
133				errorMsg.WriteString("        • Example: specstory check claude -c \"~/.claude/local/claude\"")
134			}
135		case "permission_denied":
136			fmt.Fprintf(&errorMsg, "  🔒 Permission denied when trying to run: %s\n", claudeCmd)
137			errorMsg.WriteString("\n")
138			errorMsg.WriteString("  💡 Here's how to fix this:\n")
139			fmt.Fprintf(&errorMsg, "     • Check file permissions: chmod +x %s\n", claudeCmd)
140			errorMsg.WriteString("     • Try running with elevated permissions if needed")
141		case "unexpected_output":
142			fmt.Fprintf(&errorMsg, "  ⚠️  Unexpected output from 'claude -v': %s\n", strings.TrimSpace(stderrOutput))
143			errorMsg.WriteString("\n")
144			errorMsg.WriteString("  💡 This might not be Claude Code. Expected output containing '(Claude Code)'.\n")
145			errorMsg.WriteString("     • Make sure you have Claude Code installed, not a different 'claude' command\n")
146			errorMsg.WriteString("     • Visit https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/quickstart for installation")
147		default:
148			errorMsg.WriteString("  ⚠️  Error running 'claude -v'\n")
149			if stderrOutput != "" {
150				fmt.Fprintf(&errorMsg, "  📋 Error details: %s\n", stderrOutput)
151			}
152			errorMsg.WriteString("\n")
153			errorMsg.WriteString("  💡 Troubleshooting tips:\n")
154			errorMsg.WriteString("     • Make sure Claude Code is properly installed\n")
155			errorMsg.WriteString("     • Try running 'claude -v' directly in your terminal\n")
156			errorMsg.WriteString("     • Check https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/quickstart for installation help")
157		}
158	
159		return errorMsg.String()
160	}

162	// Check verifies Claude Code installation and returns version info
163	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
164		// Parse the command (no resume session for version check)
165		claudeCmd, _ := parseClaudeCommand(customCommand, "")
166	
167		// Determine if custom command was used
168		isCustomCommand := customCommand != ""
169	
170		// Resolve the actual path of the command
171		resolvedPath := claudeCmd
172		if !filepath.IsAbs(claudeCmd) {
173			// Try to find the command in PATH
174			if path, err := exec.LookPath(claudeCmd); err == nil {
175				resolvedPath = path
176			}
177		}
178	
179		// Run claude -v to check version (ignore custom args for version check)
180		cmd := exec.Command(claudeCmd, "-v")
181		var out bytes.Buffer
182		var errOut bytes.Buffer
183		cmd.Stdout = &out
184		cmd.Stderr = &errOut
185	
186		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
187			// Track installation check failure
188			errorType := "unknown"
189	
190			var execErr *exec.Error
191			var pathErr *os.PathError
192	
193			// Check error types in order of specificity
194			switch {
195			case errors.As(err, &execErr) && execErr.Err == exec.ErrNotFound:
196				errorType = "not_found"
197			case errors.As(err, &pathErr):
198				if errors.Is(pathErr.Err, os.ErrNotExist) {
199					errorType = "not_found"
200				} else if errors.Is(pathErr.Err, os.ErrPermission) {
201					errorType = "permission_denied"
202				}
203			case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
204				errorType = "permission_denied"
205			}
206	
207			stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(errOut.String())
208			analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCheckInstallFailed, analytics.Properties{
209				"provider":       "claude",
210				"custom_command": isCustomCommand,
211				"command_path":   claudeCmd,
212				"error_type":     errorType,
213				"error_message":  err.Error(),
214			})
215	
216			errorMessage := buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, claudeCmd, isCustomCommand, stderrOutput)
217	
218			return spi.CheckResult{
219				Success:      false,
220				Version:      "",
221				Location:     resolvedPath,
222				ErrorMessage: errorMessage,
223			}
224		}
225	
226		// Check if output contains "Claude Code"
227		output := out.String()
228		if !strings.Contains(output, "(Claude Code)") {
229			// Track unexpected output error
230			analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCheckInstallFailed, analytics.Properties{
231				"provider":       "claude",
232				"custom_command": isCustomCommand,
233				"command_path":   claudeCmd,
234				"error_type":     "unexpected_output",
235				"output":         strings.TrimSpace(output),
236			})
237	
238			errorMessage := buildCheckErrorMessage("unexpected_output", claudeCmd, isCustomCommand, output)
239	
240			return spi.CheckResult{
241				Success:      false,
242				Version:      "",
243				Location:     resolvedPath,
244				ErrorMessage: errorMessage,
245			}
246		}
247	
248		// Success! Track it
249		analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCheckInstallSuccess, analytics.Properties{
250			"provider":       "claude",
251			"custom_command": isCustomCommand,
252			"command_path":   resolvedPath,
253			"version":        strings.TrimSpace(output),
254		})
255	
256		return spi.CheckResult{
257			Success:      true,
258			Version:      strings.TrimSpace(output),
259			Location:     resolvedPath,
260			ErrorMessage: "",
261		}
262	}

264	// DetectAgent checks if Claude Code has been used in the given project directory
265	func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
266		// Get the Claude Code project directory for the given path
267		claudeProjectPath, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectDir(projectPath)
268		if err != nil {
269			slog.Debug("DetectAgent: Failed to get Claude Code project directory", "error", err)
270			return false
271		}
272	
273		// Check if the Claude Code project directory exists
274		if info, err := os.Stat(claudeProjectPath); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
275			slog.Debug("DetectAgent: Claude Code project found", "path", claudeProjectPath)
276			return true
277		}
278	
279		slog.Debug("DetectAgent: No Claude Code project found", "expected_path", claudeProjectPath)
280	
281		// If helpOutput is requested, provide helpful guidance
282		if helpOutput {
283			fmt.Println() // Add visual separation
284			log.UserWarn("No Claude Code project found for this directory.\n")
285			log.UserMessage("Claude Code hasn't created a project folder for your current directory yet.\n")
286			log.UserMessage("This happens when Claude Code hasn't been run in this directory.\n\n")
287			log.UserMessage("To fix this:\n")
288			log.UserMessage("  1. Run 'specstory run' to start Claude Code in this directory\n")
289			log.UserMessage("  2. Or run Claude Code directly with `claude`, then try syncing again\n\n")
290			log.UserMessage("Expected project folder: %s\n", claudeProjectPath)
291			fmt.Println() // Add trailing newline
292		}
293	
294		return false
295	}

297	// GetAgentChatSessions retrieves all chat sessions for the given project path
298	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
299		// Get the Claude Code project directory
300		claudeProjectDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectDir(projectPath)
301		if err != nil {
302			return nil, err
303		}
304	
305		// Check if project directory exists
306		if _, err := os.Stat(claudeProjectDir); os.IsNotExist(err) {
307			return []spi.AgentChatSession{}, nil // No sessions if no project
308		}
309	
310		// Parse JSONL files with progress callback
311		parser := NewJSONLParser()
312		err = parser.ParseProjectSessionsWithProgress(claudeProjectDir, progress)
313		if err != nil {
314			return nil, err
315		}
316	
317		// Convert sessions to AgentChatSession structs
318		result := make([]spi.AgentChatSession, 0, len(parser.Sessions))
319		for _, session := range parser.Sessions {
320			// Skip empty sessions (no records)
321			if len(session.Records) == 0 {
322				continue
323			}
324	
325			// Process session (filter warmup, generate SessionData)
326			chatSession := processSession(session, projectPath, debugRaw)
327			if chatSession != nil {
328				result = append(result, *chatSession)
329			}
330		}
331	
332		return result, nil
333	}

335	// GetAgentChatSession retrieves a single chat session by ID for the given project path
336	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath string, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
337		// Get the Claude Code project directory
338		claudeProjectDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectDir(projectPath)
339		if err != nil {
340			return nil, err
341		}
342	
343		// Check if project directory exists
344		if _, err := os.Stat(claudeProjectDir); os.IsNotExist(err) {
345			return nil, nil // No sessions if no project
346		}
347	
348		// Parse only the session we're looking for
349		parser := NewJSONLParser()
350		err = parser.ParseSingleSession(claudeProjectDir, sessionID)
351		if err != nil {
352			// If session not found, return nil (not an error)
353			if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "not found") {
354				return nil, nil
355			}
356			return nil, err
357		}
358	
359		// Find the session
360		sessionPointer := parser.FindSession(sessionID)
361		if sessionPointer == nil {
362			return nil, nil
363		}
364		session := *sessionPointer
365	
366		// Skip empty sessions (no records)
367		if len(session.Records) == 0 {
368			return nil, nil
369		}
370	
371		// Process session (filter warmup, generate SessionData)
372		return processSession(session, projectPath, debugRaw), nil
373	}

375	// ExecAgentAndWatch executes Claude Code in interactive mode and watches for session updates
376	func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
377		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: Starting Claude Code execution and monitoring",
378			"projectPath", projectPath,
379			"customCommand", customCommand,
380			"resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID,
381			"debugRaw", debugRaw)
382	
383		// Validate resume session ID if provided (Claude Code uses UUID format)
384		if resumeSessionID != "" {
385			resumeSessionID = strings.TrimSpace(resumeSessionID)
386			// Simple UUID validation for Claude Code sessions
387			if len(resumeSessionID) != 36 || !strings.Contains(resumeSessionID, "-") {
388				return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID format for Claude Code: %s (must be a UUID)", resumeSessionID)
389			}
390			slog.Info("Resuming Claude Code session", "sessionId", resumeSessionID)
391		}
392	
393		// Set up the callback which enables real-time markdown generation and cloud sync during
394		// interactive sessions. As Claude Code writes JSONL updates, the watcher detects
395		// changes and invokes this callback, allowing immediate processing without blocking
396		// the agent's execution. The defer ensures cleanup when the agent exits.
397		SetWatcherCallback(sessionCallback)
398		defer ClearWatcherCallback()
399	
400		// Set debug raw mode for the watcher
401		SetWatcherDebugRaw(debugRaw)
402	
403		// Start watching for project directory in the background
404		slog.Info("Initializing project directory monitoring...")
405	
406		if err := WatchForProjectDir(); err != nil {
407			// Log the error but don't fail - watcher might work later
408			slog.Error("Failed to start project directory watcher", "error", err)
409		}
410	
411		// Execute Claude Code - this blocks until Claude exits
412		slog.Info("Executing Claude Code", "command", customCommand)
413		err := ExecuteClaude(customCommand, resumeSessionID)
414	
415		// Stop the watcher goroutine before returning
416		slog.Info("Claude Code has exited, stopping watcher")
417		StopWatcher()
418	
419		// Return any execution error
420		if err != nil {
421			return fmt.Errorf("claude Code execution failed: %w", err)
422		}
423	
424		return nil
425	}
426	
427	// WatchAgent watches for Claude Code agent activity and calls the callback with AgentChatSession
428	// Does NOT execute the agent - only watches for existing activity
429	// Runs until error or context cancellation
430	func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
431		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Starting Claude Code activity monitoring",
432			"projectPath", projectPath,
433			"debugRaw", debugRaw)
434	
435		// The watcher callback directly passes AgentChatSession (which now contains SessionData)
436		wrappedCallback := func(agentChatSession *spi.AgentChatSession) {
437			slog.Debug("WatchAgent: Received AgentChatSession",
438				"sessionID", agentChatSession.SessionID,
439				"hasSessionData", agentChatSession.SessionData != nil)
440	
441			// Call the user's callback with the AgentChatSession
442			sessionCallback(agentChatSession)
443		}
444	
445		// Set up the callback for the watcher
446		SetWatcherCallback(wrappedCallback)
447		defer ClearWatcherCallback()
448	
449		// Set debug raw mode for the watcher
450		SetWatcherDebugRaw(debugRaw)
451	
452		// Get the Claude Code project directory for the specified project path
453		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Initializing project directory monitoring...")
454	
455		claudeProjectDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectDir(projectPath)
456		if err != nil {
457			slog.Error("WatchAgent: Failed to get Claude Code project directory", "error", err)
458			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get project directory: %w", err)
459		}
460	
461		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Project directory found", "directory", claudeProjectDir)
462	
463		if err := startProjectWatcher(claudeProjectDir); err != nil {
464			slog.Error("WatchAgent: Failed to start project watcher", "error", err)
465			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start watcher: %w", err)
466		}
467	
468		// Block until context is cancelled
469		// The watcher runs in a background goroutine and will continue
470		// until context is cancelled or the process exits
471		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Watcher started, blocking until context cancelled")
472	
473		// Wait for context cancellation
474		<-ctx.Done()
475	
476		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Context cancelled, stopping watcher")
477		StopWatcher()
478	
479		return ctx.Err()
480	}
481	
482	// isSyntheticMessage checks if a message is synthetic/internal and should be skipped
483	// when looking for the first real user message (e.g. for the session title/slug).
484	// Filters warmup prompts, title-generation prompts, and slash-command noise (the
485	// command invocation, its local stdout/stderr, and the local-command caveat) — these
486	// are conversation scaffolding, not the user's actual prompt. Without this, a session
487	// that opens with a slash command gets an empty title and falls back to its UUID.
488	func isSyntheticMessage(content string) bool {
489		// warmup and the <TEXTBLOCK> title-generation wrapper can be embedded anywhere
490		// in the record, so match them with Contains.
491		if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(content), "warmup") {
492			return true
493		}
494		if strings.Contains(content, "<TEXTBLOCK>") {
495			return true
496		}
497		// The slash-command scaffolding tags (shared with reconstruction via
498		// spi.SyntheticCommandTags) and the interrupt marker REPLACE the prompt, so they
499		// appear at the very START of the record. Match by prefix so a real prompt that
500		// merely mentions a tag mid-sentence is still treated as real. The interrupt
501		// marker's "…for tool use" variant is caught by the same prefix.
502		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(content)
503		for _, marker := range spi.SyntheticCommandTags {
504			if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, marker) {
505				return true
506			}
507		}
508		return strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "[Request interrupted by user")
509	}
510	
511	// extractContentText extracts plain text from a message content field.
512	// The content field may be either a plain string or a JSON array of typed content
513	// blocks (e.g. [{type:"text",text:"..."},{type:"tool_use",...}]).
514	// When it's an array, all "text"-type blocks are joined with newlines.
515	// This handles the Claude Code JSONL format where IDE context tags (e.g.
516	// <ide_opened_file>) are injected as separate text blocks before the real question.
517	func extractContentText(content interface{}) string {
518		switch v := content.(type) {
519		case string:
520			return v
521		case []interface{}:
522			var parts []string
523			for _, block := range v {
524				if m, ok := block.(map[string]interface{}); ok {
525					if t, _ := m["type"].(string); t == "text" {
526						if text, ok := m["text"].(string); ok && text != "" {
527							parts = append(parts, text)
528						}
529					}
530				}
531			}
532			slog.Debug("extractContentText: extracted text from content block array",
533				"blockCount", len(v),
534				"textParts", len(parts))
535			return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
536		default:
537			return ""
538		}
539	}
540	
541	// findFirstUserMessage finds the first user message in a session for slug generation
542	// Returns empty string if no suitable user message is found
543	func findFirstUserMessage(session Session) string {
544		for _, record := range session.Records {
545			// Check if this is a user message
546			if recordType, ok := record.Data["type"].(string); !ok || recordType != "user" {
547				continue
548			}
549	
550			// Skip meta user messages
551			if isMeta, ok := record.Data["isMeta"].(bool); ok && isMeta {
552				continue
553			}
554	
555			// Extract content from message - content may be a string or a list of blocks
556			if message, ok := record.Data["message"].(map[string]interface{}); ok {
557				content := extractContentText(message["content"])
558				if content != "" {
559					// Skip synthetic messages (warmup, title generation prompts, etc.)
560					if isSyntheticMessage(content) {
561						continue
562					}
563					return content
564				}
565			}
566		}
567		return ""
568	}
569	
570	// FileSlugFromRootRecord generates the slug part of the filename from the session
571	// Returns the human-readable slug derived from the first user message, or empty string if none
572	func FileSlugFromRootRecord(session Session) string {
573		// Find the first user message and generate slug from it
574		firstUserMessage := findFirstUserMessage(session)
575		slog.Debug("FileSlugFromRootRecord: First user message",
576			"sessionId", session.SessionUuid,
577			"message", firstUserMessage)
578	
579		slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(firstUserMessage)
580		slog.Debug("FileSlugFromRootRecord: Generated slug",
581			"sessionId", session.SessionUuid,
582			"slug", slug)
583	
584		return slug
585	}

587	// ListAgentChatSessions retrieves lightweight session metadata without full parsing
588	// This is much faster than GetAgentChatSessions as it only reads minimal data from each session
589	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
590		// Get the Claude Code project directory
591		claudeProjectDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectDir(projectPath)
592		if err != nil {
593			return nil, err
594		}
595	
596		// Check if project directory exists
597		if _, err := os.Stat(claudeProjectDir); os.IsNotExist(err) {
598			return []spi.SessionMetadata{}, nil // No sessions if no project
599		}
600	
601		// Collect all JSONL files in the project directory
602		var sessionFiles []string
603		err = filepath.Walk(claudeProjectDir, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
604			if err != nil {
605				return err
606			}
607			if info.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".jsonl") {
608				return nil
609			}
610			sessionFiles = append(sessionFiles, path)
611			return nil
612		})
613		if err != nil {
614			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to scan project directory: %w", err)
615		}
616	
617		// Extract metadata from each session file
618		sessions := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(sessionFiles))
619		for _, filePath := range sessionFiles {
620			metadata, err := extractSessionMetadata(filePath)
621			if err != nil {
622				slog.Warn("Failed to extract session metadata",
623					"file", filePath,
624					"error", err)
625				continue
626			}
627	
628			// Skip warmup-only sessions (no metadata means warmup-only)
629			if metadata == nil {
630				slog.Debug("Skipping warmup-only session", "file", filePath)
631				continue
632			}
633	
634			sessions = append(sessions, *metadata)
635		}
636	
637		return sessions, nil
638	}
639	
640	// claudeSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one pass:
641	// identity + first-message metadata, plus the originating cwd (Claude Code stamps a
642	// top-level "cwd" on every conversational record). foundRealMessage is false for
643	// warmup-only sessions (no real messages).
644	type claudeSessionScan struct {
645		sessionID        string
646		timestamp        string
647		firstUserMessage string
648		commandFallback  string // slash command title when there is no free-text prompt
649		cwd              string
650		foundRealMessage bool
651	}
652	
653	// scanClaudeSession reads minimal data from a session file: session id, first-real
654	// timestamp, first user message, and originating cwd. Shared by the project-scoped
655	// metadata path and the global enumeration (ListAllAgentChatSessions).
656	func scanClaudeSession(filePath string) (*claudeSessionScan, error) {
657		file, err := os.Open(filePath)
658		if err != nil {
659			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open session file: %w", err)
660		}
661		defer func() {
662			_ = file.Close()
663		}()
664	
665		reader := bufio.NewReader(file)
666		scan := &claudeSessionScan{}
667	
668		// Read records until we find everything we need.
669		// Why: ReadString can return data AND io.EOF on the last line (no trailing newline),
670		// so we always process the line first, then check for EOF once at the bottom.
671		lineNum := 0
672		for {
673			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
674			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
675				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read line: %w", readErr)
676			}
677	
678			lineNum++
679			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
680	
681			if line != "" {
682				// Parse JSON record
683				var record map[string]interface{}
684				if jsonErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &record); jsonErr != nil {
685					slog.Warn("Skipping malformed JSONL line",
686						"file", filepath.Base(filePath),
687						"line", lineNum,
688						"error", jsonErr)
689				} else {
690					// Extract session ID (from any record)
691					if scan.sessionID == "" {
692						if sid, ok := record["sessionId"].(string); ok {
693							scan.sessionID = sid
694						}
695					}
696	
697					// Capture the originating cwd (first record that carries one). This is
698					// the input to project-identity resolution for the restore index.
699					if scan.cwd == "" {
700						if cwd, ok := record["cwd"].(string); ok && cwd != "" {
701							scan.cwd = cwd
702						}
703					}
704	
705					// Only process non-sidechain, non-system records for message extraction
706					isSidechain, _ := record["isSidechain"].(bool)
707					recordType, hasType := record["type"].(string)
708					isSystemRecord := hasType && (recordType == "file-history-snapshot" || recordType == "file-change")
709	
710					if !isSidechain && !isSystemRecord {
711						scan.foundRealMessage = true
712						// created_at = the first real record that actually carries a timestamp.
713						// (The leading {mode,sessionId,type} record has none, so we can't gate
714						// timestamp capture on "first real record" — it would stay empty.)
715						if scan.timestamp == "" {
716							if ts, ok := record["timestamp"].(string); ok && ts != "" {
717								scan.timestamp = ts
718							}
719						}
720	
721						// Extract first user message for slug (if this is a user message)
722						// Content may be a string or a list of typed blocks (see extractContentText)
723						if scan.firstUserMessage == "" && hasType && recordType == "user" {
724							isMeta, _ := record["isMeta"].(bool)
725							if !isMeta {
726								if message, ok := record["message"].(map[string]interface{}); ok {
727									content := extractContentText(message["content"])
728									if content != "" {
729										if isSyntheticMessage(content) {
730											// A slash-command session may have no free-text prompt;
731											// remember the command name as a fallback title.
732											if scan.commandFallback == "" {
733												scan.commandFallback = extractCommandName(content)
734											}
735										} else {
736											scan.firstUserMessage = content
737										}
738									}
739								}
740							}
741						}
742					}
743				}
744			}
745	
746			// Single exit: found everything we need, or reached end of file
747			if (scan.sessionID != "" && scan.timestamp != "" && scan.firstUserMessage != "" && scan.cwd != "") || readErr == io.EOF {
748				break
749			}
750		}
751	
752		// Fall back to the slash command when there was no real user prompt (so a
753		// command-only session shows e.g. "/code-review" instead of its UUID).
754		if scan.firstUserMessage == "" {
755			scan.firstUserMessage = scan.commandFallback
756		}
757		return scan, nil
758	}
759	
760	// extractCommandName pulls the slash command from a Claude Code command record, e.g.
761	// "<command-name>/code-review</command-name>…" -> "/code-review". Falls back to the
762	// bare command-message name (prefixed with "/"). Returns "" when none is present.
763	func extractCommandName(content string) string {
764		if c := between(content, "<command-name>", "</command-name>"); c != "" {
765			return c
766		}
767		if c := between(content, "<command-message>", "</command-message>"); c != "" {
768			return "/" + c
769		}
770		return ""
771	}
772	
773	// between returns the text between the first open/close markers, trimmed, or "".
774	func between(s, openTag, closeTag string) string {
775		_, after, ok := strings.Cut(s, openTag)
776		if !ok {
777			return ""
778		}
779		inner, _, ok := strings.Cut(after, closeTag)
780		if !ok {
781			return ""
782		}
783		return strings.TrimSpace(inner)
784	}
785	
786	// extractSessionMetadata reads minimal data from a session file to extract metadata
787	// Returns nil if the session is warmup-only (no real messages)
788	func extractSessionMetadata(filePath string) (*spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
789		scan, err := scanClaudeSession(filePath)
790		if err != nil {
791			return nil, err
792		}
793	
794		// If no real message was found, this is a warmup-only session
795		if !scan.foundRealMessage {
796			return nil, nil
797		}
798	
799		return &spi.SessionMetadata{
800			SessionID: scan.sessionID,
801			CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
802			Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
803			Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
804		}, nil
805	}
806	
807	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every Claude Code session across all projects. It is the
808	// no-progress form of ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress.
809	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
810		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
811	}
812	
813	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates every Claude Code session across all projects by
814	// walking ~/.claude/projects/*/ for *.jsonl (the originating cwd comes from inside each session;
815	// the project directory name is a lossy, irreversible encoding of the path), reporting scan
816	// progress into r (nil-safe). Headers are scanned in parallel across CPUs; output order is
817	// irrelevant (reindex dedups and sorts later). Implements spi.ProgressEnumerator. See
818	// docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
819	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
820		projectsDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectsDir()
821		if err != nil {
822			// No projects directory yet → nothing to enumerate (not an error).
823			return []spi.GlobalSessionRef{}, nil
824		}
825	
826		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(projectsDir, "claude", r, func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
827			scan, scanErr := scanClaudeSession(path)
828			if scanErr != nil {
829				return nil, scanErr
830			}
831			if !scan.foundRealMessage {
832				return nil, nil // warmup-only or sidechain-only transcript (not a session)
833			}
834			return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
835				SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
836				CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
837				Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
838				Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
839				NativePath: path,
840				OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
841			}, nil
842		})
843	}
844
