```text
394					outputJSON, _ := payload["output"].(string)
395	
396					if callID == "" || outputJSON == "" {
397						continue
398					}
399	
400					// Find the pending tool call
401					if pending, exists := pendingTools[callID]; exists {
402						// Parse the output JSON
403						var outputData map[string]interface{}
404						if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(outputJSON), &outputData); err == nil {
405							pending.toolInfo.Output = outputData
406						} else {
407							pending.toolInfo.Output = map[string]interface{}{"raw": outputJSON}
408						}
409						delete(pendingTools, callID)
410					}
411	
412				case "custom_tool_call":
413					// Custom tool call (e.g., apply_patch)
414					if currentExchange == nil {
415						currentExchange = &Exchange{
416							StartTime: timestamp,
417							Messages:  []Message{},
418						}
419					}
420	
421					toolName, _ := payload["name"].(string)
422					inputText, _ := payload["input"].(string)
423					callID, _ := payload["call_id"].(string)
424	
425					if toolName == "" {
426						continue
427					}
428	
429					// For custom tools, input is plain text, not JSON
430					input := map[string]interface{}{
431						"input": inputText,
432					}
433	
434					// Create tool message
435					toolMsg := Message{
436						ID:        fmt.Sprintf("ct_%d", i),
437						Timestamp: timestamp,
438						Role:      "agent",
439						Model:     currentModel,
440						Tool: &ToolInfo{
441							Name:   toolName,
442							Type:   classifyToolType(toolName),
443							UseID:  callID,
444							Input:  input,
445							Output: nil, // Will be filled when we find the output
446						},
447						PathHints: extractPathHints(toolName, input, inputText, workspaceRoot),
448					}
449	
450					currentExchange.Messages = append(currentExchange.Messages, toolMsg)
451					currentExchange.EndTime = timestamp
452	
453					// Track this tool call to match with output later
454					if callID != "" {
455						pendingTools[callID] = &PendingToolCall{
456							message:   &currentExchange.Messages[len(currentExchange.Messages)-1],
457							toolInfo:  currentExchange.Messages[len(currentExchange.Messages)-1].Tool,
458							timestamp: timestamp,
459						}
460					}
461	
462				case "custom_tool_call_output":
463					// Custom tool call output - merge into the pending tool call
464					callID, _ := payload["call_id"].(string)
465					outputJSON, _ := payload["output"].(string)
466	
467					if callID == "" || outputJSON == "" {
468						continue
469					}
470	
471					// Find the pending tool call
472					if pending, exists := pendingTools[callID]; exists {
473						// Parse the output JSON
474						var outputData map[string]interface{}
475						if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(outputJSON), &outputData); err == nil {
476							pending.toolInfo.Output = outputData
477						} else {
478							pending.toolInfo.Output = map[string]interface{}{"raw": outputJSON}
479						}
480						delete(pendingTools, callID)
481					}
482				}
483			}
484		}
485	
486		// Add the last exchange if exists
487		if currentExchange != nil && len(currentExchange.Messages) > 0 {
488			exchanges = append(exchanges, *currentExchange)
489		}
490	
491		return exchanges, nil
492	}
493	
494	// formatToolWithSummary generates custom summary and formatted markdown for a Codex tool
495	// Returns (summary, formattedMarkdown) where summary is the custom content for <summary> tag
496	// and formattedMarkdown is additional content to display in the tool-use block
497	func formatToolWithSummary(tool *ToolInfo, workspaceRoot string) (string, string) {
498		var summary string
499		var formattedMd strings.Builder
500	
501		// Format tool input based on whether it's a function call or custom tool
502		if tool.Input != nil {
503			// Check if this is a custom tool (has string input in "input" field)
504			if inputStr, ok := tool.Input["input"].(string); ok {
505				// Custom tool with text input (e.g., apply_patch)
506				formattedMd.WriteString(formatCustomToolCall(tool.Name, inputStr))
507			} else if tool.Name == "shell_command" || tool.Name == "exec_command" {
508				// Shell command: normalize "cmd" → "command" for exec_command
509				toolInput := tool.Input
510				if _, ok := toolInput["cmd"]; ok {
511					if _, hasCommand := toolInput["command"]; !hasCommand {
512						toolInput["command"] = toolInput["cmd"]
513					}
514				}
515				inputJSON, _ := json.Marshal(toolInput)
516				shellSummary, shellBody := formatShellWithSummary(string(inputJSON))
517				if shellSummary != "" {
518					// Single-line command goes in summary
519					summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** %s", tool.Name, shellSummary)
520				}
521				if shellBody != "" {
522					formattedMd.WriteString(shellBody)
523				}
524			} else {
525				// Other function calls with JSON arguments
526				inputJSON, _ := json.Marshal(tool.Input)
527				formattedMd.WriteString(formatToolCall(tool.Name, string(inputJSON)))
528			}
529		}
530	
531		// Format tool output if present
532		if tool.Output != nil {
533			if outputStr, ok := tool.Output["raw"].(string); ok {
534				// Clean and truncate output if needed
535				cleaned := strings.TrimSpace(outputStr)
536				// Only show output if there's actual content
537				if cleaned != "" {
538					if formattedMd.Len() > 0 {
539						formattedMd.WriteString("\n")
540					}
541					if len(cleaned) > 5000 {
542						cleaned = cleaned[:5000] + "\n... (truncated)"
543					}
544					formattedMd.WriteString("```\n" + cleaned + "\n```")
545				}
546			}
547		}
548	
549		return summary, strings.TrimSpace(formattedMd.String())
550	}
551	
552	// classifyToolType maps Codex tool names to standard tool types
553	func classifyToolType(toolName string) string {
554		switch toolName {
555		case "shell", "shell_command", "exec_command": // `shell` is legacy
556			return "shell"
557		case "update_plan":
558			return "task"
559		case "view_image":
560			return "read"
561		case "apply_patch":
562			return "write"
563		case "list_mcp_resources", "list_mcp_resource_templates", "read_mcp_resource":
564			return "generic"
565		default:
566			return "unknown"
567		}
568	}
569	
570	// extractPathHints extracts file paths from tool inputs.
571	// For apply_patch: parses patch format for file paths.
572	// For other tools: checks common path fields like "path", "file", etc.
573	func extractPathHints(toolName string, input map[string]interface{}, inputText string, workspaceRoot string) []string {
574		var paths []string
575	
576		if toolName == "apply_patch" {
577			// Parse patch format to extract file paths
578			// Look for lines like "*** Modify File: path", "*** Create File: path", "*** Delete File: path"
579			if inputText != "" {
580				paths = extractPathsFromPatch(inputText, workspaceRoot)
581			} else if inputStr, ok := input["input"].(string); ok {
582				paths = extractPathsFromPatch(inputStr, workspaceRoot)
583			}
584		} else {
585			// For other tools, check common path fields
586			pathFields := []string{"path", "file", "filename", "file_path"}
587			for _, field := range pathFields {
588				if value, ok := input[field].(string); ok && value != "" {
589					normalizedPath := spi.NormalizePath(value, workspaceRoot)
590					if !contains(paths, normalizedPath) {
591						paths = append(paths, normalizedPath)
592					}
593				}
594			}
595	
596			// Extract paths from shell commands (redirect targets, file-creating commands)
597			// exec_command uses "cmd", shell_command uses "command"
598			command, _ := input["command"].(string)
599			if command == "" {
600				command, _ = input["cmd"].(string)
601			}
602			if command != "" {
603				cwd, _ := input["workdir"].(string)
604				if cwd == "" {
605					cwd = workspaceRoot
606				}
607				shellPaths := spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, cwd, workspaceRoot)
608				for _, sp := range shellPaths {
609					if !contains(paths, sp) {
610						paths = append(paths, sp)
611					}
612				}
613			}
614		}
615	
616		return paths
617	}
618	
619	// extractPathsFromPatch parses apply_patch input to find file paths
620	func extractPathsFromPatch(patchText string, workspaceRoot string) []string {
621		var paths []string
622		lines := strings.Split(patchText, "\n")
623	
624		for _, line := range lines {
625			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
626	
627			// Look for patch markers - both "Create File" and "Add File" are valid
628			markers := []string{
629				"*** Modify File:",
630				"*** Update File:",
631				"*** Create File:",
632				"*** Add File:",
633				"*** Delete File:",
634				"*** Rename File:",
635				"*** Remove File:",
636			}
637	
638			for _, marker := range markers {
639				if strings.HasPrefix(line, marker) {
640					path := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, marker))
641					if path != "" {
642						normalizedPath := spi.NormalizePath(path, workspaceRoot)
643						if !contains(paths, normalizedPath) {
644							paths = append(paths, normalizedPath)
645						}
646					}
647					break
648				}
649			}
650	
651			// For rename, also check for "*** New Name:" marker
652			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "*** New Name:") {
653				path := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "*** New Name:"))
654				if path != "" {
655					normalizedPath := spi.NormalizePath(path, workspaceRoot)
656					if !contains(paths, normalizedPath) {
657						paths = append(paths, normalizedPath)
658					}
659				}
660			}
661		}
662	
663		return paths
664	}
665	
666	// contains checks if a string slice contains a value
667	func contains(slice []string, value string) bool {
668		for _, item := range slice {
669			if item == value {
670				return true
671			}
672		}
673		return false
674	}
675	
676	// extractUsageFromTokenCount extracts token usage from a token_count event's info.last_token_usage
677	// Codex CLI emits token_count events with the structure:
678	//
679	//	{
680	//	  "type": "event_msg",
681	//	  "payload": {
682	//	    "type": "token_count",
683	//	    "info": {
684	//	      "last_token_usage": { "input_tokens": N, "cached_input_tokens": N, "output_tokens": N, "reasoning_output_tokens": N, ... },
685	//	      "total_token_usage": { ... }
686	//	    }
687	//	  }
688	//	}
689	//
690	// We use last_token_usage for per-turn usage (total_token_usage is cumulative).
691	// Codex CLI uses its own token field names, stored in the Codex-specific fields of Usage.
692	func extractUsageFromTokenCount(payload map[string]interface{}) *Usage {
693		info, ok := payload["info"].(map[string]interface{})
694		if !ok {
695			return nil
696		}
697	
698		// Use last_token_usage for per-turn metrics (not cumulative)
699		lastUsage, ok := info["last_token_usage"].(map[string]interface{})
700		if !ok {
701			return nil
702		}
703	
704		return &Usage{
705			// Common fields
706			InputTokens:  schema.GetIntFromMap(lastUsage, "input_tokens"),
707			OutputTokens: schema.GetIntFromMap(lastUsage, "output_tokens"),
708			// Codex CLI specific fields
709			CachedInputTokens:     schema.GetIntFromMap(lastUsage, "cached_input_tokens"),
710			ReasoningOutputTokens: schema.GetIntFromMap(lastUsage, "reasoning_output_tokens"),
711		}
712	}
```

```bash
import json,sys
from collections import Counter
roles=Counter(); types=Counter(); blocktypes=Counter(); toolnames=Counter()
usage_keys=Counter(); tc_keys=Counter(); tr_keys=Counter(); user_content_kinds=Counter()
stopreasons=Counter()
for line in sys.stdin:
    line=line.strip()
    if not line: continue
    try: e=json.loads(line)
    except Exception: continue
    types[e.get('type')]+=1
    m=e.get('message')
    if isinstance(m,dict):
        roles[m.get('role')]+=1
        c=m.get('content')
        if m.get('role')=='user':
            user_content_kinds[type(c).__name__]+=1
            if isinstance(c,list):
                for b in c: blocktypes['user:'+str(b.get('type')) if isinstance(b,dict) else 'user:?']+=1
        if m.get('role')=='assistant':
            stopreasons[m.get('stopReason')]+=1
            u=m.get('usage')
            if isinstance(u,dict): usage_keys[tuple(sorted(u.keys()))]+=1
            if isinstance(c,list):
                for b in c:
                    if isinstance(b,dict):
                        blocktypes['asst:'+str(b.get('type'))]+=1
                        if b.get('type')=='toolCall':
                            tc_keys[tuple(sorted(b.keys()))]+=1
                            toolnames[b.get('name')]+=1
        if m.get('role')=='toolResult':
            tr_keys[tuple(sorted(k for k in m.keys()))]+=1
print('types',types)
print('roles',roles)
print('user_content_kinds',user_content_kinds)
print('blocktypes',blocktypes)
print('toolnames',toolnames)
print('usage_keys',usage_keys)
print('tc_keys',tc_keys)
print('tr_keys',tr_keys)
print('stopreasons',stopreasons)
"
```

```text
37	// Check verifies the pi binary is on PATH and reports its version.
38	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
39		cmdName := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand)
40		isCustom := cmdName != ""
41		if cmdName == "" {
42			cmdName = defaultCmd
43		}
44		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
45		if err != nil {
46			slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
47			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "not_found", err.Error())
48			return spi.CheckResult{
49				Success:      false,
50				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi binary '%s' not found on PATH", cmdName),
51			}
52		}
53		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
54		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
55		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
56		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
57		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
58			slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err)
59			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())
60			return spi.CheckResult{
61				Success:      false,
62				Location:     resolved,
63				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi version probe failed: %v", err),
64			}
65		}
66		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
67		if version == "" {
68			version = "unknown"
69		}
70		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
71		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
72	}

136	// findProjectSession locates the session file with the given ID within the
137	// project's pi session directory. Returns "" if not found.
138	func findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
139		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
140		if err != nil {
141			return "", err
142		}
143		for _, f := range files {
144			h, err := readHeader(f)
145			if err != nil || h == nil {
146				continue
147			}
148			if h.ID == sessionID {
149				return f, nil
150			}
151		}
152		return "", nil
153	}
154	
155	// readHeader parses only the first line of a session file and returns it only
156	// if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty id).
157	// Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them.
158	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
159		f, err := os.Open(path)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, err
162		}
163		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
164		dec := json.NewDecoder(f)
165		var h sessionHeader
166		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
170			return nil, nil
171		}
172		return &h, nil
173	}
174	
175	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
176	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
177	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
178	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
179		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, err
182		}
183		var out []sessionFile
184		for _, f := range files {
185			h, err := readHeader(f)
186			if err != nil {
187				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
188				continue
189			}
190			if h == nil {
191				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
192			}
193			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}

200		path, err := findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID)

211	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
212		files, err := listProjectSessions(projectPath)
213		if err != nil {
214			return nil, err
215		}
216		total := len(files)
217		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
218		for i, sf := range files {
219			chat, pErr := parseToAgentSession(sf.Path, debugRaw)
220			if pErr != nil {
221				slog.Debug("pi: skipping session", "path", sf.Path, "error", pErr)
222			} else if chat != nil {
223				result = append(result, *chat)
224			}
225			if progress != nil {
226				progress(i+1, total)
227			}
228		}
229		return result, nil
230	}

232	// parseToAgentSession parses one session file into an AgentChatSession,
233	// writing debug-raw artifacts when debugRaw is true.
234	func parseToAgentSession(path string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
235		data, err := ParseSession(path)
236		if err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239		if debugRaw {
240			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(path, data); dErr != nil {
241				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
242			}
243		}
244		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
245		if err != nil {
246			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
247		}
248		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
249			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
250			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
251			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
252			SessionData: data,
253			RawData:     string(raw),
254		}, nil
255	}
256	
257	// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single pi session directly from its native
258	// file path, skipping the by-id discovery search. originCwd is the session's
259	// originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd), passed through
260	// as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
261	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath. Implements spi.PathSessionReader
262	// so `specstory reindex` uses the O(N) path-keyed fast path instead of the
263	// O(N²) by-id lookup.
264	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
265		data, err := ParseSession(nativePath)
266		if err != nil {
267			return nil, err
268		}
269		if data.WorkspaceRoot == "" && originCwd != "" {
270			data.WorkspaceRoot = originCwd
271		}
272		if debugRaw {
273			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(nativePath, data); dErr != nil {
274				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
275			}
276		}
277		raw, err := os.ReadFile(nativePath)
278		if err != nil {
279			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
280		}
281		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
282			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
283			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
284			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
285			SessionData: data,
286			RawData:     string(raw),
287		}, nil
288	}
289	
290	// ListAgentChatSessions returns lightweight metadata for all project sessions,
291	// deriving Slug/Name from the first user message via a bounded single-pass scan
292	// (no full parse), matching how other providers populate metadata.
293	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
294		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
295		if err != nil {
296			return nil, err
297		}
298		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
299		for _, f := range files {
300			scan, scanErr := scanPiSession(f)
301			if scanErr != nil {
302				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", scanErr)
303				continue
304			}
305			if scan == nil || !scan.foundUser {
306				continue
307			}
308			result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
309				SessionID: scan.sessionID,
310				CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
311				Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
312				Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
313			})
314		}
315		return result, nil
316	}
317	
318	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every pi session across all projects,
319	// each ref carrying its originating cwd (read from the session header).
320	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
321		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
322	}
323	
324	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all pi sessions with live scan
325	// progress, using the shared parallel scanner. Each ref carries Slug/Name
326	// derived from the first user message and the originating cwd from the header.
327	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
328		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
329		if err != nil {
330			return nil, err
331		}
332		if _, statErr := os.Stat(root); statErr != nil {
333			if os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
334				return nil, nil
335			}
336			return nil, statErr
337		}
338		scan := func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
339			s, sErr := scanPiSession(path)
340			if sErr != nil {
341				return nil, sErr
342			}
343			if s == nil {
344				return nil, nil // non-session file
345			}
346			return scanToGlobalRef(s, path), nil
347		}
348		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)
349	}
350	
351	// piSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one bounded
352	// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan
353	// stops as soon as it has the first user message, so it does NOT parse the whole
354	// session. foundUser is false for sessions with no real user prompt; scanPiSession
355	// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
356	type piSessionScan struct {
357		sessionID        string
358		timestamp        string
359		firstUserMessage string
360		cwd              string
361		foundUser        bool
362	}
363	
364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
409	
410	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {
414			return nil
415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
420			Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
421			NativePath: path,
422			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
423		}
424	}
```

```text
1	package piagent
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7		"path/filepath"
8	
9		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
10		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
11	)
12	
13	// writeDebugRaw writes numbered JSON files (one per non-header entry) plus the
14	// central session-data.json via the shared spi helper. This matches the
15	// --debug-raw contract used by every provider.
16	func writeDebugRaw(sessionPath string, data *schema.SessionData) error {
17		if err := spi.WriteDebugSessionData(data.SessionID, data); err != nil {
18			return err
19		}
20		dir := spi.GetDebugDir(data.SessionID)
21		entries, err := readRawEntries(sessionPath)
22		if err != nil {
23			return err
24		}
25		return writeNumberedEntries(dir, entries)
26	}
27	
28	// writeNumberedEntries writes each raw entry as 1.json, 2.json, ... in dir.
29	func writeNumberedEntries(dir string, entries []json.RawMessage) error {
30		for i, raw := range entries {
31			filePath := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", i+1))
32			payload, mErr := json.MarshalIndent(raw, "", "  ")
33			if mErr != nil {
34				continue
35			}
36			if wErr := os.WriteFile(filePath, payload, 0o644); wErr != nil {
37				return wErr
38			}
39		}
40		return nil
41	}
42	
43	// readRawEntries returns each non-header line of a session file as a raw JSON
44	// value, for debug-raw burst output. Uses bufio.Reader (via readLines) so
45	// arbitrarily large lines are captured without the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap.
46	func readRawEntries(path string) ([]json.RawMessage, error) {
47		var out []json.RawMessage
48		first := true
49		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
50			if first {
51				first = false // skip the session header line
52				return nil
53			}
54			out = append(out, json.RawMessage(line))
55			return nil
56		})
57		return out, err
58	}
```

```text
13	// writeDebugRaw writes numbered JSON files (one per non-header entry) plus the
14	// central session-data.json via the shared spi helper. This matches the
15	// --debug-raw contract used by every provider.
16	func writeDebugRaw(sessionPath string, data *schema.SessionData) error {
17		if err := spi.WriteDebugSessionData(data.SessionID, data); err != nil {
18			return err
19		}
20		dir := spi.GetDebugDir(data.SessionID)
21		entries, err := readRawEntries(sessionPath)
22		if err != nil {
23			return err
24		}
25		return writeNumberedEntries(dir, entries)
26	}
27	
28	// writeNumberedEntries writes each raw entry as 1.json, 2.json, ... in dir.
29	func writeNumberedEntries(dir string, entries []json.RawMessage) error {
30		for i, raw := range entries {
31			filePath := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", i+1))
32			payload, mErr := json.MarshalIndent(raw, "", "  ")
33			if mErr != nil {
34				continue
35			}
36			if wErr := os.WriteFile(filePath, payload, 0o644); wErr != nil {
37				return wErr
38			}
39		}
40		return nil
41	}
42	
43	// readRawEntries returns each non-header line of a session file as a raw JSON
44	// value, for debug-raw burst output. Uses bufio.Reader (via readLines) so
45	// arbitrarily large lines are captured without the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap.
46	func readRawEntries(path string) ([]json.RawMessage, error) {
47		var out []json.RawMessage
48		first := true
49		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
50			if first {
51				first = false // skip the session header line
52				return nil
53			}
54			out = append(out, json.RawMessage(line))
55			return nil
56		})
57		return out, err
58	}
```

```text
187	func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
188		// Try to find sessions using the shared helper (stop on first match)

190

193			// Check if it's a home directory error
194			if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "home directory") {
195				slog.Debug("DetectAgent: Failed to resolve user home directory", "error", err)
196				if helpOutput {
197					fmt.Println()
198					log.UserWarn("Could not scan Codex CLI sessions for this directory.\n")
199					log.UserMessage("Reason: failed to determine your home directory.\n")
200					fmt.Println()
201				}
202				return false
203			}
204

206			if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "sessions directory not accessible") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "sessions root") {

216					log.UserMessage("  1. Run `specstory run codex` to launch Codex CLI in this project\n")
217					log.UserMessage("  2. Or start Codex CLI manually, then run `specstory sync codex` afterward\n\n")
218					log.UserMessage("Expected sessions directory: %s\n", sessionsRoot)
219					fmt.Println()
220				}
221				return false
222			}
223	
224			// Unknown error

226			return false

228	
229		// Check if we found any sessions
```

```text
8		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
9		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
10	)
11	
12	// entryType constants for pi JSONL v3 session entries.
13	const (
14		entrySession             = "session"
15		entryMessage             = "message"
16		entryModelChange         = "model_change"
17		entryThinkingLevelChange = "thinking_level_change"
18		entryCompaction          = "compaction"
19		entryBranchSummary       = "branch_summary"
20		entryCustom              = "custom"
21		entryCustomMessage       = "custom_message"
22		entryLabel               = "label"
23		entrySessionInfo         = "session_info"
24	)
25	
26	// messageRole constants for pi message entries.
27	const (
28		roleUser          = "user"
29		roleAssistant     = "assistant"
30		roleToolResult    = "toolResult"
31		roleBashExecution = "bashExecution"
32		roleCustom        = "custom"
33		roleBranchSummary = "branchSummary"
34		roleCompaction    = "compactionSummary"
35	)
36	
37	// rawEntry is the minimal envelope every pi entry shares. The message payload
38	// (for type=="message") is kept as raw json.RawMessage so we can decode it per
39	// role without fighting a single union struct. Compaction entries carry
40	// firstKeptEntryId as a top-level field (no message wrapper).
41	type rawEntry struct {
42		Type             string          `json:"type"`
43		ID               string          `json:"id"`
44		ParentID         *string         `json:"parentId"` // null for the first entry
45		Timestamp        string          `json:"timestamp"`
46		FirstKeptEntryID string          `json:"firstKeptEntryId,omitempty"` // compaction entries only
47		Message          json.RawMessage `json:"message,omitempty"`
48	}
49	
50	// sessionHeader is the first line of a pi session file (no id/parentId).
51	type sessionHeader struct {
52		Type      string `json:"type"`
53		Version   int    `json:"version"`
54		ID        string `json:"id"`
55		Timestamp string `json:"timestamp"`
56		Cwd       string `json:"cwd"`
57	}
58	
59	// contentBlock is one element of an assistant or user message content array.
60	type contentBlock struct {
61		Type     string         `json:"type"`
62		Text     string         `json:"text,omitempty"`
63		Thinking string         `json:"thinking,omitempty"`
64		ID       string         `json:"id,omitempty"`
65		Name     string         `json:"name,omitempty"`
66		Args     map[string]any `json:"arguments,omitempty"`
67	}
68	
69	// userMessage is a pi user-role message: content is string OR []contentBlock.
70	type userMessage struct {
71		Role      string          `json:"role"`
72		Content   json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
73		Timestamp int64           `json:"timestamp"`
74	}
75	
76	// assistantMessage is a pi assistant-role message.
77	type assistantMessage struct {
78		Role         string         `json:"role"`
79		Content      []contentBlock `json:"content"`
80		Provider     string         `json:"provider"`
81		Model        string         `json:"model"`
82		API          string         `json:"api"`
83		StopReason   string         `json:"stopReason"`
84		ErrorMessage string         `json:"errorMessage,omitempty"`
85		Usage        *piUsage       `json:"usage,omitempty"`
86	}
87	
88	// piUsage is the token-usage shape on a pi assistant message.
89	type piUsage struct {
90		Input       int64 `json:"input"`
91		Output      int64 `json:"output"`
92		CacheRead   int64 `json:"cacheRead"`
93		CacheWrite  int64 `json:"cacheWrite"`
94		TotalTokens int64 `json:"totalTokens"`
95	}
96	
97	// toolResultMessage is a pi toolResult-role message (a top-level entry).
98	type toolResultMessage struct {
99		Role       string          `json:"role"`
100		ToolCallID string          `json:"toolCallId"`
101		ToolName   string          `json:"toolName"`
102		Content    []contentBlock  `json:"content"`
103		Details    json.RawMessage `json:"details,omitempty"` // tool-specific metadata (e.g. exitCode)
104		IsError    bool            `json:"isError"`
105	}
106	
107	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path
108	// branch into the unified schema.SessionData. It honors compaction entries:
109	// when a compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId
110	// are dropped from the conversation (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
112		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		if header == nil {
117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
118		}
119		if header.Type != entrySession {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
121		}
122		if header.ID == "" {
123			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
124		}
125		if len(entries) == 0 {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
127		}
128		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
129		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
130	}
131	
132	// piProviderVersion derives the provider version string recorded on SessionData
133	// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
134	// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
135	func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
136		if header.Version > 0 {
137			return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
138		}
139		return "v1"
140	}
141	
142	// buildSessionData maps the ordered leaf-path entries into schema.SessionData.
143	func buildSessionData(header *sessionHeader, ordered []rawEntry) *schema.SessionData {
144		return &schema.SessionData{
145			SchemaVersion: "1.0",
146			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{
147				ID:      providerID,
148				Name:    providerName,
149				Version: piProviderVersion(header),
150			},
151			SessionID:     header.ID,
152			CreatedAt:     header.Timestamp,
153			WorkspaceRoot: header.Cwd,
154			Exchanges:     buildExchanges(ordered),
155		}
156	}
157	
158	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
159	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
160	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo. Control entries
161	// (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the conversation body.
162	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
163		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
164		var current *schema.Exchange
165		commit := func() {
166			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
167				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
168			}
169		}
170		for _, e := range ordered {
171			if e.Type != entryMessage {
172				continue
173			}
174			switch messageRole(e) {
175			case roleUser:
176				commit()
177				current = &schema.Exchange{
178					ExchangeID: e.ID,
179					StartTime:  e.Timestamp,
180					EndTime:    e.Timestamp,
181					Messages:   []schema.Message{buildUserMessage(e)},
182				}
183			case roleAssistant:
184				current = appendAssistant(current, e)
185			case roleToolResult:
186				mergeToolResult(current, e)
187			}
188		}
189		commit()
190		return exchanges
191	}
192	
193	// appendAssistant appends an assistant message to the current exchange, creating
194	// one if none exists yet.
195	func appendAssistant(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) *schema.Exchange {
196		if current == nil {
197			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
198		}
199		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, buildAgentMessages(e)...)
200		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
201		return current
202	}
203	
204	// messageRole extracts .message.role from a message entry.
205	func messageRole(e rawEntry) string {
206		var m struct {
207			Role string `json:"role"`
208		}
209		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m)
210		return m.Role
211	}
212	
213	// mergeToolResult folds a toolResult entry into the matching agent ToolInfo in
214	// the current exchange, keyed by toolCallId == ToolInfo.UseID. It also advances
215	// the exchange EndTime to the toolResult's timestamp so downstream stats that
216	// read the last exchange's EndTime report the real final-event time.
217	func mergeToolResult(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) {
218		if current == nil {
219			return
220		}
221		var tr toolResultMessage
222		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &tr); err != nil {
223			return
224		}
225		content := toolResultContent(tr)
226		for i := range current.Messages {
227			msg := &current.Messages[i]
228			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.UseID == tr.ToolCallID {
229				msg.Tool.Output = buildToolOutput(content, tr)
230				msg.Timestamp = e.Timestamp
231				current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
232				return
233			}
234		}
235	}
236	
237	// toolResultContent joins the text blocks of a toolResult message.
238	func toolResultContent(tr toolResultMessage) string {
239		var parts []string
240		for _, b := range tr.Content {
241			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
242				parts = append(parts, b.Text)
243			}
244		}
245		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
246	}
247	
248	// buildUserMessage maps a pi user message entry to a schema user Message.
249	// pi user content is either a plain string or an array of {type:text|image}.
250	func buildUserMessage(e rawEntry) schema.Message {
251		var um userMessage
252		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &um)
253		parts := userContentParts(um.Content)
254		return schema.Message{
255			ID:        e.ID,
256			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
257			Role:      schema.RoleUser,
258			Content:   parts,
259		}
260	}
261	
262	// userContentParts decodes a pi user message's content (string or array) into
263	// schema ContentParts. Image blocks are dropped in v1 (recorded as a gap).
264	func userContentParts(raw json.RawMessage) []schema.ContentPart {
265		if len(raw) == 0 {
266			return nil
267		}
268		if raw[0] == '"' {
269			var s string
270			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
271				return []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: s}}
272			}
273		}
274		var blocks []contentBlock
275		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
276			return nil
277		}
278		var parts []schema.ContentPart
279		for _, b := range blocks {
280			if b.Type == schema.ContentTypeText && b.Text != "" {
281				parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
282			}
283		}
284		return parts
285	}
286	
287	// buildAgentMessages maps a pi assistant message entry to one or more schema
288	// Messages: one Message holds the text+thinking content parts; each toolCall
289	// block becomes its own agent Message carrying a ToolInfo.
290	func buildAgentMessages(e rawEntry) []schema.Message {
291		var am assistantMessage
292		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &am); err != nil {
293			return nil
294		}
295		var parts []schema.ContentPart
296		var messages []schema.Message
297		for _, b := range am.Content {
298			switch b.Type {
299			case schema.ContentTypeText:
300				if b.Text != "" {
301					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
302				}
303			case schema.ContentTypeThinking:
304				if b.Thinking != "" {
305					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: b.Thinking})
306				}
307			case "toolCall":
308				messages = append(messages, buildToolMessage(e, b, am))
309			}
310		}
311		if len(parts) > 0 {
312			head := schema.Message{
313				ID:        e.ID,
314				Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
315				Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
316				Model:     am.Model,
317				Content:   parts,
318				Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
319			}
320			return append([]schema.Message{head}, messages...)
321		}
322		if len(messages) == 0 {
323			return buildErrorMessage(e, am)
324		}
325		// Tool-call-only assistant message: carry model+usage once on the first
326		// tool message so no metadata is lost and no schema-invalid empty message
327		// is emitted.
328		messages[0].Model = am.Model
329		if messages[0].Usage == nil {
330			messages[0].Usage = mapUsage(am.Usage)
331		}
332		return messages
333	}
334	
335	// buildToolMessage builds an agent Message wrapping a ToolInfo from a toolCall.
336	// The parent assistant message's model is passed through so tool messages carry
337	// the same model metadata as text/thinking messages. The Message ID is derived
338	// from the parent entry id + the toolCall id, so multiple toolCalls in one
339	// assistant message get distinct Message IDs (downstream provenance keys use
340	// msg.ID as a deterministic component).
341	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
342		return schema.Message{
343			ID:        toolMessageID(e.ID, b.ID),
344			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
345			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
346			Model:     am.Model,
347			Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{
348				Name:  b.Name,
349				Type:  classifyToolType(b.Name),
350				UseID: b.ID,
351				Input: b.Args,
352			},
353		}
354	}
355	
356	// toolMessageID builds a unique Message ID for a tool-call message from the
357	// parent entry id and the toolCall id. This avoids duplicate Message IDs when a
358	// single assistant entry contains multiple toolCall blocks.
359	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {
360		if callID != "" {
361			return entryID + ":" + callID
362		}
363		return entryID
364	}
365	
366	// buildToolOutput constructs the ToolInfo.Output map from a toolResult's
367	// content, error flag, and optional details blob. details (e.g. exitCode) is
368	// decoded into a generic value so downstream consumers (markdown rendering,
369	// cloud) can surface structured tool metadata without re-parsing raw JSON.
370	func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
371		out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
372		if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
373			var details any
374			if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {
375				out["details"] = details
376			}
377		}
378		return out
379	}
380	
381	// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map
382	// to InputTokens/OutputTokens; cacheRead/cacheWrite map to the Claude-style
383	// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics).
384	func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
385		if u == nil {
386			return nil
387		}
388		return &schema.Usage{
389			InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
390			OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
391			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
392			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
393		}
394	}
395	
396	// buildErrorMessage surfaces an assistant entry with stopReason=error and an
397	// empty content array (no text/thinking/toolCalls) as an agent text message so
398	// the error event is not dropped from the transcript (and compaction boundaries
399	// stay interpretable). Returns nil if there is no errorMessage to surface.
400	func buildErrorMessage(e rawEntry, am assistantMessage) []schema.Message {
401		if strings.TrimSpace(am.ErrorMessage) == "" {
402			return nil
403		}
404		return []schema.Message{{
405			ID:        e.ID,
406			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
407			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
408			Model:     am.Model,
409			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "[error] " + am.ErrorMessage}},
410			Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
411		}}
412	}
413	
414	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
415	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
416	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
417	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
418		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
419			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
420				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
421					continue
422				}
423				for _, part := range msg.Content {
424					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {
425						return spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(t)
426					}
427				}
428			}
429		}
430		return ""
431	}
432	
433	// classifyToolType maps pi tool names to the schema tool-type taxonomy.
434	func classifyToolType(name string) string {
435		switch strings.ToLower(name) {
436		case "read":
437			return schema.ToolTypeRead
438		case "edit", "write":
439			return schema.ToolTypeWrite
440		case "bash", "ls":
441			return schema.ToolTypeShell
442		case "grep", "find", "web_search", "fetch_content":
443			return schema.ToolTypeSearch
444		case "until_done_set", "until_done_plan", "until_done_task_update",
445			"until_done_progress", "until_done_complete", "until_done_block",
446			"until_done_replan", "until_done_distill":
447			return schema.ToolTypeTask
448		default:
449			return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
450		}
451	}
452	
453	// firstUserText extracts the first user message text from a message entry, if
454	// its role is "user". Returns "" for non-user messages or empty content.
455	func firstUserText(e rawEntry) string {
456		var m struct {
457			Role    string          `json:"role"`
458			Content json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
459		}
460		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m); err != nil {
461			return ""
462		}
463		if m.Role != roleUser {
464			return ""
465		}
466		return userContentString(m.Content)
467	}
468	
469	// userContentString extracts a plain string from a pi user message content
470	// field (either a string or an array of {type:text} blocks). The result is
471	// trimmed so the scan path produces the same Slug/Name as the full-parse path
472	// (deriveSlug trims too).
473	func userContentString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
474		if len(raw) == 0 {
475			return ""
476		}
477		var s string
478		if raw[0] == '"' {
479			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
480				return strings.TrimSpace(s)
481			}
482		}
483		var blocks []contentBlock
484		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
485			return ""
486		}
487		for _, b := range blocks {
488			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
489				return strings.TrimSpace(b.Text)
490			}
491		}
492		return ""
493	}
494
```

```text
37	// Check verifies the pi binary is on PATH and reports its version.
38	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
39		cmdName := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand)
40		isCustom := cmdName != ""
41		if cmdName == "" {
42			cmdName = defaultCmd
43		}
44		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
45		if err != nil {
46			slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
47			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "not_found", err.Error())
48			return spi.CheckResult{
49				Success:      false,
50				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi binary '%s' not found on PATH", cmdName),
51			}
52		}
53		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
54		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
55		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
56		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
57		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
58			slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err)
59			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())
60			return spi.CheckResult{
61				Success:      false,
62				Location:     resolved,
63				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi version probe failed: %v", err),
64			}
65		}
66		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
67		if version == "" {
68			version = "unknown"
69		}
70		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
71		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
72	}

136	// findProjectSession locates the session file with the given ID within the
137	// project's pi session directory. Returns "" if not found.
138	func findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
139		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
140		if err != nil {
141			return "", err
142		}
143		for _, f := range files {
144			h, err := readHeader(f)
145			if err != nil || h == nil {
146				continue
147			}
148			if h.ID == sessionID {
149				return f, nil
150			}
151		}
152		return "", nil
153	}
154	
155	// readHeader parses only the first line of a session file and returns it only
156	// if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty id).
157	// Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them.
158	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
159		f, err := os.Open(path)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, err
162		}
163		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
164		dec := json.NewDecoder(f)
165		var h sessionHeader
166		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
170			return nil, nil
171		}
172		return &h, nil
173	}
174	
175	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
176	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
177	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
178	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
179		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, err
182		}
183		var out []sessionFile
184		for _, f := range files {
185			h, err := readHeader(f)
186			if err != nil {
187				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
188				continue
189			}
190			if h == nil {
191				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
192			}
193			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}

212		files, err := listProjectSessions(projectPath)
213		if err != nil {
214			return nil, err
215		}
216		total := len(files)
217		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
218		for i, sf := range files {

220			if pErr != nil {

222			} else if chat != nil {
223				result = append(result, *chat)
224			}
225			if progress != nil {
226				progress(i+1, total)
227			}
228		}
229		return result, nil
230	}

233	// writing debug-raw artifacts when debugRaw is true.
234	func parseToAgentSession(path string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
235		data, err := ParseSession(path)
236		if err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239		if debugRaw {
240			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(path, data); dErr != nil {
241				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
242			}
243		}
244		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
245		if err != nil {
246			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
247		}
248		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
249			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
250			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
251			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
252			SessionData: data,
253			RawData:     string(raw),
254		}, nil
255	}

257	// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single pi session directly from its native
258	// file path, skipping the by-id discovery search. originCwd is the session's
259	// originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd), passed through
260	// as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
261	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath. Implements spi.PathSessionReader
262	// so `specstory reindex` uses the O(N) path-keyed fast path instead of the
263	// O(N²) by-id lookup.
264	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
265		data, err := ParseSession(nativePath)
266		if err != nil {
267			return nil, err
268		}
269		if data.WorkspaceRoot == "" && originCwd != "" {
270			data.WorkspaceRoot = originCwd
271		}
272		if debugRaw {
273			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(nativePath, data); dErr != nil {
274				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
275			}
276		}
277		raw, err := os.ReadFile(nativePath)
278		if err != nil {
279			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
280		}
281		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
282			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
283			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
284			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
285			SessionData: data,

287		}, nil
288	}

291	// deriving Slug/Name from the first user message via a bounded single-pass scan

293	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
294		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
295		if err != nil {
296			return nil, err
297		}
298		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
299		for _, f := range files {

301			if scanErr != nil {
302				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", scanErr)
303				continue
304			}
305			if scan == nil || !scan.foundUser {
306				continue
307			}
308			result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
309				SessionID: scan.sessionID,
310				CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
311				Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
312				Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
313			})

318	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every pi session across all projects,

324	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all pi sessions with live scan
325	// progress, using the shared parallel scanner. Each ref carries Slug/Name
326	// derived from the first user message and the originating cwd from the header.
327	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
328		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
329		if err != nil {
330			return nil, err
331		}
332		if _, statErr := os.Stat(root); statErr != nil {
333			if os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
334				return nil, nil
335			}
336			return nil, statErr
337		}
338		scan := func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
339			s, sErr := scanPiSession(path)
340			if sErr != nil {
341				return nil, sErr
342			}
343			if s == nil {
344				return nil, nil // non-session file
345			}
346			return scanToGlobalRef(s, path), nil
347		}
348		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)
349	}
350	
351	// piSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one bounded
352	// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan
353	// stops as soon as it has the first user message, so it does NOT parse the whole
354	// session. foundUser is false for sessions with no real user prompt; scanPiSession
355	// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
356	type piSessionScan struct {
357		sessionID        string
358		timestamp        string
359		firstUserMessage string
360		cwd              string
361		foundUser        bool
362	}
363	
364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
409	
410	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {
414			return nil
415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
420			Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
421			NativePath: path,
422			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
423		}
424	}
```

```text
1	package piagent
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// piSessionsRoot returns ~/.pi/agent/sessions, the directory under which pi
11	// stores one subdirectory per working directory (each named with the encoded
12	// cwd, see EncodeCwd). It does not require the directory to exist.
13	func piSessionsRoot() (string, error) {
14		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
15		if err != nil {
16			return "", fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot resolve home dir: %w", err)
17		}
18		return filepath.Join(home, ".pi", "agent", "sessions"), nil
19	}
20	
21	// EncodeCwd maps a working directory to pi's session-subdirectory name.
22	// pi replaces every '/' in the absolute path with '-' and wraps the result with
23	// a leading '-' and a trailing '--', producing e.g. "/Users/jane/proj" ->
24	// "--Users-jane-proj--". The encoding is derived from real session dirs:
25	// "/Users/jakelevirne" -> "--Users-jakelevirne--" and
26	// "/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory" -> "--Users-jakelevirne-dev-getspecstory--".
27	func EncodeCwd(cwd string) string {
28		encoded := strings.ReplaceAll(cwd, "/", "-")
29		return "-" + encoded + "--"
30	}
31	
32	// ProjectSessionDir returns the absolute path to pi's session subdirectory for
33	// the given project, WITHOUT requiring it to exist. Callers (DetectAgent, sync)
34	// check existence separately. The path is symlink-resolved before encoding so
35	// it matches the directory pi actually wrote to (pi encodes the real cwd); a
36	// relative or symlinked projectPath would otherwise produce a different name.
37	func ProjectSessionDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
38		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
39		if err != nil {
40			return "", err
41		}
42		cwd := strings.TrimSpace(projectPath)
43		if cwd == "" {
44			cwd, err = os.Getwd()
45			if err != nil {
46				return "", fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot get working dir: %w", err)
47			}
48		}
49		realPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cwd)
50		if err != nil {
51			realPath = cwd // fall back to the raw path if resolution fails
52		}
53		return filepath.Join(root, EncodeCwd(realPath)), nil
54	}
55	
56	// SessionFilesInProject lists the *.jsonl files in the project's pi session
57	// directory. Returns an empty slice (no error) if the directory does not exist.
58	func SessionFilesInProject(projectPath string) ([]string, error) {
59		dir, err := ProjectSessionDir(projectPath)
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
64		if err != nil {
65			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
66				return nil, nil
67			}
68			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading session dir %s: %w", dir, err)
69		}
70		var files []string
71		for _, e := range entries {
72			if e.IsDir() {
73				continue
74			}
75			if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".jsonl") {
76				continue
77			}
78			files = append(files, filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
79		}
80		return files, nil
81	}
```

```text
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// Skip entries missing the envelope fields the tree walk and exchange
91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}
```

```text
19	// xmlTagsRe matches XML-style tag blocks including their content, such as
20	// <ide_opened_file>...</ide_opened_file> or self-closing <tag />.
21	// These are injected by IDE tools/system prompts and should be stripped before
22	// processing user message text for filename or display purposes.
23	//
24	// The regex has two alternations:
25	//   - <tag ...>content</tag>  — matched with (?s) so . spans newlines; uses .*? (lazy)
26	//     to consume the shortest content between matching open/close tags.
27	//   - <tag ... />             — self-closing tags.
28	//
29	// Known limitation: nested tags with the same name (e.g. <t><t>x</t></t>) will
30	// only match up to the first closing tag, leaving a dangling </t>. This is
31	// acceptable because IDE-injected tags are not nested this way.
32	var xmlTagsRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*(?:\s[^>]*)?>.*?</[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*>|<[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*(?:\s[^>]*)?/>`)
33	
34	// whitespaceRe collapses any run of Unicode whitespace into a single space.
35	var whitespaceRe = regexp.MustCompile(`\s+`)
36	
37	// stripXMLTags removes XML-style tag blocks (and their content) from s and
38	// returns the trimmed result with normalized whitespace. This cleans up injected
39	// IDE/system context that precedes the real user message text while preserving
40	// word boundaries where tags appeared between tokens.
41	func stripXMLTags(s string) string {
42		cleaned := xmlTagsRe.ReplaceAllString(s, " ")
43		cleaned = strings.TrimSpace(cleaned)
44		cleaned = whitespaceRe.ReplaceAllString(cleaned, " ")
45		return cleaned
46	}
47	
48	// extractWordsFromMessage extracts up to maxWords from the message, handling various edge cases
49	func extractWordsFromMessage(message string, maxWords int) []string {
50		if message == "" {
51			return []string{}
52		}
53	
54		// Normalize unicode and remove accents
55		t := transform.Chain(norm.NFD, runes.Remove(runes.In(unicode.Mn)), norm.NFC)
56		normalized, _, _ := transform.String(t, message)
57	
58		// Convert to lowercase
59		normalized = strings.ToLower(normalized)
60	
61		// Replace special characters with their word equivalents
62		normalized = strings.ReplaceAll(normalized, "@", " at ")
63		normalized = strings.ReplaceAll(normalized, "&", " and ")
64		normalized = strings.ReplaceAll(normalized, "#", " hash ")
65	
66		// Remove all punctuation and special characters, replace with spaces
67		// This regex keeps letters, numbers, and spaces
68		re := regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-z0-9\s]+`)
69		normalized = re.ReplaceAllString(normalized, " ")
70	
71		// Split into words and filter out empty strings
72		words := strings.Fields(normalized)
73	
74		// Take up to maxWords
75		if len(words) > maxWords {
76			words = words[:maxWords]
77		}
78	
79		return words
80	}
81	
82	// generateFilenameFromWords creates a filename from words, handling edge cases.
83	// Enforces lowercase to guarantee filesystem-safe, consistent filenames regardless
84	// of how the words were prepared by the caller.
85	func generateFilenameFromWords(words []string) string {
86		if len(words) == 0 {
87			return ""
88		}
89	
90		// Join words with hyphens and enforce lowercase as a safety guarantee
91		filename := strings.ToLower(strings.Join(words, "-"))
92	
93		// Ensure no double hyphens
94		for strings.Contains(filename, "--") {
95			filename = strings.ReplaceAll(filename, "--", "-")
96		}
97	
98		// Remove leading/trailing hyphens
99		filename = strings.Trim(filename, "-")
100	
101		return filename
102	}
103	
104	// GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage generates a filename based on the first user message content
105	func GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(message string) string {
106		words := extractWordsFromMessage(stripXMLTags(message), 4)
107		return generateFilenameFromWords(words)
108	}

111	// The name is truncated to 100 characters at a word boundary and cleaned of excess whitespace
112	func GenerateReadableName(message string) string {
113		if message == "" {
114			return ""
115		}

136		}

138		// Add ellipsis to indicate truncation

142	// appendRemainingParts appends the remaining path components from parts[startIdx:] to the
143	// result path, skipping any empty components. This is used when we can't canonicalize the
144	// rest of the path (e.g., directory doesn't exist or can't be read).
145	func appendRemainingParts(result string, parts []string, startIdx int) string {
146		for j := startIdx; j < len(parts); j++ {
147			if parts[j] != "" {
148				result = filepath.Join(result, parts[j])
149			}
150		}
151		return result
152	}
153	
154	// GetCanonicalPath resolves a path to its canonical form by resolving symlinks
155	// and correcting case. This is important on case-insensitive filesystems like macOS
156	// where "/Users/Foo" and "/users/foo" refer to the same directory but would produce
157	// different hash values.
158	//
159	// The algorithm works by walking the path component by component, starting from the root.
160	// For each component, it opens the parent directory and reads its actual entries,
161	// performing case-insensitive matching to find the correct casing on disk.
162	// This ensures that the returned path matches the real filesystem casing, which is
163	// important for consistent hashing and avoiding subtle bugs on case-insensitive filesystems.
164	//
165	// Note: This can be slow for long paths or directories with many entries, since it
166	// requires reading each directory's contents.
167	//
168	// If a component doesn't exist on disk, the remaining path components are
169	// appended as-is, making this function safe to use with paths that don't
170	// fully exist yet.
171	func GetCanonicalPath(p string) (string, error) {
172		// Ensure we have an absolute, clean path
173		p = filepath.Clean(p)
174		if !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
175			var err error
176			p, err = filepath.Abs(p)
177			if err != nil {
178				return "", err
179			}
180		}
181	
182		// Resolve any symlinks in the path to get the real physical path
183		// This is critical for ensuring consistent path hashing across different
184		// ways of accessing the same directory (e.g., through a symlink vs directly)
185		realPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(p)
186		if err == nil && realPath != p {
187			// Successfully resolved symlinks - update p to the resolved path for case normalization
188			p = realPath
189		} else if err != nil {
190			// Symlink resolution failed (e.g., path doesn't exist yet),
191			// continue with the original path - we'll still normalize the case below
192			slog.Warn("GetCanonicalPath: symlink resolution failed, using original path",
193				"path", p, "error", err)
194		}
195	
196		// Split into components
197		parts := strings.Split(p, string(os.PathSeparator))
198	
199		// Start with root
200		result := string(os.PathSeparator)
201	
202		// Skip empty first element (before leading /) that results from splitting "/foo/bar"
203		firstPartIndex := 1
204	
205		// Build path component by component
206		for i := firstPartIndex; i < len(parts); i++ {
207			if parts[i] == "" {
208				continue
209			}
210	
211			// Open current result directory to read its contents
212			f, err := os.Open(result)
213			if err != nil {
214				// Can't read directory - might not exist yet
215				// Append remaining path as-is
216				return appendRemainingParts(result, parts, i), nil
217			}
218	
219			names, err := f.Readdirnames(-1)
220			_ = f.Close() // Best effort close, error doesn't affect result
221			if err != nil {
222				return "", err
223			}
224	
225			// Find the correct case
226			found := false
227			for _, name := range names {
228				if strings.EqualFold(name, parts[i]) {
229					result = filepath.Join(result, name)
230					found = true
231					break
232				}
233			}
234	
235			if !found {
236				// Component doesn't exist, append remaining as-is
237				result = appendRemainingParts(result, parts, i)
238				break
239			}
240		}
241	
242		return result, nil
243	}
244

263	//
264	// When debugBaseDirOverride is set (via SetDebugBaseDir), the directory structure

272	func GetDebugDir(sessionID string) string {
```

```text
    return join(resolvedAgentDir, "sessions", safePath);
}
```

```text
260	// The debug directory is used to store detailed JSON records and debugging
261	// information for SpecStory CLI sessions. This is shared across all providers
262	// (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor CLI) to maintain a consistent debug structure.
263	//
264	// When debugBaseDirOverride is set (via SetDebugBaseDir), the directory structure
265	// is: <override>/<sessionID>/
266	// Otherwise: .specstory/debug/<sessionID>/
267	//
268	// Example:
269	//
270	//	debugDir := spi.GetDebugDir("abc123-def456")
271	//	// Returns: ".specstory/debug/abc123-def456"
272	func GetDebugDir(sessionID string) string {
273		if debugBaseDirOverride != "" {
274			return filepath.Join(debugBaseDirOverride, sessionID)
275		}
276		return filepath.Join(".specstory", "debug", sessionID)
277	}
278	
279	// WriteDebugSessionData writes the SessionData as formatted JSON to the debug directory.
280	// This provides a standardized, provider-agnostic debug output alongside provider-specific raw data.
281	//
282	// The file is written to: .specstory/debug/<sessionID>/session-data.json
283	//
284	// Returns an error if the debug directory cannot be created or the file cannot be written.
285	func WriteDebugSessionData(sessionID string, sessionData *schema.SessionData) error {
286		if sessionData == nil {
287			return fmt.Errorf("sessionData is nil")
288		}
289	
290		// Get debug directory
291		debugDir := GetDebugDir(sessionID)
292	
293		// Create debug directory if it doesn't exist
294		if err := os.MkdirAll(debugDir, 0755); err != nil {
295			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create debug directory: %w", err)
296		}
297	
298		// Marshal SessionData to pretty-printed JSON
299		jsonData, err := json.MarshalIndent(sessionData, "", "  ")
300		if err != nil {
301			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal SessionData: %w", err)
302		}
303	
304		// Write to session-data.json
305		filePath := filepath.Join(debugDir, "session-data.json")
306		if err := os.WriteFile(filePath, jsonData, 0644); err != nil {
307			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session-data.json: %w", err)
308		}
309	
310		// Log absolute path for debugging
311		absPath, _ := filepath.Abs(filePath)
312		slog.Debug("Wrote debug session data", "sessionId", sessionID, "path", absPath)
313		return nil
314	}
315
```

```text
136

141		for i, s := range sessions {

143				SessionMetadata: s,
144				Provider:        providerID,
145			}
146		}
147	
148		if err := outputSessions(sessionsWithProvider); err != nil {
149			return err
150		}
151	
152		analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventListSessions, analytics.Properties{
153			"provider":      providerID,
154			"session_count": len(sessions),
155		})
156	
157		return nil
158	}

160	// listAllProviders lists sessions from all providers that have activity.
161	func listAllProviders(registry *factory.Registry) error {
162		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
163		if err != nil {
164			slog.Error("Failed to get current working directory", "error", err)
165			return err
166		}
167	
168		providerIDs := registry.ListIDs()
169		providersWithActivity := []string{}
170	
171		for _, id := range providerIDs {
172			provider, err := registry.Get(id)
173			if err != nil {
174				slog.Warn("Failed to get provider", "id", id, "error", err)
175				continue
176			}
177	
178			if provider.DetectAgent(cwd, false) {
179				providersWithActivity = append(providersWithActivity, id)
180			}
181		}
182	
183		if len(providersWithActivity) == 0 {
184			if !log.IsSilent() {
185				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr)
186				log.UserWarn("No coding agent activity found for this project directory.\n\n")
187	
188				log.UserMessage("We checked for activity in '%s' from the following agents:\n", cwd)
189				for _, id := range providerIDs {
190					if provider, err := registry.Get(id); err == nil {
191						log.UserMessage("- %s\n", provider.Name())
192					}
193				}
194				log.UserMessage("\nBut didn't find any activity.\n")
195			}
196	
197			if flags.json {
198				fmt.Println("[]")
199			}
```

```text
// GetAgentChatSession retrieves a chat session by ID.
func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath string, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	// Find the specific session (will short-circuit when found)
	sessions, err := findCodexSessions(projectPath, sessionID, false)
	if err != nil {
		// If sessions directory doesn't exist, return nil (not an error)
		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "sessions directory not accessible") ||
			strings.Contains(err.Error(), "sessions root") ||
			strings.Contains(err.Error(), "home directory") {
			return nil, nil
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to find codex sessions: %w", err)
	}

	// Session not found (empty result)
	if len(sessions) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}

	// Process the first (and only) session using shared helper
	return processSessionToAgentChat(&sessions[0], projectPath, debugRaw)
}

// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single Codex session directly from its native file
// path, implementing spi.PathSessionReader. It skips findCodexSessions' whole-tree walk —
// which is what makes the by-id GetAgentChatSession O(N) per call, and a reindex of every
// session O(N²) — by reading session_meta from the known file and handing off to the same
// processSessionToAgentChat the by-id path uses. originCwd is the workspace root, matching
// what GetAgentChatSession passes as projectPath.
func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	meta, err := loadCodexSessionMeta(nativePath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load codex session meta: %w", err)
	}
	// debugRaw is only set when a caller wants provider-specific raw dumps + RawData; reindex
	// (the only caller) never does. Honor it via the full path so that behavior is unchanged.
	if debugRaw {
		info := codexSessionInfo{
			SessionID:   strings.TrimSpace(meta.Payload.ID),
			SessionPath: nativePath,
			Meta:        meta,
		}
		return processSessionToAgentChat(&info, originCwd, debugRaw)
	}
	// Index fast path: read records only (skip the whole-file rawData string reindex never
	// reads) and skip slug derivation (reindex uses the slug from enumeration). The SessionData
	// produced here is identical to the full path's.
	records, err := readSessionRecords(nativePath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session data: %w", err)
	}
	if len(records) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}
	sessionData, err := GenerateAgentSession(records, originCwd)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to generate SessionData: %w", err)
	}
	return &spi.AgentChatSession{
		SessionID:   strings.TrimSpace(meta.Payload.ID),
		CreatedAt:   meta.Timestamp,
		SessionData: sessionData,
	}, nil
}
```
