```text
/**
 * Project one selected session entry into LLM/runtime messages.
 * Plain custom entries are display/state entries and do not participate in context.
 */
export function sessionEntryToContextMessages(entry) {
    if (entry.type === "message") {
        const message = entry.message;
        // Session files are parsed without validation; old versions, forks, or
        // hand-edited files can contain messages with null/missing content.
        if ((message.role === "user" || message.role === "assistant" || message.role === "toolResult") &&
            message.content == null) {
            return [{ ...message, content: [] }];
        }
        return [message];
    }
    if (entry.type === "custom_message") {
        return [
            createCustomMessage(entry.customType, entry.content ?? [], entry.display, entry.details, entry.timestamp),
        ];
    }
    if (entry.type === "branch_summary" && entry.summary) {
        return [createBranchSummaryMessage(entry.summary, entry.fromId, entry.timestamp)];
    }
    if (entry.type === "compaction") {
        return [createCompactionSummaryMessage(entry.summary, entry.tokensBefore, entry.timestamp)];
    }
    return [];
}
/**
 * Build the active, compaction-aware session entry list.
 *
 * This follows the current leaf path. If the path contains compaction entries,
 * the latest compaction is represented by the compaction entry itself, followed
 * by the kept entries starting at firstKeptEntryId and all entries after the
 * compaction entry. Older summarized entries are omitted.
 */
export function buildContextEntries(entries, leafId, byId) {
    const path = buildSessionPath(entries, leafId, byId);
    let compaction = null;
    for (const entry of path) {
        if (entry.type === "compaction") {
            compaction = entry;
        }
    }
    if (!compaction) {
        return path;
    }
    const compactionIdx = path.findIndex((entry) => entry.id === compaction.id);
    if (compactionIdx < 0) {
        return path;
    }
    const contextEntries = [compaction];
    let foundFirstKept = false;
    for (let i = 0; i < compactionIdx; i++) {
        const entry = path[i];
        if (entry.id === compaction.firstKeptEntryId) {
            foundFirstKept = true;
        }
        if (foundFirstKept) {
            contextEntries.push(entry);
        }
    }
    contextEntries.push(...path.slice(compactionIdx + 1));
    return contextEntries;
}
/**
 * Build the session context from entries using tree traversal.
 * If leafId is provided, walks from that entry to root.
 * Handles compaction and branch summaries along the path.
 */
export function buildSessionContext(entries, leafId, byId) {
    const path = buildSessionPath(entries, leafId, byId);
    const { thinkingLevel, model } = getSessionContextSettings(path);
    const messages = buildContextEntries(entries, leafId, byId).flatMap(sessionEntryToContextMessages);
    return { messages, thinkingLevel, model };
}
```

```text
91	// PushAgentEvents pushes a slice of agent events to the engine and returns

93	// are logged but do not stop processing.
94	func PushAgentEvents(ctx context.Context, engine *Engine, events []AgentEvent) []*ProvenanceRecord {
95		var records []*ProvenanceRecord
96	
97		for _, event := range events {
98			record, err := engine.PushAgentEvent(ctx, event)
99			if err != nil {
100				slog.Warn("Failed to push agent event",
101					"eventID", event.ID,
102					"filePath", event.FilePath,
103					"error", err)
104				continue
105			}
106			if record != nil {
107				records = append(records, record)
108			}
109		}
110	
111		return records
112	}
113	
114	// ProcessSessionEvents extracts agent events from session data, pushes them to
115	// the engine, and returns any resulting provenance records.
116	// Safe to call with a nil engine — returns nil immediately.
117	func ProcessSessionEvents(ctx context.Context, engine *Engine, sessionData *schema.SessionData) []*ProvenanceRecord {
118		if engine == nil || sessionData == nil {
119			return nil
120		}
121	
122		events := ExtractAgentEvents(sessionData)
123		if len(events) == 0 {
124			return nil
125		}
126	
127		slog.Debug("Extracted agent events from session",
128			"sessionID", sessionData.SessionID,
129			"eventCount", len(events))
130	
131		return PushAgentEvents(ctx, engine, events)
132	}
133
```

224	// renderToolInfo renders tool use information
225	func renderToolInfo(tool *ToolInfo) string {
226		var markdown strings.Builder
227	
228		// Get the tool type for the data attribute
229		toolType := tool.Type
230		if toolType == "" {
231			toolType = "generic"
232		}
233	
234		// Open tool-use tag
235		fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, ToolUseOpenTag, toolType, tool.Name)
236		markdown.WriteString("\n")
237	
238		// Generate summary tag
239		if tool.Summary != nil && *tool.Summary != "" {
240			// Provider provided custom summary content
241			fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, "<summary>%s</summary>\n", *tool.Summary)
242		} else {
243			// Generate default summary
244			fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, "<summary>Tool use: **%s**</summary>\n", tool.Name)
245		}
246	
247		// Use pre-formatted markdown from provider if present
248		if tool.FormattedMarkdown != nil && *tool.FormattedMarkdown != "" {
249			markdown.WriteString(*tool.FormattedMarkdown)
250			// Ensure there's a newline before the closing tag
251			// Some providers include it, some don't - normalize here
252			if !strings.HasSuffix(*tool.FormattedMarkdown, "\n") {
253				markdown.WriteString("\n")
254			}
255		} else {
256			// Fallback to generic formatting
257			markdown.WriteString(renderGenericTool(tool))
258		}
259	
260		// Close tool-use tag
261		markdown.WriteString(ToolUseCloseTag)
262		markdown.WriteString("\n")
263	
264		return markdown.String()
265	}

267	// renderGenericTool renders a tool without provider-specific formatting
268	// Displays all available information as key-value pairs
269	// Note: The <summary> tag is already written by the caller (renderToolMessage)
270	func renderGenericTool(tool *ToolInfo) string {
271		var markdown strings.Builder
272		markdown.WriteString("\n")
273	
274		// Display input as key-value pairs if present
275		// Sort keys for deterministic output order
276		if len(tool.Input) > 0 {
277			markdown.WriteString("**Input:**\n\n")
278	
279			// Extract and sort keys for deterministic ordering
280			keys := make([]string, 0, len(tool.Input))
281			for key := range tool.Input {
282				// Skip internal fields like _cwd
283				if !strings.HasPrefix(key, "_") {
284					keys = append(keys, key)
285				}
286			}
287			sort.Strings(keys)
288	
289			for _, key := range keys {
290				fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, "- %s: `%v`\n", key, tool.Input[key])
291			}
292			markdown.WriteString("\n")

```text
13	// GlobalSessionRef is a lightweight, project-discovering reference to a single
14	// native session, returned by Provider.ListAllAgentChatSessions.
15	//
16	// Unlike the project-scoped ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath), the project is NOT
17	// an input here: each ref carries the originating working directory (read from inside
18	// the session) so the caller — the `specstory reindex` command — can resolve project
19	// identity with utils.ComputeProjectID. The project is discovered, not supplied.
20	//
21	// It is intentionally metadata-only (no full SessionData parse); reindex re-fetches
22	// full data per ref via GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID) when it needs the
23	// conversation body. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
24	type GlobalSessionRef struct {
25		SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
26		CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601 creation timestamp (first turn), may be empty
27		Slug       string // filename-safe slug derived from the first user message
28		Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
29		NativePath string // absolute path the provider opens to read this session
30		OriginCwd  string // working directory the session was launched from (-> project_id)
31	}
32	
33	// PathSessionReader is an OPTIONAL capability a Provider may implement: parse a single
34	// session directly from its already-known native file path, skipping the by-id discovery
35	// search that GetAgentChatSession performs.
36	//
37	// Why: some providers locate a session by scanning their native store. Codex's by-id
38	// lookup walks the entire ~/.codex/sessions tree on every call, so resolving N sessions
39	// that way is O(N²). reindex already holds each session's exact file path
40	// (GlobalSessionRef.NativePath) from enumeration, so a path-keyed parse turns that back
41	// into O(N). reindex prefers this when a provider implements it and the ref carries a
42	// NativePath, and falls back to GetAgentChatSession otherwise.
43	//
44	// originCwd is the session's originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd),
45	// passed through as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
46	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath.
47	type PathSessionReader interface {
48		GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*AgentChatSession, error)
49	}
50	
51	// ScanReporter accumulates a provider's enumeration progress (sessions found) so the CLI can
52	// render a live "scanning" display. It is safe for concurrent use and safe to call on a nil
53	// receiver (a no-op), so providers can report unconditionally.
54	type ScanReporter struct {
55		found atomic.Int64
56	}
57	
58	// Add records that n more sessions have been found. Files that yield no session (warmup-only or
59	// sidechain-only transcripts) are deliberately not counted, so the running total reflects real
60	// sessions rather than raw files.
61	func (r *ScanReporter) Add(n int) {
62		if r != nil {
63			r.found.Add(int64(n))
64		}
65	}
66	
67	// Found returns the number of sessions found so far.
68	func (r *ScanReporter) Found() int64 {
69		if r == nil {
70			return 0
71		}
72		return r.found.Load()
73	}
74	
75	// ProgressEnumerator is an OPTIONAL Provider capability: enumerate all sessions while reporting
76	// scan progress into r (which may be nil — ScanReporter is nil-safe, so report unconditionally).
77	// Providers that don't implement it are enumerated via ListAllAgentChatSessions with no live
78	// feedback. reindex uses this to render a per-agent "Scanning agents…" display.
79	type ProgressEnumerator interface {
80		ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *ScanReporter) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
81	}
82	
83	// ScanSessionsInParallel walks root for *.jsonl session files and scans each one concurrently
84	// with scan, returning the collected refs. It is the shared engine behind each provider's
85	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress: providers differ only in where their sessions live (root)
86	// and how a single file's header maps to a GlobalSessionRef (scan).
87	//
88	// scan returns (ref, nil) to include a session, (nil, nil) to skip a non-session file
89	// (warmup-only / empty / sidechain-only), or (nil, err) to log-and-skip a malformed file.
90	// Files are independent and the per-file read+parse is CPU-bound, so scanning fans out across
91	// CPUs; output order is unspecified (reindex dedups and sorts later). r counts sessions found
92	// (not files scanned) and is nil-safe. label names the provider in scan-failure logs.
93	func ScanSessionsInParallel(root, label string, r *ScanReporter, scan func(path string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error)) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error) {
94		// Phase 1: collect file paths (dirents only — no opens).
95		var paths []string
96		walkErr := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
97			if err != nil {
98				return nil // skip unreadable entries rather than abort the whole sweep
99			}
100			if d.IsDir() || filepath.Ext(path) != ".jsonl" {
101				return nil
102			}
103			paths = append(paths, path)
104			return nil
105		})
106		if walkErr != nil {
107			return nil, fmt.Errorf("walking %s sessions: %w", label, walkErr)
108		}
109	
110		// Phase 2: scan headers in parallel. min(NumCPU, 12) is always ≥ 1, so no lower-bound guard.
111		workers := min(runtime.NumCPU(), 12)
112		pathCh := make(chan string, workers)
113		refs := make([]GlobalSessionRef, 0, len(paths))
114		var mu sync.Mutex
115		var wg sync.WaitGroup
116		for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
117			wg.Add(1)
118			go func() {
119				defer wg.Done()
120				for path := range pathCh {
121					ref, scanErr := safeScan(scan, path)
122					if scanErr != nil {
123						slog.Warn("reindex: failed to scan session", "agent", label, "path", path, "error", scanErr)
124						continue
125					}
126					if ref == nil {
127						continue // not a session (warmup / empty / sidechain)
128					}
129					mu.Lock()
130					refs = append(refs, *ref)
131					mu.Unlock()
132					r.Add(1) // count sessions found, not files scanned
133				}
134			}()
135		}
136		for _, path := range paths {
137			pathCh <- path
138		}
139		close(pathCh)
140		wg.Wait()
141		return refs, nil
142	}
143	
144	// safeScan runs scan(path), converting a panic into an error so one malformed session file is
145	// logged and skipped (via the caller's normal error path) rather than crashing the whole sweep.
146	func safeScan(scan func(string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error), path string) (ref *GlobalSessionRef, err error) {
147		defer func() {
148			if r := recover(); r != nil {
149				ref, err = nil, fmt.Errorf("panic scanning session: %v", r)
150			}
151		}()
152		return scan(path)
153	}
```

```bash
python3 << 'EOF'
import json

def surviving(path):
    entries=[]
    header=None
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            line=line.strip()
            if not line: continue
            e=json.loads(line)
            if header is None:
                header=e; continue
            if not e.get('type') or not e.get('id'): continue
            entries.append(e)
    byid={e['id']:e for e in entries}
    # leaf = last entry in file order
    cur=entries[-1]; path_=[]; visited=set()
    while cur['id'] not in visited:
        visited.add(cur['id']); path_.append(cur)
        pid=cur.get('parentId')
        if pid is None or pid not in byid: break
        cur=byid[pid]
    path_.reverse()
    # apply compaction: last compaction wins
    last=-1
    for i,e in enumerate(path_):
        if e['type']=='compaction': last=i
    if last>=0:
        kept=e_kept=path_[last].get('firstKeptEntryId','')
        idx=next((i for i,x in enumerate(path_) if x['id']==kept), -1)
        path_ = path_[idx:] if idx>=0 else path_[last:]
    return [(e['id'],e['type'], (e.get('message') or {}).get('role','')) for e in path_]
```

```bash
            line=line.strip()
            if not line: continue
            try: e=json.loads(line)

            if isinstance(m,dict) and m.get('role')=='assistant':

                total+=1
                r=u.get('reasoning')
                if r: 
                    nonzero+=1
                    if example is None: example=(os.path.basename(f), e.get('id'), r)

print('example:',example)
EOF
```

```text
    _buildIndex() {
        this.byId.clear();
        this.labelsById.clear();
        this.labelTimestampsById.clear();
        this.leafId = null;
        for (const entry of this.fileEntries) {
            if (entry.type === "session")
                continue;
            this.byId.set(entry.id, entry);
            this.leafId = entry.id;
            if (entry.type === "label") {
                if (entry.label) {
                    this.labelsById.set(entry.targetId, entry.label);
                    this.labelTimestampsById.set(entry.targetId, entry.timestamp);
                }
                else {
                    this.labelsById.delete(entry.targetId);
                    this.labelTimestampsById.delete(entry.targetId);
                }
            }
        }

    _rewriteFile() {
        if (!this.persist || !this.sessionFile)

        const fd = openSync(this.sessionFile, "w");
        try {
            for (const entry of this.fileEntries) {
                writeFileSync(fd, `${JSON.stringify(entry)}\n`);
            }
        }
        return entry.id;

    appendSessionInfo(name) {

        const entry = {
            type: "session_info",
            id: generateId(this.byId),
            parentId: this.leafId,
            timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),

/**
```

```text
export function migrateAuthToAuthJson() {
    const agentDir = getAgentDir();
    const authPath = join(agentDir, "auth.json");
    const oauthPath = join(agentDir, "oauth.json");
    const settingsPath = join(agentDir, "settings.json");
    // Skip if auth.json already exists
    if (existsSync(authPath))

    const migrated = {};
    const providers = [];
    // Migrate oauth.json
    if (existsSync(oauthPath)) {
        try {
            const oauth = JSON.parse(readFileSync(oauthPath, "utf-8"));
            for (const [provider, cred] of Object.entries(oauth)) {
                migrated[provider] = { type: "oauth", ...cred };
                providers.push(provider);
            }
            renameSync(oauthPath, `${oauthPath}.migrated`);
        }
        catch {
            // Skip on error
        }
    }
    // Migrate settings.json apiKeys
    if (existsSync(settingsPath)) {
        try {
            const content = readFileSync(settingsPath, "utf-8");
            const settings = JSON.parse(content);
            if (settings.apiKeys && typeof settings.apiKeys === "object") {
                for (const [provider, key] of Object.entries(settings.apiKeys)) {
                    if (!migrated[provider] && typeof key === "string") {
                        migrated[provider] = { type: "api_key", key };
                        providers.push(provider);
                    }
                }
                delete settings.apiKeys;
                writeFileSync(settingsPath, JSON.stringify(settings, null, 2));
            }
        }
        catch {
            // Skip on error
        }
    }
    if (Object.keys(migrated).length > 0) {
        mkdirSync(dirname(authPath), { recursive: true });
        writeFileSync(authPath, JSON.stringify(migrated, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });
    }
    return providers;
}
```

```text
53	// ExtractUUIDFromFilename extracts the UUID from a JSONL filename (exported for use in watcher)
54	func ExtractUUIDFromFilename(filename string) string {
55		// Remove directory path and .jsonl extension
56		base := filepath.Base(filename)
57		base = strings.TrimSuffix(base, ".jsonl")
58	
59		// The UUID is the last part of the filename after the last hyphen
60		// e.g., "-Users-sean-Source-SpecStory-compositions-game-4-30cc3569-a9d4-429e-981a-ab73e3ddee5f"
61		parts := strings.Split(base, "-")
62		if len(parts) >= 5 {
63			// UUID format: 8-4-4-4-12 characters
64			// So we need at least 5 parts from the end
65			uuidParts := parts[len(parts)-5:]
66			uuid := strings.Join(uuidParts, "-")
67			// Validate it looks like a UUID
68			if len(uuid) == 36 && len(uuidParts[0]) == 8 && len(uuidParts[1]) == 4 &&
69				len(uuidParts[2]) == 4 && len(uuidParts[3]) == 4 && len(uuidParts[4]) == 12 {
70				return uuid
71			}
72		}
73	
74		// Fallback: use the whole filename
75		return base
76	}

117	// WriteDebugJSON writes a pretty-printed JSON file for a JSONL record
118	func WriteDebugJSON(jsonlFile string, lineNumber int, data map[string]interface{}) error {
119		if !jsonlBurstMode {
120			return nil
121		}
122	
123		// If we have a target file set, only write debug for that file
124		if debugTargetFile != "" {
125			if jsonlFile != debugTargetFile {
126				// Also try comparing just the base filenames in case paths differ
127				if filepath.Base(jsonlFile) != filepath.Base(debugTargetFile) {
128					return nil
129				}
130			}
131		}
132	
133		// Extract UUID from filename
134		uuid := ExtractUUIDFromFilename(jsonlFile)
135		filename := fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", lineNumber)
136	
137		return writeJSONToDebugDir(uuid, filename, data, "Debug")
138	}
139	
140	// CleanDebugDirectory removes all files from a debug directory before writing new ones
141	func CleanDebugDirectory(uuid string) error {
142		debugDir := spi.GetDebugDir(uuid)
143	
144		// Check if directory exists
145		if _, err := os.Stat(debugDir); os.IsNotExist(err) {
146			// Directory doesn't exist, nothing to clean
147			return nil
148		}
149	
150		// Remove all files in the directory
151		entries, err := os.ReadDir(debugDir)
152		if err != nil {
153			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read debug directory for UUID %s: %v", uuid, err)
154		}
155	
156		for _, entry := range entries {
157			if !entry.IsDir() {
158				filePath := filepath.Join(debugDir, entry.Name())
159				if err := os.Remove(filePath); err != nil {
160					slog.Warn("Failed to remove file",
161						"path", filePath,
162						"uuid", uuid,
163						"error", err)
164				}
165			}
166		}
167	
168		return nil
169	}
170	
171	// WriteSpecstoryBurstJSON writes a pretty-printed JSON file for a record in specstory burst mode
172	func WriteSpecstoryBurstJSON(sessionUuid string, lineNumber int, data map[string]interface{}) error {
173		if !specstoryBurstMode {
174			return nil
175		}
176	
177		filename := fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", lineNumber)
178		return writeJSONToDebugDir(sessionUuid, filename, data, "Specstory burst")
179	}
180	
181	// WriteDebugRawJSON writes a pretty-printed JSON file for a record in debug-raw mode
182	// This replaces the old specstory-burst functionality
183	func WriteDebugRawJSON(sessionUuid string, lineNumber int, data map[string]interface{}) error {
184		filename := fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", lineNumber)
185		return writeJSONToDebugDir(sessionUuid, filename, data, "Debug raw")
186	}
187	
188	// writeDebugRawFiles writes debug JSON files for a Claude Code session.
189	// Returns a map from record index to file number for reference in markdown generation.
190	func writeDebugRawFiles(session Session) map[int]int {
191		recordToFileNumber := make(map[int]int)
192	
193		// Clean the debug directory first
194		if err := CleanDebugDirectory(session.SessionUuid); err != nil {
195			slog.Warn("Failed to clean debug directory for debug-raw", "error", err)
196			return recordToFileNumber
197		}
198	
199		// Write ALL records as JSON files, numbered sequentially
200		fileNumber := 0
201		for i, record := range session.Records {
202			fileNumber++
203			_ = WriteDebugRawJSON(session.SessionUuid, fileNumber, record.Data)
204			recordToFileNumber[i] = fileNumber
205		}
206	
207		return recordToFileNumber
208	}
```

```text
// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
	byID := indexByID(entries)
	leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
	path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
	reverse(path)
	return applyCompaction(path)
}

// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
	m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
	for _, e := range entries {
		m[e.ID] = e
	}
	return m
}

// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
	var path []rawEntry
	cur := leaf
	visited := make(map[string]bool)
	for !visited[cur.ID] {
		visited[cur.ID] = true
		path = append(path, cur)
		if cur.ParentID == nil {
			break
		}
		parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
		if !ok {
			break
		}
		cur = parent
	}
	return path
}

// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
	for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
		s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
	}
}

// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
	last := -1
	for i, e := range path {
		if e.Type == entryCompaction {
			last = i

	if last < 0 {
		return path
	}
	keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
	if keptID == "" {
		return path[last:]
	}
	if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
		return path[idx:]
	}
	return path[last:]
}
```

```text
318		return max(nameWidth, 10) // Minimum width of 10 for NAME
319	}

321	// truncateString truncates a string to maxLen runes, adding "..." if truncated.
322	func truncateString(s string, maxLen int) string {
323		runes := []rune(s)
324		if len(runes) <= maxLen {
325			return s
326		}
327		if maxLen <= 3 {
328			return string(runes[:maxLen])
329		}
330		return string(runes[:maxLen-3]) + "..."
331	}
332	
333	// formatCreatedAt formats an ISO 8601 timestamp to human-readable format.
334	func formatCreatedAt(timestamp string) string {
335		t, ok := parseCreatedAtTimestamp(timestamp)
336		if !ok {
337			return timestamp // Return original if parsing fails
338		}
339		return t.Local().Format("Jan 02, 2006 15:04")
340	}
341	
342	// parseCreatedAtTimestamp parses various ISO 8601 timestamp formats.
343	func parseCreatedAtTimestamp(value string) (time.Time, bool) {
344		if value == "" {
345			return time.Time{}, false
346		}
347	
348		if t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, value); err == nil {
349			return t, true
350		}
351		if t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, value); err == nil {
352			return t, true
353		}
354	
355		return time.Time{}, false
356	}
357	
358	// compareCreatedAtOldestFirst compares two timestamps for sorting (oldest first).
359	func compareCreatedAtOldestFirst(a, b string) int {
360		if a == b {
361			return 0
362		}
363	
364		ta, oka := parseCreatedAtTimestamp(a)
365		tb, okb := parseCreatedAtTimestamp(b)
366	
367		if oka && okb {
368			if ta.Before(tb) {
369				return -1
370			}
371			if ta.After(tb) {
372				return 1
373			}
374			return strings.Compare(a, b)
375		}
376		if oka && !okb {
377			return -1
378		}
379		if !oka && okb {
380			return 1
381		}
382	
383		return strings.Compare(a, b)
384	}
385	
386	// sortSessionMetadataOldestFirst sorts sessions by creation time (oldest first).
387	func sortSessionMetadataOldestFirst(sessions []spi.SessionMetadata) {
388		sort.SliceStable(sessions, func(i, j int) bool {
389			a, b := sessions[i], sessions[j]
390			if cmp := compareCreatedAtOldestFirst(a.CreatedAt, b.CreatedAt); cmp != 0 {
391				return cmp < 0
392			}
393			if a.SessionID != b.SessionID {
394				return a.SessionID < b.SessionID
395			}
396			return a.Slug < b.Slug
397		})
398	}
399	
400	// sortSessionMetadataWithProviderOldestFirst sorts sessions with provider info by creation time.
401	func sortSessionMetadataWithProviderOldestFirst(sessions []sessionMetadataWithProvider) {
402		sort.SliceStable(sessions, func(i, j int) bool {
403			a, b := sessions[i], sessions[j]
404			if cmp := compareCreatedAtOldestFirst(a.CreatedAt, b.CreatedAt); cmp != 0 {
405				return cmp < 0
406			}
407			if a.Provider != b.Provider {
408				return a.Provider < b.Provider
409			}
410			if a.SessionID != b.SessionID {
411				return a.SessionID < b.SessionID
412			}
413			return a.Slug < b.Slug
414		})
415	}
```

```text
const defaultFactoryCommand = "droid"

// Provider implements the SPI Provider interface for Factory Droid CLI.
type Provider struct{}

// NewProvider creates a new Factory Droid CLI provider instance.
func NewProvider() *Provider {
	return &Provider{}
}

func (p *Provider) Name() string {
	return "Factory Droid CLI"
}

// Check verifies that the Droid CLI is available and returns its resolved
// location and version information based on the provided custom command override.
func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
	cmdName, _ := parseDroidCommand(customCommand)
	isCustom := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != ""
	versionFlag := "--version"

	resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
	if err != nil {
		msg := buildCheckErrorMessage("not_found", cmdName, isCustom, "")
		trackCheckFailure("droid", isCustom, cmdName, "", versionFlag, "", "not_found", err.Error())
		return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, Location: "", ErrorMessage: msg}
	}

	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
		stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
		msg := buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, resolved, isCustom, stderrOutput)
		trackCheckFailure("droid", isCustom, cmdName, resolved, versionFlag, stderrOutput, errorType, err.Error())
		return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, Location: resolved, ErrorMessage: msg}
	}

	versionOutput := sanitizeDroidVersion(stdout.String())
	version := extractDroidVersion(versionOutput)
	if version == "" {
		version = strings.TrimSpace(versionOutput)
	}
	trackCheckSuccess("droid", isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version, versionFlag)
	return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
}

----

func buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType string, command string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
	var builder strings.Builder
	switch errorType {
	case "not_found":
		builder.WriteString("Factory Droid CLI was not found.\n\n")
		if isCustom {
			builder.WriteString("• Verify the custom path you provided is executable.\n")
			fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "• Provided command: %s\n", command)
		} else {
			builder.WriteString("• Install the Factory CLI and ensure `droid` is on your PATH.\n")
			builder.WriteString("• Re-run `specstory check droid` after installation.\n")
		}
	case "permission_denied":
		builder.WriteString("SpecStory cannot execute the Factory CLI due to permissions.\n\n")
		fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "Try: chmod +x %s\n", command)
	default:
		builder.WriteString("`droid --version` failed.\n\n")
		if stderr != "" {
			builder.WriteString("Error output:\n")
			builder.WriteString(stderr)
			builder.WriteString("\n\n")
		}
		builder.WriteString("Run `droid --version` manually to diagnose, then retry.")
	}
	return builder.String()
}

var ansiRegexp = regexp.MustCompile(`\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]`)

func sanitizeDroidVersion(raw string) string {
	clean := strings.ReplaceAll(raw, "\r", "")
	clean = ansiRegexp.ReplaceAllString(clean, "")
	return clean
}

func extractDroidVersion(raw string) string {
	lines := strings.Split(raw, "\n")
	var filtered []string
	for _, line := range lines {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}
		filtered = append(filtered, line)
	}
	if len(filtered) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return filtered[len(filtered)-1]
}

func trackCheckSuccess(provider string, custom bool, commandPath string, resolvedPath string, version string, versionFlag string) {
	props := analytics.Properties{
		"provider":       provider,
		"custom_command": custom,
		"command_path":   commandPath,
		"resolved_path":  resolvedPath,
		"version":        version,
		"version_flag":   versionFlag,
	}
	analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCheckInstallSuccess, props)
}

func trackCheckFailure(provider string, custom bool, commandPath string, resolvedPath string, versionFlag string, stderrOutput string, errorType string, message string) {
	props := analytics.Properties{
		"provider":       provider,
		"custom_command": custom,
		"command_path":   commandPath,
		"resolved_path":  resolvedPath,
		"version_flag":   versionFlag,
		"error_type":     errorType,
		"error_message":  message,
	}
	if stderrOutput != "" {
		props["stderr"] = stderrOutput
	}
	analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventCheckInstallFailed, props)
}
```

```text
60	// sessions rather than raw files.
61	func (r *ScanReporter) Add(n int) {
62		if r != nil {
63			r.found.Add(int64(n))
64		}
65	}
66	
67	// Found returns the number of sessions found so far.
68	func (r *ScanReporter) Found() int64 {
69		if r == nil {
70			return 0
71		}
72		return r.found.Load()
73	}
74	
75	// ProgressEnumerator is an OPTIONAL Provider capability: enumerate all sessions while reporting
76	// scan progress into r (which may be nil — ScanReporter is nil-safe, so report unconditionally).
77	// Providers that don't implement it are enumerated via ListAllAgentChatSessions with no live
78	// feedback. reindex uses this to render a per-agent "Scanning agents…" display.
79	type ProgressEnumerator interface {
80		ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *ScanReporter) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
81	}
82	
83	// ScanSessionsInParallel walks root for *.jsonl session files and scans each one concurrently
84	// with scan, returning the collected refs. It is the shared engine behind each provider's
85	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress: providers differ only in where their sessions live (root)
86	// and how a single file's header maps to a GlobalSessionRef (scan).
87	//
88	// scan returns (ref, nil) to include a session, (nil, nil) to skip a non-session file
89	// (warmup-only / empty / sidechain-only), or (nil, err) to log-and-skip a malformed file.
90	// Files are independent and the per-file read+parse is CPU-bound, so scanning fans out across
91	// CPUs; output order is unspecified (reindex dedups and sorts later). r counts sessions found
92	// (not files scanned) and is nil-safe. label names the provider in scan-failure logs.
93	func ScanSessionsInParallel(root, label string, r *ScanReporter, scan func(path string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error)) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error) {
94		// Phase 1: collect file paths (dirents only — no opens).
95		var paths []string
96		walkErr := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
97			if err != nil {
98				return nil // skip unreadable entries rather than abort the whole sweep
99			}
100			if d.IsDir() || filepath.Ext(path) != ".jsonl" {
101				return nil
102			}
103			paths = append(paths, path)
104			return nil
105		})
106		if walkErr != nil {
107			return nil, fmt.Errorf("walking %s sessions: %w", label, walkErr)
108		}
109	
110		// Phase 2: scan headers in parallel. min(NumCPU, 12) is always ≥ 1, so no lower-bound guard.
111		workers := min(runtime.NumCPU(), 12)
112		pathCh := make(chan string, workers)
113		refs := make([]GlobalSessionRef, 0, len(paths))
114		var mu sync.Mutex
115		var wg sync.WaitGroup
116		for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
117			wg.Add(1)
118			go func() {
119				defer wg.Done()
120				for path := range pathCh {
121					ref, scanErr := safeScan(scan, path)
122					if scanErr != nil {
123						slog.Warn("reindex: failed to scan session", "agent", label, "path", path, "error", scanErr)
124						continue
125					}
126					if ref == nil {
127						continue // not a session (warmup / empty / sidechain)
128					}
129					mu.Lock()
130					refs = append(refs, *ref)
131					mu.Unlock()
132					r.Add(1) // count sessions found, not files scanned
133				}
134			}()
135		}
136		for _, path := range paths {
137			pathCh <- path
138		}
139		close(pathCh)
140		wg.Wait()
141		return refs, nil
142	}
143	
144	// safeScan runs scan(path), converting a panic into an error so one malformed session file is
145	// logged and skipped (via the caller's normal error path) rather than crashing the whole sweep.
146	func safeScan(scan func(string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error), path string) (ref *GlobalSessionRef, err error) {
147		defer func() {
148			if r := recover(); r != nil {
149				ref, err = nil, fmt.Errorf("panic scanning session: %v", r)
150			}
151		}()
152		return scan(path)
153	}
```

```text
		t.Errorf("SessionID = %q, want v1-uuid", data.SessionID)
	}
	if data.Provider.Version != "v1" {
		t.Errorf("Provider.Version = %q, want v1", data.Provider.Version)
	}
	if len(data.Exchanges) == 0 {
		t.Error("v1 session produced no exchanges")
	}
	if !data.Validate() {
		t.Error("Validate() returned false for v1 session")
	}
}
```

```text
// piSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one bounded
// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan
// stops as soon as it has the first user message, so it does NOT parse the whole
// session. foundUser is false for sessions with no real user prompt; scanPiSession
// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
type piSessionScan struct {
	sessionID        string
	timestamp        string
	firstUserMessage string
	cwd              string
	foundUser        bool
}

// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
	scan := &piSessionScan{}
	headerRead := false
	err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
		if !headerRead {
			var h sessionHeader
			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
				return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
			}
			if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
				return errStopRead // not a pi session header
			}
			scan.sessionID = h.ID
			scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
			scan.cwd = h.Cwd
			headerRead = true
			return nil
		}
		var e rawEntry
		if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
			return nil // skip malformed line
		}
		if e.Type != entryMessage {
			return nil
		}
		if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
			scan.firstUserMessage = msg
			scan.foundUser = true
			return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
		}
		return nil
	})
```

```text
# Version 1 Session File Structure and Migration

## V1 Entry Structure

Version 1 session entries **do not have `id` and `parentId` fields**. They are a plain linear sequence without tree structure. Each entry is simply a JSON object on a separate JSONL line, representing messages and metadata in order.

## V1 Header Structure

The v1 header lacks a `version` field. According to the code:

> "v1 sessions don't have this"

The header contains `type`, `id`, `timestamp`, and `cwd`, but omits the `version` field entirely.

## Migration Code (V1 to V2)

The migration function `migrateV1ToV2()` assigns IDs and establishes parent-child relationships:

> "for (const entry of entries) { if (entry.type === 'session') { entry.version = 2; continue; } entry.id = generateId(ids); entry.parentId = prevId; prevId = entry.id;"

This process:
- Generates a unique ID for each entry
- Sets `parentId` to the previous entry's ID (establishing linear chain)
- Converts any `firstKeptEntryIndex` references to `firstKeptEntryId` for compaction entries
- Sets `version: 2` on the header

The result transforms the flat sequence into a tree structure where each entry points to its predecessor.
```

```text
1	package session
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"os"

10	
11		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
12	)
13	
14	// SessionStatistics contains computed statistics for a single session
15	type SessionStatistics struct {
16		UserMessageCount  int    `json:"user_message_count"`
17		AgentMessageCount int    `json:"agent_message_count"`
18		StartTimestamp    string `json:"start_timestamp"`
19		EndTimestamp      string `json:"end_timestamp"`
20		MarkdownSizeBytes int    `json:"markdown_size_bytes"`
21		Provider          string `json:"provider"`
22		LastUpdated       string `json:"last_updated"`
23	}
24	
25	// StatisticsFile is the root structure for the statistics.json file
26	type StatisticsFile struct {
27		Sessions map[string]SessionStatistics `json:"sessions"`
28	}
29	
30	// StatisticsCollector handles thread-safe statistics collection and persistence.
31	// Stats are accumulated in memory via AddSessionStats and written to disk in a
32	// single read-modify-write cycle when Flush is called.
33	type StatisticsCollector struct {
34		statsPath string
35		mu        sync.Mutex
36		pending   map[string]SessionStatistics // in-memory buffer of stats awaiting flush
37	}
38	
39	// NewStatisticsCollector creates a new statistics collector that writes to the given path
40	func NewStatisticsCollector(statsPath string) *StatisticsCollector {
41		return &StatisticsCollector{
42			statsPath: statsPath,
43			pending:   make(map[string]SessionStatistics),
44		}
45	}
46	
47	// ComputeSessionStatistics extracts statistics from SessionData and markdown content
48	func ComputeSessionStatistics(sessionData *schema.SessionData, markdownContent string, providerID string) SessionStatistics {
49		stats := SessionStatistics{
50			Provider:          providerID,
51			MarkdownSizeBytes: len(markdownContent),
52			LastUpdated:       time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
53		}
54	
55		// Count user and agent messages by iterating through exchanges
56		userMsgCount := 0
57		agentMsgCount := 0
58		for _, exchange := range sessionData.Exchanges {
59			for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
60				if msg.Role == schema.RoleUser {
61					userMsgCount++
62				} else {
63					agentMsgCount++
64				}
65			}
66		}
67		stats.UserMessageCount = userMsgCount
68		stats.AgentMessageCount = agentMsgCount
69	
70		// Extract start timestamp - use first exchange start time if available, else session CreatedAt
71		if len(sessionData.Exchanges) > 0 && sessionData.Exchanges[0].StartTime != "" {
72			stats.StartTimestamp = sessionData.Exchanges[0].StartTime
73		} else {
74			stats.StartTimestamp = sessionData.CreatedAt
75		}
76	
77		// Extract end timestamp - use last exchange end time if available, else session UpdatedAt, else CreatedAt
78		if len(sessionData.Exchanges) > 0 {
79			lastExchange := sessionData.Exchanges[len(sessionData.Exchanges)-1]
80			if lastExchange.EndTime != "" {
81				stats.EndTimestamp = lastExchange.EndTime
82			} else if sessionData.UpdatedAt != "" {
83				stats.EndTimestamp = sessionData.UpdatedAt
84			} else {
85				stats.EndTimestamp = sessionData.CreatedAt
86			}
87		} else if sessionData.UpdatedAt != "" {
88			stats.EndTimestamp = sessionData.UpdatedAt
89		} else {
90			stats.EndTimestamp = sessionData.CreatedAt
91		}
92	
93		return stats
94	}
95	
96	// AddSessionStats accumulates session statistics in memory. Call Flush to
97	// persist all pending stats to disk in a single I/O operation.
98	func (c *StatisticsCollector) AddSessionStats(sessionID string, stats SessionStatistics) {
99		c.mu.Lock()
100		defer c.mu.Unlock()
101	
102		c.pending[sessionID] = stats
103		slog.Debug("Buffered session statistics", "sessionId", sessionID)
104	}
105	
106	// Flush writes all pending session statistics to the statistics.json file in a
107	// single read-modify-write cycle, then clears the pending buffer.
108	func (c *StatisticsCollector) Flush() error {
109		c.mu.Lock()
110		defer c.mu.Unlock()
111	
112		// Nothing to flush
113		if len(c.pending) == 0 {
114			return nil
115		}
116	
117		statsPath := c.statsPath
118	
119		// Read existing statistics file
120		statsFile := StatisticsFile{
121			Sessions: make(map[string]SessionStatistics),
122		}
123	
124		data, err := os.ReadFile(statsPath)
125		if err == nil {
126			// File exists, try to parse it
127			if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &statsFile); err != nil {
128				// Corrupt JSON - log warning and start fresh
129				slog.Warn("Failed to parse existing statistics.json, starting fresh", "error", err)
130				statsFile.Sessions = make(map[string]SessionStatistics)
131			}
132		} else if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
133			// Error other than "file doesn't exist"
134			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read statistics file: %w", err)
135		}
136	
137		// Merge all pending stats into the file
138		for sessionID, stats := range c.pending {
139			statsFile.Sessions[sessionID] = stats
140		}
141	
142		// Marshal to JSON with indentation for readability
143		jsonData, err := json.MarshalIndent(statsFile, "", "  ")
144		if err != nil {
145			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal statistics: %w", err)
146		}
147		jsonData = append(jsonData, '\n')
148	
149		// Write atomically using temp file + rename
150		tempPath := statsPath + ".tmp"
151		if err := os.WriteFile(tempPath, jsonData, 0644); err != nil {
152			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write temp statistics file: %w", err)
153		}
154	
155		if err := os.Rename(tempPath, statsPath); err != nil {
156			// Clean up temp file on failure
157			_ = os.Remove(tempPath)
158			return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename temp statistics file: %w", err)
159		}
160	
161		slog.Debug("Flushed session statistics", "count", len(c.pending), "path", statsPath)
162	
163		// Clear pending buffer
164		c.pending = make(map[string]SessionStatistics)
165		return nil
166	}
167
```

```bash
import json,sys
```

```text
1	package utils

4		"context"

12	)
13	
14	// WatchAgents starts watchers for all registered providers concurrently.
15	// Convenience wrapper around WatchProviders that resolves the full provider registry.
16	func WatchAgents(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
17		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
18		providers := registry.GetAll()
19	
20		if len(providers) == 0 {
21			return fmt.Errorf("no providers registered")
22		}
23	
24		return WatchProviders(ctx, projectPath, providers, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
25	}
26	
27	// WatchProviders starts watchers for the given providers concurrently.
28	// Calls sessionCallback when any provider detects activity.
29	// Runs until context is cancelled or all watchers stop.
30	// Context cancellation (Ctrl+C) is treated as a clean exit, not an error.
31	//
32	// Parameters:
33	//   - ctx: Context for cancellation and timeout control
34	//   - projectPath: Agent's working directory to watch
35	//   - providers: map of provider ID to provider instance to watch
36	//   - debugRaw: whether to write debug raw data files
37	//   - sessionCallback: called with provider ID and AgentChatSession data on each update
38	//
39	// The callback includes the provider ID to help consumers route/filter sessions.
40	// The callback should not block as it may delay other provider notifications.
41	func WatchProviders(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, providers map[string]spi.Provider, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
42		slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting multi-provider watch", "projectPath", projectPath, "providerCount", len(providers), "debugRaw", debugRaw)
43	
44		// Track last-seen message count per session to suppress duplicate callbacks.
45		// Providers fire callbacks on every JSONL change, but not all changes produce
46		// new messages in the parsed SessionData. Messages are append-only, so a
47		// matching total count means nothing meaningful changed.
48		var mu sync.Mutex
49		lastMsgCount := make(map[string]int)
50	
51		var wg sync.WaitGroup
52		errChan := make(chan error, len(providers))
53	
54		for providerID, provider := range providers {
55			wg.Add(1)
56			go func() {
57				defer wg.Done()
58	
59				slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting watcher for provider", "providerID", providerID, "providerName", provider.Name())
60	
61				// Wrap the callback to deduplicate and include provider ID
62				wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
63					if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
64						return
65					}
66	
67					// Count total messages across all exchanges
68					totalMsgs := 0
69					for _, exchange := range session.SessionData.Exchanges {
70						totalMsgs += len(exchange.Messages)
71					}
72	
73					// Skip if message count hasn't changed for this session
74					mu.Lock()
75					prev, seen := lastMsgCount[session.SessionID]
76					if seen && prev == totalMsgs {
77						mu.Unlock()
78						slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
79							"providerID", providerID,
80							"sessionID", session.SessionID,
81							"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
82						return
83					}
84					lastMsgCount[session.SessionID] = totalMsgs
85					mu.Unlock()
86	
87					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
88						"providerID", providerID,
89						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
90						"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
91	
92					sessionCallback(providerID, session)
93				}
94	
95				err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
96				if err != nil {
97					// Context cancellation is expected when user presses Ctrl+C, not an error
98					if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
99						slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
100						errChan <- nil
101					} else {
102						slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
103						errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
104					}
105				} else {
106					errChan <- nil
107				}
108			}()
109		}
110	
111		// Wait for all watchers to complete (they run until Ctrl+C)
112		wg.Wait()
113	
114		// Drain error channel — errors are already logged in the goroutines with full context
115		for range len(providers) {
116			<-errChan
117		}
118	
119		return nil
120	}
121
```

```text
// TestFormatEntries_CompactionDropsPreKept covers the compaction entry's
// firstKeptEntryId field on full_format.jsonl: firstKeptEntryId=a2, so the
// common answer (before a2) is dropped and the post-compaction prompt survives.
func TestFormatEntries_CompactionDropsPreKept(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "full_format.jsonl"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
	}
	var hasCommon, hasPost bool
	for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
		for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
			for _, part := range msg.Content {
				if strings.Contains(part.Text, "common answer") {
					hasCommon = true
				}
				if strings.Contains(part.Text, "after compaction prompt") {
					hasPost = true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if hasCommon {
		t.Error("entry before firstKeptEntryId was not dropped by compaction")
	}
	if !hasPost {
		t.Error("post-compaction prompt was dropped")
	}
}

// TestFormatEntries_RealWorldCompactionAndBashExecution uses a trimmed slice of
// a real pi session (testdata/real_world.jsonl) to assert the hard-to-synthesize
// format features: a compaction entry carrying details.readFiles/modifiedFiles +
// tokensBefore, a bashExecution message role (skipped from exchanges), and that
// compaction drops the pre-kept user prompt while keeping the post-compaction one.
func TestFormatEntries_RealWorldCompactionAndBashExecution(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "real_world.jsonl"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
	}
	if data.SessionID != "real-world-uuid" {
		t.Errorf("SessionID = %q, want real-world-uuid", data.SessionID)
	}
	if !data.Validate() {
		t.Error("Validate() returned false for the real-world session")
	}
	var hasPreCompaction, hasPostCompaction, hasBashExecContent bool
	for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
		for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
			for _, part := range msg.Content {
				if strings.Contains(part.Text, "Read README.md and NOTES.md") {
					hasPreCompaction = true
				}
				if strings.Contains(part.Text, "summarize it now") {
					hasPostCompaction = true
				}
				if strings.Contains(part.Text, "total 24") {
					hasBashExecContent = true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if hasPreCompaction {
		t.Error("pre-compaction user prompt was not dropped by compaction")
	}
	if !hasPostCompaction {
		t.Error("post-compaction user prompt was dropped by compaction")
	}
	if hasBashExecContent {
		t.Error("bashExecution content leaked into exchanges (should be skipped)")
	}
}
```

```bash
import json, glob
files = glob.glob('/Users/jakelevirne/.pi/agent/sessions/*/*.jsonl') + glob.glob('/Users/jakelevirne/.pi/agent/sessions/*/*/*/*.jsonl')

        try: entries.append(json.loads(line))
        except: pass
    # last entry
    last = entries[-1]
    if last.get('type')!='message':
        print('LAST NOT MESSAGE:', p, last.get('type'), 'parentId=',last.get('parentId'))
    # custom entries parent info

    # compaction keys
    for e in entries:
        if e.get('type')=='compaction':
            print('compaction keys:', list(e.keys()))
print('total null-parent mid-file:', null_parent_mid)
EOF
```

```text
- Cross-platform support (Linux, macOS)
- Seamless integration with terminal coding agents
- Command-line wrapper for terminal coding agents with markdown auto-save
- Sync all your prior conversations to local markdown files
- Optional: Syncs your markdown files to the SpecStory Cloud for easy search and chat
- Open source under the Apache 2.0 license

## Agent Support

The following coding agents are supported in the SpecStory CLI:

| Agent                                                     | Provider                                  | Data Format | Source Location         |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------|-------------------------|

### Agent Provider SPI (Service Provider Interface)

There is also an [Agent SPI (Service Provider Interface)](/pkg/spi/) that allows you to extend the SpecStory CLI with support for new agent providers. Creating a provider to support a new agent, using the Provider SPI is documented [here](./docs/PROVIDER-SPI.md). Pull requests are welcome!

## Installation & Usage

Full end-user installation and usage instructions are in the [SpecStory CLI Documentation](https://docs.specstory.com/integrations/terminal-coding-agents). Installation for developers is covered [here](#development).
```

FINDING [severity=low] (from parser-treewalk reviewer):
Title: Real (unmigrated) pi v1 session files fail to parse because their entries have no id/parentId; the v1_legacy fixture does not match the real v1 format
File: specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/jsonl_parser.go line 92
Description: Genuine pi v1 files have NO id/parentId on entries — pi's migrateV1ToV2 (dist/core/session-manager.js:30-53) generates ids at load time and only then rewrites the file (lines 572-573). For an on-disk v1 file that hasn't been reopened by a modern pi, readEntries skips every entry at the `e.Type == "" || e.ID == ""` check, so ParseSession fails with "session has no entries" (agent_session.go:126) and the session silently never syncs. testdata/v1_legacy.jsonl models 'v1' as v3-shaped entries (with id/parentId) minus the header version field, so TestFormatTree_Version1Legacy (format_test.go:407) passes against a file shape that never existed in the wild, giving false confidence that legacy sessions are handled. FINDING [severity=low] (from parser-treewalk reviewer):
Title: Scan-path Slug/Name uses file-order first user message, diverging from the leaf-path slug when the first message was re-edited (root branch)
File: specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/provider.go line 311
Description: scanPiSession walks the file in append order and stops at the first message entry with user text (provider.go:387-396), performing no tree traversal, and its result feeds SessionRef Slug/Name (provider.go:311-312, 339+). ParseSession derives the slug from the leaf path via deriveSlug (provider.go:251, 284). pi explicitly supports re-editing the FIRST user message via resetLeaf() (session-manager.js:981-985: next append creates a new root with parentId=null), which leaves the abandoned original prompt earlier in the file. On such a session, the listing/reindex title and slug come from the abandoned prompt while the generated markdown slug comes from the active branch's prompt — a user-visible inconsistency the linear claudecode/codexcli formats cannot exhibit (their file order always equals conversation order, so sharing their scan pattern is not equivalent here).
Evidence: provider.go:369+ scanPiSession: iterates readLines in file order, `if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" { ... return errStopRead }` with no parentId/leaf logic; agent_session.go:473 comment claims "the scan path produces the same Slug/Name as the full-parse path", which only holds for unbranched roots. pi resetLeaf doc: "Use this when navigating to re-edit the first user message."

Description: pi stores a user-visible session display name as session_info tree entries and resolves the CURRENT name as the latest session_info entry's `name` (session-manager.js getSessionName, walking entries in reverse). piagent declares the entrySessionInfo constant but nothing reads the `name` field: rawEntry has no Name field and Name/Slug are always derived from the first user message (provider.go:311-312). Real sessions on this machine carry names, e.g. `{"type":"session_info","id":"d7464d59","parentId":null,...,"name":"pi-format-demo-web"}` (and one session has two session_info entries, i.e. a rename). A pi user who named their session sees an unrelated first-prompt-derived title in SpecStory listings. claudecode, by comparison, goes out of its way to capture the analogous summary/title records (claudecode/jsonl_parser.go:384-416).
Evidence: agent_session.go:23 `entrySessionInfo = "session_info"` is the only reference to session_info in the package (no `name` decode anywhere); real fixture: ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-jakelevirne-dev-tmp-pi-format-demo--/2026-07-09T21-21-13-447Z_*.jsonl line 2 contains name "pi-format-demo-web"; pi getSessionName() returns the latest session_info entry's trimmed name.

Description: deriveSlug walks data.Exchanges, which are built from the compaction-trimmed leaf path (ParseSession -> leafPathEntries -> applyCompaction), so after a compaction the slug comes from the first KEPT user message. For any compacted or branched session the two paths yield different Slug/Name for the same session: sync writes the markdown file as `<timestamp>-<parseSlug>.md` (session/session.go:64 uses AgentChatSession.Slug from deriveSlug), while `specstory list` (ListAgentChatSessions) and reindex's buildSession (reindex.go:559 uses ref.Slug from the scan) show the scan slug; the LiveIndexer path (reindex.go:519) writes the parse slug, so the index row's slug even flips between reindex and live-sync updates. claudecode/codexcli never trim history, so their scan and parse slugs always agree. Reproducible with the PR's own testdata/real_world.jsonl: scan yields 'Read README.md and NOTES.md...' while parse yields 'summarize it now...'.
Evidence: agent_session.go:417-431 deriveSlug iterates post-trim data.Exchanges; provider.go:387-399 scanPiSession scans raw file lines and stops at the first user text (`if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" { ... return errStopRead }`) with no leaf-path/compaction awareness; format_test.go TestFormatEntries_RealWorldCompactionAndBashExecution proves the pre-compaction prompt is absent from exchanges while it is the first user line in the file; cmd/reindex.go:519 `Slug: sess.Slug` (full parse) vs :559 `Slug: ref.Slug` (scan).

Context you must honor: claudecode/codexcli are the accepted bar; LOC limits, RawData double-read, and unsupported run/watch/reconstruct stubs are out of scope by owner decision. go test/vet/lint pass on this branch. Default to isReal=false if uncertain or if the issue is cosmetic beyond its stated severity. Return your verdict via the schema; explanation must cite what you actually read.

```text
1	package piagent
2	
3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"log/slog"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"strings"
13	)
14	
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// Skip entries missing the envelope fields the tree walk and exchange
91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}
104	
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
187	
188	// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
189	// if not found.
190	func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
191		for i, e := range path {
192			if e.ID == keptID {
193				return i
194			}
195		}
196		return -1
197	}
198
```

```text
39		cmdName := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand)
40		isCustom := cmdName != ""
41		if cmdName == "" {
42			cmdName = defaultCmd
43		}
44		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)

52		}
53		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
54		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
55		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
56		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
57		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
58			slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err)
59			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())
60			return spi.CheckResult{

66		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
67		if version == "" {

70		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
71		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}

366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
409	
410	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {
414			return nil
415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
420			Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
421			NativePath: path,
422			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
423		}
424	}
```

```text
107	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path
108	// branch into the unified schema.SessionData. It honors compaction entries:
109	// when a compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId
110	// are dropped from the conversation (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
112		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		if header == nil {
117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
118		}
119		if header.Type != entrySession {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
121		}
122		if header.ID == "" {
123			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
124		}
125		if len(entries) == 0 {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
127		}
128		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
129		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
130	}

132	// piProviderVersion derives the provider version string recorded on SessionData
133	// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
134	// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
135	func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
136		if header.Version > 0 {
137			return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
138		}
139		return "v1"
140	}
141	
142	// buildSessionData maps the ordered leaf-path entries into schema.SessionData.
143	func buildSessionData(header *sessionHeader, ordered []rawEntry) *schema.SessionData {
144		return &schema.SessionData{
145			SchemaVersion: "1.0",
146			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{
147				ID:      providerID,
148				Name:    providerName,
149				Version: piProviderVersion(header),
150			},
151			SessionID:     header.ID,
152			CreatedAt:     header.Timestamp,
153			WorkspaceRoot: header.Cwd,
154			Exchanges:     buildExchanges(ordered),
155		}
156	}

158	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
159	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
160	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo. Control entries
161	// (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the conversation body.
162	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
163		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
164		var current *schema.Exchange
165		commit := func() {
166			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
167				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
168			}
169		}
170		for _, e := range ordered {
171			if e.Type != entryMessage {
172				continue
173			}
174			switch messageRole(e) {
175			case roleUser:
176				commit()
177				current = &schema.Exchange{
178					ExchangeID: e.ID,
179					StartTime:  e.Timestamp,
180					EndTime:    e.Timestamp,
181					Messages:   []schema.Message{buildUserMessage(e)},
182				}
183			case roleAssistant:
184				current = appendAssistant(current, e)
185			case roleToolResult:
186				mergeToolResult(current, e)
187			}
188		}
189		commit()
190		return exchanges
191	}

193	// appendAssistant appends an assistant message to the current exchange, creating
194	// one if none exists yet.
195	func appendAssistant(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) *schema.Exchange {
196		if current == nil {
197			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
198		}
199		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, buildAgentMessages(e)...)
200		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
201		return current
202	}

213	// mergeToolResult folds a toolResult entry into the matching agent ToolInfo in
214	// the current exchange, keyed by toolCallId == ToolInfo.UseID. It also advances
215	// the exchange EndTime to the toolResult's timestamp so downstream stats that
216	// read the last exchange's EndTime report the real final-event time.
217	func mergeToolResult(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) {
218		if current == nil {
219			return
220		}

222		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &tr); err != nil {
223			return
224		}

228			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.UseID == tr.ToolCallID {
229				msg.Tool.Output = buildToolOutput(content, tr)
230				msg.Timestamp = e.Timestamp
231				current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
232				return
233			}
234		}
235	}

241			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
242				parts = append(parts, b.Text)
243			}
244		}
245		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
246	}

249	// pi user content is either a plain string or an array of {type:text|image}.

251		var um userMessage
252		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &um)
253		parts := userContentParts(um.Content)

255			ID:        e.ID,
256			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
257			Role:      schema.RoleUser,
258			Content:   parts,
259		}
260	}

262	// userContentParts decodes a pi user message's content (string or array) into
263	// schema ContentParts. Image blocks are dropped in v1 (recorded as a gap).
264	func userContentParts(raw json.RawMessage) []schema.ContentPart {
265		if len(raw) == 0 {
266			return nil
267		}
268		if raw[0] == '"' {
269			var s string
270			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
271				return []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: s}}
272			}
273		}
274		var blocks []contentBlock
275		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
276			return nil
277		}
278		var parts []schema.ContentPart
279		for _, b := range blocks {
280			if b.Type == schema.ContentTypeText && b.Text != "" {
281				parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
282			}
283		}
284		return parts
285	}

287	// buildAgentMessages maps a pi assistant message entry to one or more schema
288	// Messages: one Message holds the text+thinking content parts; each toolCall
289	// block becomes its own agent Message carrying a ToolInfo.
290	func buildAgentMessages(e rawEntry) []schema.Message {
291		var am assistantMessage
292		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &am); err != nil {
293			return nil
294		}
295		var parts []schema.ContentPart
296		var messages []schema.Message
297		for _, b := range am.Content {
298			switch b.Type {
299			case schema.ContentTypeText:
300				if b.Text != "" {
301					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
302				}
303			case schema.ContentTypeThinking:
304				if b.Thinking != "" {
305					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: b.Thinking})
306				}
307			case "toolCall":
308				messages = append(messages, buildToolMessage(e, b, am))
309			}
310		}
311		if len(parts) > 0 {
312			head := schema.Message{
313				ID:        e.ID,
314				Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
315				Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
316				Model:     am.Model,
317				Content:   parts,
318				Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
319			}
320			return append([]schema.Message{head}, messages...)
321		}
322		if len(messages) == 0 {
323			return buildErrorMessage(e, am)
324		}
325		// Tool-call-only assistant message: carry model+usage once on the first
326		// tool message so no metadata is lost and no schema-invalid empty message
327		// is emitted.
328		messages[0].Model = am.Model
329		if messages[0].Usage == nil {

331		}
332		return messages
333	}

335	// buildToolMessage builds an agent Message wrapping a ToolInfo from a toolCall.
336	// The parent assistant message's model is passed through so tool messages carry
337	// the same model metadata as text/thinking messages. The Message ID is derived
338	// from the parent entry id + the toolCall id, so multiple toolCalls in one
339	// assistant message get distinct Message IDs (downstream provenance keys use
340	// msg.ID as a deterministic component).
341	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
342		return schema.Message{
343			ID:        toolMessageID(e.ID, b.ID),
344			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
345			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
346			Model:     am.Model,
347			Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{
348				Name:  b.Name,
349				Type:  classifyToolType(b.Name),
350				UseID: b.ID,
351				Input: b.Args,
352			},
353		}
354	}
355	
356	// toolMessageID builds a unique Message ID for a tool-call message from the
357	// parent entry id and the toolCall id. This avoids duplicate Message IDs when a
358	// single assistant entry contains multiple toolCall blocks.
359	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {
360		if callID != "" {
361			return entryID + ":" + callID
362		}
363		return entryID
364	}
365	
366	// buildToolOutput constructs the ToolInfo.Output map from a toolResult's
367	// content, error flag, and optional details blob. details (e.g. exitCode) is
368	// decoded into a generic value so downstream consumers (markdown rendering,
369	// cloud) can surface structured tool metadata without re-parsing raw JSON.
370	func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
371		out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
372		if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
373			var details any
374			if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {
375				out["details"] = details
376			}
377		}
378		return out
379	}
```
