```text
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
```

```text
// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path
// branch into the unified schema.SessionData. It honors compaction entries:
// when a compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId
// are dropped from the conversation (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
	header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if header == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
	}
	if header.Type != entrySession {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
	}
	if header.ID == "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
	}
	if len(entries) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
	}
	ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
	return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
}

// piProviderVersion derives the provider version string recorded on SessionData
// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
	if header.Version > 0 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
	}
	return "v1"
}
```

```text
69:- Fixed `pi update` for pnpm installations to suggest pruning pnpm's self-update cache when the executable points at a removed cached version ([#6279](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/6279) by [@rajp152k](https://github.com/rajp152k)).
167:- pi-ai's old global API (`stream`/`complete`/`completeSimple`, `getModel`/`getModels`/`getProviders`, `registerApiProvider`, `getEnvApiKey`, ...) moved off the `@earendil-works/pi-ai` root entrypoint to `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat`. Extensions are not affected at runtime: the extension loader resolves the pi-ai root to the compat entrypoint (a strict superset), so existing extensions keep working unchanged. Extension sources that typecheck against pi-ai's published types should switch those imports to `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat` (or migrate to the new `createModels()`/provider-factory API). The compat entrypoint and the loader alias will be removed in a future release with a migration guide.
418:- Fixed invalid `models.json` syntax to skip startup config migrations and report the normal file-path-aware models error instead of a raw JSON parse stack trace ([#5418](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5418)).

693:- Fixed Amazon Bedrock message conversion to skip unknown content blocks instead of failing the stream, inherited from `@earendil-works/pi-ai` ([#4223](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/4223)).
```

```text
27	// Provider implements spi.Provider for the pi coding agent.
28	// pi stores sessions as JSONL v3 trees under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/.
29	type Provider struct{}
30	
31	// NewProvider returns a new pi provider instance.
32	func NewProvider() *Provider { return &Provider{} }
33	
34	// Name returns the human-readable provider name.
35	func (p *Provider) Name() string { return providerName }
36	
37	// Check verifies the pi binary is on PATH and reports its version.
38	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
39		cmdName := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand)
40		isCustom := cmdName != ""
41		if cmdName == "" {
42			cmdName = defaultCmd
43		}
44		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
45		if err != nil {
46			slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
47			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "not_found", err.Error())
48			return spi.CheckResult{
49				Success:      false,
50				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi binary '%s' not found on PATH", cmdName),
51			}
52		}
53		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
54		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
55		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
56		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
57		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
58			slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err)
59			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())
60			return spi.CheckResult{
61				Success:      false,
62				Location:     resolved,
63				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi version probe failed: %v", err),
64			}
65		}
66		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
67		if version == "" {
68			version = "unknown"
69		}
70		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
71		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
72	}

130	// sessionFile pairs a discovered pi session file with its header metadata.
131	type sessionFile struct {
132		Path   string
133		Header sessionHeader
134	}
135	
136	// findProjectSession locates the session file with the given ID within the
137	// project's pi session directory. Returns "" if not found.
138	func findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
139		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
140		if err != nil {
141			return "", err
142		}
143		for _, f := range files {
144			h, err := readHeader(f)
145			if err != nil || h == nil {
146				continue
147			}
148			if h.ID == sessionID {
149				return f, nil
150			}
151		}
152		return "", nil
153	}
154	
155	// readHeader parses only the first line of a session file and returns it only
156	// if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty id).
157	// Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them.
158	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
159		f, err := os.Open(path)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, err
162		}
163		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
164		dec := json.NewDecoder(f)
165		var h sessionHeader
166		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
170			return nil, nil
171		}
172		return &h, nil
173	}
174	
175	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
176	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
177	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
178	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
179		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, err
182		}
183		var out []sessionFile
184		for _, f := range files {
185			h, err := readHeader(f)
186			if err != nil {
187				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
188				continue
189			}
190			if h == nil {
191				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
192			}
193			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}

198	// GetAgentChatSession returns a single pi session by ID for the project.
199	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
200		path, err := findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID)
201		if err != nil {
202			return nil, err
203		}
204		if path == "" {
205			return nil, nil
206		}
207		return parseToAgentSession(path, debugRaw)
208	}

210	// GetAgentChatSessions returns all pi sessions for the project.
211	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
212		files, err := listProjectSessions(projectPath)
213		if err != nil {
214			return nil, err
215		}
216		total := len(files)
217		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
218		for i, sf := range files {
219			chat, pErr := parseToAgentSession(sf.Path, debugRaw)
220			if pErr != nil {
221				slog.Debug("pi: skipping session", "path", sf.Path, "error", pErr)
222			} else if chat != nil {
223				result = append(result, *chat)
224			}
225			if progress != nil {
226				progress(i+1, total)
227			}
228		}
229		return result, nil
230	}

232	// parseToAgentSession parses one session file into an AgentChatSession,
233	// writing debug-raw artifacts when debugRaw is true.
234	func parseToAgentSession(path string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
235		data, err := ParseSession(path)
236		if err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239		if debugRaw {
240			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(path, data); dErr != nil {
241				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
242			}
243		}
244		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
245		if err != nil {
246			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
247		}
248		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
249			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
250			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
251			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
252			SessionData: data,
253			RawData:     string(raw),
254		}, nil
255	}
256	
257	// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single pi session directly from its native
258	// file path, skipping the by-id discovery search. originCwd is the session's
259	// originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd), passed through
260	// as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
261	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath. Implements spi.PathSessionReader
262	// so `specstory reindex` uses the O(N) path-keyed fast path instead of the
263	// O(N²) by-id lookup.
264	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
265		data, err := ParseSession(nativePath)
266		if err != nil {
267			return nil, err
268		}
269		if data.WorkspaceRoot == "" && originCwd != "" {
270			data.WorkspaceRoot = originCwd
271		}
272		if debugRaw {
273			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(nativePath, data); dErr != nil {
274				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
275			}
276		}
277		raw, err := os.ReadFile(nativePath)
278		if err != nil {
279			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
280		}
281		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
282			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
283			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
284			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
285			SessionData: data,
286			RawData:     string(raw),
287		}, nil
288	}

290	// ListAgentChatSessions returns lightweight metadata for all project sessions,
291	// deriving Slug/Name from the first user message via a bounded single-pass scan
292	// (no full parse), matching how other providers populate metadata.
293	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
294		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
295		if err != nil {
296			return nil, err
297		}
298		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
299		for _, f := range files {
300			scan, scanErr := scanPiSession(f)
301			if scanErr != nil {
302				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", scanErr)
303				continue
304			}
305			if scan == nil || !scan.foundUser {
306				continue
307			}
308			result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
309				SessionID: scan.sessionID,
310				CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
311				Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
312				Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
313			})
314		}
315		return result, nil
316	}

318	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every pi session across all projects,
319	// each ref carrying its originating cwd (read from the session header).
320	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
321		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
322	}
323	
324	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all pi sessions with live scan
325	// progress, using the shared parallel scanner. Each ref carries Slug/Name
326	// derived from the first user message and the originating cwd from the header.
327	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
328		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
329		if err != nil {
330			return nil, err
331		}
332		if _, statErr := os.Stat(root); statErr != nil {
333			if os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
334				return nil, nil
335			}
336			return nil, statErr
337		}
338		scan := func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
339			s, sErr := scanPiSession(path)
340			if sErr != nil {
341				return nil, sErr
342			}
343			if s == nil {
344				return nil, nil // non-session file
345			}
346			return scanToGlobalRef(s, path), nil
347		}
348		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)
349	}
350	
351	// piSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one bounded
352	// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan
353	// stops as soon as it has the first user message, so it does NOT parse the whole
354	// session. foundUser is false for sessions with no real user prompt; scanPiSession
355	// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
356	type piSessionScan struct {
357		sessionID        string
358		timestamp        string
359		firstUserMessage string
360		cwd              string
361		foundUser        bool
362	}
363	
364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
409	
410	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {
414			return nil
415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
420			Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
421			NativePath: path,
422			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
423		}
424	}
425
```

```text
// hasRenderableContent reports whether a message would produce visible output:
// a tool use, or a text/thinking part with non-whitespace text. Only the part
// types that renderContentParts actually emits are counted, so "renderable" here
// stays in lock-step with what gets written — a stray part of any other type
// can't trick us into emitting a bare role header. PathHints are deliberately
// excluded: renderMessage never emits them, so a pathHints-only message has no
// body. Messages with nothing renderable are skipped.
func hasRenderableContent(msg Message) bool {
	if msg.Tool != nil {
		return true
	}
	for _, part := range msg.Content {
		switch part.Type {
		case schema.ContentTypeText, schema.ContentTypeThinking:
			if strings.TrimSpace(part.Text) != "" {
				return true
```
```text
			}

// launchResume reconstructs (cross-agent) or natively resumes the planned session and
// runs the agent with auto-save + provenance — the shared tail of `resume` and `search`.
func launchResume(plan *resumePlan, cwd string, o resumeLaunchOpts) error {
	// Setup output configuration and project identity (needed for auto-save + cloud).
	outConfig, err := utils.SetupOutputConfig(o.outputDir, o.flagDebugDir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := utils.EnsureHistoryDirectoryExists(outConfig); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if _, err := utils.NewProjectIdentityManager(cwd).EnsureProjectIdentity(); err != nil {
		slog.Error("Failed to ensure project identity", "error", err)
	}

	CheckAndWarnAuthentication(o.noCloudSync)
	if o.onlyCloudSync && !cloud.IsAuthenticated() {
		return utils.ValidationError{Message: "--only-cloud-sync requires authentication. Please run 'specstory login' first"}
	}

	analytics.SetAgentProviders([]string{plan.to.Name()})
	analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventResumeActivated, analytics.Properties{
		"from_provider": plan.fromID,
		"to_provider":   plan.toID,
		"cross_agent":   plan.fromID != plan.toID,
	})

	resumeSessionID, err := prepareResumeTarget(plan, cwd, os.Stdout)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// Context for graceful cancellation (Ctrl+C).
	ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer cancel()

	// Provenance infrastructure (mirrors run/watch).
	provenanceEngine, provenanceCleanup, err := provenance.StartEngine(o.provenanceEnabled)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer provenanceCleanup()
	fsCleanup, err := provenance.StartFSWatcher(ctx, provenanceEngine, cwd)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer fsCleanup()

	// Keep sessions.db current in real time alongside the markdown writes (nil/no-op if the
	// index can't be opened — never block the resumed agent on it).
	liveIndex := NewLiveIndexer(cwd)
	defer liveIndex.Close()

	// Auto-save callback: identical behavior to run/watch.
	sessionCallback := func(sess *spi.AgentChatSession) {
		if sess == nil {
			return
		}
		_, perr := session.ProcessSingleSession(context.Background(), sess, outConfig, session.ProcessingOptions{
			OnlyCloudSync:      o.onlyCloudSync,
			IsAutosave:         true,
			DebugRaw:           o.debugRaw,
			UseUTC:             o.useUTC,
			NoTelemetryPrompts: o.noTelemetryPrompts,
		})
		if perr != nil {
			slog.Error("Failed to process session update", "sessionId", sess.SessionID, "error", perr)
		}
		// Mirror the markdown write into the restore index (agent we resumed INTO).
		liveIndex.Record(plan.toID, sess)
		provenance.ProcessEvents(ctx, provenanceEngine, sess)
	}

	slog.Info("Launching resume", "provider", plan.to.Name(), "resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID)
	if err := plan.to.ExecAgentAndWatch(cwd, "", resumeSessionID, o.debugRaw, sessionCallback); err != nil {
		slog.Error("Agent resume failed", "provider", plan.to.Name(), "error", err)
		return err
	}
	return nil
}

// prepareResumeTarget produces the native session ID to hand to ExecAgentAndWatch.
// Same-agent resume reuses the existing session; cross-agent reconstructs the
// source SessionData into the target's native store and returns the fresh ID.
func prepareResumeTarget(plan *resumePlan, cwd string, out io.Writer) (string, error) {
	// Same agent: native resume on the existing session, no transform.
	if plan.fromID == plan.toID {
		fprintf(out, "\nResuming %s session %s in place...\n", plan.from.Name(), shortID(plan.sessionID))
```

```text
// TestFormatTree_Version1Legacy covers version 1: a linear entry sequence where
// the header omits the version field. The parser must still map it.
func TestFormatTree_Version1Legacy(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "v1_legacy.jsonl"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
	}
	if data.SessionID != "v1-uuid" {
		t.Errorf("SessionID = %q, want v1-uuid", data.SessionID)
	}
	if data.Provider.Version != "v1" {
		t.Errorf("Provider.Version = %q, want v1", data.Provider.Version)
	}
	if len(data.Exchanges) == 0 {
		t.Error("v1 session produced no exchanges")
	}
	if !data.Validate() {
		t.Error("Validate() returned false for v1 session")
	}
}
```

```text
21:- Fixed inherited Anthropic message conversion to preserve thinking blocks with empty thinking text but a valid signature instead of dropping them, avoiding thinking-block errors on newer Claude models ([#6457](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/6457) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai)).

167:- pi-ai's old global API (`stream`/`complete`/`completeSimple`, `getModel`/`getModels`/`getProviders`, `registerApiProvider`, `getEnvApiKey`, ...) moved off the `@earendil-works/pi-ai` root entrypoint to `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat`. Extensions are not affected at runtime: the extension loader resolves the pi-ai root to the compat entrypoint (a strict superset), so existing extensions keep working unchanged. Extension sources that typecheck against pi-ai's published types should switch those imports to `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat` (or migrate to the new `createModels()`/provider-factory API). The compat entrypoint and the loader alias will be removed in a future release with a migration guide.
192:- **Safer update flow** - `pi update` installs the exact checked Pi version, and update notices show the changelog URL, making upgrades more predictable. See [Install and Manage](docs/packages.md#install-and-manage).
206:- Fixed `pi update` to install the exact version returned by the Pi update check, make `--force` reinstall that checked version, fail instead of falling back to an unversioned reinstall when no version is available, and report both the old and updated versions.
315:- Fixed successful `pi update` on Windows to exit naturally instead of calling `process.exit(0)`, avoiding a Node.js/libuv assertion after version-check network requests ([#5805](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5805)).
418:- Fixed invalid `models.json` syntax to skip startup config migrations and report the normal file-path-aware models error instead of a raw JSON parse stack trace ([#5418](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5418)).
420:- Fixed CLI help and version output, including plain redirected `--help`/`--version` output and simplified `list`/`config` help text.
624:- Published a 0.74.2 rescue release that tells Node 20 users to upgrade Node before updating to newer Pi versions ([#4876](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/4876)).
639:- Added interactive update notes after `pi update` runs, so users can see the installed version's changelog before continuing ([#4724](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/4724) by [@mitsuhiko](https://github.com/mitsuhiko)).
693:- Fixed Amazon Bedrock message conversion to skip unknown content blocks instead of failing the stream, inherited from `@earendil-works/pi-ai` ([#4223](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/4223)).
708:- Raised the minimum supported Node.js version to 22.19.0.
771:- **Self-update support for the npm scope migration**: `pi update --self` now supports the upcoming package rename from `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` to `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`. After the new package is published, existing global installs can update through the normal self-update flow; pi will uninstall the old global package and install the package name returned by the version check endpoint.
781:- Changed `pi update --self` to honor the active package name returned by the Pi version check endpoint, defaulting to the current package when omitted and uninstalling the old global package before installing a renamed package.
844:- Replaced `compat.reasoningEffortMap` in `models.json` and `pi.registerProvider()` model definitions with model-level `thinkingLevelMap` ([#3208](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3208)). Migration: move old mappings from `compat.reasoningEffortMap` to `thinkingLevelMap`. Use string values for provider-specific thinking values and `null` for unsupported pi levels that should be hidden and skipped by cycling. See `docs/models.md#thinking-level-map` and `docs/custom-provider.md`.
856:- Fixed self-update detection so `pi` correctly identifies when a newer version is available and applies updates ([#3942](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3942), [#3980](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3980), [#3922](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3922)).
925:- Pi update checks now use `pi.dev` and identify Pi with a `pi/<version>` user agent. See [docs/packages.md](docs/packages.md). ([#3877](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/3877) by [@mitsuhiko](https://github.com/mitsuhiko))
933:- Changed Pi version checks to identify Pi with a `pi/<version>` user agent ([#3877](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/3877) by [@mitsuhiko](https://github.com/mitsuhiko)).
942:- Fixed `pi update` to skip self-update reinstalls when the installed version is already current ([#3853](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3853)).
1015:- Fixed provider retry/timeout settings wiring by adding `retry.provider.{timeoutMs,maxRetries,maxRetryDelayMs}`, migrating legacy `retry.maxDelayMs`, and forwarding provider controls into `streamSimple` request options ([#3627](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3627))
1080:- TypeBox 1.x migration for extensions and SDK integrations, including TypeBox-native tool argument validation that now works in eval-restricted runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers. See [docs/extensions.md](docs/extensions.md) and [docs/sdk.md](docs/sdk.md).
1087:- Migrated first-party coding-agent code, SDK/examples/docs, and package metadata from `@sinclair/typebox` 0.34.x to `typebox` 1.x. New extensions, SDK integrations, and pi packages should depend on and import from `typebox`. Legacy extension loading still aliases the root `@sinclair/typebox` package, but `@sinclair/typebox/compiler` is no longer shimmed. This migration also picks up the new `@mariozechner/pi-ai` TypeBox-native validator path, so tool argument validation now works in eval-restricted runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers instead of being skipped ([#3112](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3112))
1088:- Session-replacement commands now invalidate captured pre-replacement session-bound extension objects after `ctx.newSession()`, `ctx.fork()`, and `ctx.switchSession()`. Old `pi` and command `ctx` references now throw instead of silently targeting the replaced session. Migration: if code needs to keep working in the replacement session after one of those calls, pass `withSession` to that same method and do the post-switch work there. In practice, move post-switch `pi.sendUserMessage()`, `pi.sendMessage()`, and command-ctx/session-manager access into `withSession`, and use only the `ReplacedSessionContext` passed to that callback for session-bound operations. Footguns: `withSession` runs after the old extension instance has already received `session_shutdown`, old cleanup may already have invalidated captured state, captured old `pi` / old command `ctx` are stale, and previously extracted raw objects such as `const sm = ctx.sessionManager` remain the caller's responsibility and must not be reused after the switch.
1138:- Changed SDK and CLI tool selection from cwd-bound built-in tool instances to tool-name allowlists. `createAgentSession({ tools })` now expects `string[]` names such as `"read"` and `"bash"` instead of `Tool[]`, `--tools` now allowlists built-in, extension, and custom tools by name, and `--no-tools` now disables all tools by default rather than only built-ins. Migrate SDK code from `tools: [readTool, bashTool]` to `tools: ["read", "bash"]` ([#2835](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/2835), [#3452](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3452))
1162:- Fixed `pi update` reinstalling npm packages that are already at the latest published version by checking the installed package version before running `npm install <pkg>@latest` ([#3000](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/3000))
1329:Interactive mode now sends a lightweight anonymous install/update telemetry ping to `https://pi.dev/install?version=x.y.z` after it writes `lastChangelogVersion` in `settings.json`.
1332:- Pi needs a reliable per-version usage signal to understand whether releases are being adopted and to help justify funding continued development.
1338:- On a fresh interactive install, Pi writes `lastChangelogVersion`, then sends the ping.
1339:- On later interactive startups, if the local changelog contains entries newer than the previously stored `lastChangelogVersion`, Pi writes the new `lastChangelogVersion`, then sends the ping.
1343:- Only the Pi version in the request path, for example `https://pi.dev/install?version=0.67.1`.
```

```text
441	// eliminateDuplicates removes duplicate records by uuid, keeping the earliest by timestamp
442	func (p *JSONLParser) eliminateDuplicates(records []JSONLRecord) []JSONLRecord {
443		// Map to track records by uuid
444		recordMap := make(map[string]JSONLRecord)
445	
446		for _, record := range records {
447			uuid, ok := record.Data["uuid"].(string)
448			if !ok || uuid == "" {
449				// Skip records without uuid
450				continue
451			}
452	
453			// If we haven't seen this uuid before, add it
454			if existing, exists := recordMap[uuid]; !exists {
455				recordMap[uuid] = record
456			} else {
457				// Compare timestamps and keep the earliest
458				existingTS, _ := existing.Data["timestamp"].(string)
459				currentTS, _ := record.Data["timestamp"].(string)
460				if currentTS < existingTS {
461					slog.Debug("eliminateDuplicates: Duplicate uuid - keeping newer timestamp",
462						"uuid", uuid,
463						"newTimestamp", currentTS,
464						"oldTimestamp", existingTS)
465					recordMap[uuid] = record
466				} else if currentTS != existingTS {
467					slog.Debug("eliminateDuplicates: Duplicate uuid - keeping older timestamp",
468						"uuid", uuid,
469						"oldTimestamp", existingTS,
470						"newTimestamp", currentTS)
471				}
472			}
473		}
474	
475		// Convert map back to slice
476		uniqueRecords := make([]JSONLRecord, 0, len(recordMap))
477		for _, record := range recordMap {
478			uniqueRecords = append(uniqueRecords, record)
479		}
480	
481		// Sort by timestamp for deterministic order
482		sort.Slice(uniqueRecords, func(i, j int) bool {
483			tsI, _ := uniqueRecords[i].Data["timestamp"].(string)
484			tsJ, _ := uniqueRecords[j].Data["timestamp"].(string)
485			return tsI < tsJ
486		})
487	
488		return uniqueRecords
489	}
490	
491	// mergeDagsWithSameSessionId merges DAGs that have the same session ID
492	// This handles cases where Claude Code resumes a session, creating multiple roots for the same session
493	func (p *JSONLParser) mergeDagsWithSameSessionId(dags [][]JSONLRecord) [][]JSONLRecord {
494		// Map to group DAGs by session ID
495		sessionDagMap := make(map[string][][]JSONLRecord)
496	
497		for _, dag := range dags {
498			if len(dag) == 0 {
499				continue
500			}
501	
502			// Find the session ID for this DAG
503			sessionId := ""
504			for _, record := range dag {
505				if sid, ok := record.Data["sessionId"].(string); ok && sid != "" {
506					sessionId = sid
507					break
508				}
509			}
510	
511			// If no session ID found, treat it as a unique DAG
512			if sessionId == "" {
513				sessionId = fmt.Sprintf("no-session-%p", &dag)
514			}
515	
516			sessionDagMap[sessionId] = append(sessionDagMap[sessionId], dag)
517		}
518	
519		// Merge DAGs with the same session ID
520		mergedDags := [][]JSONLRecord{}
521		for sessionId, dagsForSession := range sessionDagMap {
522			if len(dagsForSession) == 1 {
523				// No merging needed
524				mergedDags = append(mergedDags, dagsForSession[0])
525			} else {
526				// Merge multiple DAGs for the same session
527				slog.Debug("Merging multiple DAGs for session", "sessionId", sessionId, "dagCount", len(dagsForSession))
528				mergedDag := []JSONLRecord{}
529				for _, dag := range dagsForSession {
530					mergedDag = append(mergedDag, dag...)
531				}
532				mergedDags = append(mergedDags, mergedDag)
533			}
534		}
535	
536		return mergedDags
537	}

539	// buildDAGs constructs parent/child DAGs from records
540	func (p *JSONLParser) buildDAGs(records []JSONLRecord) [][]JSONLRecord {
541		// Build a parentUuid->children adjacency map in one pass. Precomputing children here is what
542		// keeps DAG building O(N): the traversal below can then look a node's children up directly.
543		// The previous version re-scanned the entire record set to find children at every node it
544		// visited, making a whole-project parse O(N²) — tens of seconds for a project with ~25k
545		// records (the dominant cost of `specstory sync`).
546		childrenByParent := make(map[string][]JSONLRecord)
547		roots := []JSONLRecord{}
548		for _, record := range records {
549			if _, ok := record.Data["uuid"].(string); !ok {
550				continue // a record with no uuid can be neither traversed nor linked
551			}
552			if parentUuid, ok := record.Data["parentUuid"].(string); ok {
553				childrenByParent[parentUuid] = append(childrenByParent[parentUuid], record)
554			} else if record.Data["parentUuid"] == nil {
555				// A nil parentUuid marks a root node (the start of a conversation).
556				roots = append(roots, record)
557			}
558		}
559	
560		// Sort each child list by timestamp once, giving the same deterministic traversal order the
561		// per-node sort used to — but paid O(N log N) total across the forest instead of per visit.
562		for parentUuid := range childrenByParent {
563			children := childrenByParent[parentUuid]
564			sort.Slice(children, func(i, j int) bool {
565				tsI, _ := children[i].Data["timestamp"].(string)
566				tsJ, _ := children[j].Data["timestamp"].(string)
567				return tsI < tsJ
568			})
569		}
570	
571		// Build a DAG for each root
572		dags := [][]JSONLRecord{}
573		for _, root := range roots {
574			dag := p.buildDAGFromRoot(root, childrenByParent)
575			if len(dag) > 0 {
576				dags = append(dags, dag)
577			}
578		}
579	
580		return dags
581	}
582	
583	// buildDAGFromRoot builds a DAG starting from a root node, following the precomputed
584	// parentUuid->children adjacency (already timestamp-sorted in buildDAGs).
585	func (p *JSONLParser) buildDAGFromRoot(root JSONLRecord, childrenByParent map[string][]JSONLRecord) []JSONLRecord {
586		dag := []JSONLRecord{}
587		visited := make(map[string]bool)
588	
589		var traverse func(node JSONLRecord)
590		traverse = func(node JSONLRecord) {
591			uuid, ok := node.Data["uuid"].(string)
592			if !ok || visited[uuid] {
593				return
594			}
595	
596			visited[uuid] = true
597			dag = append(dag, node)
598	
599			// Children are precomputed and already sorted by timestamp.
600			for _, child := range childrenByParent[uuid] {
601				traverse(child)
602			}
603		}
604	
605		traverse(root)
606		return dag
607	}
608	
609	// flattenDAG flattens a DAG into an array ordered by timestamp
610	func (p *JSONLParser) flattenDAG(dag []JSONLRecord) []JSONLRecord {
611		// Sort by timestamp, with parent-child relationships as tiebreaker
612		sort.Slice(dag, func(i, j int) bool {
613			tsI, _ := dag[i].Data["timestamp"].(string)
614			tsJ, _ := dag[j].Data["timestamp"].(string)
615			if tsI != tsJ {
616				return tsI < tsJ
617			}
618			// If timestamps are equal, check parent-child relationship
619			uuidI, _ := dag[i].Data["uuid"].(string)
620			uuidJ, _ := dag[j].Data["uuid"].(string)
621			parentI, _ := dag[i].Data["parentUuid"].(string)
622			parentJ, _ := dag[j].Data["parentUuid"].(string)
623	
624			// If j is the parent of i, j should come first
625			if parentI == uuidJ {
626				return false
627			}
628			// If i is the parent of j, i should come first
629			if parentJ == uuidI {
630				return true
631			}
632			// Otherwise, sort by UUID for deterministic ordering
633			return uuidI < uuidJ
634		})
635	
636		return dag
637	}
```

```text
543	func findFirstUserMessage(session Session) string {
544		for _, record := range session.Records {
545			// Check if this is a user message
546			if recordType, ok := record.Data["type"].(string); !ok || recordType != "user" {
547				continue
548			}
549	
550			// Skip meta user messages

553			}
554	
555			// Extract content from message - content may be a string or a list of blocks

557				content := extractContentText(message["content"])
558				if content != "" {

562					}

606			}

612		})
613		if err != nil {
614			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to scan project directory: %w", err)
615		}
616	
617		// Extract metadata from each session file
618		sessions := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(sessionFiles))
619		for _, filePath := range sessionFiles {
620			metadata, err := extractSessionMetadata(filePath)
621			if err != nil {
622				slog.Warn("Failed to extract session metadata",
623					"file", filePath,
624					"error", err)
625				continue
626			}
627	
628			// Skip warmup-only sessions (no metadata means warmup-only)
629			if metadata == nil {
630				slog.Debug("Skipping warmup-only session", "file", filePath)
631				continue
632			}
633	
634			sessions = append(sessions, *metadata)
635		}
636	
637		return sessions, nil
638	}
```

```text
        this.sessionFile = resolvePath(sessionFile);
        if (existsSync(this.sessionFile)) {

            const header = this.fileEntries.find((e) => e.type === "session");
            this.sessionId = header?.id ?? createSessionId();
            if (migrateToCurrentVersion(this.fileEntries)) {
                this._rewriteFile();

            this._buildIndex();

            this.newSession();
```

```text
// BuildSessionFilePath constructs the full markdown file path for a session.
// All callers need consistent filename generation from session metadata.
func BuildSessionFilePath(session *spi.AgentChatSession, historyDir string, useUTC bool) string {
	timestamp, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, session.CreatedAt)
	timestampStr := FormatFilenameTimestamp(timestamp, useUTC)

	filename := timestampStr
	if session.Slug != "" {
		filename = fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", timestampStr, session.Slug)
	}
	return filepath.Join(historyDir, filename+".md")
}

// ProcessingOptions holds flags that control session processing behavior.
type ProcessingOptions struct {
	OnlyCloudSync      bool // Skip local markdown writes and only sync to cloud
	ShowOutput         bool // Print progress to stdout
	IsAutosave         bool // Called from run/watch (true) vs sync command (false)
	DebugRaw           bool // Enable schema validation (only in debug mode to avoid overhead)
	UseUTC             bool // Timestamp format: true=UTC, false=local
```

```text
261	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath. Implements spi.PathSessionReader
262	// so `specstory reindex` uses the O(N) path-keyed fast path instead of the
263	// O(N²) by-id lookup.
264	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
265		data, err := ParseSession(nativePath)

269		if data.WorkspaceRoot == "" && originCwd != "" {

274				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
275			}
276		}

292	// (no full parse), matching how other providers populate metadata.
293	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
294		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
295		if err != nil {
296			return nil, err
297		}
298		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
299		for _, f := range files {
300			scan, scanErr := scanPiSession(f)
301			if scanErr != nil {
302				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", scanErr)
303				continue
304			}
305			if scan == nil || !scan.foundUser {
306				continue
307			}
308			result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
309				SessionID: scan.sessionID,
310				CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
311				Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
312				Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
313			})
314		}
315		return result, nil
316	}
```

```text
     * Start a new branch from an earlier entry.

    branch(branchFromId) {
        if (!this.byId.has(branchFromId)) {

        }
        this.leafId = branchFromId;
    }
    /**
     * Reset the leaf pointer to null (before any entries).
     * The next appendXXX() call will create a new root entry (parentId = null).
     * Use this when navigating to re-edit the first user message.

    resetLeaf() {
        this.leafId = null;

     * Same as branch(), but also appends a branch_summary entry that captures
     * context from the abandoned conversation path.
     */
    branchWithSummary(branchFromId, summary, details, fromHook) {
        if (branchFromId !== null && !this.byId.has(branchFromId)) {
            throw new Error(`Entry ${branchFromId} not found`);
        }
        this.leafId = branchFromId;
        const entry = {
            type: "branch_summary",
            id: generateId(this.byId),
            parentId: branchFromId,
            timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
            fromId: branchFromId ?? "root",
            summary,
```

```text
58:- Fixed the fork menu to ignore duplicate selection of the same entry ([#6430](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/6430) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai)).
70:- Fixed Xiaomi Token Plan model metadata to follow the upstream models.dev token-plan catalogs, removing unsupported `mimo-v2-omni` variants ([#6204](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6204)).
369:- Fixed experimental first-time setup to skip forked sessions instead of rerunning the setup prompts ([#5627](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/5627) by [@vegarsti](https://github.com/vegarsti)).
382:- Fixed `/fork` to keep session parent chains connected when the forked path contains labels ([#5669](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5669)).
552:- Fixed Xiaomi Token Plan model metadata to omit unsupported `mimo-v2-flash` variants ([#5075](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5075)).
655:- Fixed forked session runtime state to keep the active session id aligned with the fork target ([#4799](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/4799) by [@Perlence](https://github.com/Perlence)).
782:- Changed extension loading to use upstream `jiti` 2.7 instead of the `@mariozechner/jiti` fork ([#4244](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/4244) by [@pi0](https://github.com/pi0)).
813:- Added three Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan regional providers visible in `/login`: `xiaomi-token-plan-cn` (`XIAOMI_TOKEN_PLAN_CN_API_KEY`), `xiaomi-token-plan-ams` (`XIAOMI_TOKEN_PLAN_AMS_API_KEY`), `xiaomi-token-plan-sgp` (`XIAOMI_TOKEN_PLAN_SGP_API_KEY`). Each defaults to `mimo-v2.5-pro` ([#4112](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/4112) by [@Phoen1xCode](https://github.com/Phoen1xCode)).
836:- **Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan provider** - New Anthropic-compatible provider with `XIAOMI_API_KEY` auth, default model (`mimo-v2.5-pro`), and `/login` display. See [docs/providers.md](docs/providers.md). ([#4005](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/4005) by [@Phoen1xCode](https://github.com/Phoen1xCode)).
1088:- Session-replacement commands now invalidate captured pre-replacement session-bound extension objects after `ctx.newSession()`, `ctx.fork()`, and `ctx.switchSession()`. Old `pi` and command `ctx` references now throw instead of silently targeting the replaced session. Migration: if code needs to keep working in the replacement session after one of those calls, pass `withSession` to that same method and do the post-switch work there. In practice, move post-switch `pi.sendUserMessage()`, `pi.sendMessage()`, and command-ctx/session-manager access into `withSession`, and use only the `ReplacedSessionContext` passed to that callback for session-bound operations. Footguns: `withSession` runs after the old extension instance has already received `session_shutdown`, old cleanup may already have invalidated captured state, captured old `pi` / old command `ctx` are stale, and previously extracted raw objects such as `const sm = ctx.sessionManager` remain the caller's responsibility and must not be reused after the switch.
1101:- Fixed extension session-replacement flows so `ctx.newSession()`, `ctx.fork()`, `ctx.switchSession()`, and imported-session replacements fully rebind before post-switch work runs, added `withSession` replacement callbacks with fresh `ReplacedSessionContext` helpers, and make stale pre-replacement `pi` / `ctx` session-bound accesses throw instead of silently targeting the wrong session ([#2860](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/2860))
1134:- `/clone` duplicates the current active branch into a new session, while extensions can choose whether to fork `before` or `at` an entry via `ctx.fork(..., { position })`. See [README.md](README.md), [docs/extensions.md](docs/extensions.md), and [docs/session.md](docs/session.md).
1146:- Added `/clone` to duplicate the current active branch into a new session, while keeping `/fork` focused on forking from a previous user message ([#2962](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/2962))
1147:- Added `ctx.fork()` support for `position: "before" | "at"` so extensions and integrations can branch before a user message or duplicate the current point in the conversation; the interactive clone/fork UX builds on that runtime support ([#3431](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/3431) by [@mitsuhiko](https://github.com/mitsuhiko))
1150:- Added `reason` and `targetSessionFile` metadata to `session_shutdown` extension events, so extensions can distinguish quit, reload, new-session, resume, and fork teardown paths ([#2863](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/2863))
1423:- **Session runtime API**: `createAgentSessionRuntime()` and `AgentSessionRuntime` provide a closure-based runtime that recreates cwd-bound services and session config on every session switch. Startup, `/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, and import all use the same creation path. See [docs/sdk.md](docs/sdk.md) and [examples/sdk/13-session-runtime.ts](examples/sdk/13-session-runtime.ts).
1424:- **Label timestamps in `/tree`**: Toggle timestamps on tree entries with `Shift+T`, with smart date formatting and timestamp preservation through branching ([#2691](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/2691) by [@w-winter](https://github.com/w-winter))
1430:- Removed extension post-transition events `session_switch` and `session_fork`. Use `session_start` with `event.reason` (`"startup" | "reload" | "new" | "resume" | "fork"`). For `"new"`, `"resume"`, and `"fork"`, `session_start` includes `previousSessionFile`.
1431:- Removed session-replacement methods from `AgentSession`. Use `AgentSessionRuntime` for `newSession()`, `switchSession()`, `fork()`, and `importFromJsonl()`. Cross-cwd session replacement rebuilds all cwd-bound runtime state and replaces the live `AgentSession` instance.
1441:pi.on("session_fork", async (_event, ctx) => { ... });
```

```text
// hasRenderableContent reports whether a message would produce visible output:
// a tool use, or a text/thinking part with non-whitespace text. Only the part
// types that renderContentParts actually emits are counted, so "renderable" here
// stays in lock-step with what gets written — a stray part of any other type
// can't trick us into emitting a bare role header. PathHints are deliberately
// excluded: renderMessage never emits them, so a pathHints-only message has no
// body. Messages with nothing renderable are skipped.
func hasRenderableContent(msg Message) bool {
	if msg.Tool != nil {
		return true
	}
	for _, part := range msg.Content {
		switch part.Type {
		case schema.ContentTypeText, schema.ContentTypeThinking:
			if strings.TrimSpace(part.Text) != "" {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}
```

```text
		// Mirror the markdown write into the restore index (agent we resumed INTO).
		liveIndex.Record(plan.toID, sess)
		provenance.ProcessEvents(ctx, provenanceEngine, sess)

	slog.Info("Launching resume", "provider", plan.to.Name(), "resumeSessionID", resumeSessionID)
```

File: specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/agent_session.go line 417
Description: deriveSlug walks data.Exchanges, which are built from the compaction-trimmed leaf path (ParseSession -> leafPathEntries -> applyCompaction), so after a compaction the slug comes from the first KEPT user message. But scanPiSession (provider.go:369) reads the file top-down in FILE order and takes the first user text it finds — which is the original pre-compaction prompt (or a prompt on an abandoned /tree branch). For any compacted or branched session the two paths yield different Slug/Name for the same session: sync writes the markdown file as `<timestamp>-<parseSlug>.md` (session/session.go:64 uses AgentChatSession.Slug from deriveSlug), while `specstory list` (ListAgentChatSessions) and reindex's buildSession (reindex.go:559 uses ref.Slug from the scan) show the scan slug; the LiveIndexer path (reindex.go:519) writes the parse slug, so the index row's slug even flips between reindex and live-sync updates. claudecode/codexcli never trim history, so their scan and parse slugs always agree. Reproducible with the PR's own testdata/real_world.jsonl: scan yields 'Read README.md and NOTES.md...' while parse yields 'summarize it now...'.
Evidence: agent_session.go:417-431 deriveSlug iterates post-trim data.Exchanges; provider.go:387-399 scanPiSession scans raw file lines and stops at the first user text (`if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" { ... return errStopRead }`) with no leaf-path/compaction awareness; format_test.go TestFormatEntries_RealWorldCompactionAndBashExecution proves the pre-compaction prompt is absent from exchanges while it is the first user line in the file; cmd/reindex.go:519 `Slug: sess.Slug` (full parse) vs :559 `Slug: ref.Slug` (scan).

Context you must honor: claudecode/codexcli are the accepted bar; LOC limits, RawData double-read, and unsupported run/watch/reconstruct stubs are out of scope by owner decision. go test/vet/lint pass on this branch. Default to isReal=false if uncertain or if the issue is cosmetic beyond its stated severity. Return your verdict via the schema; explanation must cite what you actually read.

```text
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)

128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {

175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
```

```text
351	// piSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one bounded
352	// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan
353	// stops as soon as it has the first user message, so it does NOT parse the whole
354	// session. foundUser is false for sessions with no real user prompt; scanPiSession
355	// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
356	type piSessionScan struct {
357		sessionID        string
358		timestamp        string
359		firstUserMessage string
360		cwd              string
361		foundUser        bool
362	}
363	
364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}

411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {

415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),

421			NativePath: path,
```

```text
func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
	out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
	if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
		var details any
		if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {
			out["details"] = details
		}
	}
	return out
}

// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map
// to InputTokens/OutputTokens; cacheRead/cacheWrite map to the Claude-style
// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics).
func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
	if u == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return &schema.Usage{
		InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
		OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
		CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
		CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
	}
}
```

```text
50	// processSession filters warmup messages and converts a Session to an AgentChatSession
51	// Returns nil if the session is warmup-only (no real messages)
52	func processSession(session Session, workspaceRoot string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
53		// Write debug files first (even for warmup-only sessions)
54		if debugRaw {
55			// Write debug files and get the record-to-file mapping
56			_ = writeDebugRawFiles(session) // Unused but needed for side effect
57		}
58	
59		// Filter warmup messages
60		filteredRecords := filterWarmupMessages(session.Records)
61	
62		// Skip if no real messages remain after filtering warmup
63		if len(filteredRecords) == 0 {
64			slog.Debug("Skipping warmup-only session", "sessionId", session.SessionUuid)
65			return nil
66		}
67	
68		// Create session with filtered records
69		filteredSession := Session{
70			SessionUuid: session.SessionUuid,
71			Records:     filteredRecords,
72		}
73	
74		// Get timestamp from root record
75		rootRecord := filteredSession.Records[0]
76		timestamp := rootRecord.Data["timestamp"].(string)
77	
78		// Get the slug
79		slug := FileSlugFromRootRecord(filteredSession)
80	
81		// Generate SessionData from filtered session
82		sessionData, err := GenerateAgentSession(filteredSession, workspaceRoot)
83		if err != nil {
84			slog.Error("Failed to generate SessionData", "sessionId", session.SessionUuid, "error", err)
85			return nil
86		}
87	
88		// Convert session records to JSONL format for raw data
89		// Note: Uses unfiltered session.Records (not filteredSession.Records) to preserve
90		// all records including warmup messages in the raw data for complete audit trail
91		var rawDataBuilder strings.Builder
92		for _, record := range session.Records {
93			jsonBytes, _ := json.Marshal(record.Data)
94			rawDataBuilder.Write(jsonBytes)
95			rawDataBuilder.WriteString("\n")
96		}
97	
98		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
99			SessionID:   session.SessionUuid,
100			CreatedAt:   timestamp, // ISO 8601 timestamp
101			Slug:        slug,
102			SessionData: sessionData,
103			RawData:     rawDataBuilder.String(),
104		}
105	}
```

```text
	ClientName    string `json:"clientName"`

	SessionsUpdated   int32    // Existed but needed update
	SessionsCreated   int32    // New sessions created
	SessionsErrored   int32    // Failed with non-2xx response
```

```text
// Prefers the Title field if available, otherwise uses the first user message
func generateDroidSessionName(session *fdSession) string {
	// Use title if available (already human-readable)
	if title := strings.TrimSpace(session.Title); title != "" {
		// Apply the same length limit as other providers for consistency
		return spi.GenerateReadableName(title)
	}

	// Fall back to first user message
	for _, block := range session.Blocks {
		if block.Role == "user" {
			text := strings.TrimSpace(block.Text)
			if text != "" {
				return spi.GenerateReadableName(text)
			}
		}
```

```text
262	// so `specstory reindex` uses the O(N) path-keyed fast path instead of the
263	// O(N²) by-id lookup.
```

```text
763	func extractCommandName(content string) string {
764		if c := between(content, "<command-name>", "</command-name>"); c != "" {
765			return c
766		}
767		if c := between(content, "<command-message>", "</command-message>"); c != "" {
768			return "/" + c
769		}
770		return ""
771	}
772	
773	// between returns the text between the first open/close markers, trimmed, or "".
774	func between(s, openTag, closeTag string) string {
775		_, after, ok := strings.Cut(s, openTag)
776		if !ok {
777			return ""
778		}
779		inner, _, ok := strings.Cut(after, closeTag)
780		if !ok {
781			return ""
782		}
783		return strings.TrimSpace(inner)
784	}
785	
786	// extractSessionMetadata reads minimal data from a session file to extract metadata
787	// Returns nil if the session is warmup-only (no real messages)
788	func extractSessionMetadata(filePath string) (*spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
789		scan, err := scanClaudeSession(filePath)
790		if err != nil {
791			return nil, err
792		}
793	
794		// If no real message was found, this is a warmup-only session
795		if !scan.foundRealMessage {
796			return nil, nil
797		}
798	
799		return &spi.SessionMetadata{
800			SessionID: scan.sessionID,
801			CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
802			Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
803			Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
804		}, nil
805	}

817	// irrelevant (reindex dedups and sorts later). Implements spi.ProgressEnumerator. See
818	// docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
819	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
820		projectsDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectsDir()

823			return []spi.GlobalSessionRef{}, nil

826		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(projectsDir, "claude", r, func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {

828			if scanErr != nil {
829				return nil, scanErr

831			if !scan.foundRealMessage {

835				SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
836				CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
837				Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
838				Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
839				NativePath: path,
```

```text
107	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path
```

```text
109	// when a compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId
110	// are dropped from the conversation (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
112		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		if header == nil {
117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
118		}
119		if header.Type != entrySession {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
121		}
122		if header.ID == "" {
123			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
124		}
125		if len(entries) == 0 {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
127		}
128		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
129		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
130	}

132	// piProviderVersion derives the provider version string recorded on SessionData
133	// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
134	// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
135	func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
136		if header.Version > 0 {
137			return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
138		}
139		return "v1"
140	}

142	// buildSessionData maps the ordered leaf-path entries into schema.SessionData.
143	func buildSessionData(header *sessionHeader, ordered []rawEntry) *schema.SessionData {
144		return &schema.SessionData{
145			SchemaVersion: "1.0",
146			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{
147				ID:      providerID,
148				Name:    providerName,
149				Version: piProviderVersion(header),
150			},
151			SessionID:     header.ID,
152			CreatedAt:     header.Timestamp,
153			WorkspaceRoot: header.Cwd,
154			Exchanges:     buildExchanges(ordered),
155		}
156	}

158	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
159	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
160	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo. Control entries
161	// (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the conversation body.
162	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
163		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
164		var current *schema.Exchange
165		commit := func() {
166			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
167				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
168			}
169		}
170		for _, e := range ordered {
171			if e.Type != entryMessage {
172				continue
173			}
174			switch messageRole(e) {
175			case roleUser:
176				commit()
177				current = &schema.Exchange{
178					ExchangeID: e.ID,
179					StartTime:  e.Timestamp,
180					EndTime:    e.Timestamp,
181					Messages:   []schema.Message{buildUserMessage(e)},
182				}
183			case roleAssistant:
184				current = appendAssistant(current, e)
185			case roleToolResult:
186				mergeToolResult(current, e)
187			}
188		}
189		commit()
190		return exchanges
191	}

196		if current == nil {
197			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
198		}
199		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, buildAgentMessages(e)...)
200		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
201		return current
202	}

213	// mergeToolResult folds a toolResult entry into the matching agent ToolInfo in
214	// the current exchange, keyed by toolCallId == ToolInfo.UseID. It also advances
215	// the exchange EndTime to the toolResult's timestamp so downstream stats that
216	// read the last exchange's EndTime report the real final-event time.
217	func mergeToolResult(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) {
218		if current == nil {
219			return
220		}
221		var tr toolResultMessage
222		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &tr); err != nil {
223			return
224		}
225		content := toolResultContent(tr)
226		for i := range current.Messages {
227			msg := &current.Messages[i]
228			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.UseID == tr.ToolCallID {
229				msg.Tool.Output = buildToolOutput(content, tr)
230				msg.Timestamp = e.Timestamp
231				current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
232				return
233			}
234		}
235	}

237	// toolResultContent joins the text blocks of a toolResult message.
238	func toolResultContent(tr toolResultMessage) string {
239		var parts []string
240		for _, b := range tr.Content {
241			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
242				parts = append(parts, b.Text)
243			}
244		}
245		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
246	}
247	
248	// buildUserMessage maps a pi user message entry to a schema user Message.
249	// pi user content is either a plain string or an array of {type:text|image}.
250	func buildUserMessage(e rawEntry) schema.Message {
251		var um userMessage
252		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &um)
253		parts := userContentParts(um.Content)
254		return schema.Message{
255			ID:        e.ID,
256			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
257			Role:      schema.RoleUser,
258			Content:   parts,
259		}
260	}
261	
262	// userContentParts decodes a pi user message's content (string or array) into
263	// schema ContentParts. Image blocks are dropped in v1 (recorded as a gap).
264	func userContentParts(raw json.RawMessage) []schema.ContentPart {
265		if len(raw) == 0 {
266			return nil
267		}
268		if raw[0] == '"' {
269			var s string
270			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
271				return []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: s}}
272			}
273		}
274		var blocks []contentBlock
275		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
276			return nil
277		}
278		var parts []schema.ContentPart
279		for _, b := range blocks {
280			if b.Type == schema.ContentTypeText && b.Text != "" {
281				parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
282			}
283		}
284		return parts
285	}
286	
287	// buildAgentMessages maps a pi assistant message entry to one or more schema
288	// Messages: one Message holds the text+thinking content parts; each toolCall
289	// block becomes its own agent Message carrying a ToolInfo.
290	func buildAgentMessages(e rawEntry) []schema.Message {
291		var am assistantMessage
292		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &am); err != nil {
293			return nil
294		}
295		var parts []schema.ContentPart
296		var messages []schema.Message
297		for _, b := range am.Content {
298			switch b.Type {
299			case schema.ContentTypeText:
300				if b.Text != "" {
301					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
302				}
303			case schema.ContentTypeThinking:
304				if b.Thinking != "" {
305					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: b.Thinking})
306				}
307			case "toolCall":
308				messages = append(messages, buildToolMessage(e, b, am))
309			}
310		}
311		if len(parts) > 0 {
312			head := schema.Message{
313				ID:        e.ID,
314				Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
315				Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
316				Model:     am.Model,
317				Content:   parts,
318				Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
319			}
320			return append([]schema.Message{head}, messages...)
321		}
322		if len(messages) == 0 {
323			return buildErrorMessage(e, am)
324		}
325		// Tool-call-only assistant message: carry model+usage once on the first
326		// tool message so no metadata is lost and no schema-invalid empty message
327		// is emitted.
328		messages[0].Model = am.Model
329		if messages[0].Usage == nil {
330			messages[0].Usage = mapUsage(am.Usage)
331		}
332		return messages
333	}
334	
335	// buildToolMessage builds an agent Message wrapping a ToolInfo from a toolCall.
336	// The parent assistant message's model is passed through so tool messages carry
337	// the same model metadata as text/thinking messages. The Message ID is derived
338	// from the parent entry id + the toolCall id, so multiple toolCalls in one
339	// assistant message get distinct Message IDs (downstream provenance keys use
340	// msg.ID as a deterministic component).
341	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
342		return schema.Message{
343			ID:        toolMessageID(e.ID, b.ID),
344			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
345			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
346			Model:     am.Model,
347			Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{
348				Name:  b.Name,
349				Type:  classifyToolType(b.Name),
350				UseID: b.ID,
351				Input: b.Args,
352			},
353		}
354	}
355	
356	// toolMessageID builds a unique Message ID for a tool-call message from the
357	// parent entry id and the toolCall id. This avoids duplicate Message IDs when a
358	// single assistant entry contains multiple toolCall blocks.
359	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {
360		if callID != "" {
361			return entryID + ":" + callID
362		}
363		return entryID
364	}
365	
366	// buildToolOutput constructs the ToolInfo.Output map from a toolResult's
367	// content, error flag, and optional details blob. details (e.g. exitCode) is
368	// decoded into a generic value so downstream consumers (markdown rendering,
369	// cloud) can surface structured tool metadata without re-parsing raw JSON.
370	func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
371		out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
372		if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
373			var details any
374			if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {
375				out["details"] = details
376			}
377		}
378		return out
379	}
380	
381	// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map
382	// to InputTokens/OutputTokens; cacheRead/cacheWrite map to the Claude-style
383	// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics).
384	func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
385		if u == nil {
386			return nil
387		}
388		return &schema.Usage{
389			InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
390			OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
391			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
392			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
393		}
394	}
395	
396	// buildErrorMessage surfaces an assistant entry with stopReason=error and an
397	// empty content array (no text/thinking/toolCalls) as an agent text message so
398	// the error event is not dropped from the transcript (and compaction boundaries
399	// stay interpretable). Returns nil if there is no errorMessage to surface.
400	func buildErrorMessage(e rawEntry, am assistantMessage) []schema.Message {
401		if strings.TrimSpace(am.ErrorMessage) == "" {
402			return nil
403		}
404		return []schema.Message{{
405			ID:        e.ID,
406			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
407			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
408			Model:     am.Model,
409			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "[error] " + am.ErrorMessage}},
410			Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
411		}}
412	}
413	
414	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
415	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
416	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
417	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
418		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
419			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
420				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
421					continue
422				}
423				for _, part := range msg.Content {
424					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {
425						return spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(t)
426					}
427				}
428			}
429		}
430		return ""
431	}
432	
433	// classifyToolType maps pi tool names to the schema tool-type taxonomy.
434	func classifyToolType(name string) string {
435		switch strings.ToLower(name) {
436		case "read":
437			return schema.ToolTypeRead
438		case "edit", "write":
439			return schema.ToolTypeWrite
440		case "bash", "ls":
441			return schema.ToolTypeShell
442		case "grep", "find", "web_search", "fetch_content":
443			return schema.ToolTypeSearch
444		case "until_done_set", "until_done_plan", "until_done_task_update",
445			"until_done_progress", "until_done_complete", "until_done_block",
446			"until_done_replan", "until_done_distill":
447			return schema.ToolTypeTask
448		default:
449			return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
450		}
451	}
452	
453	// firstUserText extracts the first user message text from a message entry, if
454	// its role is "user". Returns "" for non-user messages or empty content.
455	func firstUserText(e rawEntry) string {
456		var m struct {
457			Role    string          `json:"role"`
458			Content json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
459		}
460		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m); err != nil {
461			return ""
462		}
463		if m.Role != roleUser {
464			return ""
465		}
466		return userContentString(m.Content)
467	}
468	
469	// userContentString extracts a plain string from a pi user message content
470	// field (either a string or an array of {type:text} blocks). The result is
471	// trimmed so the scan path produces the same Slug/Name as the full-parse path
472	// (deriveSlug trims too).
473	func userContentString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
474		if len(raw) == 0 {
475			return ""
476		}
477		var s string
478		if raw[0] == '"' {
479			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
480				return strings.TrimSpace(s)
481			}
482		}
483		var blocks []contentBlock
484		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
485			return ""
486		}
487		for _, b := range blocks {
488			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
489				return strings.TrimSpace(b.Text)
490			}
491		}
492		return ""
493	}
```

```text
107	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path
108	// branch into the unified schema.SessionData. It honors compaction entries:
109	// when a compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId
110	// are dropped from the conversation (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
112		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		if header == nil {
117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
118		}
119		if header.Type != entrySession {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
121		}
122		if header.ID == "" {
123			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
124		}
125		if len(entries) == 0 {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
127		}
128		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
129		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
```

Evidence: agent_session.go:174-187 `switch messageRole(e) { case roleUser: ... case roleAssistant: ... case roleToolResult: ... }` — no roleBashExecution case; testdata/real_world.jsonl:8 contains a real bashExecution entry with command "ls -la" and full output; format_test.go:142 asserts 'bashExecution content leaked into exchanges (should be skipped)'.

Context you must honor: claudecode/codexcli are the accepted bar; LOC limits, RawData double-read, and unsupported run/watch/reconstruct stubs are out of scope by owner decision. go test/vet/lint pass on this branch. Default to isReal=false if uncertain or if the issue is cosmetic beyond its stated severity. Return your verdict via the schema; explanation must cite what you actually read.
