318	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every pi session across all projects,
319	// each ref carrying its originating cwd (read from the session header).

321		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
322	}
323	
324	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all pi sessions with live scan
325	// progress, using the shared parallel scanner. Each ref carries Slug/Name
326	// derived from the first user message and the originating cwd from the header.
327	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
328		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
329		if err != nil {
330			return nil, err
331		}
332		if _, statErr := os.Stat(root); statErr != nil {
333			if os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
334				return nil, nil
335			}
336			return nil, statErr
337		}
338		scan := func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
339			s, sErr := scanPiSession(path)
340			if sErr != nil {
341				return nil, sErr
342			}
343			if s == nil {
344				return nil, nil // non-session file
345			}
346			return scanToGlobalRef(s, path), nil
347		}
348		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)
349	}
350	
351	// piSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one bounded
352	// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan
353	// stops as soon as it has the first user message, so it does NOT parse the whole
354	// session. foundUser is false for sessions with no real user prompt; scanPiSession
355	// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
356	type piSessionScan struct {
357		sessionID        string
358		timestamp        string
359		firstUserMessage string
360		cwd              string
361		foundUser        bool
362	}
363	
364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
409	
410	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {
414			return nil
415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
420			Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
421			NativePath: path,
422			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
423		}
424	}

3	import (

10	// piSessionsRoot returns ~/.pi/agent/sessions, the directory under which pi
11	// stores one subdirectory per working directory (each named with the encoded
12	// cwd, see EncodeCwd). It does not require the directory to exist.
13	func piSessionsRoot() (string, error) {
14		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
15		if err != nil {
16			return "", fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot resolve home dir: %w", err)
17		}
18		return filepath.Join(home, ".pi", "agent", "sessions"), nil
19	}
20	
21	// EncodeCwd maps a working directory to pi's session-subdirectory name.
22	// pi replaces every '/' in the absolute path with '-' and wraps the result with
23	// a leading '-' and a trailing '--', producing e.g. "/Users/jane/proj" ->
24	// "--Users-jane-proj--". The encoding is derived from real session dirs:
25	// "/Users/jakelevirne" -> "--Users-jakelevirne--" and
26	// "/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory" -> "--Users-jakelevirne-dev-getspecstory--".
27	func EncodeCwd(cwd string) string {
28		encoded := strings.ReplaceAll(cwd, "/", "-")
29		return "-" + encoded + "--"
30	}
31	
32	// ProjectSessionDir returns the absolute path to pi's session subdirectory for
33	// the given project, WITHOUT requiring it to exist. Callers (DetectAgent, sync)
34	// check existence separately. The path is symlink-resolved before encoding so
35	// it matches the directory pi actually wrote to (pi encodes the real cwd); a
36	// relative or symlinked projectPath would otherwise produce a different name.
37	func ProjectSessionDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
38		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
39		if err != nil {
40			return "", err
41		}
42		cwd := strings.TrimSpace(projectPath)
43		if cwd == "" {
44			cwd, err = os.Getwd()
45			if err != nil {
46				return "", fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot get working dir: %w", err)
47			}
48		}
49		realPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cwd)
50		if err != nil {
51			realPath = cwd // fall back to the raw path if resolution fails
52		}
53		return filepath.Join(root, EncodeCwd(realPath)), nil
54	}
55	
56	// SessionFilesInProject lists the *.jsonl files in the project's pi session
57	// directory. Returns an empty slice (no error) if the directory does not exist.
58	func SessionFilesInProject(projectPath string) ([]string, error) {
59		dir, err := ProjectSessionDir(projectPath)
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
64		if err != nil {
65			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
66				return nil, nil
67			}
68			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading session dir %s: %w", dir, err)
69		}
70		var files []string
71		for _, e := range entries {
72			if e.IsDir() {
73				continue
74			}
75			if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".jsonl") {
76				continue
77			}
78			files = append(files, filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
79		}
80		return files, nil
81	}

12	// projectDirNameRegex matches any character that is not alphanumeric or a dash.
13	// Claude Code replaces each such character with a dash to map a working directory
14	// to a project folder name under ~/.claude/projects.
15	var projectDirNameRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9-]`)
16	
17	// encodeProjectDirName converts a real (symlink-resolved) path into Claude Code's
18	// project directory name: non-alphanumeric/dash characters become dashes, with a
19	// guaranteed leading dash. Example: "/Users/sean/app" -> "-Users-sean-app".
20	func encodeProjectDirName(realPath string) string {
21		name := projectDirNameRegex.ReplaceAllString(realPath, "-")
22		if !strings.HasPrefix(name, "-") {
23			name = "-" + name
24		}
25		return name
26	}
27	
28	// resolveClaudeProjectDir returns ~/.claude/projects/<encoded> for the given
29	// project path, resolving symlinks, WITHOUT requiring the directory to exist.
30	// Used when writing a reconstructed session into the store (the caller creates
31	// the directory). Distinct from GetClaudeCodeProjectDir, which requires the
32	// projects directory to already exist.
33	func resolveClaudeProjectDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
34		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
35		if err != nil {
36			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get user home directory: %v", err)
37		}
38	
39		cwd := projectPath
40		if cwd == "" {
41			cwd, err = os.Getwd()
42			if err != nil {
43				return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get current working directory: %v", err)
44			}
45		}
46	
47		// Resolve symlinks to match Claude Code's behavior; fall back to the raw path
48		// if resolution fails (e.g., a path component does not exist yet).
49		realPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cwd)
50		if err != nil {
51			realPath = cwd
52		}
53	
54		return filepath.Join(homeDir, ".claude", "projects", encodeProjectDirName(realPath)), nil
55	}
56	
57	// GetClaudeCodeProjectsDir returns the path to the Claude Code projects directory
58	func GetClaudeCodeProjectsDir() (string, error) {
59		// Get user's home directory
60		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
61		if err != nil {
62			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get user home directory: %v", err)
63		}
64	
65		// Construct the path to .claude/projects
66		projectsDir := filepath.Join(homeDir, ".claude", "projects")
67	
68		// Check if the directory exists
69		if _, err := os.Stat(projectsDir); err != nil {
70			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
71				return "", fmt.Errorf("claude projects directory not found at %s", projectsDir)
72			}
73			return "", fmt.Errorf("error checking Claude projects directory: %v", err)
74		}
75	
76		return projectsDir, nil
77	}
78	
79	// GetClaudeCodeProjectDir returns the Claude Code project directory for the given path.
80	// If no path is provided (empty string), it uses the current working directory.
81	// It resolves any symlinks in the path to match Claude Code's behavior, which uses the real path
82	// when creating project directories. Claude Code requires a specific naming convention to map
83	// working directories to project folders: each non-alphanumeric character is replaced with a dash
84	// to create a unique, filesystem-safe identifier
85	func GetClaudeCodeProjectDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
86		// Use provided path or get current working directory
87		var cwd string
88		var err error
89		if projectPath == "" {
90			cwd, err = os.Getwd()
91			if err != nil {
92				return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get current working directory: %v", err)
93			}
94		} else {
95			cwd = projectPath
96		}
97	
98		// Resolve any symlinks in the path to match Claude Code's behavior
99		// Claude Code uses the real path when creating project directories, so
100		// if the user's working directory contains symlinks, we need to resolve
101		// them to find the correct project directory in ~/.claude/projects/
102		realPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cwd)
103		if err != nil {
104			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve symlinks in working directory: %v", err)
105		}
106	
107		// Log if the path was changed by symlink resolution
108		if realPath != cwd {
109			slog.Debug("GetClaudeCodeProjectDir: Resolved symlinks in working directory",
110				"original", cwd,
111				"resolved", realPath)
112		}
113	
114		// Convert path to project directory format (matching Claude Code's behavior).
115		// Example: "/Users/sean/My Projects(1)/app" becomes "-Users-sean-My-Projects-1--app"
116		projectDirName := encodeProjectDirName(realPath)
117	
118		// Log the transformation for debugging path issues
119		slog.Debug("GetClaudeCodeProjectDir: Transformed working directory to project name",
120			"cwd", cwd,
121			"projectDirName", projectDirName)
122	
123		// Get Claude projects directory
124		projectsDir, err := GetClaudeCodeProjectsDir()
125		if err != nil {
126			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get Claude projects directory: %v", err)
127		}
128	
129		fullProjectPath := filepath.Join(projectsDir, projectDirName)
130		slog.Debug("GetClaudeCodeProjectDir: Constructed full project path",
131			"projectPath", fullProjectPath)
132	
133		return fullProjectPath, nil
134	}

352	// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan
353	// stops as soon as it has the first user message, so it does NOT parse the whole
354	// session. foundUser is false for sessions with no real user prompt; scanPiSession
355	// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
356	type piSessionScan struct {
357		sessionID        string
358		timestamp        string
359		firstUserMessage string
360		cwd              string
361		foundUser        bool
362	}
363	
364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
409	
410	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {
414			return nil
415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
420			Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
421			NativePath: path,
422			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
423		}
424	}

111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {

1	package piagent
2	
3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"log/slog"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"strings"
13	)
14	
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// Skip entries missing the envelope fields the tree walk and exchange
91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}
104	
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
187	
188	// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
189	// if not found.
190	func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
191		for i, e := range path {
192			if e.ID == keptID {
193				return i
194			}
195		}
196		return -1
197	}

51			}

57		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {

59			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())
60			return spi.CheckResult{

62				Location:     resolved,

65		}
66		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
67		if version == "" {
68			version = "unknown"
69		}
70		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
71		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
72	}

1	package utils

3	import (
4		"context"

8		"sync"
9	
10		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"

12	)
13	
14	// WatchAgents starts watchers for all registered providers concurrently.
15	// Convenience wrapper around WatchProviders that resolves the full provider registry.
16	func WatchAgents(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
17		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
18		providers := registry.GetAll()
19	
20		if len(providers) == 0 {
21			return fmt.Errorf("no providers registered")
22		}
23	
24		return WatchProviders(ctx, projectPath, providers, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
25	}
26	
27	// WatchProviders starts watchers for the given providers concurrently.
28	// Calls sessionCallback when any provider detects activity.
29	// Runs until context is cancelled or all watchers stop.
30	// Context cancellation (Ctrl+C) is treated as a clean exit, not an error.
31	//
32	// Parameters:
33	//   - ctx: Context for cancellation and timeout control
34	//   - projectPath: Agent's working directory to watch
35	//   - providers: map of provider ID to provider instance to watch
36	//   - debugRaw: whether to write debug raw data files
37	//   - sessionCallback: called with provider ID and AgentChatSession data on each update
38	//
39	// The callback includes the provider ID to help consumers route/filter sessions.
40	// The callback should not block as it may delay other provider notifications.
41	func WatchProviders(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, providers map[string]spi.Provider, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
42		slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting multi-provider watch", "projectPath", projectPath, "providerCount", len(providers), "debugRaw", debugRaw)
43	
44		// Track last-seen message count per session to suppress duplicate callbacks.
45		// Providers fire callbacks on every JSONL change, but not all changes produce
46		// new messages in the parsed SessionData. Messages are append-only, so a
47		// matching total count means nothing meaningful changed.
48		var mu sync.Mutex
49		lastMsgCount := make(map[string]int)
50	
51		var wg sync.WaitGroup
52		errChan := make(chan error, len(providers))
53	
54		for providerID, provider := range providers {
55			wg.Add(1)
56			go func() {
57				defer wg.Done()
58	
59				slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting watcher for provider", "providerID", providerID, "providerName", provider.Name())
60	
61				// Wrap the callback to deduplicate and include provider ID
62				wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
63					if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
64						return
65					}
66	
67					// Count total messages across all exchanges
68					totalMsgs := 0
69					for _, exchange := range session.SessionData.Exchanges {
70						totalMsgs += len(exchange.Messages)
71					}
72	
73					// Skip if message count hasn't changed for this session
74					mu.Lock()
75					prev, seen := lastMsgCount[session.SessionID]
76					if seen && prev == totalMsgs {
77						mu.Unlock()
78						slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
79							"providerID", providerID,
80							"sessionID", session.SessionID,
81							"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
82						return
83					}
84					lastMsgCount[session.SessionID] = totalMsgs
85					mu.Unlock()
86	
87					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
88						"providerID", providerID,
89						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
90						"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
91	
92					sessionCallback(providerID, session)
93				}
94	
95				err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
96				if err != nil {
97					// Context cancellation is expected when user presses Ctrl+C, not an error
98					if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
99						slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
100						errChan <- nil
101					} else {
102						slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
103						errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
104					}
105				} else {
106					errChan <- nil
107				}
108			}()
109		}
110	
111		// Wait for all watchers to complete (they run until Ctrl+C)
112		wg.Wait()
113	
114		// Drain error channel — errors are already logged in the goroutines with full context
115		for range len(providers) {
116			<-errChan
117		}
118	
119		return nil
120	}
121

381	// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map
382	// to InputTokens/OutputTokens; cacheRead/cacheWrite map to the Claude-style
383	// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics).
384	func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
385		if u == nil {
386			return nil
387		}
388		return &schema.Usage{
389			InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
390			OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
391			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
392			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
393		}
394	}
395	
396	// buildErrorMessage surfaces an assistant entry with stopReason=error and an
397	// empty content array (no text/thinking/toolCalls) as an agent text message so
398	// the error event is not dropped from the transcript (and compaction boundaries
399	// stay interpretable). Returns nil if there is no errorMessage to surface.
400	func buildErrorMessage(e rawEntry, am assistantMessage) []schema.Message {
401		if strings.TrimSpace(am.ErrorMessage) == "" {
402			return nil
403		}
404		return []schema.Message{{
405			ID:        e.ID,
406			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
407			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
408			Model:     am.Model,
409			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "[error] " + am.ErrorMessage}},
410			Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
411		}}
412	}

414	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
415	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
416	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
417	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
418		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
419			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
420				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
421					continue
422				}
423				for _, part := range msg.Content {
424					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {
425						return spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(t)
426					}
427				}
428			}
429		}
430		return ""
431	}
432	
433	// classifyToolType maps pi tool names to the schema tool-type taxonomy.
434	func classifyToolType(name string) string {
435		switch strings.ToLower(name) {
436		case "read":
437			return schema.ToolTypeRead
438		case "edit", "write":
439			return schema.ToolTypeWrite
440		case "bash", "ls":
441			return schema.ToolTypeShell
442		case "grep", "find", "web_search", "fetch_content":
443			return schema.ToolTypeSearch
444		case "until_done_set", "until_done_plan", "until_done_task_update",
445			"until_done_progress", "until_done_complete", "until_done_block",
446			"until_done_replan", "until_done_distill":
447			return schema.ToolTypeTask
448		default:
449			return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
450		}
451	}
452	
453	// firstUserText extracts the first user message text from a message entry, if
454	// its role is "user". Returns "" for non-user messages or empty content.
455	func firstUserText(e rawEntry) string {
456		var m struct {
457			Role    string          `json:"role"`
458			Content json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
459		}
460		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m); err != nil {
461			return ""
462		}
463		if m.Role != roleUser {
464			return ""
465		}
466		return userContentString(m.Content)
467	}
468	
469	// userContentString extracts a plain string from a pi user message content
470	// field (either a string or an array of {type:text} blocks). The result is
471	// trimmed so the scan path produces the same Slug/Name as the full-parse path
472	// (deriveSlug trims too).
473	func userContentString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
474		if len(raw) == 0 {
475			return ""
476		}
477		var s string
478		if raw[0] == '"' {
479			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
480				return strings.TrimSpace(s)
481			}
482		}
483		var blocks []contentBlock
484		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
485			return ""
486		}
487		for _, b := range blocks {
488			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
489				return strings.TrimSpace(b.Text)
490			}
491		}
492		return ""
493	}

	if r == nil {

	}

func ScanSessionsInParallel(root, label string, r *ScanReporter, scan func(path string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error)) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error) {
	// Phase 1: collect file paths (dirents only — no opens).

	workers := min(runtime.NumCPU(), 12)

15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)

25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}

71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}

91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}

106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}

125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}

148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}

156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple

159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction

161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {

164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {

166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {

170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {

174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]

107	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path

111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
112		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err

124		}
125		if len(entries) == 0 {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
127		}
128		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
129		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
130	}

158	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
159	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
160	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo. Control entries
161	// (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the conversation body.
162	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
163		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
164		var current *schema.Exchange
165		commit := func() {
166			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {

27	// Provider implements spi.Provider for the pi coding agent.
28	// pi stores sessions as JSONL v3 trees under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/.
29	type Provider struct{}
30	
31	// NewProvider returns a new pi provider instance.
32	func NewProvider() *Provider { return &Provider{} }

34	// Name returns the human-readable provider name.
35	func (p *Provider) Name() string { return providerName }

37	// Check verifies the pi binary is on PATH and reports its version.
38	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
39		cmdName := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand)
40		isCustom := cmdName != ""
41		if cmdName == "" {
42			cmdName = defaultCmd
43		}
44		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
45		if err != nil {
46			slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
47			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "not_found", err.Error())
48			return spi.CheckResult{
49				Success:      false,
50				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi binary '%s' not found on PATH", cmdName),
51			}
52		}
53		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
54		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
55		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
56		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
57		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
58			slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err)
59			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())
60			return spi.CheckResult{
61				Success:      false,
62				Location:     resolved,
63				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi version probe failed: %v", err),
64			}
65		}
66		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
67		if version == "" {
68			version = "unknown"
69		}
70		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
71		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
72	}

130	// sessionFile pairs a discovered pi session file with its header metadata.
131	type sessionFile struct {
132		Path   string
133		Header sessionHeader
134	}
135	
136	// findProjectSession locates the session file with the given ID within the
137	// project's pi session directory. Returns "" if not found.
138	func findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
139		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
140		if err != nil {
141			return "", err
142		}
143		for _, f := range files {
144			h, err := readHeader(f)
145			if err != nil || h == nil {
146				continue
147			}
148			if h.ID == sessionID {
149				return f, nil
150			}
151		}
152		return "", nil
153	}
154	
155	// readHeader parses only the first line of a session file and returns it only
156	// if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty id).
157	// Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them.
158	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
159		f, err := os.Open(path)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, err
162		}
163		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
164		dec := json.NewDecoder(f)
165		var h sessionHeader
166		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
170			return nil, nil
171		}
172		return &h, nil
173	}
174	
175	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
176	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
177	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
178	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
179		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, err
182		}
183		var out []sessionFile
184		for _, f := range files {
185			h, err := readHeader(f)
186			if err != nil {
187				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
188				continue
189			}
190			if h == nil {
191				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
192			}
193			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}
197	
198	// GetAgentChatSession returns a single pi session by ID for the project.
199	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
200		path, err := findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID)
201		if err != nil {
202			return nil, err
203		}
204		if path == "" {
205			return nil, nil
206		}
207		return parseToAgentSession(path, debugRaw)
208	}
209	
210	// GetAgentChatSessions returns all pi sessions for the project.
211	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
212		files, err := listProjectSessions(projectPath)
213		if err != nil {
214			return nil, err
215		}
216		total := len(files)
217		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
218		for i, sf := range files {
219			chat, pErr := parseToAgentSession(sf.Path, debugRaw)
220			if pErr != nil {
221				slog.Debug("pi: skipping session", "path", sf.Path, "error", pErr)
222			} else if chat != nil {
223				result = append(result, *chat)
224			}
225			if progress != nil {
226				progress(i+1, total)
227			}
228		}
229		return result, nil
230	}

232	// parseToAgentSession parses one session file into an AgentChatSession,
233	// writing debug-raw artifacts when debugRaw is true.
234	func parseToAgentSession(path string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
235		data, err := ParseSession(path)
236		if err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239		if debugRaw {
240			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(path, data); dErr != nil {
241				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
242			}
243		}
244		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
245		if err != nil {
246			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
247		}
248		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
249			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
250			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
251			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
252			SessionData: data,
253			RawData:     string(raw),
254		}, nil
255	}
256	
257	// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single pi session directly from its native
258	// file path, skipping the by-id discovery search. originCwd is the session's
259	// originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd), passed through
260	// as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
261	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath. Implements spi.PathSessionReader
262	// so `specstory reindex` uses the O(N) path-keyed fast path instead of the
263	// O(N²) by-id lookup.
264	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
265		data, err := ParseSession(nativePath)
266		if err != nil {
267			return nil, err
268		}
269		if data.WorkspaceRoot == "" && originCwd != "" {
270			data.WorkspaceRoot = originCwd
271		}
272		if debugRaw {
273			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(nativePath, data); dErr != nil {
274				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
275			}
276		}
277		raw, err := os.ReadFile(nativePath)
278		if err != nil {
279			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
280		}
281		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
282			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
283			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
284			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
285			SessionData: data,
286			RawData:     string(raw),
287		}, nil
288	}
289	
290	// ListAgentChatSessions returns lightweight metadata for all project sessions,
291	// deriving Slug/Name from the first user message via a bounded single-pass scan
292	// (no full parse), matching how other providers populate metadata.
293	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
294		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
295		if err != nil {
296			return nil, err
297		}
298		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
299		for _, f := range files {
300			scan, scanErr := scanPiSession(f)
301			if scanErr != nil {
302				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", scanErr)
303				continue
304			}
305			if scan == nil || !scan.foundUser {
306				continue
307			}
308			result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
309				SessionID: scan.sessionID,
310				CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
311				Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
312				Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
313			})
314		}
315		return result, nil
316	}
317	
318	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every pi session across all projects,
319	// each ref carrying its originating cwd (read from the session header).
320	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
321		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
322	}
323	
324	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all pi sessions with live scan
325	// progress, using the shared parallel scanner. Each ref carries Slug/Name
326	// derived from the first user message and the originating cwd from the header.
327	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
328		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
329		if err != nil {
330			return nil, err
331		}
332		if _, statErr := os.Stat(root); statErr != nil {
333			if os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
334				return nil, nil
335			}
336			return nil, statErr
337		}
338		scan := func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
339			s, sErr := scanPiSession(path)
340			if sErr != nil {
341				return nil, sErr
342			}
343			if s == nil {
344				return nil, nil // non-session file
345			}
346			return scanToGlobalRef(s, path), nil
347		}
348		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)
349	}
350	
351	// piSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one bounded
352	// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan
353	// stops as soon as it has the first user message, so it does NOT parse the whole
354	// session. foundUser is false for sessions with no real user prompt; scanPiSession
355	// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
356	type piSessionScan struct {
357		sessionID        string
358		timestamp        string
359		firstUserMessage string
360		cwd              string
361		foundUser        bool
362	}
363	
364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
409	
410	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {
414			return nil
415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
420			Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
421			NativePath: path,
422			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
423		}
424	}
425

1	package utils
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"log/slog"
8		"sync"
9	
10		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
11		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/factory"
12	)
13	
14	// WatchAgents starts watchers for all registered providers concurrently.
15	// Convenience wrapper around WatchProviders that resolves the full provider registry.
16	func WatchAgents(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
17		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
18		providers := registry.GetAll()
19	
20		if len(providers) == 0 {
21			return fmt.Errorf("no providers registered")
22		}
23	
24		return WatchProviders(ctx, projectPath, providers, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
25	}
26	
27	// WatchProviders starts watchers for the given providers concurrently.
28	// Calls sessionCallback when any provider detects activity.
29	// Runs until context is cancelled or all watchers stop.
30	// Context cancellation (Ctrl+C) is treated as a clean exit, not an error.
31	//
32	// Parameters:
33	//   - ctx: Context for cancellation and timeout control
34	//   - projectPath: Agent's working directory to watch
35	//   - providers: map of provider ID to provider instance to watch
36	//   - debugRaw: whether to write debug raw data files
37	//   - sessionCallback: called with provider ID and AgentChatSession data on each update
38	//
39	// The callback includes the provider ID to help consumers route/filter sessions.
40	// The callback should not block as it may delay other provider notifications.
41	func WatchProviders(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, providers map[string]spi.Provider, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
42		slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting multi-provider watch", "projectPath", projectPath, "providerCount", len(providers), "debugRaw", debugRaw)
43	
44		// Track last-seen message count per session to suppress duplicate callbacks.
45		// Providers fire callbacks on every JSONL change, but not all changes produce
46		// new messages in the parsed SessionData. Messages are append-only, so a
47		// matching total count means nothing meaningful changed.
48		var mu sync.Mutex
49		lastMsgCount := make(map[string]int)
50	
51		var wg sync.WaitGroup
52		errChan := make(chan error, len(providers))
53	
54		for providerID, provider := range providers {
55			wg.Add(1)
56			go func() {
57				defer wg.Done()
58	
59				slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting watcher for provider", "providerID", providerID, "providerName", provider.Name())
60	
61				// Wrap the callback to deduplicate and include provider ID
62				wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
63					if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
64						return
65					}
66	
67					// Count total messages across all exchanges
68					totalMsgs := 0
69					for _, exchange := range session.SessionData.Exchanges {
70						totalMsgs += len(exchange.Messages)
71					}
72	
73					// Skip if message count hasn't changed for this session
74					mu.Lock()
75					prev, seen := lastMsgCount[session.SessionID]
76					if seen && prev == totalMsgs {
77						mu.Unlock()
78						slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
79							"providerID", providerID,
80							"sessionID", session.SessionID,
81							"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
82						return
83					}
84					lastMsgCount[session.SessionID] = totalMsgs
85					mu.Unlock()
86	
87					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
88						"providerID", providerID,
89						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
90						"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
91	
92					sessionCallback(providerID, session)
93				}
94	
95				err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
96				if err != nil {
97					// Context cancellation is expected when user presses Ctrl+C, not an error
98					if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
99						slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
100						errChan <- nil
101					} else {
102						slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
103						errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
104					}
105				} else {
106					errChan <- nil
107				}
108			}()
109		}
110	
111		// Wait for all watchers to complete (they run until Ctrl+C)
112		wg.Wait()
113	
114		// Drain error channel — errors are already logged in the goroutines with full context
115		for range len(providers) {
116			<-errChan
117		}
118	
119		return nil
120	}
121
```

136	// findProjectSession locates the session file with the given ID within the
137	// project's pi session directory. Returns "" if not found.
138	func findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
139		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
140		if err != nil {
141			return "", err
142		}
143		for _, f := range files {
144			h, err := readHeader(f)
145			if err != nil || h == nil {
146				continue
147			}
148			if h.ID == sessionID {
149				return f, nil
150			}
151		}
152		return "", nil
153	}
154	
155	// readHeader parses only the first line of a session file and returns it only
156	// if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty id).
157	// Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them.
158	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
159		f, err := os.Open(path)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, err
162		}
163		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
164		dec := json.NewDecoder(f)
165		var h sessionHeader
166		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
170			return nil, nil
171		}
172		return &h, nil
173	}
174	
175	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
176	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
177	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
178	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
179		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, err
182		}
183		var out []sessionFile
184		for _, f := range files {
185			h, err := readHeader(f)
186			if err != nil {
187				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
188				continue
189			}
190			if h == nil {
191				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
192			}
193			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}

20		if len(providers) == 0 {
21			return fmt.Errorf("no providers registered")
22		}
23	
24		return WatchProviders(ctx, projectPath, providers, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
25	}
26	
27	// WatchProviders starts watchers for the given providers concurrently.
28	// Calls sessionCallback when any provider detects activity.
29	// Runs until context is cancelled or all watchers stop.
30	// Context cancellation (Ctrl+C) is treated as a clean exit, not an error.
31	//
32	// Parameters:
33	//   - ctx: Context for cancellation and timeout control
34	//   - projectPath: Agent's working directory to watch
35	//   - providers: map of provider ID to provider instance to watch
36	//   - debugRaw: whether to write debug raw data files
37	//   - sessionCallback: called with provider ID and AgentChatSession data on each update
38	//
39	// The callback includes the provider ID to help consumers route/filter sessions.
40	// The callback should not block as it may delay other provider notifications.
41	func WatchProviders(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, providers map[string]spi.Provider, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
42		slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting multi-provider watch", "projectPath", projectPath, "providerCount", len(providers), "debugRaw", debugRaw)
43	
44		// Track last-seen message count per session to suppress duplicate callbacks.
45		// Providers fire callbacks on every JSONL change, but not all changes produce
46		// new messages in the parsed SessionData. Messages are append-only, so a
47		// matching total count means nothing meaningful changed.
48		var mu sync.Mutex
49		lastMsgCount := make(map[string]int)
50	
51		var wg sync.WaitGroup
52		errChan := make(chan error, len(providers))
53	
54		for providerID, provider := range providers {
55			wg.Add(1)
56			go func() {
57				defer wg.Done()
58	
59				slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting watcher for provider", "providerID", providerID, "providerName", provider.Name())
60	
61				// Wrap the callback to deduplicate and include provider ID
62				wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
63					if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
64						return
65					}
66	
67					// Count total messages across all exchanges
68					totalMsgs := 0
69					for _, exchange := range session.SessionData.Exchanges {
70						totalMsgs += len(exchange.Messages)
71					}
72	
73					// Skip if message count hasn't changed for this session
74					mu.Lock()
75					prev, seen := lastMsgCount[session.SessionID]
76					if seen && prev == totalMsgs {
77						mu.Unlock()
78						slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
79							"providerID", providerID,
80							"sessionID", session.SessionID,
81							"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
82						return
83					}
84					lastMsgCount[session.SessionID] = totalMsgs
85					mu.Unlock()
86	
87					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
88						"providerID", providerID,
89						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
90						"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
91	
92					sessionCallback(providerID, session)
93				}
94	
95				err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
96				if err != nil {
97					// Context cancellation is expected when user presses Ctrl+C, not an error
98					if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
99						slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
100						errChan <- nil
101					} else {
102						slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
103						errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
104					}
105				} else {
106					errChan <- nil
107				}
108			}()
109		}
110	
111		// Wait for all watchers to complete (they run until Ctrl+C)
112		wg.Wait()
113	
114		// Drain error channel — errors are already logged in the goroutines with full context
115		for range len(providers) {
116			<-errChan
117		}
118	
119		return nil
120	}
121
```

// sessionMarkdown returns the session as markdown for the preview — the real specstory
// render when the session can be re-parsed (needs a cwd), else the plain FTS body.
func sessionMarkdown(registry *factory.Registry, store *sessionindex.Store, s *sessionindex.Session) string {
	if s.OriginCwd != "" {
		if prov, err := registry.Get(s.Agent); err == nil {
			if full, err := prov.GetAgentChatSession(s.OriginCwd, s.SessionID, false); err == nil &&
				full != nil && full.SessionData != nil {
				if md, err := session.GenerateMarkdownFromAgentSession(full.SessionData, false, true); err == nil {
					return md
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if body, _ := store.SessionBody(s.Agent, s.SessionID); strings.TrimSpace(body) != "" {
		return "```\n" + body + "\n```"
	}
	return "_(no readable content for this session)_"
}

57		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {

141			return "", err
142		}
143		for _, f := range files {
144			h, err := readHeader(f)
145			if err != nil || h == nil {
146				continue
147			}
148			if h.ID == sessionID {
149				return f, nil
150			}
151		}
152		return "", nil
153	}
154	
155	// readHeader parses only the first line of a session file and returns it only
156	// if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty id).
157	// Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them.
158	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
159		f, err := os.Open(path)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, err
162		}
163		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
164		dec := json.NewDecoder(f)
165		var h sessionHeader
166		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
170			return nil, nil
171		}
172		return &h, nil
173	}
174	
175	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
176	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
177	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
178	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
179		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, err
182		}
183		var out []sessionFile
184		for _, f := range files {
185			h, err := readHeader(f)
186			if err != nil {
187				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
188				continue
189			}
190			if h == nil {
191				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
192			}
193			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}
197	
198	// GetAgentChatSession returns a single pi session by ID for the project.
199	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
200		path, err := findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID)
201		if err != nil {
202			return nil, err
203		}
204		if path == "" {
205			return nil, nil
206		}
207		return parseToAgentSession(path, debugRaw)
208	}
209	
210	// GetAgentChatSessions returns all pi sessions for the project.
211	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
212		files, err := listProjectSessions(projectPath)
213		if err != nil {
214			return nil, err
215		}
216		total := len(files)
217		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
218		for i, sf := range files {
219			chat, pErr := parseToAgentSession(sf.Path, debugRaw)
220			if pErr != nil {
221				slog.Debug("pi: skipping session", "path", sf.Path, "error", pErr)
222			} else if chat != nil {
223				result = append(result, *chat)
224			}
225			if progress != nil {
226				progress(i+1, total)
227			}
228		}
229		return result, nil
230	}
231	
232	// parseToAgentSession parses one session file into an AgentChatSession,
233	// writing debug-raw artifacts when debugRaw is true.
234	func parseToAgentSession(path string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
235		data, err := ParseSession(path)
236		if err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239		if debugRaw {
240			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(path, data); dErr != nil {
241				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
242			}
243		}
244		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
245		if err != nil {
246			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
247		}
248		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
249			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
250			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
251			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
252			SessionData: data,
253			RawData:     string(raw),
254		}, nil
255	}
256	
257	// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single pi session directly from its native
258	// file path, skipping the by-id discovery search. originCwd is the session's
259	// originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd), passed through
260	// as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
261	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath. Implements spi.PathSessionReader
262	// so `specstory reindex` uses the O(N) path-keyed fast path instead of the
263	// O(N²) by-id lookup.
264	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
265		data, err := ParseSession(nativePath)
266		if err != nil {
267			return nil, err
268		}
269		if data.WorkspaceRoot == "" && originCwd != "" {
270			data.WorkspaceRoot = originCwd
271		}
272		if debugRaw {
273			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(nativePath, data); dErr != nil {
274				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
275			}
276		}
277		raw, err := os.ReadFile(nativePath)
278		if err != nil {
279			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
280		}
281		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
282			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
283			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
284			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
285			SessionData: data,
286			RawData:     string(raw),
287		}, nil
288	}

312				Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
313			})
314		}
315		return result, nil
316	}

// parseFullSession reads a session's full data for indexing. It prefers a provider's
// path-keyed parse (spi.PathSessionReader) using the ref's already-known NativePath, which
// avoids the provider's by-id discovery search — for Codex that search walks the entire
// ~/.codex/sessions tree, so this is the difference between an O(N) and an O(N²) reindex.
// Providers without the capability (or refs lacking a NativePath) fall back to the by-id
// lookup. Parsing the known NativePath is also more consistent: the row's freshness
// fingerprint is stat'd from NativePath, so the body now comes from that same file.
func parseFullSession(prov spi.Provider, ref spi.GlobalSessionRef) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
	if pr, ok := prov.(spi.PathSessionReader); ok && ref.NativePath != "" {
		return pr.GetAgentChatSessionByPath(ref.NativePath, ref.OriginCwd, false)
	}
	return prov.GetAgentChatSession(ref.OriginCwd, ref.SessionID, false)
}

// drainToStore writes parsed sessions to the index in batched transactions.
func drainToStore(store *sessionindex.Store, ch <-chan sessionindex.Session) error {
	batch := make([]sessionindex.Session, 0, reindexWriteBatch)
	flush := func() error {
		if err := store.UpsertBatch(batch); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		batch = batch[:0]
		return nil
	}
	for sess := range ch {
		batch = append(batch, sess)
		if len(batch) >= reindexWriteBatch {
			if err := flush(); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
```

import json

entries = []
header = None
with open(path) as f:
    for i, line in enumerate(f):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        obj = json.loads(line)
        if header is None:
            header = obj
            continue
        entries.append(obj)

print("header id:", header.get("id"))
print("num entries:", len(entries))

def usertext(e):
    m = e.get("message") or {}
    if m.get("role") != "user":
        return None
    c = m.get("content")
    if isinstance(c, str):
        return c.strip()
    if isinstance(c, list):
        for b in c:
            if b.get("type") == "text" and b.get("text"):
                return b["text"].strip()
    return None

# file-order first user message (scan path)
for e in entries:
    if e.get("type") == "message":
        t = usertext(e)
        if t:
            print("SCAN first user (file order):", repr(t[:80]))
            break

# leaf path walk (full parse)
by_id = {e["id"]: e for e in entries if e.get("id")}
leaf = entries[-1]
path_entries = []
cur = leaf
visited = set()
while cur["id"] not in visited:
    visited.add(cur["id"])
    path_entries.append(cur)
    pid = cur.get("parentId")
    if pid is None or pid not in by_id:
        break
    cur = by_id[pid]
path_entries.reverse()

# apply compaction: last compaction on path
last = -1
for i, e in enumerate(path_entries):
    if e.get("type") == "compaction":
        last = i
print("compaction entries on leaf path at index:", last, "of", len(path_entries))
if last >= 0:
    kept = path_entries[last].get("firstKeptEntryId", "")
    print("firstKeptEntryId:", kept)
    idx = next((i for i, e in enumerate(path_entries) if e["id"] == kept), -1)
    if kept and idx >= 0:
        trimmed = path_entries[idx:]
    else:
        trimmed = path_entries[last:]
else:
    trimmed = path_entries

# full-parse first user message on trimmed path
for e in trimmed:
    if e.get("type") == "message":
        t = usertext(e)
        if t:
            print("FULL-PARSE first user (trimmed leaf path):", repr(t[:80]))
            break

# also show all user messages in file order for context
print("\nall user messages in file order:")
for e in entries:
    if e.get("type") == "message":
        t = usertext(e)
        if t:
            print("  ", e["id"], repr(t[:70]))
print("\ncompaction entries in file:")
for e in entries:
    if e.get("type") == "compaction":
        print("  ", e["id"], "parent:", e.get("parentId"), "firstKept:", e.get("firstKeptEntryId"))
print("\nleaf entry:", leaf.get("id"), leaf.get("type"))
EOF

# Intent is the new source code

**Turn your AI development conversations into searchable, shareable knowledge.**

## SpecStory CLI

SpecStory CLI is a cross-platform command-line tool for saving AI coding coversations from terminal coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Droid CLI, etc.).

It saves your AI coding conversations as local markdown files of each session. It can optionally sync your markdown files to the [SpecStory Cloud](https://cloud.specstory.com), turning your AI chat history into a centralized knowledge system that you can chat with and search.

## Features

- Cross-platform support (Linux, macOS)
- Seamless integration with terminal coding agents
- Command-line wrapper for terminal coding agents with markdown auto-save
- Sync all your prior conversations to local markdown files
- Optional: Syncs your markdown files to the SpecStory Cloud for easy search and chat
- Open source under the Apache 2.0 license

## Agent Support

The following coding agents are supported in the SpecStory CLI:

| Agent                                                     | Provider                                  | Data Format | Source Location         |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------|-------------------------|
| [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) | [claudecode](pkg/providers/claudecode/)   | JSONL       | `~/.claude/projects/`   |
| [Codex CLI](https://www.openai.com/codex/cli/)            | [codexcli](pkg/providers/codexcli/)       | JSONL       | `~/.codex/sessions/`    |
| [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli)                      | [cursorcli](pkg/providers/cursorcli/)     | SQLite      | `~/.cursor/chats/`      |
| [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli)               | [droidcli](pkg/providers/droidcli/)       | JSONL       | `~/.factory/sessions/`  |
| [Gemini CLI](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-cli)            | [geminicli](pkg/providers/geminicli/)     | JSON        | `~/.gemini/tmp/`        |
| [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI)    | [deepseektui](pkg/providers/deepseektui/) | JSON        | `~/.deepseek/sessions/` |
| [Pi](https://pi.dev)                                      | [piagent](pkg/providers/piagent/)         | JSONL       | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` |

### Agent Provider SPI (Service Provider Interface)

There is also an [Agent SPI (Service Provider Interface)](/pkg/spi/) that allows you to extend the SpecStory CLI with support for new agent providers. Creating a provider to support a new agent, using the Provider SPI is documented [here](./docs/PROVIDER-SPI.md). Pull requests are welcome!

## Installation & Usage

Full end-user installation and usage instructions are in the [SpecStory CLI Documentation](https://docs.specstory.com/integrations/terminal-coding-agents). Installation for developers is covered [here](#development).

### Quickstart Usage

Basic usage: `specstory [flags]`

For help:

```zsh
specstory help
```

or

```zsh
specstory help <command>
# e.g.
specstory help run
```

Interactive auto-save mode:

```zsh
# Defaults to Claude Code if no provider is specified.
specstory run <provider>
# e.g.
specstory run codex
```

Syncing all files for the current project:

```zsh
# Defaults to syncing for all providers if no provider is specified
specstory sync <provider>
```

With a specific session UUID:

```zsh
```

// sessionMarkdown returns the session as markdown for the preview — the real specstory
// render when the session can be re-parsed (needs a cwd), else the plain FTS body.
func sessionMarkdown(registry *factory.Registry, store *sessionindex.Store, s *sessionindex.Session) string {
	if s.OriginCwd != "" {
		if prov, err := registry.Get(s.Agent); err == nil {
			if full, err := prov.GetAgentChatSession(s.OriginCwd, s.SessionID, false); err == nil &&
				full != nil && full.SessionData != nil {
				if md, err := session.GenerateMarkdownFromAgentSession(full.SessionData, false, true); err == nil {
					return md
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if body, _ := store.SessionBody(s.Agent, s.SessionID); strings.TrimSpace(body) != "" {
		return "```\n" + body + "\n```"
	}
	return "_(no readable content for this session)_"
}

# SpecStory CLI's Agent SPI

The SpecStory CLI's Agent SPI (Service Provider Interface) allows developers to extend the SpecStory CLI by implementing support for new AI coding agents.

## Overview

The SPI defines a standard interface that all agent providers must implement. This enables SpecStory CLI to work uniformly with multiple AI coding agents while each provider handles the specifics of its native data formats.

### Currently Supported Providers

| Provider ID | Display Name | Session Storage |
|-------------|--------------|-----------------|
| `claude` | Claude Code | `~/.claude/projects/<hash>/<session-id>.jsonl` |
| `cursor` | Cursor CLI | `~/.cursor/chats/<project-hash>/<session-id>/store.db` |
| `codex` | Codex CLI | `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<session-id>.jsonl` |
| `gemini` | Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/tmp/<hash>/chats/<session-id>.json` |
| `pi` | Pi | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl` |

## Quick Start: Implementing a New Provider

To add support for a new AI coding agent:

1. Create a new package under `pkg/providers/<yourprovider>/`
2. Implement the `spi.Provider` interface (see [Provider Interface](#provider-interface))
3. Register your provider in `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`

## Architecture

### Package Structure

```
pkg/
├── spi/
│   ├── provider.go        # Provider interface and CheckResult type
│   ├── cmdline.go         # Command line parsing utilities
│   ├── path_utils.go      # Path utilities (canonical paths, slugs, debug output)
│   ├── factory/
│   │   └── registry.go    # Provider registry (imports all providers)
│   └── schema/
│       └── types.go       # Unified SessionData schema
```

815	// the project directory name is a lossy, irreversible encoding of the path), reporting scan

818	// docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
819	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {

# Intent is the new source code

**Turn your AI development conversations into searchable, shareable knowledge.**

## SpecStory CLI

SpecStory CLI is a cross-platform command-line tool for saving AI coding coversations from terminal coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Droid CLI, etc.).

It saves your AI coding conversations as local markdown files of each session. It can optionally sync your markdown files to the [SpecStory Cloud](https://cloud.specstory.com), turning your AI chat history into a centralized knowledge system that you can chat with and search.

## Features

- Cross-platform support (Linux, macOS)
- Seamless integration with terminal coding agents
- Command-line wrapper for terminal coding agents with markdown auto-save
- Sync all your prior conversations to local markdown files
- Optional: Syncs your markdown files to the SpecStory Cloud for easy search and chat
- Open source under the Apache 2.0 license

## Agent Support

The following coding agents are supported in the SpecStory CLI:

| Agent                                                     | Provider                                  | Data Format | Source Location         |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------|-------------------------|
| [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) | [claudecode](pkg/providers/claudecode/)   | JSONL       | `~/.claude/projects/`   |
| [Codex CLI](https://www.openai.com/codex/cli/)            | [codexcli](pkg/providers/codexcli/)       | JSONL       | `~/.codex/sessions/`    |
| [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli)                      | [cursorcli](pkg/providers/cursorcli/)     | SQLite      | `~/.cursor/chats/`      |
| [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli)               | [droidcli](pkg/providers/droidcli/)       | JSONL       | `~/.factory/sessions/`  |
| [Gemini CLI](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-cli)            | [geminicli](pkg/providers/geminicli/)     | JSON        | `~/.gemini/tmp/`        |
| [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI)    | [deepseektui](pkg/providers/deepseektui/) | JSON        | `~/.deepseek/sessions/` |
| [Pi](https://pi.dev)                                      | [piagent](pkg/providers/piagent/)         | JSONL       | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` |

### Agent Provider SPI (Service Provider Interface)

There is also an [Agent SPI (Service Provider Interface)](/pkg/spi/) that allows you to extend the SpecStory CLI with support for new agent providers. Creating a provider to support a new agent, using the Provider SPI is documented [here](./docs/PROVIDER-SPI.md). Pull requests are welcome!

## Installation & Usage

Full end-user installation and usage instructions are in the [SpecStory CLI Documentation](https://docs.specstory.com/integrations/terminal-coding-agents). Installation for developers is covered [here](#development).

### Quickstart Usage

Basic usage: `specstory [flags]`

For help:

```zsh
specstory help
```

or

```zsh
specstory help <command>
# e.g.
specstory help run
```
