# SpecStory CLI's Agent SPI

The SpecStory CLI's Agent SPI (Service Provider Interface) allows developers to extend the SpecStory CLI by implementing support for new AI coding agents.

## Overview

The SPI defines a standard interface that all agent providers must implement. This enables SpecStory CLI to work uniformly with multiple AI coding agents while each provider handles the specifics of its native data formats.

### Currently Supported Providers

| Provider ID | Display Name | Session Storage |
|-------------|--------------|-----------------|
| `claude` | Claude Code | `~/.claude/projects/<hash>/<session-id>.jsonl` |
| `cursor` | Cursor CLI | `~/.cursor/chats/<project-hash>/<session-id>/store.db` |
| `codex` | Codex CLI | `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<session-id>.jsonl` |
| `gemini` | Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/tmp/<hash>/chats/<session-id>.json` |
| `pi` | Pi | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl` |

## Quick Start: Implementing a New Provider

To add support for a new AI coding agent:

1. Create a new package under `pkg/providers/<yourprovider>/`
2. Implement the `spi.Provider` interface (see [Provider Interface](#provider-interface))
3. Register your provider in `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`

## Architecture

### Package Structure

```
pkg/
├── spi/
│   ├── provider.go        # Provider interface and CheckResult type
│   ├── cmdline.go         # Command line parsing utilities
│   ├── path_utils.go      # Path utilities (canonical paths, slugs, debug output)
│   ├── factory/
│   │   └── registry.go    # Provider registry (imports all providers)
│   └── schema/
│       └── types.go       # Unified SessionData schema
```

package piagent

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/analytics"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

const (
	providerID    = "pi"
	providerName  = "Pi"
	defaultCmd    = "pi"
	versionFlag   = "--version"
	notYetSupport = "pi: %s not yet supported for the pi provider (v1 ships sync/list/search/reindex only)"
)

// Provider implements spi.Provider for the pi coding agent.
// pi stores sessions as JSONL v3 trees under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/.
type Provider struct{}

// NewProvider returns a new pi provider instance.
func NewProvider() *Provider { return &Provider{} }

// Name returns the human-readable provider name.
func (p *Provider) Name() string { return providerName }

// Check verifies the pi binary is on PATH and reports its version.
func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
	cmdName := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand)
	isCustom := cmdName != ""
	if cmdName == "" {
		cmdName = defaultCmd
	}
	resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
		trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "not_found", err.Error())
		return spi.CheckResult{
			Success:      false,
			ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi binary '%s' not found on PATH", cmdName),
		}
	}
	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err)
		trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())
		return spi.CheckResult{
			Success:      false,
			Location:     resolved,
			ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi version probe failed: %v", err),
		}
	}
	version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
	if version == "" {
		version = "unknown"
	}
	trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
	return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
}

// DetectAgent reports whether pi has created sessions for the given project.
func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, _ bool) bool {
	files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Debug("pi: DetectAgent error", "error", err)
		return false
	}
	return len(files) > 0

package piagent

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/analytics"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

const (
	providerID    = "pi"
	providerName  = "Pi"
	defaultCmd    = "pi"
	versionFlag   = "--version"
	notYetSupport = "pi: %s not yet supported for the pi provider (v1 ships sync/list/search/reindex only)"
)

// Provider implements spi.Provider for the pi coding agent.
// pi stores sessions as JSONL v3 trees under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/.
type Provider struct{}

// NewProvider returns a new pi provider instance.
func NewProvider() *Provider { return &Provider{} }

// Name returns the human-readable provider name.
func (p *Provider) Name() string { return providerName }

// Check verifies the pi binary is on PATH and reports its version.
func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
	cmdName := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand)
	isCustom := cmdName != ""
	if cmdName == "" {
		cmdName = defaultCmd
	}
	resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
		trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "not_found", err.Error())
		return spi.CheckResult{
			Success:      false,
			ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi binary '%s' not found on PATH", cmdName),
		}
	}
	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err)
		trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())
		return spi.CheckResult{
			Success:      false,
			Location:     resolved,
			ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi version probe failed: %v", err),
		}
	}
	version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
	if version == "" {
		version = "unknown"
	}
	trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
	return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
}

// DetectAgent reports whether pi has created sessions for the given project.
func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, _ bool) bool {
	files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Debug("pi: DetectAgent error", "error", err)
		return false
	}

<img width="1649" height="158" alt="Group 6 (1)" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/93f0210f-c3ce-4035-91df-ec597e00a3ce" />

# Intent is the new source code

**Turn your AI development conversations into searchable, shareable knowledge.**

## SpecStory CLI

SpecStory CLI is a cross-platform command-line tool for saving AI coding coversations from terminal coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Droid CLI, etc.).

It saves your AI coding conversations as local markdown files of each session. It can optionally sync your markdown files to the [SpecStory Cloud](https://cloud.specstory.com), turning your AI chat history into a centralized knowledge system that you can chat with and search.

## Features

- Cross-platform support (Linux, macOS)
- Seamless integration with terminal coding agents
- Command-line wrapper for terminal coding agents with markdown auto-save
- Sync all your prior conversations to local markdown files
- Optional: Syncs your markdown files to the SpecStory Cloud for easy search and chat
- Open source under the Apache 2.0 license

## Agent Support

The following coding agents are supported in the SpecStory CLI:

| Agent                                                     | Provider                                  | Data Format | Source Location         |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------|-------------------------|
| [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) | [claudecode](pkg/providers/claudecode/)   | JSONL       | `~/.claude/projects/`   |
| [Codex CLI](https://www.openai.com/codex/cli/)            | [codexcli](pkg/providers/codexcli/)       | JSONL       | `~/.codex/sessions/`    |
| [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli)                      | [cursorcli](pkg/providers/cursorcli/)     | SQLite      | `~/.cursor/chats/`      |
| [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli)               | [droidcli](pkg/providers/droidcli/)       | JSONL       | `~/.factory/sessions/`  |
| [Gemini CLI](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-cli)            | [geminicli](pkg/providers/geminicli/)     | JSON        | `~/.gemini/tmp/`        |
| [DeepSeek TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI)    | [deepseektui](pkg/providers/deepseektui/) | JSON        | `~/.deepseek/sessions/` |
| [Pi](https://pi.dev)                                      | [piagent](pkg/providers/piagent/)         | JSONL       | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` |

### Agent Provider SPI (Service Provider Interface)

There is also an [Agent SPI (Service Provider Interface)](/pkg/spi/) that allows you to extend the SpecStory CLI with support for new agent providers. Creating a provider to support a new agent, using the Provider SPI is documented [here](./docs/PROVIDER-SPI.md). Pull requests are welcome!

## Installation & Usage

Full end-user installation and usage instructions are in the [SpecStory CLI Documentation](https://docs.specstory.com/integrations/terminal-coding-agents). Installation for developers is covered [here](#development).

### Quickstart Usage

Basic usage: `specstory [flags]`

For help:

```zsh
specstory help
```

or

```zsh
specstory help <command>
# e.g.
specstory help run
```

Interactive auto-save mode:

```zsh
# Defaults to Claude Code if no provider is specified.
specstory run <provider>
# e.g.
specstory run codex
```

Syncing all files for the current project:

```zsh
# Defaults to syncing for all providers if no provider is specified
specstory sync <provider>
```

With a specific session UUID:

```zsh
```

589	// parseFullSession reads a session's full data for indexing. It prefers a provider's
590	// path-keyed parse (spi.PathSessionReader) using the ref's already-known NativePath, which
591	// avoids the provider's by-id discovery search — for Codex that search walks the entire
592	// ~/.codex/sessions tree, so this is the difference between an O(N) and an O(N²) reindex.
593	// Providers without the capability (or refs lacking a NativePath) fall back to the by-id
594	// lookup. Parsing the known NativePath is also more consistent: the row's freshness
595	// fingerprint is stat'd from NativePath, so the body now comes from that same file.
596	func parseFullSession(prov spi.Provider, ref spi.GlobalSessionRef) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {

598			return pr.GetAgentChatSessionByPath(ref.NativePath, ref.OriginCwd, false)
599		}
600		return prov.GetAgentChatSession(ref.OriginCwd, ref.SessionID, false)
601	}

606		flush := func() error {

609			}
610			batch = batch[:0]
611			return nil
612		}
613		for sess := range ch {

```text
# SpecStory CLI's Agent SPI

The SpecStory CLI's Agent SPI (Service Provider Interface) allows developers to extend the SpecStory CLI by implementing support for new AI coding agents.

## Overview

The SPI defines a standard interface that all agent providers must implement. This enables SpecStory CLI to work uniformly with multiple AI coding agents while each provider handles the specifics of its native data formats.

### Currently Supported Providers

| Provider ID | Display Name | Session Storage |
|-------------|--------------|-----------------|
| `claude` | Claude Code | `~/.claude/projects/<hash>/<session-id>.jsonl` |
| `cursor` | Cursor CLI | `~/.cursor/chats/<project-hash>/<session-id>/store.db` |
| `codex` | Codex CLI | `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<session-id>.jsonl` |
| `gemini` | Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/tmp/<hash>/chats/<session-id>.json` |
| `pi` | Pi | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl` |

## Quick Start: Implementing a New Provider

To add support for a new AI coding agent:

1. Create a new package under `pkg/providers/<yourprovider>/`
2. Implement the `spi.Provider` interface (see [Provider Interface](#provider-interface))
3. Register your provider in `pkg/spi/factory/registry.go`

## Architecture

### Package Structure

```
pkg/
├── spi/
│   ├── provider.go        # Provider interface and CheckResult type
│   ├── cmdline.go         # Command line parsing utilities
│   ├── path_utils.go      # Path utilities (canonical paths, slugs, debug output)
│   ├── factory/
│   │   └── registry.go    # Provider registry (imports all providers)
│   └── schema/
│       └── types.go       # Unified SessionData schema
└── providers/
    ├── claudecode/        # Claude Code provider implementation
    ├── cursorcli/         # Cursor CLI provider implementation
    ├── codexcli/          # Codex CLI provider implementation
    ├── geminicli/         # Gemini CLI provider implementation
    └── piagent/           # Pi provider implementation
```

### Dependency Flow

```
main.go
  → spi/factory (registry)
      → spi (interfaces)
      → providers/claudecode
      → providers/cursorcli
      → providers/codexcli
      → providers/geminicli
      → providers/piagent
```

15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// Skip entries missing the envelope fields the tree walk and exchange
91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}
104	
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
187	
188	// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
189	// if not found.
190	func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
191		for i, e := range path {
192			if e.ID == keptID {
193				return i
194			}
195		}
196		return -1
197	}

	defaultAgent := "the default agent"

// Provider implements spi.Provider for the pi coding agent.
// pi stores sessions as JSONL v3 trees under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/.
type Provider struct{}

// NewProvider returns a new pi provider instance.
func NewProvider() *Provider { return &Provider{} }

// Name returns the human-readable provider name.
func (p *Provider) Name() string { return providerName }

// Check verifies the pi binary is on PATH and reports its version.
func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
	cmdName := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand)
	isCustom := cmdName != ""
	if cmdName == "" {
		cmdName = defaultCmd
	}
	resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
		trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "not_found", err.Error())
		return spi.CheckResult{
			Success:      false,
			ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi binary '%s' not found on PATH", cmdName),
		}
	}
	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err)
		trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())

// sessionMarkdown returns the session as markdown for the preview — the real specstory
// render when the session can be re-parsed (needs a cwd), else the plain FTS body.
func sessionMarkdown(registry *factory.Registry, store *sessionindex.Store, s *sessionindex.Session) string {
	if s.OriginCwd != "" {
		if prov, err := registry.Get(s.Agent); err == nil {
			if full, err := prov.GetAgentChatSession(s.OriginCwd, s.SessionID, false); err == nil &&
				full != nil && full.SessionData != nil {
				if md, err := session.GenerateMarkdownFromAgentSession(full.SessionData, false, true); err == nil {
					return md
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if body, _ := store.SessionBody(s.Agent, s.SessionID); strings.TrimSpace(body) != "" {
		return "```\n" + body + "\n```"
	}
	return "_(no readable content for this session)_"
}

107	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path
108	// branch into the unified schema.SessionData. It honors compaction entries:
109	// when a compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId
110	// are dropped from the conversation (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
112		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		if header == nil {
117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
118		}
119		if header.Type != entrySession {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
121		}
122		if header.ID == "" {
123			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
124		}
125		if len(entries) == 0 {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
127		}
128		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
129		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
130	}

132	// piProviderVersion derives the provider version string recorded on SessionData
133	// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
134	// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
135	func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
136		if header.Version > 0 {
137			return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
138		}
139		return "v1"
140	}

142	// buildSessionData maps the ordered leaf-path entries into schema.SessionData.
143	func buildSessionData(header *sessionHeader, ordered []rawEntry) *schema.SessionData {
144		return &schema.SessionData{
145			SchemaVersion: "1.0",
146			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{
147				ID:      providerID,
148				Name:    providerName,
149				Version: piProviderVersion(header),
150			},
151			SessionID:     header.ID,
152			CreatedAt:     header.Timestamp,
153			WorkspaceRoot: header.Cwd,
154			Exchanges:     buildExchanges(ordered),
155		}
156	}

158	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
159	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
160	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo. Control entries
161	// (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the conversation body.
162	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
163		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
164		var current *schema.Exchange
165		commit := func() {
166			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
167				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
168			}
169		}
170		for _, e := range ordered {
171			if e.Type != entryMessage {
172				continue
173			}
174			switch messageRole(e) {
175			case roleUser:
176				commit()
177				current = &schema.Exchange{
178					ExchangeID: e.ID,
179					StartTime:  e.Timestamp,
180					EndTime:    e.Timestamp,
181					Messages:   []schema.Message{buildUserMessage(e)},
182				}
183			case roleAssistant:
184				current = appendAssistant(current, e)
185			case roleToolResult:
186				mergeToolResult(current, e)
187			}
188		}
189		commit()
190		return exchanges
191	}

193	// appendAssistant appends an assistant message to the current exchange, creating
194	// one if none exists yet.
195	func appendAssistant(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) *schema.Exchange {
196		if current == nil {
197			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
198		}
199		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, buildAgentMessages(e)...)
200		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
201		return current
202	}

214	// the current exchange, keyed by toolCallId == ToolInfo.UseID. It also advances
215	// the exchange EndTime to the toolResult's timestamp so downstream stats that
216	// read the last exchange's EndTime report the real final-event time.
217	func mergeToolResult(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) {
218		if current == nil {
219			return
220		}
221		var tr toolResultMessage
222		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &tr); err != nil {
223			return
224		}
225		content := toolResultContent(tr)
226		for i := range current.Messages {
227			msg := &current.Messages[i]
228			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.UseID == tr.ToolCallID {
229				msg.Tool.Output = buildToolOutput(content, tr)
230				msg.Timestamp = e.Timestamp
231				current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
232				return
233			}
234		}
235	}

241			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
242				parts = append(parts, b.Text)
243			}
244		}
245		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
246	}

249	// pi user content is either a plain string or an array of {type:text|image}.

251		var um userMessage
252		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &um)
253		parts := userContentParts(um.Content)

255			ID:        e.ID,
256			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,

262	// userContentParts decodes a pi user message's content (string or array) into
263	// schema ContentParts. Image blocks are dropped in v1 (recorded as a gap).
264	func userContentParts(raw json.RawMessage) []schema.ContentPart {
265		if len(raw) == 0 {
266			return nil
267		}
268		if raw[0] == '"' {
269			var s string
270			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
271				return []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: s}}
272			}
273		}
274		var blocks []contentBlock
275		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
276			return nil
277		}
278		var parts []schema.ContentPart
279		for _, b := range blocks {
280			if b.Type == schema.ContentTypeText && b.Text != "" {
281				parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
282			}
283		}
284		return parts
285	}

287	// buildAgentMessages maps a pi assistant message entry to one or more schema
288	// Messages: one Message holds the text+thinking content parts; each toolCall
289	// block becomes its own agent Message carrying a ToolInfo.
290	func buildAgentMessages(e rawEntry) []schema.Message {
291		var am assistantMessage
292		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &am); err != nil {
293			return nil
294		}
295		var parts []schema.ContentPart
296		var messages []schema.Message
297		for _, b := range am.Content {
298			switch b.Type {
299			case schema.ContentTypeText:
300				if b.Text != "" {
301					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
302				}
303			case schema.ContentTypeThinking:
304				if b.Thinking != "" {
305					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: b.Thinking})
306				}
307			case "toolCall":
308				messages = append(messages, buildToolMessage(e, b, am))
309			}

311		if len(parts) > 0 {
312			head := schema.Message{
313				ID:        e.ID,
314				Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
315				Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
316				Model:     am.Model,
317				Content:   parts,
318				Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
319			}
320			return append([]schema.Message{head}, messages...)
321		}
322		if len(messages) == 0 {
323			return buildErrorMessage(e, am)

335	// buildToolMessage builds an agent Message wrapping a ToolInfo from a toolCall.

341	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
342		return schema.Message{
343			ID:        toolMessageID(e.ID, b.ID),
344			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
345			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
346			Model:     am.Model,

356	// toolMessageID builds a unique Message ID for a tool-call message from the

359	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {
360		if callID != "" {

364	}

366	// buildToolOutput constructs the ToolInfo.Output map from a toolResult's

368	// decoded into a generic value so downstream consumers (markdown rendering,

370	func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
371		out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
372		if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
373			var details any
374			if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {

381	// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map

383	// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics).
384	func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
385		if u == nil {
386			return nil
387		}
388		return &schema.Usage{
389			InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
390			OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
391			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
392			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
393		}
394	}

396	// buildErrorMessage surfaces an assistant entry with stopReason=error and an

400	func buildErrorMessage(e rawEntry, am assistantMessage) []schema.Message {
401		if strings.TrimSpace(am.ErrorMessage) == "" {
402			return nil
403		}
404		return []schema.Message{{
405			ID:        e.ID,
406			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
407			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
408			Model:     am.Model,

414	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
415	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
416	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
417	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
418		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
419			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
420				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
421					continue
422				}
423				for _, part := range msg.Content {
424					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {

426					}
427				}
428			}
429		}
430		return ""
431	}

433	// classifyToolType maps pi tool names to the schema tool-type taxonomy.
434	func classifyToolType(name string) string {
435		switch strings.ToLower(name) {
436		case "read":
437			return schema.ToolTypeRead
438		case "edit", "write":
439			return schema.ToolTypeWrite
440		case "bash", "ls":
441			return schema.ToolTypeShell
442		case "grep", "find", "web_search", "fetch_content":
443			return schema.ToolTypeSearch
444		case "until_done_set", "until_done_plan", "until_done_task_update",
445			"until_done_progress", "until_done_complete", "until_done_block",
446			"until_done_replan", "until_done_distill":
447			return schema.ToolTypeTask
448		default:
449			return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
450		}
451	}

12	// Format-coverage tests for the pi session file format
13	// (https://pi.dev/docs/latest/session-format): entry types, field-level
14	// mapping, tree structure, and compaction. Fixtures live in testdata/.
15	
16	// parseFields loads the fields.jsonl fixture (every message role + content-block
17	// type, NO compaction — so field-bearing entries survive into the exchanges).
18	func parseFields(t *testing.T) *schema.SessionData {
19		t.Helper()
20		data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "fields.jsonl"))
21		if err != nil {
22			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
23		}
24		return data
25	}
26	
27	// ---- entry types / control entries / compaction ----
28	
29	// TestFormatEntries_ControlEntriesSkipped covers the non-message entry types:
30	// model_change, thinking_level_change, session_info, label, custom, and
31	// custom_message. They must not break the parse and must not produce exchange
32	// messages (custom_message content is extension context, not a user turn).
33	func TestFormatEntries_ControlEntriesSkipped(t *testing.T) {
34		data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "full_format.jsonl"))
35		if err != nil {
36			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
37		}
38		if !data.Validate() {
39			t.Error("Validate() returned false; a control entry leaked an invalid message")
40		}
41		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
42			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
43				for _, part := range msg.Content {
44					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "Injected context from extension") {
45						t.Error("custom_message content leaked into exchanges as a user turn")
46					}
47					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "branch explored approach B") {
48						t.Error("branch_summary content leaked into exchanges")
49					}
50				}
51			}
52		}
53	}
54	
55	// TestFormatEntries_BranchSummaryEntry covers the top-level branch_summary entry
56	// (type:"branch_summary" with fromId, summary, details, fromHook). It must be
57	// skipped from exchanges without error.
58	func TestFormatEntries_BranchSummaryEntry(t *testing.T) {
59		data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "full_format.jsonl"))
60		if err != nil {
61			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
62		}
63		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {

65				for _, part := range msg.Content {

74	// TestFormatEntries_CompactionDropsPreKept covers the compaction entry's
75	// firstKeptEntryId field on full_format.jsonl: firstKeptEntryId=a2, so the
76	// common answer (before a2) is dropped and the post-compaction prompt survives.
77	func TestFormatEntries_CompactionDropsPreKept(t *testing.T) {
78		data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "full_format.jsonl"))
79		if err != nil {
80			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
81		}
82		var hasCommon, hasPost bool
83		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
84			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
85				for _, part := range msg.Content {
86					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "common answer") {
87						hasCommon = true
88					}
89					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "after compaction prompt") {
90						hasPost = true
91					}
92				}
93			}
94		}
95		if hasCommon {
96			t.Error("entry before firstKeptEntryId was not dropped by compaction")
97		}
98		if !hasPost {
99			t.Error("post-compaction prompt was dropped")
100		}
101	}

103	// TestFormatEntries_RealWorldCompactionAndBashExecution uses a trimmed slice of
104	// a real pi session (testdata/real_world.jsonl) to assert the hard-to-synthesize
105	// format features: a compaction entry carrying details.readFiles/modifiedFiles +
106	// tokensBefore, a bashExecution message role (skipped from exchanges), and that
107	// compaction drops the pre-kept user prompt while keeping the post-compaction one.
108	func TestFormatEntries_RealWorldCompactionAndBashExecution(t *testing.T) {
109		data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "real_world.jsonl"))
110		if err != nil {
111			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
112		}
113		if data.SessionID != "real-world-uuid" {
114			t.Errorf("SessionID = %q, want real-world-uuid", data.SessionID)
115		}
116		if !data.Validate() {
117			t.Error("Validate() returned false for the real-world session")
118		}
119		var hasPreCompaction, hasPostCompaction, hasBashExecContent bool
120		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
121			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
122				for _, part := range msg.Content {
123					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "Read README.md and NOTES.md") {
124						hasPreCompaction = true
125					}
126					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "summarize it now") {
127						hasPostCompaction = true
128					}
129					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "total 24") {
130						hasBashExecContent = true
131					}
132				}
133			}
134		}
135		if hasPreCompaction {
136			t.Error("pre-compaction user prompt was not dropped by compaction")
137		}
138		if !hasPostCompaction {
139			t.Error("post-compaction user prompt was dropped by compaction")
140		}
141		if hasBashExecContent {
142			t.Error("bashExecution content leaked into exchanges (should be skipped)")
143		}
144	}

146	// TestFormatEntries_CompactionHonorsFirstKeptEntryId asserts that when a
147	// compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId are
148	// dropped and entries from firstKeptEntryId forward are kept.
149	func TestFormatEntries_CompactionHonorsFirstKeptEntryId(t *testing.T) {
150		data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "compaction.jsonl"))
151		if err != nil {
152			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
153		}
154		var hasDroppedPre, hasKept, hasPost bool
155		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
156			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
157				for _, part := range msg.Content {
158					switch {
159					case strings.Contains(part.Text, "first prompt before compaction"):
160						hasDroppedPre = true
161					case strings.Contains(part.Text, "first answer before compaction"):
162						hasKept = true
163					case strings.Contains(part.Text, "after compaction"):
164						hasPost = true
165					}
166				}
167			}
168		}
169		if hasDroppedPre {
170			t.Error("pre-kept user prompt (u1) was not dropped by compaction")
171		}
172		if !hasKept {
173			t.Error("kept entry (a1, firstKeptEntryId) was dropped")
174		}
175		if !hasPost {
176			t.Error("post-compaction user prompt was dropped by compaction")
177		}
178	}

180	// TestFormatEntries_CompactionMissingKeptIdDropsPreCompaction asserts the
181	// fallback: when firstKeptEntryId is not found in the leaf path, pre-compaction
182	// entries are still dropped (kept from the compaction entry forward).
183	func TestFormatEntries_CompactionMissingKeptIdDropsPreCompaction(t *testing.T) {
184		data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "compaction_missing.jsonl"))
185		if err != nil {
186			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
187		}
188		var hasPre, hasPost bool
189		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
190			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
191				for _, part := range msg.Content {
192					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "before compaction") {
193						hasPre = true
194					}
195					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "after compaction") {
196						hasPost = true
197					}
198				}
199			}
200		}
201		if hasPre {
202			t.Error("pre-compaction user prompt retained when firstKeptEntryId was missing")
203		}
204		if !hasPost {
205			t.Error("post-compaction user prompt was dropped in the missing-kept-id fallback")
206		}
207	}

211	// TestFormatFields_SessionHeader covers the session header: id, timestamp, cwd,
212	// version, and the optional parentSession field (fork/clone marker).
213	func TestFormatFields_SessionHeader(t *testing.T) {
214		data := parseFields(t)

216			t.Errorf("SessionID = %q, want fields-uuid", data.SessionID)
217		}

222			t.Errorf("WorkspaceRoot = %q, want /test/proj", data.WorkspaceRoot)
223		}

225			t.Errorf("Provider.Version = %q, want v3", data.Provider.Version)
226		}
227	}

229	// TestFormatFields_UserMessageStringContent covers UserMessage.content as a
230	// plain string (mapped to a single text content part).
231	func TestFormatFields_UserMessageStringContent(t *testing.T) {
232		data := parseFields(t)
233		var found bool
234		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
235			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
236				if msg.Role == schema.RoleUser && len(msg.Content) == 1 &&
237					msg.Content[0].Text == "hello as a plain string" {

241		}

269	// TestFormatFields_AssistantAllFields covers the assistant message: api,
270	// provider, model, stopReason, errorMessage, and the full usage object.
271	func TestFormatFields_AssistantAllFields(t *testing.T) {
272		data := parseFields(t)
273		var a1, a2 *schema.Message
274		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
275			for i := range ex.Messages {
276				m := &ex.Messages[i]
277				if m.Role != schema.RoleAgent || m.Tool != nil || len(m.Content) == 0 {
278					continue
279				}
280				if m.Content[0].Type == schema.ContentTypeThinking {
281					a1 = m
282				}
283				if m.Model == "glm-1" && len(m.Content) == 1 && m.Content[0].Text == "done" {
284					a2 = m
285				}
286			}
287		}
288		if a1 == nil {
289			t.Fatal("assistant message with thinking not found")
290		}
291		if a1.Model != "glm-1" {
292			t.Errorf("a1 Model = %q, want glm-1", a1.Model)
293		}
294		if a1.Usage == nil {
295			t.Fatal("a1 Usage nil")
296		}
297		if a1.Usage.InputTokens != 100 || a1.Usage.OutputTokens != 50 {
298			t.Errorf("a1 usage input/output = %d/%d, want 100/50", a1.Usage.InputTokens, a1.Usage.OutputTokens)
299		}
300		if a1.Usage.CacheReadInputTokens != 10 || a1.Usage.CacheCreationInputTokens != 5 {
301			t.Errorf("a1 cache read/create = %d/%d, want 10/5", a1.Usage.CacheReadInputTokens, a1.Usage.CacheCreationInputTokens)
302		}
303		if a2 == nil {
304			t.Fatal("assistant message with stopReason=error not found")
305		}
306		if a2.Usage == nil || a2.Usage.OutputTokens != 20 {
307			t.Errorf("a2 output tokens = %v, want 20", a2.Usage)
308		}
309	}

311	// TestFormatFields_ToolResultFields covers the toolResult message: toolCallId,
312	// toolName, content (text), isError, and details. The result must merge into the
313	// matching tool message's ToolInfo.Output keyed by toolCallId.
314	func TestFormatFields_ToolResultFields(t *testing.T) {
315		data := parseFields(t)
316		var tool *schema.Message
317		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
318			for i := range ex.Messages {
319				if ex.Messages[i].Tool != nil && ex.Messages[i].Tool.UseID == "call-1" {
320					tool = &ex.Messages[i]
321				}
322			}
323		}
324		if tool == nil {
325			t.Fatal("tool message with UseID call-1 not found")
326		}
327		if tool.Tool.Name != "bash" || tool.Tool.Type != schema.ToolTypeShell {
328			t.Errorf("tool name/type = %q/%q, want bash/shell", tool.Tool.Name, tool.Tool.Type)
329		}
330		if tool.Tool.Output == nil {
331			t.Fatal("tool output not merged from toolResult")
332		}
333		content, _ := tool.Tool.Output["content"].(string)
334		if content != "file1\nfile2" {
335			t.Errorf("tool output content = %q, want file1\\nfile2", content)
336		}
337		if isErr, _ := tool.Tool.Output["is_error"].(bool); isErr {
338			t.Error("tool output is_error = true, want false")
339		}
340		details, hasDetails := tool.Tool.Output["details"]
341		if !hasDetails {
342			t.Fatal("tool output missing 'details' — toolResult details were dropped")
343		}
344		detMap, ok := details.(map[string]any)
345		if !ok {
346			t.Fatalf("details is %T, want map[string]any", details)
347		}
348		if exitCode, _ := detMap["exitCode"].(float64); exitCode != 0 {
349			t.Errorf("details.exitCode = %v, want 0", detMap["exitCode"])
350		}
351	}

373	// ---- tree structure / versions ----
374	
375	// TestFormatTree_BranchingLeafSelection covers the tree structure: when a
376	// session branches (one parent, two children), the parser walks the current
377	// leaf path — the LAST entry in file order — not the alternate branch.
378	func TestFormatTree_BranchingLeafSelection(t *testing.T) {
379		data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "branching.jsonl"))
380		if err != nil {
381			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
382		}
383		var hasLeft, hasRight bool
384		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
385			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
386				for _, part := range msg.Content {
387					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "left branch") {
388						hasLeft = true
389					}
390					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "right branch") {
391						hasRight = true
392					}
393				}
394			}
395		}
396		if hasLeft {
397			t.Error("alternate (non-leaf) branch was included; parser should walk only the leaf path")
398		}
399		if !hasRight {
400			t.Error("leaf branch was dropped; parser should walk the last entry's path to root")
401		}
402	}

425	// TestFormatTree_ToolCallOnlyAssistantRetainsModelAndUsage covers an assistant
426	// message containing only toolCall blocks (no text/thinking): it must still
427	// carry model + usage on the tool message and emit no schema-invalid empty
428	// agent message.
429	func TestFormatTree_ToolCallOnlyAssistantRetainsModelAndUsage(t *testing.T) {
430		tmp := t.TempDir()
431		path := filepath.Join(tmp, "toolonly.jsonl")
432		session := `{"type":"session","version":3,"id":"toolonly-uuid","timestamp":"2026-07-09T10:00:00.000Z","cwd":"/test"}
433	` +
434			`{"type":"message","id":"u1","parentId":null,"timestamp":"2026-07-09T10:00:01.000Z","message":{"role":"user","content":"run ls","timestamp":1783600001000}}
435	` +
436			`{"type":"message","id":"a1","parentId":"u1","timestamp":"2026-07-09T10:00:02.000Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"toolCall","id":"call-1","name":"bash","arguments":{"command":"ls"}}],"provider":"fireworks","model":"glm","usage":{"input":10,"output":5,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"totalTokens":15,"cost":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"total":0}}}}
437	`
438		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(session), 0o644); err != nil {
439			t.Fatalf("write fixture: %v", err)
440		}
441		data, err := ParseSession(path)
442		if err != nil {
443			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
444		}
445		var toolMsg *schema.Message
446		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
447			for i := range ex.Messages {
448				if ex.Messages[i].Tool != nil {
449					toolMsg = &ex.Messages[i]
450				}
451			}
452		}
453		if toolMsg == nil {
454			t.Fatal("no tool message produced from tool-call-only assistant entry")
455		}
456		if toolMsg.Model != "glm" {
457			t.Errorf("tool message Model = %q, want glm", toolMsg.Model)
458		}
459		if toolMsg.Usage == nil || toolMsg.Usage.InputTokens == 0 {
460			t.Error("tool message did not retain usage from the assistant entry")
461		}
462		if !data.Validate() {
463			t.Error("SessionData.Validate() returned false")
464		}
465	}

467	// TestFormatTree_LatestCompactionWins asserts that when a session has multiple
468	// compaction entries on the leaf path, the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId
469	// determines the kept context (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
470	func TestFormatTree_LatestCompactionWins(t *testing.T) {
471		data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "multi_compaction.jsonl"))
472		if err != nil {
473			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
474		}
475		var hasA1, hasU2, hasU3 bool
476		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
477			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
478				for _, part := range msg.Content {
479					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "answer one") {
480						hasA1 = true
481					}
482					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "prompt two") {
483						hasU2 = true
484					}
485					if strings.Contains(part.Text, "prompt three") {
486						hasU3 = true
487					}
488				}
489			}
490		}
491		if hasA1 {
492			t.Error("a1 was retained — the oldest compaction won; the latest should have dropped it")
493		}
494		if !hasU2 {
495			t.Error("u2 (the latest compaction's firstKeptEntryId) was dropped")
496		}
497		if !hasU3 {
498			t.Error("u3 (post-latest-compaction) was dropped")
499		}
500	}

504	// from the user message timestamp.

509	` +
510			`{"type":"message","id":"u1","parentId":null,"timestamp":"2026-07-09T10:00:05.000Z","message":{"role":"user","content":"orphan prompt","timestamp":1783600005000}}
511	`

513			t.Fatalf("write fixture: %v", err)

515		data, err := ParseSession(path)
516		if err != nil {
517			t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)

519		if len(data.Exchanges) != 1 {
520			t.Fatalf("want 1 exchange, got %d", len(data.Exchanges))
521		}
522		ex := data.Exchanges[0]
523		if ex.EndTime != "2026-07-09T10:00:05.000Z" {
524			t.Errorf("user-only exchange EndTime = %q, want the user message timestamp", ex.EndTime)
525		}
526	}

1	package piagent
2	
3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"log/slog"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"strings"
13	)
14	
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// Skip entries missing the envelope fields the tree walk and exchange
91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}
104	
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
187	
188	// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
189	// if not found.
190	func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
191		for i, e := range path {
192			if e.ID == keptID {
193				return i
194			}
195		}
196		return -1
197	}

40	// firstKeptEntryId as a top-level field (no message wrapper).
41	type rawEntry struct {
42		Type             string          `json:"type"`
43		ID               string          `json:"id"`
44		ParentID         *string         `json:"parentId"` // null for the first entry
45		Timestamp        string          `json:"timestamp"`
46		FirstKeptEntryID string          `json:"firstKeptEntryId,omitempty"` // compaction entries only
47		Message          json.RawMessage `json:"message,omitempty"`
48	}
49	
50	// sessionHeader is the first line of a pi session file (no id/parentId).
51	type sessionHeader struct {
52		Type      string `json:"type"`
53		Version   int    `json:"version"`
54		ID        string `json:"id"`
55		Timestamp string `json:"timestamp"`
56		Cwd       string `json:"cwd"`
57	}
58	
59	// contentBlock is one element of an assistant or user message content array.
60	type contentBlock struct {
61		Type     string         `json:"type"`
62		Text     string         `json:"text,omitempty"`
63		Thinking string         `json:"thinking,omitempty"`
64		ID       string         `json:"id,omitempty"`
65		Name     string         `json:"name,omitempty"`
66		Args     map[string]any `json:"arguments,omitempty"`
67	}
68	
69	// userMessage is a pi user-role message: content is string OR []contentBlock.
70	type userMessage struct {
71		Role      string          `json:"role"`
72		Content   json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
73		Timestamp int64           `json:"timestamp"`
74	}
75	
76	// assistantMessage is a pi assistant-role message.
77	type assistantMessage struct {
78		Role         string         `json:"role"`
79		Content      []contentBlock `json:"content"`
80		Provider     string         `json:"provider"`
81		Model        string         `json:"model"`
82		API          string         `json:"api"`
83		StopReason   string         `json:"stopReason"`
84		ErrorMessage string         `json:"errorMessage,omitempty"`
85		Usage        *piUsage       `json:"usage,omitempty"`
86	}
87	
88	// piUsage is the token-usage shape on a pi assistant message.
89	type piUsage struct {
90		Input       int64 `json:"input"`
91		Output      int64 `json:"output"`
92		CacheRead   int64 `json:"cacheRead"`
93		CacheWrite  int64 `json:"cacheWrite"`
94		TotalTokens int64 `json:"totalTokens"`
95	}
96	
97	// toolResultMessage is a pi toolResult-role message (a top-level entry).
98	type toolResultMessage struct {
99		Role       string          `json:"role"`
100		ToolCallID string          `json:"toolCallId"`
101		ToolName   string          `json:"toolName"`
102		Content    []contentBlock  `json:"content"`
103		Details    json.RawMessage `json:"details,omitempty"` // tool-specific metadata (e.g. exitCode)
104		IsError    bool            `json:"isError"`
105	}
106	
107	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path
108	// branch into the unified schema.SessionData. It honors compaction entries:
109	// when a compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId
110	// are dropped from the conversation (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
112		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		if header == nil {
117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
118		}
119		if header.Type != entrySession {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
121		}
122		if header.ID == "" {
123			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
124		}
125		if len(entries) == 0 {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
127		}
128		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
129		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
130	}
131	
132	// piProviderVersion derives the provider version string recorded on SessionData
133	// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
134	// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
135	func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
136		if header.Version > 0 {
137			return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
138		}
139		return "v1"
140	}
141	
142	// buildSessionData maps the ordered leaf-path entries into schema.SessionData.
143	func buildSessionData(header *sessionHeader, ordered []rawEntry) *schema.SessionData {
144		return &schema.SessionData{
145			SchemaVersion: "1.0",
146			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{
147				ID:      providerID,
148				Name:    providerName,
149				Version: piProviderVersion(header),
150			},
151			SessionID:     header.ID,
152			CreatedAt:     header.Timestamp,
153			WorkspaceRoot: header.Cwd,
154			Exchanges:     buildExchanges(ordered),
155		}
156	}
157	
158	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
159	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
160	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo. Control entries
161	// (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the conversation body.
162	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
163		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
164		var current *schema.Exchange
165		commit := func() {
166			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
167				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
168			}
169		}
170		for _, e := range ordered {
171			if e.Type != entryMessage {
172				continue
173			}
174			switch messageRole(e) {
175			case roleUser:
176				commit()
177				current = &schema.Exchange{
178					ExchangeID: e.ID,
179					StartTime:  e.Timestamp,
180					EndTime:    e.Timestamp,
181					Messages:   []schema.Message{buildUserMessage(e)},
182				}
183			case roleAssistant:
184				current = appendAssistant(current, e)
185			case roleToolResult:
186				mergeToolResult(current, e)
187			}
188		}
189		commit()
190		return exchanges
191	}
192	
193	// appendAssistant appends an assistant message to the current exchange, creating
194	// one if none exists yet.
195	func appendAssistant(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) *schema.Exchange {
196		if current == nil {
197			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
198		}
199		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, buildAgentMessages(e)...)
200		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
201		return current
202	}
203	
204	// messageRole extracts .message.role from a message entry.
205	func messageRole(e rawEntry) string {
206		var m struct {
207			Role string `json:"role"`
208		}
209		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m)
210		return m.Role
211	}
212	
213	// mergeToolResult folds a toolResult entry into the matching agent ToolInfo in
214	// the current exchange, keyed by toolCallId == ToolInfo.UseID. It also advances
215	// the exchange EndTime to the toolResult's timestamp so downstream stats that
216	// read the last exchange's EndTime report the real final-event time.
217	func mergeToolResult(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) {
218		if current == nil {
219			return
220		}
221		var tr toolResultMessage
222		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &tr); err != nil {
223			return
224		}
225		content := toolResultContent(tr)
226		for i := range current.Messages {
227			msg := &current.Messages[i]
228			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.UseID == tr.ToolCallID {
229				msg.Tool.Output = buildToolOutput(content, tr)
230				msg.Timestamp = e.Timestamp
231				current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
232				return
233			}
234		}
235	}
236	
237	// toolResultContent joins the text blocks of a toolResult message.
238	func toolResultContent(tr toolResultMessage) string {
239		var parts []string
240		for _, b := range tr.Content {
241			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
242				parts = append(parts, b.Text)
243			}
244		}
245		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
246	}
247	
248	// buildUserMessage maps a pi user message entry to a schema user Message.
249	// pi user content is either a plain string or an array of {type:text|image}.
250	func buildUserMessage(e rawEntry) schema.Message {
251		var um userMessage
252		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &um)
253		parts := userContentParts(um.Content)
254		return schema.Message{
255			ID:        e.ID,
256			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
257			Role:      schema.RoleUser,
258			Content:   parts,
259		}
260	}
261	
262	// userContentParts decodes a pi user message's content (string or array) into
263	// schema ContentParts. Image blocks are dropped in v1 (recorded as a gap).
264	func userContentParts(raw json.RawMessage) []schema.ContentPart {
265		if len(raw) == 0 {
266			return nil
267		}
268		if raw[0] == '"' {
269			var s string
270			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
271				return []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: s}}
272			}
273		}
274		var blocks []contentBlock
275		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
276			return nil
277		}
278		var parts []schema.ContentPart
279		for _, b := range blocks {
280			if b.Type == schema.ContentTypeText && b.Text != "" {
281				parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
282			}
283		}
284		return parts
285	}
286	
287	// buildAgentMessages maps a pi assistant message entry to one or more schema
288	// Messages: one Message holds the text+thinking content parts; each toolCall
289	// block becomes its own agent Message carrying a ToolInfo.
290	func buildAgentMessages(e rawEntry) []schema.Message {
291		var am assistantMessage
292		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &am); err != nil {
293			return nil
294		}
295		var parts []schema.ContentPart
296		var messages []schema.Message
297		for _, b := range am.Content {
298			switch b.Type {
299			case schema.ContentTypeText:
300				if b.Text != "" {
301					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
302				}
303			case schema.ContentTypeThinking:
304				if b.Thinking != "" {
305					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: b.Thinking})
306				}
307			case "toolCall":
308				messages = append(messages, buildToolMessage(e, b, am))
309			}
310		}
311		if len(parts) > 0 {
312			head := schema.Message{
313				ID:        e.ID,
314				Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
315				Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
316				Model:     am.Model,
317				Content:   parts,
318				Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
319			}
320			return append([]schema.Message{head}, messages...)
321		}
322		if len(messages) == 0 {
323			return buildErrorMessage(e, am)
324		}
325		// Tool-call-only assistant message: carry model+usage once on the first
326		// tool message so no metadata is lost and no schema-invalid empty message
327		// is emitted.
328		messages[0].Model = am.Model
329		if messages[0].Usage == nil {
330			messages[0].Usage = mapUsage(am.Usage)
331		}
332		return messages
333	}
334	
335	// buildToolMessage builds an agent Message wrapping a ToolInfo from a toolCall.
336	// The parent assistant message's model is passed through so tool messages carry
337	// the same model metadata as text/thinking messages. The Message ID is derived
338	// from the parent entry id + the toolCall id, so multiple toolCalls in one
339	// assistant message get distinct Message IDs (downstream provenance keys use
340	// msg.ID as a deterministic component).
341	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
342		return schema.Message{
343			ID:        toolMessageID(e.ID, b.ID),
344			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
345			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
346			Model:     am.Model,
347			Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{
348				Name:  b.Name,
349				Type:  classifyToolType(b.Name),
350				UseID: b.ID,
351				Input: b.Args,
352			},
353		}
354	}
355	
356	// toolMessageID builds a unique Message ID for a tool-call message from the
357	// parent entry id and the toolCall id. This avoids duplicate Message IDs when a
358	// single assistant entry contains multiple toolCall blocks.
359	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {
360		if callID != "" {
361			return entryID + ":" + callID
362		}
363		return entryID
364	}
365	
366	// buildToolOutput constructs the ToolInfo.Output map from a toolResult's
367	// content, error flag, and optional details blob. details (e.g. exitCode) is
368	// decoded into a generic value so downstream consumers (markdown rendering,
369	// cloud) can surface structured tool metadata without re-parsing raw JSON.
370	func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
371		out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
372		if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
373			var details any
374			if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {
375				out["details"] = details
376			}
377		}
378		return out
379	}
380	
381	// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map
382	// to InputTokens/OutputTokens; cacheRead/cacheWrite map to the Claude-style
383	// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics).
384	func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
385		if u == nil {
386			return nil
387		}
388		return &schema.Usage{
389			InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
390			OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
391			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
392			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
393		}
394	}
395	
396	// buildErrorMessage surfaces an assistant entry with stopReason=error and an
397	// empty content array (no text/thinking/toolCalls) as an agent text message so
398	// the error event is not dropped from the transcript (and compaction boundaries
399	// stay interpretable). Returns nil if there is no errorMessage to surface.
400	func buildErrorMessage(e rawEntry, am assistantMessage) []schema.Message {
401		if strings.TrimSpace(am.ErrorMessage) == "" {
402			return nil
403		}
404		return []schema.Message{{
405			ID:        e.ID,
406			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
407			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
408			Model:     am.Model,
409			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "[error] " + am.ErrorMessage}},
410			Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
411		}}
412	}
413	
414	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
415	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
416	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
417	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
418		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
419			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
420				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
421					continue
422				}
423				for _, part := range msg.Content {
424					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {
425						return spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(t)
426					}
427				}
428			}
429		}
430		return ""
431	}
432	
433	// classifyToolType maps pi tool names to the schema tool-type taxonomy.
434	func classifyToolType(name string) string {
435		switch strings.ToLower(name) {
436		case "read":
437			return schema.ToolTypeRead
438		case "edit", "write":
439			return schema.ToolTypeWrite
440		case "bash", "ls":
441			return schema.ToolTypeShell
442		case "grep", "find", "web_search", "fetch_content":
443			return schema.ToolTypeSearch
444		case "until_done_set", "until_done_plan", "until_done_task_update",
445			"until_done_progress", "until_done_complete", "until_done_block",
446			"until_done_replan", "until_done_distill":
447			return schema.ToolTypeTask
448		default:
449			return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
450		}
451	}
452	
453	// firstUserText extracts the first user message text from a message entry, if
454	// its role is "user". Returns "" for non-user messages or empty content.
455	func firstUserText(e rawEntry) string {
456		var m struct {
457			Role    string          `json:"role"`
458			Content json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
459		}
460		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m); err != nil {
461			return ""
462		}
463		if m.Role != roleUser {
464			return ""
465		}
466		return userContentString(m.Content)
467	}
468	
469	// userContentString extracts a plain string from a pi user message content
470	// field (either a string or an array of {type:text} blocks). The result is
471	// trimmed so the scan path produces the same Slug/Name as the full-parse path
472	// (deriveSlug trims too).
473	func userContentString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
474		if len(raw) == 0 {
475			return ""
476		}
477		var s string
478		if raw[0] == '"' {
479			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
480				return strings.TrimSpace(s)
481			}
482		}
483		var blocks []contentBlock
484		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
485			return ""
486		}
487		for _, b := range blocks {
488			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
489				return strings.TrimSpace(b.Text)
490			}
491		}
492		return ""
493	}
494

function createSessionId(): string {
	return uuidv7();
}

export function assertValidSessionId(id: string): void {
	if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9._-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?$/.test(id)) {
		throw new Error(
			"Session id must be non-empty, contain only alphanumeric characters, '-', '_', and '.', and start and end with an alphanumeric character",
		);
	}
}

/** Generate a unique short ID (8 hex chars, collision-checked) */
function generateId(byId: { has(id: string): boolean }): string {
	for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
		const id = randomUUID().slice(0, 8);
		if (!byId.has(id)) return id;
	}
	// Fallback to full UUID if somehow we have collisions
	return randomUUID();
}

/** Migrate v1 → v2: add id/parentId tree structure. Mutates in place. */
function migrateV1ToV2(entries: FileEntry[]): void {
	const ids = new Set<string>();
	let prevId: string | null = null;

	for (const entry of entries) {
		if (entry.type === "session") {
			entry.version = 2;
			continue;
		}

		entry.id = generateId(ids);
		entry.parentId = prevId;
		prevId = entry.id;

		// Convert firstKeptEntryIndex to firstKeptEntryId for compaction
		if (entry.type === "compaction") {
			const comp = entry as CompactionEntry & { firstKeptEntryIndex?: number };
			if (typeof comp.firstKeptEntryIndex === "number") {
				const targetEntry = entries[comp.firstKeptEntryIndex];
				if (targetEntry && targetEntry.type !== "session") {
					comp.firstKeptEntryId = targetEntry.id;
				}
				delete comp.firstKeptEntryIndex;
			}
		}
	}
}

/** Migrate v2 → v3: rename hookMessage role to custom. Mutates in place. */
function migrateV2ToV3(entries: FileEntry[]): void {
	for (const entry of entries) {
		if (entry.type === "session") {
			entry.version = 3;
			continue;
		}

		// Update message entries with hookMessage role
		if (entry.type === "message") {
			const msgEntry = entry as SessionMessageEntry;
			if (msgEntry.message && (msgEntry.message as { role: string }).role === "hookMessage") {
				(msgEntry.message as { role: string }).role = "custom";
			}
		}
	}
}

/**
 * Run all necessary migrations to bring entries to current version.
 * Mutates entries in place. Returns true if any migration was applied.
 */
function migrateToCurrentVersion(entries: FileEntry[]): boolean {
	const header = entries.find((e) => e.type === "session") as SessionHeader | undefined;
	const version = header?.version ?? 1;

	if (version >= CURRENT_SESSION_VERSION) return false;

	if (version < 2) migrateV1ToV2(entries);
	if (version < 3) migrateV2ToV3(entries);

	return true;
}

/** Exported for testing */
export function migrateSessionEntries(entries: FileEntry[]): void {
	migrateToCurrentVersion(entries);
}

107	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL v3 session file and maps its current leaf-path
108	// branch into the unified schema.SessionData. It honors compaction entries:
109	// when a compaction entry is on the leaf path, entries before firstKeptEntryId
110	// are dropped from the conversation (matching pi's buildContextEntries).
111	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
112		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		if header == nil {
117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
118		}
119		if header.Type != entrySession {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
121		}
122		if header.ID == "" {
123			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
124		}
125		if len(entries) == 0 {
126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
127		}
128		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
129		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
130	}

132	// piProviderVersion derives the provider version string recorded on SessionData
133	// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
134	// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
135	func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
136		if header.Version > 0 {
137			return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
138		}
139		return "v1"
140	}

142	// buildSessionData maps the ordered leaf-path entries into schema.SessionData.
143	func buildSessionData(header *sessionHeader, ordered []rawEntry) *schema.SessionData {
144		return &schema.SessionData{
145			SchemaVersion: "1.0",
146			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{
147				ID:      providerID,
148				Name:    providerName,
149				Version: piProviderVersion(header),
150			},
151			SessionID:     header.ID,
152			CreatedAt:     header.Timestamp,
153			WorkspaceRoot: header.Cwd,
154			Exchanges:     buildExchanges(ordered),
155		}

158	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
159	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
160	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo. Control entries
161	// (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the conversation body.
162	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
163		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
164		var current *schema.Exchange
165		commit := func() {
166			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
167				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
168			}
169		}
170		for _, e := range ordered {
171			if e.Type != entryMessage {
172				continue
173			}
174			switch messageRole(e) {
175			case roleUser:
176				commit()
177				current = &schema.Exchange{
178					ExchangeID: e.ID,
179					StartTime:  e.Timestamp,
180					EndTime:    e.Timestamp,
181					Messages:   []schema.Message{buildUserMessage(e)},
182				}
183			case roleAssistant:
184				current = appendAssistant(current, e)
185			case roleToolResult:
186				mergeToolResult(current, e)
187			}
188		}
189		commit()
190		return exchanges

487		for _, b := range blocks {
488			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
489				return strings.TrimSpace(b.Text)

491		}
