```text
14	
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// Skip entries missing the envelope fields the tree walk and exchange
91			// grouping rely on; a stray entry with no id can mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" || e.ID == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type or id", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			entries = append(entries, e)
97			return nil
98		})
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, nil, err
101		}
102		return header, entries, nil
103	}
104	
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
```

```text
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))

125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {

135			if cur.ParentID == nil {

137			}

159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
187	
188	// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
189	// if not found.
190	func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
191		for i, e := range path {
192			if e.ID == keptID {
193				return i
194			}
195		}
196		return -1
197	}
```

Title: readHeader buffers unbounded first JSON value with no size cap, unlike codexcli's 64KB header limit and piagent's own 250MB line cap
File: specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/provider.go line 164
Description: readHeader uses json.NewDecoder(f).Decode(&h), which reads and buffers the ENTIRE first JSON value of the file with no size limit before decoding. It is called on every *.jsonl file in the project's pi session dir by findProjectSession and listProjectSessions, i.e. on every `specstory sync` / `specstory sync -u <id>` for the project. A local attacker (or corrupt tool) who drops a .jsonl into ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/ whose first JSON value is multi-GB (e.g. {"type":"session","id":"x","pad":"AAAA..."}) causes the CLI to buffer the whole value in RAM on every invocation, with no error/skip path — potentially OOM-killing the process before any of piagent's other guards run. This deviates from BOTH accepted siblings: codexcli's equivalent header probes hard-cap the meta line at 64KB (loadCodexSessionMeta uses a default bufio.Scanner, and scanCodexSessionHeader explicitly errors with 'codex session meta exceeds line limit' at bufio.MaxScanTokenSize), and every other content read in piagent itself (readLines, used by readEntries/scanPiSession) enforces the 250MB maxReasonableLineSize cap that jsonl_parser.go documents as the OOM guard. readHeader bypasses readLines entirely and applies no check. Impact is bounded (allocation is transient, and a file passing the probe still hits the 250MB cap inside ParseSession), hence low severity — but it is the only header/content read path in piagent, claudecode, or codexcli with no size discipline at all.

```text
362	}
363	
364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
409	
410	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {
414			return nil
415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
420			Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
421			NativePath: path,
422			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
423		}
424	}
425
```

```text
// TestFormatEntries_CompactionMissingKeptIdDropsPreCompaction asserts the
// fallback: when firstKeptEntryId is not found in the leaf path, pre-compaction
// entries are still dropped (kept from the compaction entry forward).
func TestFormatEntries_CompactionMissingKeptIdDropsPreCompaction(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := ParseSession(loadFixture(t, "compaction_missing.jsonl"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParseSession returned error: %v", err)
	}
	var hasPre, hasPost bool
	for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
		for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
			for _, part := range msg.Content {
				if strings.Contains(part.Text, "before compaction") {
					hasPre = true
				}
				if strings.Contains(part.Text, "after compaction") {
					hasPost = true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if hasPre {
		t.Error("pre-compaction user prompt retained when firstKeptEntryId was missing")
	}
	if !hasPost {
		t.Error("post-compaction user prompt was dropped in the missing-kept-id fallback")
	}
}
```

```text
37	// Check verifies the pi binary is on PATH and reports its version.
38	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
39		cmdName := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand)
40		isCustom := cmdName != ""
41		if cmdName == "" {
42			cmdName = defaultCmd
43		}
44		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
45		if err != nil {
46			slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
47			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "not_found", err.Error())
48			return spi.CheckResult{
49				Success:      false,
50				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi binary '%s' not found on PATH", cmdName),
51			}
52		}
53		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
54		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
55		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
56		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
57		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
58			slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err)
59			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, "version_probe_failed", err.Error())
60			return spi.CheckResult{
61				Success:      false,
62				Location:     resolved,
63				ErrorMessage: fmt.Sprintf("pi version probe failed: %v", err),
64			}
65		}
66		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
67		if version == "" {
68			version = "unknown"
69		}
70		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
71		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
72	}

136	// findProjectSession locates the session file with the given ID within the
137	// project's pi session directory. Returns "" if not found.
138	func findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
139		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
140		if err != nil {
141			return "", err
142		}
143		for _, f := range files {
144			h, err := readHeader(f)
145			if err != nil || h == nil {
146				continue
147			}
148			if h.ID == sessionID {
149				return f, nil
150			}
151		}
152		return "", nil
153	}
154	
155	// readHeader parses only the first line of a session file and returns it only
156	// if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty id).
157	// Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them.
158	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
159		f, err := os.Open(path)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, err
162		}
163		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
164		dec := json.NewDecoder(f)
165		var h sessionHeader
166		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
170			return nil, nil
171		}
172		return &h, nil
173	}
174	
175	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
176	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
177	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
178	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
179		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, err
182		}
183		var out []sessionFile
184		for _, f := range files {
185			h, err := readHeader(f)
186			if err != nil {
187				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
188				continue
189			}
190			if h == nil {
191				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
192			}
193			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}

200		path, err := findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID)
201		if err != nil {
202			return nil, err
203		}
204		if path == "" {
205			return nil, nil
206		}
207		return parseToAgentSession(path, debugRaw)

210	// GetAgentChatSessions returns all pi sessions for the project.
211	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
212		files, err := listProjectSessions(projectPath)
213		if err != nil {
214			return nil, err
215		}
216		total := len(files)
217		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
218		for i, sf := range files {
219			chat, pErr := parseToAgentSession(sf.Path, debugRaw)
220			if pErr != nil {
221				slog.Debug("pi: skipping session", "path", sf.Path, "error", pErr)
222			} else if chat != nil {
223				result = append(result, *chat)
224			}
225			if progress != nil {
226				progress(i+1, total)
227			}
228		}
229		return result, nil
230	}

232	// parseToAgentSession parses one session file into an AgentChatSession,
233	// writing debug-raw artifacts when debugRaw is true.
234	func parseToAgentSession(path string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
235		data, err := ParseSession(path)
236		if err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239		if debugRaw {
240			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(path, data); dErr != nil {
241				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
242			}
243		}
244		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
245		if err != nil {
246			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
247		}
248		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
249			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
250			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
251			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
252			SessionData: data,
253			RawData:     string(raw),
254		}, nil
255	}

281		return &spi.AgentChatSession{

283			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
284			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
285			SessionData: data,
286			RawData:     string(raw),
287		}, nil
288	}
289	
290	// ListAgentChatSessions returns lightweight metadata for all project sessions,
291	// deriving Slug/Name from the first user message via a bounded single-pass scan
292	// (no full parse), matching how other providers populate metadata.
293	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
294		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
295		if err != nil {
296			return nil, err
297		}
298		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
299		for _, f := range files {
300			scan, scanErr := scanPiSession(f)
301			if scanErr != nil {
302				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", scanErr)
303				continue
304			}
305			if scan == nil || !scan.foundUser {
306				continue
307			}
308			result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
309				SessionID: scan.sessionID,
310				CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
311				Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
312				Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
313			})
314		}
315		return result, nil
316	}
317	
318	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every pi session across all projects,
319	// each ref carrying its originating cwd (read from the session header).
320	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
321		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
322	}
323	
324	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all pi sessions with live scan
325	// progress, using the shared parallel scanner. Each ref carries Slug/Name
326	// derived from the first user message and the originating cwd from the header.
327	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
328		root, err := piSessionsRoot()
329		if err != nil {
330			return nil, err
331		}
332		if _, statErr := os.Stat(root); statErr != nil {
333			if os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
334				return nil, nil
335			}
336			return nil, statErr
337		}
338		scan := func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
339			s, sErr := scanPiSession(path)
340			if sErr != nil {
341				return nil, sErr
342			}
343			if s == nil {
344				return nil, nil // non-session file
345			}
346			return scanToGlobalRef(s, path), nil
347		}
348		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)
349	}
350	
351	// piSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one bounded
352	// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan
353	// stops as soon as it has the first user message, so it does NOT parse the whole
354	// session. foundUser is false for sessions with no real user prompt; scanPiSession
355	// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
356	type piSessionScan struct {
357		sessionID        string
358		timestamp        string
359		firstUserMessage string
360		cwd              string
361		foundUser        bool
362	}
363	
364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}
371		headerRead := false
372		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
373			if !headerRead {
374				var h sessionHeader
375				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
376					return errStopRead // not a pi session (bad first line)
377				}
378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
409	
410	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
411	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
412	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
413		if !scan.foundUser {
414			return nil
415		}
416		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
417			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
418			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
419			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
420			Name:       spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage),
421			NativePath: path,
422			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
423		}
424	}
425
```

```text
105	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root,
106	// reverses to chronological order, and applies compaction: if a compaction
107	// entry is on the path, entries before its firstKeptEntryId are dropped.
108	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
109		byID := indexByID(entries)
110		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
111		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
112		reverse(path)
113		return applyCompaction(path)
114	}
115	
116	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
117	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
118		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			m[e.ID] = e
121		}
122		return m
123	}
124	
125	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
126	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
127	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
128	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
129		var path []rawEntry
130		cur := leaf
131		visited := make(map[string]bool)
132		for !visited[cur.ID] {
133			visited[cur.ID] = true
134			path = append(path, cur)
135			if cur.ParentID == nil {
136				break
137			}
138			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
139			if !ok {
140				break
141			}
142			cur = parent
143		}
144		return path
145	}
146	
147	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
148	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
149		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
150			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// applyCompaction drops entries before the most recent compaction point when
155	// one or more compaction entries are on the path. pi's buildContextEntries
156	// builds context from the LATEST compaction's firstKeptEntryId forward (each
157	// new compaction summarizes prior compactions into itself), so when multiple
158	// compactions exist we use the last one in chronological order, not the first.
159	// If firstKeptEntryId is missing from the path, we keep from the compaction
160	// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
161	func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
162		last := -1
163		for i, e := range path {
164			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
165				last = i
166			}
167		}
168		if last < 0 {
169			return path
170		}
171		keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
172		if keptID == "" {
173			return path[last:]
174		}
175		if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
176			return path[idx:]
177		}
178		return path[last:]
179	}
180	
181	// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
182	// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
183	// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
184	func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
185		return e.FirstKeptEntryID
186	}
187	
188	// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
189	// if not found.
190	func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
191		for i, e := range path {
192			if e.ID == keptID {
193				return i
194			}
195		}
196		return -1
197	}
```

```text
export { serializeConversation } from "./utils.js";
/** Generate compaction summary data from prepared session history. */
export async function compact(preparation, models, model, customInstructions, signal, thinkingLevel) {
    const { firstKeptEntryId, messagesToSummarize, turnPrefixMessages, isSplitTurn, tokensBefore, previousSummary, fileOps, settings, } = preparation;
    if (!firstKeptEntryId) {
        return err(new CompactionError("invalid_session", "First kept entry has no UUID - session may need migration"));
    }
    let summary;
    if (isSplitTurn && turnPrefixMessages.length > 0) {
        const historyResult = messagesToSummarize.length > 0
            ? await generateSummary(messagesToSummarize, models, model, settings.reserveTokens, signal, customInstructions, previousSummary, thinkingLevel)
            : ok("No prior history.");
        if (!historyResult.ok)
            return err(historyResult.error);
        const turnPrefixResult = await generateTurnPrefixSummary(turnPrefixMessages, models, model, settings.reserveTokens, signal, thinkingLevel);
        if (!turnPrefixResult.ok)
            return err(turnPrefixResult.error);
        summary = `${historyResult.value}\n\n---\n\n**Turn Context (split turn):**\n\n${turnPrefixResult.value}`;
    }
    else {
        const summaryResult = await generateSummary(messagesToSummarize, models, model, settings.reserveTokens, signal, customInstructions, previousSummary, thinkingLevel);
        if (!summaryResult.ok)
            return err(summaryResult.error);
        summary = summaryResult.value;
    }
    const { readFiles, modifiedFiles } = computeFileLists(fileOps);
    summary += formatFileOperations(readFiles, modifiedFiles);
    return ok({
        summary,
        firstKeptEntryId,
        tokensBefore,
        details: { readFiles, modifiedFiles },
    });
```

```text
7:{"type":"message","id":"be1","parentId":"a2","timestamp":"2026-07-09T10:00:05.000Z","message":{"role":"bashExecution","command":"echo hi","output":"hi","exitC
// entry forward so pre-compaction entries are never accidentally retained.
func applyCompaction(path []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
	last := -1
	for i, e := range path {
		if e.Type == entryCompaction {
			last = i
		}
	}
	if last < 0 {
		return path
	}
	keptID := compactionFirstKept(path[last])
	if keptID == "" {
		return path[last:]
	}
	if idx := keepFromIndex(path, keptID); idx >= 0 {
		return path[idx:]
	}
	return path[last:]
}

// compactionFirstKept returns the firstKeptEntryId of a compaction entry. pi
// stores this as a top-level field on the entry (not inside a message
// payload), so it is decoded directly into rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID.
func compactionFirstKept(e rawEntry) string {
	return e.FirstKeptEntryID
}

// keepFromIndex returns the index of the entry with id==keptID in path, or -1
// if not found.
func keepFromIndex(path []rawEntry, keptID string) int {
	for i, e := range path {
		if e.ID == keptID {
			return i
		}
	}
	return -1
}
```

```text
package piagent

import (
	"bufio"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
const (
	KB                    = 1024
	MB                    = 1024 * 1024
	maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
)

// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")

// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()

	reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
	lineNum := 0
	for {
		line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
		if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
			return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
		}
		line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
		lineNum++
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if trimmed != "" {
			if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
				slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
					"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
					"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
				return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
					lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
			}
			if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
				if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
					return nil
				}
				return vErr
			}
		}
		if readErr == io.EOF {
			return nil
		}
	}
}

// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
// rather than aborting the whole parse.

	var header *sessionHeader
	var entries []rawEntry
	err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
		if header == nil {
			h := sessionHeader{}
			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
```

```text
351	// piSessionScan holds the minimal fields read from a session file in one bounded
352	// pass: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd. The scan

355	// returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
356	type piSessionScan struct {

358		timestamp        string
359		firstUserMessage string

364	// scanPiSession reads minimal data from a pi session file in one bounded pass:
365	// the header (session id, timestamp, cwd) and the first user message text, then
366	// stops. Returns (scan, nil) for a real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session
367	// file or a session with no user message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse
368	// errors so ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
369	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
370		scan := &piSessionScan{}

378				if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
379					return errStopRead // not a pi session header
380				}
381				scan.sessionID = h.ID
382				scan.timestamp = h.Timestamp
383				scan.cwd = h.Cwd
384				headerRead = true
385				return nil
386			}
387			var e rawEntry
388			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
389				return nil // skip malformed line
390			}
391			if e.Type != entryMessage {
392				return nil
393			}
394			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
395				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
396				scan.foundUser = true
397				return errStopRead // got what we need; stop reading
398			}
399			return nil
400		})
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, err
403		}
404		if !headerRead || !scan.foundUser {
405			return nil, nil // non-session file or no user message
406		}
407		return scan, nil
408	}
```

```text
// formatDuration converts time.Duration to a human-readable string with words
func formatDuration(d time.Duration) string {
	if d < time.Microsecond {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f nanoseconds", float64(d.Nanoseconds()))
	} else if d < time.Millisecond {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f microseconds", float64(d.Nanoseconds())/1000)
	} else if d < time.Second {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f milliseconds", float64(d.Nanoseconds())/1000000)
	} else if d < time.Minute {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f seconds", d.Seconds())
	} else {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f minutes", d.Minutes())
	}
}
```

```text
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {

37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()

40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)

47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
```

```text
/** Migrate v1 → v2: add id/parentId tree structure. Mutates in place. */
function migrateV1ToV2(entries) {
    const ids = new Set();
    let prevId = null;
    for (const entry of entries) {
        if (entry.type === "session") {
            entry.version = 2;
            continue;
        }
        entry.id = generateId(ids);
        entry.parentId = prevId;
        prevId = entry.id;
        // Convert firstKeptEntryIndex to firstKeptEntryId for compaction
        if (entry.type === "compaction") {
            const comp = entry;
            if (typeof comp.firstKeptEntryIndex === "number") {
                const targetEntry = entries[comp.firstKeptEntryIndex];
                if (targetEntry && targetEntry.type !== "session") {
                    comp.firstKeptEntryId = targetEntry.id;
                }
                delete comp.firstKeptEntryIndex;
            }
        }
    }
}
/** Migrate v2 → v3: rename hookMessage role to custom. Mutates in place. */
function migrateV2ToV3(entries) {
    for (const entry of entries) {
        if (entry.type === "session") {
            entry.version = 3;
            continue;
        }
        // Update message entries with hookMessage role
        if (entry.type === "message") {
            const msgEntry = entry;
            if (msgEntry.message && msgEntry.message.role === "hookMessage") {
                msgEntry.message.role = "custom";
            }
        }
    }
```
```text
}

// extractSessionIDFromFile reads a JSONL file and returns the first sessionId found.
// Uses regex for fast extraction without full JSON parsing.
// Returns empty string if no sessionId is found.
func extractSessionIDFromFile(filePath string) (string, error) {
	file, err := os.Open(filePath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to open file: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = file.Close() }()

	reader := bufio.NewReader(file)

	for {
		line, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
		if err != nil && err != io.EOF {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("error reading file: %w", err)
		}

		// Try to find sessionId via regex (faster than JSON parsing)
		if matches := sessionIDRegex.FindStringSubmatch(line); len(matches) > 1 {
			return matches[1], nil
		}

		if err == io.EOF {
			break
		}
	}

	return "", nil
}

// ParseSingleSession parses sessions and filters to a specific UUID
func (p *JSONLParser) ParseSingleSession(projectPath string, sessionUuid string) error {
	// Parse only files matching this session (silent=true since this is for single session)
	if err := p.ParseProjectSessionsForSession(projectPath, true, sessionUuid); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// Filter to just the requested session
	filteredSessions := []Session{}
	for _, session := range p.Sessions {
		if session.SessionUuid == sessionUuid {
			filteredSessions = append(filteredSessions, session)
		}
	}

	if len(filteredSessions) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("no session found for UUID %s", sessionUuid)
	}

	p.Sessions = filteredSessions
	return nil
}

// parseSessionFile parses a single JSONL file and handles summaries and sidechains
func (p *JSONLParser) parseSessionFile(filePath string) ([]JSONLRecord, error) {
	slog.Info("Parsing session file", "file", filePath)

	// Clean debug directory for jsonl-burst mode only
	// (specstory-burst cleaning happens later during markdown generation)
	if GetJsonlBurst() {
		uuid := ExtractUUIDFromFilename(filePath)
		if err := CleanDebugDirectory(uuid); err != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to clean debug directory", "error", err)
		}
	}

	file, err := os.Open(filePath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open file: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = file.Close() }() // Read-only file; close errors not actionable

	// Use bufio.Reader instead of Scanner to handle arbitrarily large lines
	// Scanner has a token size limit (even with custom buffer), but Reader does not
	reader := bufio.NewReader(file)

	lineNumber := 0
	records := []JSONLRecord{}
	var lastNonSummaryRecord *JSONLRecord
	// pendingSummary holds a summary string when it appears before any records in the file.
	// This happens when the summary is on line 1 - we can't attach it to a previous record
	// because none exists yet, so we hold it and attach it to the next record we process.
	var pendingSummary string

	for {
		// Read line using ReadString which has no size limit
		line, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
		line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")

		// EOF is expected at end of file, other errors are genuine failures
		if err != nil && err != io.EOF {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("error reading line %d: %w", lineNumber+1, err)
		}

		// Determine if we're at end of file and if we have content to process
		atEOF := err == io.EOF
		hasContent := len(line) > 0

		// Increment line number for every line read (including empty lines) to match text editor line numbers
		if hasContent || !atEOF {
			lineNumber++
		}
```

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-10 17:57:02Z)**_

The full review is done: 7 domain reviewers + 3-skeptic verification per finding (86 agents total, every finding either reproduced empirically — including against real pi sessions on this machine and pi's actual source code — or refuted). Tests, vet, and lint all pass on the branch; the working tree is clean. Here's the complete picture.

## TL;DR

The PR is in good shape structurally — the parser was verified correct against real compacted/branched pi sessions, and nearly all of the 44 resolved Copilot threads are genuinely fixed. But the review surfaced **one significant design decision with underappreciated consequences (compaction truncates transcripts), one real enumeration bug (nested subagent session files), and a cluster of sibling-parity gaps** that make pi feel like a second-class provider in ways users will notice. Nothing here is a crash or corruption; the theme is silent data loss and silent no-ops.

---

## High concern

### 1. Compacted sessions lose their entire pre-compaction history — and the summary — from markdown, search, and stats

[jsonl_parser.go:161](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/jsonl_parser.go:161), [agent_session.go:171](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/agent_session.go:171)

`applyCompaction` drops everything before `firstKeptEntryId`, and `buildExchanges` skips `type=="compaction"` entries — so the compaction **summary** is dropped too (`rawEntry` never even decodes the `summary` field). Verifiers reproduced this on a real compacted session on your machine: ParseSession returned 7 exchanges starting mid-conversation with an agent-only `[error] 400` message; the opening prompt and 17 earlier messages are gone, with no marker that anything was removed.

This was a deliberate choice (the PR description says it mirrors pi's `buildContextEntries`) — but that function models pi's *LLM context window*, not its *transcript*. The result is worse than both reference points: claudecode/codexcli render every record in the file, and pi's own UI at least shows the summary. SpecStory shows neither, even though all the data is sitting right there in the file (and in `RawData`). Compaction hits exactly the long, valuable sessions, and sync/search/statistics all inherit the truncated view. **This is the main decision to make**: parse the full leaf path for the transcript (compaction only matters for context-building, not history), or at minimum surface the summary as a marker message.

## Medium concern

### 2. reindex ingests pi's nested subagent session files that nothing else can resolve

[provider.go:348](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/provider.go:348)

`ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress` hands the sessions root to `spi.ScanSessionsInParallel`, which walks **recursively** — but pi stores subagent runs at `<session>/<hash>/run-0/session.jsonl` inside the project dir, while `SessionFilesInProject` is non-recursive. On your machine, **14 of 35 enumerated pi refs are these nested files**. They get full sessions.db rows and appear in the resume/search TUI, but `GetAgentChatSession` can't find them (verified: `specstory sync pi -s <id>` → "Session not found", TUI preview degrades to the raw FTS fallback). Either the walk should skip nested dirs for pi, or the project-scoped lookup needs to handle them.

### 3. Slug/Name diverge between the scan path and the full parse

[provider.go:369](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/provider.go:369), [agent_session.go:417](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/agent_session.go:417)

`scanPiSession` takes the first user message in **file order**; `deriveSlug` takes the first user message on the **compaction-trimmed leaf path**. Verified on the PR's own `real_world.jsonl` fixture: scan slug `read-readme-md-and` vs parse slug `summarize-it-now`. So `specstory list` and the reindex DB row show one title while the sync markdown filename uses another — and the comment on `userContentString` claiming the two paths agree is simply false. (Also triggered by pi's root-branch re-edit, where an abandoned first prompt sits earlier in the file.) Note: fixing #1 by keeping the full leaf path would resolve most of this automatically.

### 4. `EncodeCwd` doesn't match pi's actual encoder for `:` and `\`

[path_utils.go:28](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/path_utils.go:28)

Verified against pi's installed source: pi replaces `/`, `\`, **and `:`** with `-` (`.replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-")`); `EncodeCwd` only replaces `/`. A project path containing a colon (legal on macOS/Linux) computes the wrong directory name → `SessionFilesInProject` returns empty → detect/sync/list silently find zero sessions. Rare input, but the failure mode is a total errorless miss, and the fix is one line.

### 5. `specstory list pi` / `sync pi` print *nothing* when no pi sessions exist

[provider.go:75](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/provider.go:75)

`DetectAgent` discards the `helpOutput` flag, but both CLI callers (main.go, list.go) rely on the provider to print the "no sessions found, here's what to do" guidance. Reproduced with a built binary: `specstory list pi` exits 0 with zero output while `specstory list claude` in the same directory prints full guidance. Pi is the only registered provider that goes silent — a bad first-run experience for exactly the users this PR targets. (This is also the strongest of the open Copilot threads.)

### 6. pi's `reasoning` token count is silently dropped

[agent_session.go:89](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/agent_session.go:89)

Real pi sessions carry a `reasoning` field in usage (531 of ~1,179 real assistant entries on your machine have the key). `piUsage`/`mapUsage` don't map it, even though the schema has the field siblings use (`ReasoningOutputTokens` for codexcli) and telemetry aggregates it. Pi under-reports thinking-token usage vs every other provider. Tiny fix.

### 7. Two tests are vacuous — their fixtures never exercise what the docstrings claim

[format_test.go:33](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/format_test.go:33), [format_test.go:406](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/format_test.go:406)

- `TestFormatEntries_ControlEntriesSkipped`: verifiers replayed the parser — all six control entries in `full_format.jsonl` are removed by *compaction* before `buildExchanges` ever runs, so the skip logic is never actually tested; four entry types never reach `buildExchanges` in any test.
- `TestFormatTree_Version1Legacy`: real v1 files have **no id/parentId** (confirmed in pi's source — `migrateV1ToV2` synthesizes them at load); the fixture models v1 as v3-shaped entries, so it passes against a shape that never existed. A genuine unmigrated v1 file would have every entry skipped and fail with "session has no entries" — yet still *appear* in list/reindex (scan doesn't need ids) while being unsyncable. Impact is limited (pi rewrites v1→v3 on open), but the test claims coverage it doesn't have.

## Low concern

- **`specstory watch pi` lies then exits 0** ([provider.go:90](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/provider.go:90)): prints "👀 Watching… Press Ctrl+C", then the stub error is swallowed by `WatchProviders` (logged to a discarded logger) and the process exits 0. Reproduced with a built binary. The stub itself is your declared v1 scope — the concern is only the *silent success theater*.
- **`check pi -c` doesn't tilde-expand or arg-split** ([provider.go:44](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/provider.go:44)): siblings run custom commands through `spi.SplitCommandLine` + tilde expansion; verified `-c "~/.nvm/.../bin/pi"` fails with a doubly-wrong "not found on PATH" message while the identical droid invocation works.
- **Version-probe stderr is dead code** ([provider.go:53](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/provider.go:53)): captured into a buffer that is never read; siblings surface it in the error message and analytics.
- **Tool rendering uses the generic fallback** ([agent_session.go:143](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/agent_session.go:143)): pi is the only provider that never sets `ToolInfo.FormattedMarkdown`, so bash/edit tool calls render as key-value dumps instead of fenced blocks. Rendering quality, not data loss.
- **No TUI accent color for "pi"** ([session_tui_browser.go:177](specstory-cli/pkg/cmd/session_tui_browser.go:177)): pi rows render fallback gray in resume/search; one-line addition.
- **README table implies full parity** ([README.md:34](specstory-cli/README.md:34)): the sync/list/search/reindex-only scope exists nowhere user-facing — only inside the runtime error string.
- **`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` / `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` ignored** ([path_utils.go:18](specstory-cli/pkg/providers/piagent/path_utils.go:18)): pi documents these; codexcli honors the analogous `CODEX_HOME`, though claudecode ignores `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so precedent is split.
- **Deferred/uncertain** (verifiers split, impact debatable): pi's `session_info` display names ignored (user-named sessions get first-prompt titles); `PathHints` never populated (pi produces zero provenance events); `bashExecution` dropped (already item 5 in your PR's follow-up list, so just confirming it's tracked).

```text
1	package droidcli
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"os/exec"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"log/slog"
10	
11		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
12	)
13	
14	func parseDroidCommand(customCommand string) (string, []string) {
15		if strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != "" {
16			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
17			if len(parts) > 0 {
18				return expandTilde(parts[0]), parts[1:]
19			}
20		}
21		return defaultFactoryCommand, nil
22	}
23	
24	func expandTilde(path string) string {
25		if strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
26			homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
27			if err == nil {
28				return filepath.Join(homeDir, path[2:])
29			}
30		}
31		return path
32	}
33	
34	func ExecuteDroid(customCommand string, resumeSessionID string) error {
35		cmd, args := parseDroidCommand(customCommand)
36		args = ensureResumeArgs(args, resumeSessionID)
37		if resumeSessionID != "" {
38			slog.Info("ExecuteDroid: resuming session", "sessionId", resumeSessionID)
39		}
40	
41		command := exec.Command(cmd, args...)
42		command.Stdin = os.Stdin
43		command.Stdout = os.Stdout
44		command.Stderr = os.Stderr
45	
46		return command.Run()
47	}
48	
49	func ensureResumeArgs(args []string, resumeSessionID string) []string {
50		if resumeSessionID == "" {
51			return args
52		}
53	
54		for i, arg := range args {
55			if arg == "--resume" || arg == "-r" {
56				if i+1 < len(args) {
57					return args
58				}
59			}
60			if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--resume=") {
61				return args
62			}
63		}
64	
65		return append(args, "--resume", resumeSessionID)
66	}
```

```text
58	// expandTilde expands ~ to the user's home directory
59	func expandTilde(path string) string {
60		if strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
61			homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
62			if err == nil {
63				return filepath.Join(homeDir, path[2:])
64			}
65		}
66		return path

69	// parseClaudeCommand parses a custom command string into executable and arguments.
70	// If customCommand is empty, returns the default command.
71	// If resumeSessionId is provided, appends "--resume <sessionId>" to the arguments.
72	// Supports quoted strings with spaces: claude --arg "value with spaces"
73	// Example: "claude --model gpt-4" returns ("claude", ["--model", "gpt-4"])
74	func parseClaudeCommand(customCommand string, resumeSessionId string) (string, []string) {
75		var cmd string
76		var args []string
77	
78		if customCommand == "" {
79			cmd = getDefaultClaudeCommand()
80			args = nil
81		} else {
82			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
83			if len(parts) == 0 {
84				cmd = getDefaultClaudeCommand()
85				args = nil
86			} else {
87				// Expand tilde in the command path
88				cmd = expandTilde(parts[0])
89				args = parts[1:]
90			}
91		}
92	
93		// Append --resume flag if sessionId is provided
94		if resumeSessionId != "" {
95			args = append(args, "--resume", resumeSessionId)
96		}
97	
98		return cmd, args
99	}

101	// ExecuteClaude runs the Claude CLI with the given arguments
102	func ExecuteClaude(customCommand string, resumeSessionId string) error {
103		// Parse the command and any custom arguments
104		claudeCmd, customArgs := parseClaudeCommand(customCommand, resumeSessionId)
105	
106		// Log if resuming a session
107		if resumeSessionId != "" {
108			slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Resuming session", "sessionId", resumeSessionId)
109		}
110	
111		// Create the command
112		cmd := exec.Command(claudeCmd, customArgs...)
113	
114		// Set up stdin/stdout/stderr to match the parent process
115		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
116		cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
117		cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
118	
119		// Start the command
120		slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Starting Claude Code process")
121		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
122			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start claude: %v", err)
123		}
124	
125		// Wait for the command to complete
126		slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Waiting for Claude Code to exit")
127		if err := cmd.Wait(); err != nil {
128			// Don't return error if the command exited with a non-zero status
129			// This is normal for many CLI applications
130			if exitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
131				exitCode := exitErr.ExitCode()
132				slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Claude Code exited", "exitCode", exitCode)
133				os.Exit(exitCode)
134			}
135			return fmt.Errorf("claude execution failed: %v", err)
136		}
137	
138		slog.Info("ExecuteClaude: Claude Code exited normally", "exitCode", 0)
139		return nil
140	}
```

```text
168	func runCodexVersionCommand(command string) (string, string, string, error) {
169		flags := []string{"--version", "-V"}
170		var lastErr error
171		var lastStderr string
172	
173		for idx, flag := range flags {

175			var stderr bytes.Buffer
176

179			cmd.Stderr = &stderr

188				if classifyCheckError(err) != "unknown" || idx == len(flags)-1 {
189					return "", flag, lastStderr, err
190				}
191				continue
192			}
193	
194			output := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
195			if output == "" {
196				return "", flag, stderrStr, errNoVersionOutput
197			}
198	
199			return output, flag, stderrStr, nil
200		}
201	
202		if lastErr != nil {

210	func classifyCheckError(err error) string {
211		if err == nil {
212			return ""
213		}
214	
215		var execErr *exec.Error
216		if errors.As(err, &execErr) && execErr.Err == exec.ErrNotFound {
217			return "not_found"
218		}
219	
220		var pathErr *os.PathError
221		if errors.As(err, &pathErr) {
222			if errors.Is(pathErr.Err, os.ErrNotExist) {
223				return "not_found"
224			}
225			if errors.Is(pathErr.Err, os.ErrPermission) {
226				return "permission_denied"
227			}
228		}
229	
230		if errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission) {
231			return "permission_denied"
232		}
233	
234		if errors.Is(err, errNoVersionOutput) {
235			return "no_output"
236		}
237	
238		return "unknown"
239	}

257				"command", codexCmd,
258				"sessionID", resumeSessionID,
259				"customArgs", customArgs)
260			cmd = exec.Command(codexCmd, args...)
261		} else {
262			// Parse the command and get binary + args
263			codexCmd, args := parseCodexCommand(customCommand)
264

266				"command", codexCmd,
267				"args", args)

272		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
273		cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
274		cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
275	
276		// Run the command and wait for it to complete
```

```text
1	package spi
2	
3	import "strings"
4	
5	// SplitCommandLine splits a command line string into arguments, respecting quoted strings.
6	//
7	// Supports both single and double quotes. Quotes can be escaped with backslash.
8	// This is used by providers to parse custom command strings that may contain paths
9	// or arguments with spaces.
10	//
11	// Examples:
12	//   - "claude --debug" -> ["claude", "--debug"]
13	//   - `claude --config "~/My Settings/config.json"` -> ["claude", "--config", "~/My Settings/config.json"]
14	//   - `claude --msg 'It'\”s working'` -> ["claude", "--msg", "It's working"]
15	//   - `claude --path "C:\\Users\\test"` -> ["claude", "--path", "C:\Users\test"]
16	//
17	// Behavior:
18	//   - Single and double quotes are treated equivalently
19	//   - Backslash escapes the next character (including quotes and backslashes)
20	//   - Whitespace (space, tab, newline) outside quotes separates arguments
21	//   - Empty quoted strings are ignored (e.g., `cmd "" --arg` -> ["cmd", "--arg"])
22	//   - Unclosed quotes consume to end of string
23	func SplitCommandLine(s string) []string {
24		var args []string
25		var current strings.Builder
26		var inQuote rune // ' or " when inside quotes, 0 otherwise
27		var escaped bool
28	
29		for _, r := range s {
30			if escaped {
31				// Previous character was backslash, add this character literally
32				current.WriteRune(r)
33				escaped = false
34				continue
35			}
36	
37			if r == '\\' {
38				// Next character will be escaped
39				escaped = true
40				continue
41			}
42	
43			if inQuote != 0 {
44				// Inside quotes
45				if r == inQuote {
46					// End quote
47					inQuote = 0
48				} else {
49					current.WriteRune(r)
50				}
51				continue
52			}
53	
54			// Not inside quotes
55			if r == '"' || r == '\'' {
56				// Start quote
57				inQuote = r
58				continue
59			}
60	
61			if r == ' ' || r == '\t' || r == '\n' {
62				// Whitespace outside quotes - end of argument
63				if current.Len() > 0 {
64					args = append(args, current.String())
65					current.Reset()
66				}
67				continue
68			}
69	
70			// Regular character
71			current.WriteRune(r)
72		}
73	
74		// Add final argument if any
75		if current.Len() > 0 {
76			args = append(args, current.String())
77		}
78	
79		return args
80	}
81
```

```text
206

209			slog.Warn("schema validation: message.role must be 'user' or 'agent'",
```

```text
102			root = path.dirname(parent);
103		} else if (path.basename(parent) === "node_modules") {
104			root = parent;
105		}
106		if (!root) return undefined;
107		const rootParent = path.dirname(root);
108		if (path.basename(rootParent) === "lib") return { root, prefix: path.dirname(rootParent) };
109		// Windows global npm prefixes use `<prefix>\\node_modules`, which is
110		// indistinguishable from local project installs by path shape alone. Do not
111		// infer unsupported Windows custom prefixes without `npm root -g` evidence.
112		return undefined;
113	}

115	function getSelfUpdateCommandForMethod(
116		method: InstallMethod,
117		installedPackageName: string,
118		updatePackageTarget: SelfUpdatePackageTarget = installedPackageName,
119		npmCommand?: string[],
120	): SelfUpdateCommand | undefined {
121		const target = normalizeSelfUpdatePackageTarget(updatePackageTarget);
122		switch (method) {
123			case "bun-binary":
124				return undefined;
125			case "pnpm": {
126				const match = readCommandOutput("pnpm", ["root", "-g"])
127					? undefined
128					: /^(.*[\\/]global[\\/][^\\/]+)[\\/]\.pnpm[\\/]/.exec(getPackageDir());
129				const binDirArgs = match
130					? [`--config.global-bin-dir=${process.env.PNPM_HOME || dirname(dirname(match[1]))}`]
131					: [];
132				return makeSelfUpdateCommand(
133					makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("pnpm", [
134						"install",
135						"-g",
136						"--ignore-scripts",
137						"--config.minimumReleaseAge=0",
138						...binDirArgs,
139						target.installSpec,
140					]),
141					target.packageName === installedPackageName
142						? undefined
143						: makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("pnpm", ["remove", "-g", ...binDirArgs, installedPackageName]),
144				);
145			}
146			case "yarn":
147				return makeSelfUpdateCommand(
148					makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("yarn", ["global", "add", "--ignore-scripts", target.installSpec]),
149					target.packageName === installedPackageName
150						? undefined
151						: makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("yarn", ["global", "remove", installedPackageName]),
152				);
153			case "bun":
154				return makeSelfUpdateCommand(
155					makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("bun", [
156						"install",
157						"-g",
158						"--ignore-scripts",
159						"--minimum-release-age=0",
160						target.installSpec,
161					]),
162					target.packageName === installedPackageName
163						? undefined
164						: makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("bun", ["uninstall", "-g", installedPackageName]),
165				);
166			case "npm": {
167				const [command = "npm", ...npmArgs] = npmCommand ?? [];
168				const inferred = npmCommand?.length ? undefined : getInferredNpmInstall();
169				const prefixArgs = [...npmArgs, ...(inferred ? ["--prefix", inferred.prefix] : [])];
170				const installStep = makeSelfUpdateCommandStep(command, [
171					...prefixArgs,
172					"install",
173					"-g",
174					"--ignore-scripts",
175					"--min-release-age=0",
176					target.installSpec,
177				]);
178				const uninstallStep =
179					target.packageName === installedPackageName
180						? undefined
181						: makeSelfUpdateCommandStep(command, [...prefixArgs, "uninstall", "-g", installedPackageName]);
182				return makeSelfUpdateCommand(installStep, uninstallStep);
183			}
184			case "unknown":
185				return undefined;
186		}
187	}

189	function readCommandOutput(
190		command: string,
191		args: string[],
192		options: { requireSuccess?: boolean } = {},
193	): string | undefined {
194		const result = spawnProcessSync(command, args, {
195			encoding: "utf-8",
196			stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
197		});
198		if (result.status === 0) return result.stdout.trim() || undefined;
199		if (options.requireSuccess) {
200			const reason = result.error?.message || result.stderr.trim() || `exit code ${result.status ?? "unknown"}`;
201			throw new Error(`Failed to run ${[command, ...args].join(" ")}: ${reason}`);
202		}
203		return undefined;
204	}

206	function getGlobalPackageRoots(method: InstallMethod, _packageName: string, npmCommand?: string[]): string[] {
207		switch (method) {
208			case "npm": {
209				const configured = !!npmCommand?.length;
210				const [command = "npm", ...npmArgs] = npmCommand ?? [];
211				if (configured && command === "bun") {
212					const bunBin = readCommandOutput(command, [...npmArgs, "pm", "bin", "-g"], {
213						requireSuccess: true,
214					});
215					const roots = [join(homedir(), ".bun", "install", "global", "node_modules")];
216					if (bunBin) {
217						roots.push(join(dirname(bunBin), "install", "global", "node_modules"));
218					}
219					return roots;
220				}
221				const root = readCommandOutput(command, [...npmArgs, "root", "-g"], {
222					requireSuccess: configured,
223				});
224				const inferred = configured ? undefined : getInferredNpmInstall();
225				return [root, inferred?.root].filter((x): x is string => !!x);
226			}
227			case "pnpm": {
228				const root = readCommandOutput("pnpm", ["root", "-g"]);
229				if (root) return [root, dirname(root)];
230				const match = /^(.*[\\/]global[\\/][^\\/]+)[\\/]\.pnpm[\\/]/.exec(getPackageDir());
231				return match ? [match[1]] : [];
232			}
233			case "yarn": {
234				const dir = readCommandOutput("yarn", ["global", "dir"]);
235				return dir ? [dir, join(dir, "node_modules")] : [];
236			}
237			case "bun": {
238				const bunBin = readCommandOutput("bun", ["pm", "bin", "-g"]);
239				const roots = [join(homedir(), ".bun", "install", "global", "node_modules")];
240				if (bunBin) {
241					roots.push(join(dirname(bunBin), "install", "global", "node_modules"));
242				}
243				return roots;
244			}
245			case "bun-binary":
246			case "unknown":
247				return [];
248		}
249	}

251	function normalizeExistingPathForComparison(path: string, resolveSymlinks: boolean): string | undefined {
252		const resolvedPath = resolve(path);
253		if (!existsSync(resolvedPath)) {
254			return undefined;
255		}
256		let normalizedPath = resolvedPath;
257		if (resolveSymlinks) {
258			try {
259				normalizedPath = realpathSync(resolvedPath);
260			} catch {
261				return undefined;
262			}
263		}
264		if (process.platform === "win32") {
265			normalizedPath = normalizedPath.toLowerCase();
266		}
267		return normalizedPath;
268	}
269	
270	function getPathComparisonCandidates(path: string): string[] {
271		return Array.from(
272			new Set(
273				[normalizeExistingPathForComparison(path, false), normalizeExistingPathForComparison(path, true)].filter(
274					(candidate): candidate is string => !!candidate,
275				),
276			),
277		);
278	}

280	function getEntrypointPackageDir(): string | undefined {
281		const entrypoint = process.argv[1];
282		if (!entrypoint) return undefined;
283		let dir = dirname(entrypoint);
284		while (dir !== dirname(dir)) {
285			if (existsSync(join(dir, "package.json"))) {

287			}
288			dir = dirname(dir);

293	function isSelfUpdatePathWritable(): boolean {
294		const packageDir = getPackageDir();

304	function isManagedByGlobalPackageManager(method: InstallMethod, packageName: string, npmCommand?: string[]): boolean {
305		const packageDirs = [getPackageDir(), getEntrypointPackageDir()].filter((dir): dir is string => !!dir);
306		const packageDirCandidates = packageDirs.flatMap((dir) => getPathComparisonCandidates(dir));
307		return getGlobalPackageRoots(method, packageName, npmCommand).some((root) => {
308			return getPathComparisonCandidates(root).some((normalizedRoot) => {
309				const rootPrefix = normalizedRoot.endsWith(sep) ? normalizedRoot : `${normalizedRoot}${sep}`;
310				return packageDirCandidates.some((packageDir) => packageDir.startsWith(rootPrefix));
311			});
312		});
313	}

315	export function getSelfUpdateCommand(

317		npmCommand?: string[],

319	): SelfUpdateCommand | undefined {
320		const method = detectInstallMethod();
321		const command = getSelfUpdateCommandForMethod(method, packageName, updatePackageTarget, npmCommand);
322		if (!command || !isManagedByGlobalPackageManager(method, packageName, npmCommand) || !isSelfUpdatePathWritable()) {
323			return undefined;
```
