```text
export function normalizePath(input: string, options: PathInputOptions = {}): string {
	let normalized = options.trim ? input.trim() : input;
	if (options.normalizeUnicodeSpaces) {
		normalized = normalized.replace(UNICODE_SPACES, " ");
	}
	if (options.stripAtPrefix && normalized.startsWith("@")) {
		normalized = normalized.slice(1);
	}

	if (options.expandTilde ?? true) {
		const home = options.homeDir ?? homedir();
		if (normalized === "~") return home;
		if (normalized.startsWith("~/") || (process.platform === "win32" && normalized.startsWith("~\\"))) {
			return join(home, normalized.slice(2));
		}
	}

	if (/^file:\/\//.test(normalized)) {
		return fileURLToPath(normalized);
	}

	return normalized;
}

export function resolvePath(input: string, baseDir: string = process.cwd(), options: PathInputOptions = {}): string {
	const normalized = normalizePath(input, options);
	const normalizedBaseDir = normalizePath(baseDir);
	return isAbsolute(normalized) ? nodeResolvePath(normalized) : nodeResolvePath(normalizedBaseDir, normalized);
}

export function getCwdRelativePath(filePath: string, cwd: string): string | undefined {
	const resolvedCwd = resolvePath(cwd);
	const resolvedPath = resolvePath(filePath, resolvedCwd);
	const relativePath = relative(resolvedCwd, resolvedPath);
	const isInsideCwd =
		relativePath === "" ||
		(relativePath !== ".." && !relativePath.startsWith(`..${sep}`) && !isAbsolute(relativePath));

	return isInsideCwd ? relativePath || "." : undefined;
}

export function formatPathRelativeToCwdOrAbsolute(filePath: string, cwd: string): string {
	const absolutePath = resolvePath(filePath, cwd);
	return (getCwdRelativePath(absolutePath, cwd) ?? absolutePath).split(sep).join("/");
}

export function markPathIgnoredByCloudSync(path: string): void {
	const attrs =
		process.platform === "darwin"
			? ["com.dropbox.ignored", "com.apple.fileprovider.ignore#P"]
			: process.platform === "linux"
				? ["user.com.dropbox.ignored"]
				: [];

	for (const attr of attrs) {
		if (process.platform === "darwin") {
			spawnProcessSync("xattr", ["-w", attr, "1", path], { encoding: "utf-8", stdio: "ignore" });
		} else {
			spawnProcessSync("setfattr", ["-n", attr, "-v", "1", path], { encoding: "utf-8", stdio: "ignore" });
		}
	}
}
```

# Pi session/config semantics — verbatim extraction

Two parallel implementations exist. The **live/coding-agent** implementation is `packages/coding-agent/src/{config.ts,core/session-manager.ts,migrations.ts}`. A **newer harness** implementation lives in `packages/agent/src/harness/session/`. Both use the identical cwd-encoding and file-naming scheme. `APP_NAME` resolves to `"pi"` (from `package.json` `piConfig.name`, default `"pi"`), so all env var names are `PI_*`.

## 1. Env overrides — agent dir vs sessions dir

Env var names are **derived from `APP_NAME.toUpperCase()`** — `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/pi/packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:495-496`:
```ts
export const ENV_AGENT_DIR = `${APP_NAME.toUpperCase()}_CODING_AGENT_DIR`;
export const ENV_SESSION_DIR = `${APP_NAME.toUpperCase()}_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`;
```
So concretely: `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`.

**`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` points to the AGENT dir** (the `~/.pi/agent` equivalent), NOT the sessions dir. `config.ts:515-521`:
```ts
export function getAgentDir(): string {
	const envDir = process.env[ENV_AGENT_DIR];
	if (envDir) {
		return expandTildePath(envDir);
	}
	return join(homedir(), CONFIG_DIR_NAME, "agent");
}
```
`CONFIG_DIR_NAME` defaults to `.pi` (`config.ts:491`), so default agent dir = `~/.pi/agent`.

**The `"sessions"` subdir IS appended to the agent dir.** `config.ts:558-561`:
```ts
export function getSessionsDir(): string {
	return join(getAgentDir(), "sessions");
}
```
And the per-cwd default path re-appends `"sessions"` then the encoded cwd — `session-manager.ts:472-477`:
```ts
function getDefaultSessionDirPath(cwd: string, agentDir: string = getDefaultAgentDir()): string {
	const resolvedCwd = resolvePath(cwd);
	const resolvedAgentDir = resolvePath(agentDir);
	const safePath = `--${resolvedCwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, "").replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-")}--`;
	return join(resolvedAgentDir, "sessions", safePath);
}
```
So with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/x`, default sessions land at `/x/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/<file>.jsonl`.

**`PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` points to the sessions dir ITSELF** — used flat/directly, with no per-cwd encoding appended. Precedence resolution in `main.ts:572-576`:
```ts
	const envSessionDir = process.env[ENV_SESSION_DIR];
	const sessionDir =
		(parsed.sessionDir ? normalizePath(parsed.sessionDir) : undefined) ??
		(envSessionDir ? expandTildePath(envSessionDir) : undefined) ??
		startupSettingsManager.getSessionDir();
```
**Precedence (highest → lowest):** `--session-dir` (`parsed.sessionDir`) > `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` env > `settings.json` `sessionDir` (`settings-manager.ts:670-673`) > `undefined`. Help text confirms it — `cli/args.ts:375`: `Session storage directory (overridden by --session-dir)`.

When `sessionDir` stays `undefined`, `SessionManager.create/continueRecent/list` fall back to `getDefaultSessionDir(cwd)` (the per-cwd encoded dir under the agent dir). When an explicit `sessionDir` is given it's used **directly** — `SessionManager.create` (`session-manager.ts:1441-1444`):
```ts
	static create(cwd: string, sessionDir?: string, options?: NewSessionOptions): SessionManager {
		const dir = sessionDir ? normalizePath(sessionDir) : getDefaultSessionDir(cwd);
		return new SessionManager(cwd, dir, undefined, true, options);
	}
```
Because a custom flat dir can hold sessions from multiple cwds, `list`/`continueRecent` then filter by header cwd when `dir !== getDefaultSessionDirPath(cwd)` (`session-manager.ts:1470-1471`, `1550-1554`).

`expandTildePath` == `normalizePath` (`config.ts:498-500`), which expands a leading `~`/`~/` to `homedir()` by default (`utils/paths.ts:66-72`). `--session-dir` is parsed at `cli/args.ts:112-113` (`result.sessionDir = args[++i]`).

## 2. Cwd encoding (the replace chain)

`session-manager.ts:475` (verbatim), inside `getDefaultSessionDirPath`:
```ts
	const safePath = `--${resolvedCwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, "").replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-")}--`;
```
- The cwd is first `resolvePath()`-normalized.
- `.replace(/^[/\\]/, "")` strips a single leading `/` or `\`.
- `.replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-")` replaces every `/`, `\`, and `:` with `-`.
- Wrapped in leading and trailing `--`.

The identical function in the newer harness is named `encodeCwd` — `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/pi/packages/agent/src/harness/session/jsonl-repo.ts:34-36`:
```ts
function encodeCwd(cwd: string): string {
	return `--${cwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, "").replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-")}--`;
}
```
The migration copy is at `migrations.ts:112`. (There is no function literally named `buildSessionDir`/`getSessionDirName`; `getDefaultSessionDirPath` and `encodeCwd` are the actual names.)

Session **file name** within that dir — `session-manager.ts:883-884`:
```ts

			this.sessionFile = join(this.getSessionDir(), `${fileTimestamp}_${this.sessionId}.jsonl`);
```

## 3. `session_info` entries + current-session name resolution

Shape — `session-manager.ts:113-117`:
```ts
export interface SessionInfoEntry extends SessionEntryBase {
	type: "session_info";
	name?: string;
}
```
`SessionEntryBase` (`session-manager.ts:46-51`) contributes `type`, `id`, `parentId: string | null`, `timestamp`. Writing sanitizes the name — `appendSessionInfo`, `session-manager.ts:1065-1076`:
```ts
	appendSessionInfo(name: string): string {
		const sanitizedName = name.replace(/[\r\n]+/g, " ").trim();
		const entry: SessionInfoEntry = {
			type: "session_info",
			id: generateId(this.byId),
			parentId: this.leafId,
			timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
			name: sanitizedName,
		};
		this._appendEntry(entry);
		return entry.id;
	}
```
**Current display name resolves on FILE/APPEND order, not the leaf path.** `getSessionName` iterates `getEntries()` (which is `fileEntries` filtered — raw file order, not a tree walk) in reverse, returning the latest `session_info`; an empty name explicitly clears the title. `session-manager.ts:1078-1090`:
```ts
	getSessionName(): string | undefined {
		// Walk entries in reverse to find the latest session_info entry.
		// Empty names explicitly clear the session title.
		const entries = this.getEntries();
		for (let i = entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
			const entry = entries[i];
			if (entry.type === "session_info") {
				return entry.name?.trim() || undefined;
			}
		}
		return undefined;
	}
```
`getEntries()` = file order — `session-manager.ts:1230-1232`: `return this.fileEntries.filter((e): e is SessionEntry => e.type !== "session");`. The session-list loader independently uses the same "latest wins, empty clears" rule while streaming lines in file order — `buildSessionInfo`, `session-manager.ts:648-651`:
```ts
			// Extract session name (use latest, including explicit clears)
			if (entry.type === "session_info") {
				name = entry.name?.trim() || undefined;
			}
```

## 4. v1 legacy format + migrations

**v1 header has NO `version` field.** Detection defaults absent → 1. `session-manager.ts:277-287`:
```ts
function migrateToCurrentVersion(entries: FileEntry[]): boolean {
	const header = entries.find((e) => e.type === "session") as SessionHeader | undefined;
	const version = header?.version ?? 1;

	if (version >= CURRENT_SESSION_VERSION) return false;

	if (version < 2) migrateV1ToV2(entries);
	if (version < 3) migrateV2ToV3(entries);

	return true;
}
```
The header type documents this — `session-manager.ts:32-39`: `version?: number; // v1 sessions don't have this`. `CURRENT_SESSION_VERSION = 3` (`session-manager.ts:30`).

**v1 entries have NO `id`/`parentId`** (they are synthesized) and **v1 compaction used `firstKeptEntryIndex` (a numeric array index)**. `migrateV1ToV2` — `session-manager.ts:226-253` (verbatim):
```ts
/** Migrate v1 → v2: add id/parentId tree structure. Mutates in place. */
function migrateV1ToV2(entries: FileEntry[]): void {
	const ids = new Set<string>();
	let prevId: string | null = null;

	for (const entry of entries) {
		if (entry.type === "session") {
			entry.version = 2;
			continue;
		}

		entry.id = generateId(ids);
		entry.parentId = prevId;
		prevId = entry.id;

		// Convert firstKeptEntryIndex to firstKeptEntryId for compaction
		if (entry.type === "compaction") {
			const comp = entry as CompactionEntry & { firstKeptEntryIndex?: number };
			if (typeof comp.firstKeptEntryIndex === "number") {
				const targetEntry = entries[comp.firstKeptEntryIndex];
				if (targetEntry && targetEntry.type !== "session") {
					comp.firstKeptEntryId = targetEntry.id;
				}
				delete comp.firstKeptEntryIndex;
			}
		}
	}
}
```
So the synthesis is: header gets `version = 2`; each non-header entry gets `id = generateId(...)` (8 hex chars, `randomUUID().slice(0,8)` per `session-manager.ts:216-224`) and `parentId = prevId` (linear chain in file order, first entry gets `parentId = null`). Compaction's `firstKeptEntryIndex` is looked up as `entries[index]`, converted to that target entry's freshly-assigned `firstKeptEntryId`, and the old field is `delete`d. (Note: the `ids` set is created but never `.add()`-ed to during this loop, so the collision check against `ids` is effectively a no-op during v1→v2 migration.)

`migrateV2ToV3` only renames the message role `hookMessage` → `custom` and bumps header version to 3 — `session-manager.ts:255-271`:
```ts
/** Migrate v2 → v3: rename hookMessage role to custom. Mutates in place. */
function migrateV2ToV3(entries: FileEntry[]): void {
	for (const entry of entries) {
		if (entry.type === "session") {
			entry.version = 3;
			continue;
		}

		// Update message entries with hookMessage role
		if (entry.type === "message") {
			const msgEntry = entry as SessionMessageEntry;
			if (msgEntry.message && (msgEntry.message as { role: string }).role === "hookMessage") {
				(msgEntry.message as { role: string }).role = "custom";
			}
		}
	}
}
```

**Yes — pi REWRITES the migrated file to disk on open, and the header version becomes `3`.** `setSessionFile`, `session-manager.ts:845-853`:
```ts
			const header = this.fileEntries.find((e) => e.type === "session") as SessionHeader | undefined;
			this.sessionId = header?.id ?? createSessionId();

			if (migrateToCurrentVersion(this.fileEntries)) {
				this._rewriteFile();
			}

			this._buildIndex();
			this.flushed = true;
```
`_rewriteFile` (`session-manager.ts:910-920`) opens the file with `"w"` and rewrites every entry as one JSON line each. Because `migrateV1ToV2` sets `version = 2` then `migrateV2ToV3` sets `version = 3`, the persisted header ends at `version: 3`. (The newer harness rejects anything but v3 outright — `jsonl-storage.ts:70`: `if (header.version !== 3) throw invalidSession(filePath, "unsupported session version");` — i.e. the harness does not migrate; only the coding-agent `SessionManager` migrates+rewrites.)

## 5. Nested subagent / "run" sessions

**There is no `run-0/session.jsonl` (or any nested per-run directory) layout in pi.** Session files are always flat: `<sessionsRoot>/--<encoded-cwd>--/<timestamp>_<id>.jsonl`. A parent/child relationship between sessions is expressed **only** by the header's `parentSession` field (a path string), never by directory nesting.

- The built-in **subagent extension does not persist sessions at all** — it spawns a child `pi` process with `--no-session` and writes only the system prompt to an OS temp dir. `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/pi/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:294`:
  ```ts
	const args: string[] = ["--mode", "json", "-p", "--no-session"];
  ```
  and `index.ts:239-247` (`writePromptToTempFile`) uses `fs.promises.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "pi-subagent-"))` — a throwaway `$TMPDIR/pi-subagent-XXXX/prompt-*.md`, not the sessions tree. `--no-session` sets `noSession` (`cli/args.ts:104-105`), which suppresses persistence.

- **Forking** (the only "child session" mechanism) writes the new session into the *target cwd's normal encoded dir*, with `parentSession` set to the source file path — same cwd goes into the new header. `SessionManager.forkFrom` — `session-manager.ts:1508-1531`: `const dir = sessionDir ? ... : getDefaultSessionDir(resolvedTargetCwd);`, header `{ ..., cwd: resolvedTargetCwd, parentSession: resolvedSourcePath }`, filename `${fileTimestamp}_${newSessionId}.jsonl`. `createBranchedSession` (`session-manager.ts:1355-1364`) behaves the same, writing into `this.getSessionDir()` with `parentSession: previousSessionFile`. The harness `fork` mirrors this (`jsonl-repo.ts:134-161`, `parentSessionPath ?? sourceMetadata.path`).

So a subagent/child session, when persisted at all, is a sibling `.jsonl` in the same flat encoded-cwd dir, linked upward via `parentSession` — not a `run-N` subdirectory.

## 6. Compaction entries (v3)

Shape — `session-manager.ts:69-78` (verbatim):
```ts
export interface CompactionEntry<T = unknown> extends SessionEntryBase {
	type: "compaction";
	summary: string;
	firstKeptEntryId: string;
	tokensBefore: number;
	/** Extension-specific data (e.g., ArtifactIndex, version markers for structured compaction) */
	details?: T;
	/** True if generated by an extension, undefined/false if pi-generated (backward compatible) */
	fromHook?: boolean;
}
```
Top-level fields = `type`, `id`, `parentId`, `timestamp` (from `SessionEntryBase`, `session-manager.ts:46-51`) plus `summary`, `firstKeptEntryId`, `tokensBefore`. **`summary` (string) and `firstKeptEntryId` (string) are both required** (non-optional in the interface and always set by `appendCompaction`, `session-manager.ts:1027-1048`); `tokensBefore` required; `details?`/`fromHook?` optional. (Note `summary` is typed required but consumers guard on it — see below.)

**`buildContextEntries`: latest compaction wins.** `session-manager.ts:414-450` (verbatim):
```ts
export function buildContextEntries(
	entries: SessionEntry[],
	leafId?: string | null,
	byId?: Map<string, SessionEntry>,
): SessionEntry[] {
	const path = buildSessionPath(entries, leafId, byId);
	let compaction: CompactionEntry | null = null;

	for (const entry of path) {
		if (entry.type === "compaction") {
			compaction = entry;
		}
	}

	if (!compaction) {
		return path;
	}

	const compactionIdx = path.findIndex((entry) => entry.id === compaction.id);
	if (compactionIdx < 0) {
		return path;
	}

	const contextEntries: SessionEntry[] = [compaction];
	let foundFirstKept = false;
	for (let i = 0; i < compactionIdx; i++) {
		const entry = path[i];
		if (entry.id === compaction.firstKeptEntryId) {
			foundFirstKept = true;
		}
		if (foundFirstKept) {
			contextEntries.push(entry);
		}
	}
	contextEntries.push(...path.slice(compactionIdx + 1));
	return contextEntries;
}
```
Semantics: walk root→leaf path; the **last** compaction on the path wins (the loop overwrites `compaction` each time). The result is `[compaction, <entries from firstKeptEntryId .. compaction), <everything after compaction>]` — i.e. the compaction summary entry, then the kept tail starting at `firstKeptEntryId`, then all post-compaction entries. Older summarized entries before `firstKeptEntryId` are dropped. If `firstKeptEntryId` is never found in the pre-compaction slice, `foundFirstKept` stays false and nothing from before the compaction is kept.

Projection to LLM messages (where `summary` is actually read) — `sessionEntryToContextMessages`, `session-manager.ts:400-402`:
```ts
	if (entry.type === "compaction") {
		return [createCompactionSummaryMessage(entry.summary, entry.tokensBefore, entry.timestamp)];
	}
```
(For contrast, `branch_summary` projection is guarded on truthiness — `session-manager.ts:397` `entry.type === "branch_summary" && entry.summary` — whereas compaction is not guarded, consistent with `summary` being a required field on `CompactionEntry`.)

```go
func parseDroidCommand(customCommand string) (string, []string) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != "" {
		parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
		if len(parts) > 0 {
			return expandTilde(parts[0]), parts[1:]
		}
	}
	return defaultFactoryCommand, nil
}

func expandTilde(path string) string {
	if strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
		if err == nil {
			return filepath.Join(homeDir, path[2:])
		}
	}
	return path
}
```

```go
func expandTilde(path string) string {
	if strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
		homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()
		if err == nil {

func parseClaudeCommand(customCommand string, resumeSessionId string) (string, []string) {
	var cmd string
	var args []string

	if customCommand == "" {
		cmd = getDefaultClaudeCommand()
		args = nil
	} else {
		parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
		if len(parts) == 0 {
			cmd = getDefaultClaudeCommand()
			args = nil
		} else {
			// Expand tilde in the command path
			cmd = expandTilde(parts[0])
			args = parts[1:]
		}
	}

	// Append --resume flag if sessionId is provided
	if resumeSessionId != "" {
		args = append(args, "--resume", resumeSessionId)
	}

	return cmd, args
}
```

```go
func classifyCheckError(err error) string {
	var execErr *exec.Error
	var pathErr *os.PathError
	switch {
	case errors.As(err, &execErr) && execErr.Err == exec.ErrNotFound:
		return "not_found"
	case errors.As(err, &pathErr) && errors.Is(pathErr.Err, os.ErrPermission):
		return "permission_denied"
	case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
		return "permission_denied"
	default:
		return "version_failed"
	}
}
```

`buildCheckErrorMessage` (lines 245–270) — the `isCustom` branch distinguishes custom-path-not-found from not-on-PATH, and the default branch surfaces stderr:

```go
func buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType string, command string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
	var builder strings.Builder
	switch errorType {
	case "not_found":
		builder.WriteString("Factory Droid CLI was not found.\n\n")
		if isCustom {
			builder.WriteString("• Verify the custom path you provided is executable.\n")
			fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "• Provided command: %s\n", command)
		} else {
			builder.WriteString("• Install the Factory CLI and ensure `droid` is on your PATH.\n")
			builder.WriteString("• Re-run `specstory check droid` after installation.\n")
		}
	case "permission_denied":
		builder.WriteString("SpecStory cannot execute the Factory CLI due to permissions.\n\n")
		fmt.Fprintf(&builder, "Try: chmod +x %s\n", command)
	default:
		builder.WriteString("`droid --version` failed.\n\n")
		if stderr != "" {
			builder.WriteString("Error output:\n")
			builder.WriteString(stderr)
			builder.WriteString("\n\n")
		}
		builder.WriteString("Run `droid --version` manually to diagnose, then retry.")
	}
	return builder.String()
}
```

## 5. Populating ToolInfo.FormattedMarkdown and Summary

**claudecode** — `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/claudecode/agent_session.go`. Population loop (lines 52–61) — sets `FormattedMarkdown` for every tool, never sets `Summary`:

`formatToolAsMarkdown` (lines 495+) injects `_cwd` into `tool.Input`, dispatches through the `toolFormatters` registry (`markdown_tools.go:50-60`) or `formatDefaultTool`, then appends tool output (error output fenced as ```` ```text ````).

The bash/write/read formatting helpers (`/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/claudecode/markdown_tools.go`):

`formatBashTool` (lines 132–155) — fenced ```` ```bash ```` block for multi-line, inline backticks for single-line:

```go
func formatBashTool(toolName string, input map[string]interface{}, description string) string {
	var result strings.Builder
	if description != "" {
		result.WriteString(description)
		result.WriteString("\n")
	}
	if input != nil {
		if command, ok := input["command"].(string); ok && command != "" {
			// If command includes \n we wrap it in a code block
			if strings.Contains(command, "\n") {
				escapedCommand := strings.ReplaceAll(command, "```", "\\```")
				fmt.Fprintf(&result, "\n```bash\n%s\n```", escapedCommand)
			} else {
				fmt.Fprintf(&result, "\n`%s`", command)
			}
		}
	}
	return result.String()
}
```

`formatWriteTool` (lines 158–183) — fenced block with language hint from extension, reads `content` + `file_path`:

```go
func formatWriteTool(toolName string, input map[string]interface{}, description string) string {
	var result strings.Builder
	if description != "" {
		result.WriteString(description)
		result.WriteString("\n")
	}
	if input != nil {
		if content, ok := input["content"].(string); ok {
			filePath, _ := input["file_path"].(string)
			lang := getLanguageFromExtension(filePath)
			escapedContent := strings.ReplaceAll(content, "```", "\\```")
			fmt.Fprintf(&result, "\n```%s\n%s\n```", lang, escapedContent)
		}
	}
	return result.String()
}
```

`formatReadTool` (lines 186–205) — path in backticks, relativized via `_cwd`:

```go
func formatReadTool(toolName string, input map[string]interface{}, description string) string {
	var content string
	if input != nil {
		if filePath, ok := input["file_path"].(string); ok && filePath != "" {
			cwd, _ := input["_cwd"].(string)
			relativePath := makeRelativePath(filePath, cwd)
			content += fmt.Sprintf(" `%s`", relativePath)
		}
	}
	if description != "" {
		content += fmt.Sprintf(" %s", description)
	}
	return content
}
```

The registry (`markdown_tools.go:46-60`): `toolFormatter func(toolName string, input map[string]interface{}, description string) string`, mapping `Bash→formatBashTool`, `Write→formatWriteTool`, `Read→formatReadTool`, `Grep/Glob→formatGrepTool`, `MultiEdit→formatMultiEditTool`, `TodoWrite→formatTodoWriteTool`, `AskUserQuestion`, `WebFetch→formatWebTool("url")`, `WebSearch→formatWebTool("query")`. `formatDefaultTool` (lines 262–265) just returns `description`.

**codexcli** — `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/codexcli/agent_session.go`. Population loop (lines 113–127) — sets BOTH `Summary` and `FormattedMarkdown`, but only when non-empty:

```go

	for i := range exchanges {
		for j := range exchanges[i].Messages {
			msg := &exchanges[i].Messages[j]
			if msg.Tool != nil {

				if summary != "" {
					msg.Tool.Summary = &summary
				}
				if formattedMd != "" {
					msg.Tool.FormattedMarkdown = &formattedMd
				}
			}

```

`formatToolWithSummary` (lines 497–550) — routes custom-tool string input to `formatCustomToolCall`, shell tools to `formatShellWithSummary` (single-line command becomes the summary `Tool use: **name** \`cmd\``, multi-line becomes fenced body), everything else to `formatToolCall`; then appends truncated (>5000 chars) output in a bare ```` ``` ```` fence:

```go
func formatToolWithSummary(tool *ToolInfo, workspaceRoot string) (string, string) {
	var summary string
	var formattedMd strings.Builder

	if tool.Input != nil {
		if inputStr, ok := tool.Input["input"].(string); ok {
			formattedMd.WriteString(formatCustomToolCall(tool.Name, inputStr))
		} else if tool.Name == "shell_command" || tool.Name == "exec_command" {
			toolInput := tool.Input
			if _, ok := toolInput["cmd"]; ok {
				if _, hasCommand := toolInput["command"]; !hasCommand {
					toolInput["command"] = toolInput["cmd"]
				}
			}
			inputJSON, _ := json.Marshal(toolInput)
			shellSummary, shellBody := formatShellWithSummary(string(inputJSON))
			if shellSummary != "" {
				summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** %s", tool.Name, shellSummary)
			}
			if shellBody != "" {
				formattedMd.WriteString(shellBody)
			}
		} else {
			inputJSON, _ := json.Marshal(tool.Input)
			formattedMd.WriteString(formatToolCall(tool.Name, string(inputJSON)))
		}
	}

	if tool.Output != nil {
		if outputStr, ok := tool.Output["raw"].(string); ok {
			cleaned := strings.TrimSpace(outputStr)
			if cleaned != "" {
				if formattedMd.Len() > 0 {
					formattedMd.WriteString("\n")
				}
				if len(cleaned) > 5000 {
					cleaned = cleaned[:5000] + "\n... (truncated)"
				}
				formattedMd.WriteString("```\n" + cleaned + "\n```")
			}
		}
	}

	return summary, strings.TrimSpace(formattedMd.String())
}
```

`formatShellWithSummary` (`markdown_tools.go:72-91`) — the fenced-vs-inline bash helper:

```go
func formatShellWithSummary(argumentsJSON string) (string, string) {
	var args map[string]interface{}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(argumentsJSON), &args); err != nil {
		return "", ""
	}
	command, ok := args["command"].(string)
	if !ok || command == "" {
		return "", ""
	}
	// Multi-line commands go in body with bash code fence
	// Single-line commands go in summary with inline backticks
	if strings.Contains(command, "\n") {
		return "", fmt.Sprintf("```bash\n%s\n```", command)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("`%s`", command), ""
}
```

(For write-style formatting codex uses `formatApplyPatch`/`writePatchSection` in `markdown_tools.go:122-211`, emitting ```` ```diff ```` blocks with `**Operation: \`file\`**` headers.)

## 6. Populating Message.PathHints — which arg keys each sibling reads

**claudecode `extractPathHints`** — `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/claudecode/agent_session.go:439-481`. Single-path keys: `file_path`, `path`, `filename`, `old_path`, `new_path`. Array keys: `paths`, `files`, `targets`. Plus shell command extraction:

```go
func extractPathHints(input map[string]interface{}, cwd, workspaceRoot string) []string {
	var paths []string

	pathFields := []string{"file_path", "path", "filename", "old_path", "new_path"}
	arrayFields := []string{"paths", "files", "targets"}

	for _, field := range pathFields {
		if value, ok := input[field].(string); ok && value != "" {
			normalizedPath := spi.NormalizePath(value, workspaceRoot)
			if !contains(paths, normalizedPath) {
				paths = append(paths, normalizedPath)
			}
		}
	}

	for _, field := range arrayFields {
		if arr, ok := input[field].([]interface{}); ok {
			for _, item := range arr {
				if path, ok := item.(string); ok && path != "" {
					normalizedPath := spi.NormalizePath(path, workspaceRoot)
					if !contains(paths, normalizedPath) {
						paths = append(paths, normalizedPath)
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	if command, ok := input["command"].(string); ok && command != "" {
		shellPaths := spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, cwd, workspaceRoot)
		for _, sp := range shellPaths {
			if !contains(paths, sp) {
				paths = append(paths, sp)
			}
		}
	}

	return paths
}
```

Called during agent-message build with `cwd` = the record's top-level cwd (`agent_session.go:364`: `pathHints = extractPathHints(toolInput, recordCwd, workspaceRoot)`). Uses `spi.NormalizePath` and `spi.ExtractShellPathHints`, plus a local `contains` helper (lines 484–491).

**codexcli `extractPathHints`** — `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/codexcli/agent_session.go:573-617`. Special-cases `apply_patch` (parses patch markers); otherwise reads keys `path`, `file`, `filename`, `file_path`, plus shell command from `command` or `cmd` with `workdir` as cwd:

```go
func extractPathHints(toolName string, input map[string]interface{}, inputText string, workspaceRoot string) []string {
	var paths []string

	if toolName == "apply_patch" {
		if inputText != "" {
			paths = extractPathsFromPatch(inputText, workspaceRoot)
		} else if inputStr, ok := input["input"].(string); ok {
			paths = extractPathsFromPatch(inputStr, workspaceRoot)
		}
	} else {
		pathFields := []string{"path", "file", "filename", "file_path"}
		for _, field := range pathFields {
			if value, ok := input[field].(string); ok && value != "" {
				normalizedPath := spi.NormalizePath(value, workspaceRoot)
				if !contains(paths, normalizedPath) {
					paths = append(paths, normalizedPath)
				}
			}
		}

		command, _ := input["command"].(string)
		if command == "" {
			command, _ = input["cmd"].(string)
		}
		if command != "" {
			cwd, _ := input["workdir"].(string)
			if cwd == "" {
				cwd = workspaceRoot
			}
			shellPaths := spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, cwd, workspaceRoot)
			for _, sp := range shellPaths {
				if !contains(paths, sp) {
					paths = append(paths, sp)
				}
			}
		}
	}

	return paths
}
```

**droidcli `extractPathHints`** — `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/droidcli/agent_session.go:350-397`. Widest key set: `path`, `file_path`, `filePath`, `dir`, `directory`, `workdir`, `cwd`, `target`; handles string / `[]interface{}` / `json.Number`; shell command from `command` or `cmd` with cwd from `workdir` or `cwd`:

```go
func extractPathHints(input map[string]interface{}, workspaceRoot string) []string {
	fields := []string{"path", "file_path", "filePath", "dir", "directory",
		"workdir", "cwd", "target"}
	var hints []string
	if input == nil {
		return hints
	}
	for _, field := range fields {
		val, ok := input[field]
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		switch v := val.(type) {
		case string:
			addPathHint(&hints, v, workspaceRoot)
		case []interface{}:
			for _, entry := range v {
				if s, ok := entry.(string); ok {
					addPathHint(&hints, s, workspaceRoot)
				}
			}
		case json.Number:
			addPathHint(&hints, v.String(), workspaceRoot)
		}
	}

	command, _ := input["command"].(string)
	if command == "" {
		command, _ = input["cmd"].(string)
	}
	if command != "" {
		cwd, _ := input["workdir"].(string)
		if cwd == "" {
			cwd, _ = input["cwd"].(string)
		}
		if cwd == "" {
			cwd = workspaceRoot
		}
		shellPaths := spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, cwd, workspaceRoot)
		for _, sp := range shellPaths {
			addPathHint(&hints, sp, workspaceRoot)
		}
	}

	return hints
}
```

droidcli's dedup helper `addPathHint` (lines 399+) normalizes via `spi.NormalizePath` and skips duplicates. All three siblings converge on: check named keys → `spi.NormalizePath(value, workspaceRoot)` → dedup → append `spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, cwd, workspaceRoot)`.

## 7. WatchProviders + single-provider `specstory watch pi` flow

**Full `WatchProviders`** — `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/utils/watch_agents.go:41-120`:

```go
func WatchProviders(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, providers map[string]spi.Provider, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting multi-provider watch", "projectPath", projectPath, "providerCount", len(providers), "debugRaw", debugRaw)

	var mu sync.Mutex
	lastMsgCount := make(map[string]int)

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	errChan := make(chan error, len(providers))

	for providerID, provider := range providers {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()

			slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting watcher for provider", "providerID", providerID, "providerName", provider.Name())

			wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
				if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
					return
				}

				totalMsgs := 0
				for _, exchange := range session.SessionData.Exchanges {
					totalMsgs += len(exchange.Messages)
				}

				mu.Lock()
				prev, seen := lastMsgCount[session.SessionID]
				if seen && prev == totalMsgs {
					mu.Unlock()
					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
						"providerID", providerID,
						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
						"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
					return
				}
				lastMsgCount[session.SessionID] = totalMsgs
				mu.Unlock()

				slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
					"providerID", providerID,
					"sessionID", session.SessionID,
					"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)

				sessionCallback(providerID, session)
			}

			err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
			if err != nil {
				if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
					slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
					errChan <- nil
				} else {
					slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
					errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
				}
			} else {
				errChan <- nil
			}
		}()
	}

	wg.Wait()

	for range len(providers) {
		<-errChan
	}

	return nil
}
```

Important behaviors to note for pi:
- Each provider runs in its own goroutine calling `provider.WatchAgent(ctx, ...)`.
- Watcher errors are logged (`slog.Error` for real failures; `slog.Info` for context cancel). Errors are pushed to `errChan` but **the channel is only drained and discarded** — the comment at line 114 says "errors are already logged in the goroutines with full context."
- **There is NO all-providers-failed error path.** `WatchProviders` unconditionally `return nil` at line 119 after `wg.Wait()`. Even if every provider's `WatchAgent` fails immediately, the function returns `nil`. (The `context.Canceled`/`DeadlineExceeded` errors are the expected Ctrl+C path.)
- Dedup: per-session last-message-count map suppresses callbacks when total message count is unchanged.

**Single-provider flow in `watch.go`** — `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/cmd/watch.go`. Provider selection (lines 141–163):


## 9. ScanSessionsInParallel WalkDir + GlobalSessionRef

`/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/global.go`.

**`GlobalSessionRef` (lines 24–31)** — all fields:

```go
type GlobalSessionRef struct {
	SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
	CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601 creation timestamp (first turn), may be empty
	Slug       string // filename-safe slug derived from the first user message
	Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
	NativePath string // absolute path the provider opens to read this session
	OriginCwd  string // working directory the session was launched from (-> project_id)
}
```

**`ScanSessionsInParallel` WalkDir portion (lines 93–142)** — Phase 1 collects only `*.jsonl` file paths (dirs and non-`.jsonl` skipped; unreadable entries skipped, not aborted); Phase 2 fans out `min(NumCPU, 12)` workers each calling the provider's `scan(path)` via `safeScan`:

```go
func ScanSessionsInParallel(root, label string, r *ScanReporter, scan func(path string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error)) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error) {
	// Phase 1: collect file paths (dirents only — no opens).
	var paths []string
	walkErr := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return nil // skip unreadable entries rather than abort the whole sweep
		}
		if d.IsDir() || filepath.Ext(path) != ".jsonl" {
			return nil
		}
		paths = append(paths, path)
		return nil
	})
	if walkErr != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("walking %s sessions: %w", label, walkErr)
	}

	// Phase 2: scan headers in parallel. min(NumCPU, 12) is always ≥ 1, so no lower-bound guard.
	workers := min(runtime.NumCPU(), 12)
	pathCh := make(chan string, workers)
	refs := make([]GlobalSessionRef, 0, len(paths))
	var mu sync.Mutex
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			for path := range pathCh {
				ref, scanErr := safeScan(scan, path)
				if scanErr != nil {
					slog.Warn("reindex: failed to scan session", "agent", label, "path", path, "error", scanErr)
					continue
				}
				if ref == nil {
					continue // not a session (warmup / empty / sidechain)
				}
				mu.Lock()
				refs = append(refs, *ref)
				mu.Unlock()
				r.Add(1) // count sessions found, not files scanned
			}
		}()
	}
	for _, path := range paths {
		pathCh <- path
	}
	close(pathCh)
	wg.Wait()
	return refs, nil
}
```

The scan callback receives **every `*.jsonl` file path anywhere under `root`** (recursive WalkDir, no depth limit). Callback contract (doc comment lines 88–89): return `(ref, nil)` to include, `(nil, nil)` to skip a non-session file, `(nil, err)` to log-and-skip a malformed file. `safeScan` (lines 146–153) wraps each call in a panic-recover so one bad file logs-and-skips rather than crashing. The piagent already calls this at `piagent/provider.go:348`: `return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)`.

```go
// codexSessionsRoot returns the root directory where Codex stores session files.
func codexSessionsRoot(homeDir string) string {
	// Codex CLI honors CODEX_HOME as its base directory (default ~/.codex), so
	// read sessions from the same place rather than assuming the default.
	if codexHome := os.Getenv("CODEX_HOME"); codexHome != "" {
		return filepath.Join(codexHome, "sessions")
	}
	return filepath.Join(homeDir, ".codex", "sessions")
}
```

The env-var override pattern: check `os.Getenv("CODEX_HOME")`; if non-empty, join `<CODEX_HOME>/sessions`; otherwise fall back to `<homeDir>/.codex/sessions`. Same file also has `normalizeCodexPath` (lines 21–38: `filepath.Clean` → `filepath.Abs` → `filepath.EvalSymlinks`) and `readDirSortedDesc` (lines 41–52) which pi can mirror if it needs date-descending directory walking.

```go
package piagent

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// Environment overrides pi documents in `pi --help` (config.ts ENV_AGENT_DIR /
// ENV_SESSION_DIR). PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR relocates the agent dir (sessions live
// under <dir>/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/). PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR points
// at a sessions directory used FLAT — pi writes session files directly into it
// with no per-cwd encoding, so project scoping must filter by header cwd.
const (
	envAgentDir   = "PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR"
	envSessionDir = "PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR"
)

// piSessionsRoot returns the directory under which pi stores sessions and
// whether that directory uses the flat layout (files directly in the root)
// instead of the default per-cwd encoded subdirectories. Precedence mirrors
// pi's own resolution (main.ts): PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR >
// PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/sessions > ~/.pi/agent/sessions. pi's --session-dir flag
// and settings.json sessionDir are per-invocation and not visible here.
// It does not require the directory to exist.
func piSessionsRoot() (string, bool, error) {
	if dir := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(envSessionDir)); dir != "" {
		return expandTilde(dir), true, nil
	}
	if dir := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(envAgentDir)); dir != "" {
		return filepath.Join(expandTilde(dir), "sessions"), false, nil
	}
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot resolve home dir: %w", err)
	}
	return filepath.Join(home, ".pi", "agent", "sessions"), false, nil
}

// expandTilde expands a leading "~/" to the user's home directory, matching
// how pi itself expands its env overrides (expandTildePath).
func expandTilde(path string) string {
	if strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
		if err == nil {
			return filepath.Join(home, path[2:])
		}
	}
	return path
}

// EncodeCwd maps a working directory to pi's session-subdirectory name,
// mirroring pi's own encoder exactly (session-manager.js:
// `--${resolvedCwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, "").replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-")}--`):
// one leading '/' or '\' is stripped, every remaining '/', '\', and ':' becomes
// '-', and the result is wrapped in '--'. E.g. "/Users/jane/proj" ->
// "--Users-jane-proj--". Replacing the full character class matters: a project
// path containing ':' (legal on macOS/Linux) would otherwise compute a
// directory name pi never writes, silently finding zero sessions.
func EncodeCwd(cwd string) string {
	trimmed := cwd
	if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") || strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, `\`) {
		trimmed = trimmed[1:]
	}
	encoded := strings.NewReplacer("/", "-", `\`, "-", ":", "-").Replace(trimmed)
	return "--" + encoded + "--"
}

// projectCandidates returns the working-directory forms a pi session for this
// project may have been recorded under: the absolute path as given and, when
// different, its symlink-resolved form. pi encodes the cwd as its own process
// saw it, which may be either form (e.g. /tmp/foo vs /private/tmp/foo on
// macOS), so callers must check both.
func projectCandidates(projectPath string) ([]string, error) {
	cwd := strings.TrimSpace(projectPath)
	if cwd == "" {
		wd, err := os.Getwd()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot get working dir: %w", err)
		}
		cwd = wd
	}
	abs, err := filepath.Abs(cwd)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot resolve %s: %w", cwd, err)
	}
	candidates := []string{abs}
	if real, rErr := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs); rErr == nil && real != abs {
		candidates = append(candidates, real)
	}
	return candidates, nil
}

// ProjectSessionDir returns the session directory pi would use for the given
// project (for display/diagnostics), WITHOUT requiring it to exist. In the
// flat PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR layout this is the override directory
// itself; otherwise it is the encoded per-cwd subdirectory for the project's
// absolute path.
func ProjectSessionDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
	root, flat, err := piSessionsRoot()
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if flat {
		return root, nil
	}
	candidates, err := projectCandidates(projectPath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return filepath.Join(root, EncodeCwd(candidates[0])), nil
}

// SessionFilesInProject lists the pi session files belonging to the given
// project. In the default layout it unions the encoded directories for each
// project-path candidate (raw and symlink-resolved). In the flat override
// layout it lists the root and keeps files whose header cwd matches the
// project, the same filtering pi applies to custom session dirs. Returns an
// empty slice (no error) if nothing exists yet.
func SessionFilesInProject(projectPath string) ([]string, error) {
	root, flat, err := piSessionsRoot()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	candidates, err := projectCandidates(projectPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if flat {
		return flatSessionFiles(root, candidates)
	}
	var files []string
	seen := make(map[string]bool)
	for _, c := range candidates {
		dir := filepath.Join(root, EncodeCwd(c))
		dirFiles, dErr := jsonlFilesInDir(dir)
		if dErr != nil {
			return nil, dErr
		}
		for _, f := range dirFiles {
			if !seen[f] {
				seen[f] = true
				files = append(files, f)
			}
		}
	}
	return files, nil
}

// flatSessionFiles lists *.jsonl in a flat override sessions dir, keeping only
// files whose session header cwd matches one of the project candidates.
func flatSessionFiles(root string, candidates []string) ([]string, error) {
	all, err := jsonlFilesInDir(root)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var files []string
	for _, f := range all {
		h, hErr := readHeader(f)
		if hErr != nil || h == nil {
			continue // unreadable or not a pi session; skip in listing
		}
		for _, c := range candidates {
			if h.Cwd == c {
				files = append(files, f)
				break
			}
		}
	}
	return files, nil
}

// jsonlFilesInDir lists the *.jsonl files directly inside dir (no recursion).
// Returns an empty slice (no error) if the directory does not exist.
func jsonlFilesInDir(dir string) ([]string, error) {
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return nil, nil
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading session dir %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	var files []string
	for _, e := range entries {
		if e.IsDir() {
			continue
		}
		if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".jsonl") {
			continue
		}
		files = append(files, filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
	}
	return files, nil
}
```

```go
package piagent

// Temporary empirical verification against real pi sessions on this machine.
// Guarded by PI_E2E=1 so it never runs in CI. Deleted after verification.

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
)

func TestE2E_RealCompactedSession(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("PI_E2E") != "1" {
		t.Skip("set PI_E2E=1 to run")
	}
	home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
	path := filepath.Join(home, ".pi/agent/sessions/--Users-jakelevirne-dev-tmp-pi-format-demo--/2026-07-09T21-27-45-067Z_019f48c7-8cab-7f8f-bda1-70730f0d56c3.jsonl")
	if _, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("real session not present: %v", err)
	}
	data, err := ParseSession(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParseSession: %v", err)
	}
	var hasOpening, hasSummary bool
	msgCount := 0
	for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
		for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
			msgCount++
			for _, part := range msg.Content {
				if strings.Contains(part.Text, "Read README.md and NOTES.md") {
					hasOpening = true
				}
				if strings.Contains(part.Text, "## Goal") {
					hasSummary = true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	t.Logf("exchanges=%d messages=%d opening=%v summary=%v", len(data.Exchanges), msgCount, hasOpening, hasSummary)
	if !hasOpening {
		t.Error("opening prompt missing — pre-compaction history still dropped")
	}
	if !hasSummary {
		t.Error("compaction summary missing from transcript")
	}
	if !data.Validate() {
		t.Error("Validate() false on real compacted session")
	}

	// Slug agreement: scan path vs full parse.
	scan, err := scanPiSession(path)
	if err != nil || scan == nil {
		t.Fatalf("scanPiSession: %v scan=%v", err, scan)
	}
	scanSlug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage)
	parseSlug := deriveSlug(data)
	t.Logf("scanSlug=%q parseSlug=%q", scanSlug, parseSlug)
	if scanSlug != parseSlug {
		t.Errorf("slug divergence remains: scan=%q parse=%q", scanSlug, parseSlug)
	}
}

func TestE2E_GlobalScanExcludesNested(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("PI_E2E") != "1" {
		t.Skip("set PI_E2E=1 to run")
	}
	refs, err := NewProvider().ListAllAgentChatSessions()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListAllAgentChatSessions: %v", err)
	}
	nested := 0
	for _, r := range refs {
		rel := r.NativePath
		if strings.Contains(rel, "/run-") || strings.Count(strings.SplitN(rel, "/sessions/", 2)[1], "/") > 1 {
			nested++
			t.Logf("NESTED ref leaked: %s", r.NativePath)
		}
	}
	t.Logf("total refs=%d nested=%d", len(refs), nested)
	if nested > 0 {
		t.Errorf("%d nested subagent refs still enumerated", nested)
	}
}
```

The intended behavior changes (all deliberate — do NOT flag these as bugs):
1. Compaction no longer truncates the transcript; the full leaf path is kept and each compaction entry's summary renders as a marker agent message.
2. Unmigrated pi v1 files (entries with no id/parentId) get a synthesized linear chain, matching pi's migrateV1ToV2.
3. scanPiSession does a full envelope parse + leaf-path walk so scan Slug/Name matches the full parse; latest session_info name in FILE order wins, empty name clears.
4. EncodeCwd matches pi exactly (strip one leading / or \, replace [/\\:] with -). Env overrides PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR (flat dir, filter by header cwd) and PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR (+/sessions) honored. Project candidates = abs path + symlink-resolved.
5. Global enumeration keeps only depth-1 (or depth-0 flat) files, excluding nested subagent run files.
6. Check(): SplitCommandLine + tilde expansion, classifyCheckError (errors.Is unwrapping), buildCheckErrorMessage, stderr surfaced in message+analytics. DetectAgent prints guidance when helpOutput.
7. WatchProviders returns joined error when ALL watchers fail (pkg/utils change affects all providers).

9. readHeader capped at 1MB. TUI color "pi"=135. README/PROVIDER-SPI scope notes.

- Regressions for OTHER providers from the shared pkg/utils/watch_agents.go change (e.g. bare 'specstory watch' with several providers where some fail; context-cancel path still returns nil?).
- Behavioral edge cases in the new code paths: header-only files, sessions where the first entry is a compaction, v1 synthesis interacting with malformed v3 entries, flat-mode readHeader double-reads, scan errors on files listProjectSessions accepted before, EncodeCwd for "" or "/" input, projectCandidates on nonexistent paths.
- Consistency: does anything still assume the old truncating behavior (comments, docstrings, tests, PROVIDER-SPI/PR docs)? Does any code read rawEntry.FirstKeptEntryID (removed)?
- Performance: scanPiSession now full-parses every file during reindex — any pathological blowup vs before worth flagging?
Report only genuine defects with file:line evidence. Cap at 6 strongest. Empty findings array is valid. Output consumed programmatically.

```text
13	 There is also an [Agent SPI (Service Provider Interface)](/pkg/spi/) that allows you to extend the SpecStory CLI with support for new agent providers. Creating a provider to support a new agent, using the Provider SPI is documented [here](./docs/PROVIDER-SPI.md). Pull requests are welcome!

112	+// enrichToolMessages populates PathHints and Summary/FormattedMarkdown on tool
113	+// messages after tool results are merged, matching the sibling providers: path
114	+// hints feed provenance extraction, and the formatted markdown lifts tool
115	+// rendering out of the generic key/value fallback.
116	+func enrichToolMessages(exchanges []schema.Exchange, workspaceRoot string) {
117	+	for i := range exchanges {
118	+		for j := range exchanges[i].Messages {
119	+			msg := &exchanges[i].Messages[j]
120	+			if msg.Tool == nil {
121	+				continue
122	+			}
123	+			msg.PathHints = extractPathHints(msg.Tool.Input, workspaceRoot)
124	+			summary, markdown := formatToolMarkdown(msg.Tool)
125	+			if summary != "" {

127	+			}

130	+			}
131	+		}
132	+	}

135	+// extractPathHints collects file paths from a pi tool call's arguments (pi
136	+// tools use "path"; the extra keys cover extension tools) plus paths mentioned
137	+// in shell commands, normalized and deduped like the sibling providers.
138	+func extractPathHints(input map[string]any, workspaceRoot string) []string {
139	+	if input == nil {
140	+		return nil
141	+	}
142	+	var hints []string
143	+	add := func(p string) {
144	+		if p == "" {
145	+			return
146	+		}
147	+		n := spi.NormalizePath(p, workspaceRoot)
148	+		for _, h := range hints {
149	+			if h == n {
150	+				return
151	+			}
152	+		}
153	+		hints = append(hints, n)
154	+	}
155	+	for _, field := range []string{"path", "file_path", "filePath", "dir", "directory", "target"} {
156	+		switch v := input[field].(type) {
157	+		case string:
158	+			add(v)
159	+		case []any:
160	+			for _, item := range v {
161	+				if s, ok := item.(string); ok {
162	+					add(s)
163	+				}
164	+			}
165	+		}
166	+	}
167	+	if command, _ := input["command"].(string); command != "" {
168	+		for _, sp := range spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, workspaceRoot, workspaceRoot) {
169	+			add(sp)
170	+		}
171	+	}
172	+	return hints
173	+}

175	+// formatToolMarkdown builds the pre-formatted markdown (and optional summary)
176	+// for the pi tools with a natural rendering: single-line bash commands become
177	+// an inline-code summary, multi-line commands and file writes become fenced
178	+// blocks, file tools show their path. Tools without a specific format return
179	+// empty so the CLI's generic fallback (which renders input and output) is
180	+// used instead. When a specific format is produced, the tool output is
181	+// appended so the markdown stays self-contained.
182	+func formatToolMarkdown(tool *schema.ToolInfo) (string, string) {
183	+	var summary string
184	+	var b strings.Builder
185	+	in := tool.Input
186	+	switch strings.ToLower(tool.Name) {
187	+	case "bash":
188	+		cmd, _ := in["command"].(string)
189	+		if cmd == "" {
190	+			return "", ""
191	+		}
192	+		if strings.Contains(cmd, "\n") {
193	+			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "```bash\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(cmd, "```", "\\```"))
194	+		} else {
195	+			summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, cmd)
196	+		}
197	+	case "read", "edit", "ls":
198	+		p, _ := in["path"].(string)
199	+		if p == "" {
200	+			return "", ""
201	+		}
202	+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", p)
203	+	case "write":
204	+		p, _ := in["path"].(string)
205	+		if p == "" {
206	+			return "", ""
207	+		}
208	+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`\n", p)
209	+		if content, _ := in["content"].(string); content != "" {
210	+			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n```\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(content, "```", "\\```"))
211	+		}
212	+	case "grep", "find":
213	+		pattern, _ := in["pattern"].(string)
214	+		if pattern == "" {
215	+			return "", ""
216	+		}
217	+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", pattern)
218	+	default:
219	+		return "", ""
220	+	}
221	+	appendToolOutput(&b, tool)
222	+	return summary, strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
223	+}

225	+// appendToolOutput appends the merged toolResult content as a fenced block
226	+// (truncated like codexcli) so formatted tools still show their result.
227	+func appendToolOutput(b *strings.Builder, tool *schema.ToolInfo) {
228	+	if tool.Output == nil {
229	+		return
230	+	}
231	+	content, _ := tool.Output["content"].(string)
232	+	content = strings.TrimSpace(content)
233	+	if content == "" {
234	+		return
235	+	}
236	+	if len(content) > 5000 {
237	+		content = content[:5000] + "\n... (truncated)"
238	+	}
239	+	if b.Len() > 0 {
240	+		b.WriteString("\n\n")
241	+	}
242	+	if isErr, _ := tool.Output["is_error"].(bool); isErr {
243	+		b.WriteString("Error:\n")
244	+	}
245	+	b.WriteString("```\n" + content + "\n```")
246	+}
```

```text
112	+// enrichToolMessages populates PathHints and Summary/FormattedMarkdown on tool

114	+// hints feed provenance extraction, and the formatted markdown lifts tool

116	+func enrichToolMessages(exchanges []schema.Exchange, workspaceRoot string) {
117	+	for i := range exchanges {
118	+		for j := range exchanges[i].Messages {
119	+			msg := &exchanges[i].Messages[j]
120	+			if msg.Tool == nil {
121	+				continue
122	+			}
123	+			msg.PathHints = extractPathHints(msg.Tool.Input, workspaceRoot)
124	+			summary, markdown := formatToolMarkdown(msg.Tool)
125	+			if summary != "" {

127	+			}

130	+			}
131	+		}
132	+	}

135	+// extractPathHints collects file paths from a pi tool call's arguments (pi
136	+// tools use "path"; the extra keys cover extension tools) plus paths mentioned
137	+// in shell commands, normalized and deduped like the sibling providers.
138	+func extractPathHints(input map[string]any, workspaceRoot string) []string {
139	+	if input == nil {
140	+		return nil
141	+	}
142	+	var hints []string
143	+	add := func(p string) {
144	+		if p == "" {
145	+			return
146	+		}
147	+		n := spi.NormalizePath(p, workspaceRoot)
148	+		for _, h := range hints {
149	+			if h == n {
150	+				return
151	+			}
152	+		}
153	+		hints = append(hints, n)
154	+	}
155	+	for _, field := range []string{"path", "file_path", "filePath", "dir", "directory", "target"} {
156	+		switch v := input[field].(type) {
157	+		case string:
158	+			add(v)
159	+		case []any:
160	+			for _, item := range v {
161	+				if s, ok := item.(string); ok {
162	+					add(s)
163	+				}
164	+			}
165	+		}
166	+	}
167	+	if command, _ := input["command"].(string); command != "" {
168	+		for _, sp := range spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, workspaceRoot, workspaceRoot) {
169	+			add(sp)
170	+		}
171	+	}
172	+	return hints
173	+}

175	+// formatToolMarkdown builds the pre-formatted markdown (and optional summary)
176	+// for the pi tools with a natural rendering: single-line bash commands become
177	+// an inline-code summary, multi-line commands and file writes become fenced
178	+// blocks, file tools show their path. Tools without a specific format return
179	+// empty so the CLI's generic fallback (which renders input and output) is
180	+// used instead. When a specific format is produced, the tool output is
181	+// appended so the markdown stays self-contained.
182	+func formatToolMarkdown(tool *schema.ToolInfo) (string, string) {
183	+	var summary string
184	+	var b strings.Builder
185	+	in := tool.Input
186	+	switch strings.ToLower(tool.Name) {
187	+	case "bash":
188	+		cmd, _ := in["command"].(string)
189	+		if cmd == "" {
190	+			return "", ""
191	+		}
192	+		if strings.Contains(cmd, "\n") {
193	+			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "```bash\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(cmd, "```", "\\```"))
194	+		} else {
195	+			summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, cmd)
196	+		}
197	+	case "read", "edit", "ls":
198	+		p, _ := in["path"].(string)
199	+		if p == "" {
200	+			return "", ""
201	+		}
202	+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", p)
203	+	case "write":
204	+		p, _ := in["path"].(string)
205	+		if p == "" {
206	+			return "", ""
207	+		}
208	+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`\n", p)
209	+		if content, _ := in["content"].(string); content != "" {
210	+			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n```\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(content, "```", "\\```"))
211	+		}
212	+	case "grep", "find":
213	+		pattern, _ := in["pattern"].(string)
214	+		if pattern == "" {
215	+			return "", ""
216	+		}
217	+		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", pattern)
218	+	default:
219	+		return "", ""
220	+	}
221	+	appendToolOutput(&b, tool)
222	+	return summary, strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
223	+}

225	+// appendToolOutput appends the merged toolResult content as a fenced block
226	+// (truncated like codexcli) so formatted tools still show their result.
227	+func appendToolOutput(b *strings.Builder, tool *schema.ToolInfo) {
228	+	if tool.Output == nil {
229	+		return
230	+	}
231	+	content, _ := tool.Output["content"].(string)
232	+	content = strings.TrimSpace(content)
233	+	if content == "" {
234	+		return
235	+	}
236	+	if len(content) > 5000 {
237	+		content = content[:5000] + "\n... (truncated)"
238	+	}
239	+	if b.Len() > 0 {
240	+		b.WriteString("\n\n")
241	+	}
242	+	if isErr, _ := tool.Output["is_error"].(bool); isErr {
243	+		b.WriteString("Error:\n")
244	+	}
245	+	b.WriteString("```\n" + content + "\n```")
246	+}
```

```text
1	package piagent

3	import (

14	
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}

71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// An entry with no type carries nothing the mapper can use; skip it so
91			// a stray malformed line cannot mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			// Unmigrated pi v1 files store a flat linear sequence with no id/parentId
97			// (pi's migrateV1ToV2 synthesizes them at load). Chain such entries to the
98			// previous one so the tree walk sees the same linear path pi would build.
99			if e.ID == "" {
100				e.ID = fmt.Sprintf("legacy-%d", len(entries)+1)
101				if len(entries) > 0 {
102					pid := entries[len(entries)-1].ID
103					e.ParentID = &pid
104				}
105			}
106			entries = append(entries, e)
107			return nil
108		})
109		if err != nil {
110			return nil, nil, err
111		}
112		return header, entries, nil
113	}
114	
115	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root
116	// and reverses to chronological order. Compaction entries on the path are NOT
117	// applied as truncation: pi's buildContextEntries drops pre-compaction entries
118	// only to fit the LLM context window, but SpecStory's job is preserving the
119	// full transcript, so every entry on the active branch is kept (the compaction
120	// summary itself is rendered as a marker by buildExchanges).
121	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
122		byID := indexByID(entries)
123		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
124		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
125		reverse(path)
126		return path
127	}
128	
129	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
130	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
131		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
132		for _, e := range entries {
133			m[e.ID] = e
134		}
135		return m
136	}
137	
138	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
139	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
140	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
141	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
142		var path []rawEntry
143		cur := leaf
144		visited := make(map[string]bool)
145		for !visited[cur.ID] {
146			visited[cur.ID] = true
147			path = append(path, cur)
148			if cur.ParentID == nil {
149				break
150			}
151			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
152			if !ok {
153				break
154			}
155			cur = parent
156		}
157		return path
158	}
159	
160	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
161	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
162		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
163			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
164		}
165	}
166
```

```text
1364	+		extra    string
1365	+		wantName string
1366	+	}{

1368	+			name: "latest rename wins",

1370	+{"type":"session_info","id":"s2","parentId":"s1","timestamp":"2026-07-09T10:00:03.000Z","name":"My Renamed Session"}
1371	+`,
1372	+			wantName: "My Renamed Session",
1373	+		},
1374	+		{

1377	+{"type":"session_info","id":"s2","parentId":"s1","timestamp":"2026-07-09T10:00:03.000Z","name":""}
1378	+`,

1380	+		},
1381	+	}

1525	+` +
1526	+		`{"type":"message","id":"a1","parentId":"u1","timestamp":"2026-07-09T10:00:02.000Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"toolCall","id":"call-r","name":"read","arguments":{"path":"/test/proj/main.go"}},{"type":"toolCall","id":"call-b","name":"bash","arguments":{"command":"go test ./..."}}],"provider":"x","model":"m","usage":{"input":1,"output":1,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"totalTokens":2,"cost":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"total":0}}}}
1527	+`
1528	+	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(session), 0o644); err != nil {

1530	+	}

1534	+	}

1536	+	for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {

1538	+			m := &ex.Messages[i]
1539	+			if m.Tool == nil {
1540	+				continue
1541	+			}
1542	+			switch m.Tool.UseID {
1543	+			case "call-r":

1545	+			case "call-b":

1547	+			}

1552	+	}
```

```text
110	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL session file (v3 tree or unmigrated v1 linear)
111	// and maps its current leaf-path branch into the unified schema.SessionData.
112	// The FULL leaf path is kept: compaction only trims pi's LLM context window,
113	// not the transcript, so pre-compaction history is preserved and the
114	// compaction summary is rendered as a marker message.
115	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
116		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
117		if err != nil {
118			return nil, err
119		}
120		if header == nil {
121			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
122		}
123		if header.Type != entrySession {
124			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
125		}
126		if header.ID == "" {
127			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
128		}
129		if len(entries) == 0 {
130			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
131		}
132		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
133		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
134	}

137	// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
138	// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
139	func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
140		if header.Version > 0 {
141			return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
142		}
143		return "v1"
144	}

146	// buildSessionData maps the ordered leaf-path entries into schema.SessionData.
147	func buildSessionData(header *sessionHeader, ordered []rawEntry) *schema.SessionData {
148		exchanges := buildExchanges(ordered)
149		enrichToolMessages(exchanges, header.Cwd)
150		return &schema.SessionData{

152			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{

159			WorkspaceRoot: header.Cwd,
160			Exchanges:     exchanges,
161		}
162	}

164	// enrichToolMessages populates PathHints and Summary/FormattedMarkdown on tool
165	// messages after tool results are merged, matching the sibling providers: path
166	// hints feed provenance extraction, and the formatted markdown lifts tool
167	// rendering out of the generic key/value fallback.
168	func enrichToolMessages(exchanges []schema.Exchange, workspaceRoot string) {
169		for i := range exchanges {
170			for j := range exchanges[i].Messages {
171				msg := &exchanges[i].Messages[j]
172				if msg.Tool == nil {
173					continue
174				}
175				msg.PathHints = extractPathHints(msg.Tool.Input, workspaceRoot)
176				summary, markdown := formatToolMarkdown(msg.Tool)
177				if summary != "" {
178					msg.Tool.Summary = &summary
179				}
180				if markdown != "" {
181					msg.Tool.FormattedMarkdown = &markdown
182				}
183			}
184		}
185	}

187	// extractPathHints collects file paths from a pi tool call's arguments (pi
188	// tools use "path"; the extra keys cover extension tools) plus paths mentioned
189	// in shell commands, normalized and deduped like the sibling providers.
190	func extractPathHints(input map[string]any, workspaceRoot string) []string {
191		if input == nil {
192			return nil
193		}
194		var hints []string
195		add := func(p string) {
196			if p == "" {
197				return
198			}
199			n := spi.NormalizePath(p, workspaceRoot)
200			for _, h := range hints {
201				if h == n {
202					return
203				}
204			}
205			hints = append(hints, n)
206		}
207		for _, field := range []string{"path", "file_path", "filePath", "dir", "directory", "target"} {
208			switch v := input[field].(type) {
209			case string:
210				add(v)
211			case []any:
212				for _, item := range v {
213					if s, ok := item.(string); ok {
214						add(s)
215					}
216				}
217			}
218		}
219		if command, _ := input["command"].(string); command != "" {
220			for _, sp := range spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, workspaceRoot, workspaceRoot) {
221				add(sp)
222			}
223		}
224		return hints
225	}
226	
227	// formatToolMarkdown builds the pre-formatted markdown (and optional summary)
228	// for the pi tools with a natural rendering: single-line bash commands become
229	// an inline-code summary, multi-line commands and file writes become fenced
230	// blocks, file tools show their path. Tools without a specific format return
231	// empty so the CLI's generic fallback (which renders input and output) is
232	// used instead. When a specific format is produced, the tool output is
233	// appended so the markdown stays self-contained.
234	func formatToolMarkdown(tool *schema.ToolInfo) (string, string) {
235		var summary string
236		var b strings.Builder
237		in := tool.Input
238		switch strings.ToLower(tool.Name) {
239		case "bash":
240			cmd, _ := in["command"].(string)
241			if cmd == "" {
242				return "", ""
243			}
244			if strings.Contains(cmd, "\n") {
245				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "```bash\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(cmd, "```", "\\```"))
246			} else {
247				summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, cmd)
248			}
249		case "read", "edit", "ls":
250			p, _ := in["path"].(string)
251			if p == "" {
252				return "", ""
253			}
254			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", p)
255		case "write":
256			p, _ := in["path"].(string)
257			if p == "" {
258				return "", ""
259			}
260			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`\n", p)
261			if content, _ := in["content"].(string); content != "" {
262				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n```\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(content, "```", "\\```"))
263			}
264		case "grep", "find":
265			pattern, _ := in["pattern"].(string)
266			if pattern == "" {
267				return "", ""
268			}
269			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", pattern)
270		default:
271			return "", ""
272		}
273		appendToolOutput(&b, tool)
274		return summary, strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
275	}

277	// appendToolOutput appends the merged toolResult content as a fenced block
278	// (truncated like codexcli) so formatted tools still show their result.
279	func appendToolOutput(b *strings.Builder, tool *schema.ToolInfo) {
280		if tool.Output == nil {
281			return
282		}
283		content, _ := tool.Output["content"].(string)
284		content = strings.TrimSpace(content)
285		if content == "" {
286			return
287		}
288		if len(content) > 5000 {
289			content = content[:5000] + "\n... (truncated)"
290		}
291		if b.Len() > 0 {
292			b.WriteString("\n\n")
293		}
294		if isErr, _ := tool.Output["is_error"].(bool); isErr {
295			b.WriteString("Error:\n")
296		}
297		b.WriteString("```\n" + content + "\n```")
298	}

300	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
301	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
302	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo; compaction entries
303	// become marker messages so trimmed-context sessions stay self-explanatory.
304	// Other control entries (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the
305	// conversation body.
306	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
307		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
308		var current *schema.Exchange
309		commit := func() {
310			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
311				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
312			}
313		}
314		for _, e := range ordered {
315			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
316				current = appendCompaction(current, e)
317				continue
318			}
319			if e.Type != entryMessage {
320				continue
321			}
322			switch messageRole(e) {
323			case roleUser:
324				commit()
325				current = &schema.Exchange{
326					ExchangeID: e.ID,
327					StartTime:  e.Timestamp,
328					EndTime:    e.Timestamp,
329					Messages:   []schema.Message{buildUserMessage(e)},
330				}
331			case roleAssistant:
332				current = appendAssistant(current, e)
333			case roleToolResult:
334				mergeToolResult(current, e)
335			}
336		}
337		commit()
338		return exchanges
339	}

341	// appendCompaction appends a compaction entry's summary to the current exchange
342	// as a marker agent message (creating an exchange if none exists yet). The
343	// summary is what pi replaced the pre-compaction context with; rendering it
344	// keeps the transcript self-explanatory without dropping any history.
345	func appendCompaction(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) *schema.Exchange {
346		if strings.TrimSpace(e.Summary) == "" {
347			return current
348		}
349		if current == nil {
350			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
351		}
352		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, schema.Message{
353			ID:        e.ID,
354			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
355			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
356			Content: []schema.ContentPart{{
357				Type: schema.ContentTypeText,
358				Text: "[Conversation compacted — summary of the earlier context]\n\n" + e.Summary,
359			}},
360		})
361		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
362		return current
363	}
364	
365	// appendAssistant appends an assistant message to the current exchange, creating
366	// one if none exists yet.
367	func appendAssistant(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) *schema.Exchange {
368		if current == nil {
369			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
370		}
371		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, buildAgentMessages(e)...)
372		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
373		return current

385	// mergeToolResult folds a toolResult entry into the matching agent ToolInfo in
386	// the current exchange, keyed by toolCallId == ToolInfo.UseID. It also advances
387	// the exchange EndTime to the toolResult's timestamp so downstream stats that
388	// read the last exchange's EndTime report the real final-event time.
389	func mergeToolResult(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) {
390		if current == nil {
391			return
392		}
393		var tr toolResultMessage
394		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &tr); err != nil {
395			return
396		}
397		content := toolResultContent(tr)
398		for i := range current.Messages {
399			msg := &current.Messages[i]
400			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.UseID == tr.ToolCallID {
401				msg.Tool.Output = buildToolOutput(content, tr)
402				msg.Timestamp = e.Timestamp
403				current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
404				return
405			}
406		}
407	}

409	// toolResultContent joins the text blocks of a toolResult message.
410	func toolResultContent(tr toolResultMessage) string {
411		var parts []string

413			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
414				parts = append(parts, b.Text)
415			}
416		}
417		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
418	}

420	// buildUserMessage maps a pi user message entry to a schema user Message.
421	// pi user content is either a plain string or an array of {type:text|image}.
422	func buildUserMessage(e rawEntry) schema.Message {
423		var um userMessage
424		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &um)
425		parts := userContentParts(um.Content)
426		return schema.Message{

434	// userContentParts decodes a pi user message's content (string or array) into
435	// schema ContentParts. Image blocks are dropped in v1 (recorded as a gap).
436	func userContentParts(raw json.RawMessage) []schema.ContentPart {
437		if len(raw) == 0 {
438			return nil
439		}
440		if raw[0] == '"' {
441			var s string
442			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
443				return []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: s}}
444			}
445		}
446		var blocks []contentBlock
447		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
448			return nil

450		var parts []schema.ContentPart
451		for _, b := range blocks {
452			if b.Type == schema.ContentTypeText && b.Text != "" {
453				parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
454			}
455		}
456		return parts
```
