498		// tool message so no metadata is lost and no schema-invalid empty message
499		// is emitted.
500		messages[0].Model = am.Model
501		if messages[0].Usage == nil {
502			messages[0].Usage = mapUsage(am.Usage)
503		}
504		return messages
505	}
506	
507	// buildToolMessage builds an agent Message wrapping a ToolInfo from a toolCall.
508	// The parent assistant message's model is passed through so tool messages carry
509	// the same model metadata as text/thinking messages. The Message ID is derived
510	// from the parent entry id + the toolCall id, so multiple toolCalls in one
511	// assistant message get distinct Message IDs (downstream provenance keys use
512	// msg.ID as a deterministic component).
513	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
514		return schema.Message{
515			ID:        toolMessageID(e.ID, b.ID),
516			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
517			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
518			Model:     am.Model,
519			Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{
520				Name:  b.Name,
521				Type:  classifyToolType(b.Name),
522				UseID: b.ID,
523				Input: b.Args,
524			},
525		}
526	}
527	
528	// toolMessageID builds a unique Message ID for a tool-call message from the
529	// parent entry id and the toolCall id. This avoids duplicate Message IDs when a
530	// single assistant entry contains multiple toolCall blocks.
531	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {
532		if callID != "" {
533			return entryID + ":" + callID
534		}
535		return entryID
536	}
537	
538	// buildToolOutput constructs the ToolInfo.Output map from a toolResult's
539	// content, error flag, and optional details blob. details (e.g. exitCode) is
540	// decoded into a generic value so downstream consumers (markdown rendering,
541	// cloud) can surface structured tool metadata without re-parsing raw JSON.
542	func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
543		out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
544		if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
545			var details any
546			if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {
547				out["details"] = details
548			}
549		}
550		return out
551	}
552	
553	// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map
554	// to InputTokens/OutputTokens; cacheRead/cacheWrite map to the Claude-style
555	// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics); reasoning maps to the same field
556	// codexcli uses so telemetry aggregates pi thinking tokens like other providers.
557	func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
558		if u == nil {
559			return nil
560		}
561		return &schema.Usage{
562			InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
563			OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
564			ReasoningOutputTokens:    int(u.Reasoning),
565			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
566			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
567		}
568	}
569	
570	// buildErrorMessage surfaces an assistant entry with stopReason=error and an
571	// empty content array (no text/thinking/toolCalls) as an agent text message so
572	// the error event is not dropped from the transcript (and compaction boundaries
573	// stay interpretable). Returns nil if there is no errorMessage to surface.
574	func buildErrorMessage(e rawEntry, am assistantMessage) []schema.Message {
575		if strings.TrimSpace(am.ErrorMessage) == "" {
576			return nil
577		}
578		return []schema.Message{{
579			ID:        e.ID,
580			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
581			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
582			Model:     am.Model,
583			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "[error] " + am.ErrorMessage}},
584			Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
585		}}
586	}
587	
588	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
589	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
590	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
591	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
592		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
593			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
594				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
595					continue
596				}
597				for _, part := range msg.Content {
598					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {
599						return spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(t)
600					}
601				}
602			}
603		}
604		return ""
605	}
606	
607	// classifyToolType maps pi tool names to the schema tool-type taxonomy.
608	func classifyToolType(name string) string {
609		switch strings.ToLower(name) {
610		case "read":
611			return schema.ToolTypeRead
612		case "edit", "write":
613			return schema.ToolTypeWrite
614		case "bash", "ls":
615			return schema.ToolTypeShell
616		case "grep", "find", "web_search", "fetch_content":
617			return schema.ToolTypeSearch
618		case "until_done_set", "until_done_plan", "until_done_task_update",
619			"until_done_progress", "until_done_complete", "until_done_block",
620			"until_done_replan", "until_done_distill":
621			return schema.ToolTypeTask
622		default:
623			return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
624		}
625	}
626	
627	// firstUserText extracts the first user message text from a message entry, if
628	// its role is "user". Returns "" for non-user messages or empty content.
629	func firstUserText(e rawEntry) string {
630		var m struct {
631			Role    string          `json:"role"`
632			Content json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
633		}
634		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m); err != nil {
635			return ""
636		}
637		if m.Role != roleUser {
638			return ""
639		}
640		return userContentString(m.Content)
641	}
642	
643	// userContentString extracts a plain string from a pi user message content
644	// field (either a string or an array of {type:text} blocks). The result is
645	// trimmed so the scan path produces the same Slug/Name as the full-parse path
646	// (deriveSlug trims too).
647	func userContentString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
648		if len(raw) == 0 {
649			return ""
650		}
651		var s string
652		if raw[0] == '"' {
653			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
654				return strings.TrimSpace(s)
655			}
656		}
657		var blocks []contentBlock
658		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
659			return ""
660		}
661		for _, b := range blocks {
662			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
663				return strings.TrimSpace(b.Text)
664			}
665		}
666		return ""
667	}
668

30	// Provider implements spi.Provider for the pi coding agent.
31	// pi stores sessions as JSONL v3 trees under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/.
32	type Provider struct{}
33	
34	// NewProvider returns a new pi provider instance.
35	func NewProvider() *Provider { return &Provider{} }
36	
37	// Name returns the human-readable provider name.
38	func (p *Provider) Name() string { return providerName }

40	// parsePiCommand splits a custom check/run command into binary + args,
41	// expanding a leading ~ like sibling providers (spi.SplitCommandLine handles
42	// quoting). Falls back to the default `pi` binary when no custom command is
43	// given.
44	func parsePiCommand(customCommand string) (string, []string) {
45		if strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != "" {
46			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
47			if len(parts) > 0 {
48				return expandTilde(parts[0]), parts[1:]
49			}
50		}
51		return defaultCmd, nil
52	}
53	
54	// classifyCheckError buckets a Check failure for messaging and analytics,
55	// matching the sibling providers' error taxonomy. errors.Is unwraps through
56	// exec.Error/os.PathError, covering both PATH lookups (exec.ErrNotFound) and
57	// explicit custom paths (os.ErrNotExist).
58	func classifyCheckError(err error) string {
59		switch {
60		case errors.Is(err, exec.ErrNotFound) || errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist):
61			return "not_found"
62		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
63			return "permission_denied"
64		default:
65			return "version_failed"
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// buildCheckErrorMessage renders the user-facing Check failure text. The
70	// custom-command branch avoids the misleading "not found on PATH" wording when
71	// the user pointed at an explicit path, and version-probe failures surface the
72	// probe's stderr so the underlying diagnostic is not lost.
73	func buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, command string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
74		var b strings.Builder
75		switch errorType {
76		case "not_found":
77			b.WriteString("The pi coding agent was not found.\n\n")
78			if isCustom {
79				b.WriteString("• Verify the custom command/path you provided exists and is executable.\n")
80				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Provided command: %s\n", command)
81			} else {
82				b.WriteString("• Install pi (see https://pi.dev) and ensure `pi` is on your PATH.\n")
83				b.WriteString("• Re-run `specstory check pi` after installation.\n")
84			}
85		case "permission_denied":
86			b.WriteString("SpecStory cannot execute the pi binary due to permissions.\n\n")
87			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Try: chmod +x %s\n", command)
88		default:
89			b.WriteString("`pi --version` failed.\n\n")
90			if stderr != "" {
91				b.WriteString("Error output:\n")
92				b.WriteString(stderr)
93				b.WriteString("\n\n")
94			}
95			b.WriteString("Run `pi --version` manually to diagnose, then retry.")
96		}
97		return b.String()
98	}

100	// Check verifies the pi binary is available and reports its version.
101	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
102		isCustom := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != ""
103		cmdName, _ := parsePiCommand(customCommand)
104		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
105		if err != nil {
106			errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
107			slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
108			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "", errorType, err.Error())
109			return spi.CheckResult{
110				Success:      false,
111				ErrorMessage: buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, cmdName, isCustom, ""),
112			}
113		}
114		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
115		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
116		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
117		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
118		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
119			errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
120			stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
121			slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err, "stderr", stderrOutput)
122			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, stderrOutput, errorType, err.Error())
123			return spi.CheckResult{
124				Success:      false,
125				Location:     resolved,
126				ErrorMessage: buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, cmdName, isCustom, stderrOutput),
127			}
128		}
129		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
130		if version == "" {
131			version = "unknown"
132		}
133		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
134		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
135	}

211	// sessionFile pairs a discovered pi session file with its header metadata.
212	type sessionFile struct {
213		Path   string
214		Header sessionHeader
215	}
216	
217	// findProjectSession locates the session file with the given ID within the
218	// project's pi session directory. Returns "" if not found.
219	func findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
220		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
221		if err != nil {
222			return "", err
223		}
224		for _, f := range files {
225			h, err := readHeader(f)
226			if err != nil || h == nil {
227				continue
228			}
229			if h.ID == sessionID {
230				return f, nil
231			}
232		}
233		return "", nil
234	}
235	
236	// readHeader parses only the first JSON value of a session file and returns it
237	// only if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty
238	// id). Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them. The read is
239	// capped at 1MB: a real pi header is a few hundred bytes, and the cap keeps a
240	// crafted file with a multi-GB first value from being buffered into memory.
241	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
242		f, err := os.Open(path)
243		if err != nil {
244			return nil, err
245		}
246		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
247		dec := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(f, 1*MB))
248		var h sessionHeader
249		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
250			return nil, nil
251		}
252		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
253			return nil, nil
254		}
255		return &h, nil
256	}
257	
258	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
259	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
260	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
261	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
262		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
263		if err != nil {
264			return nil, err
265		}
266		var out []sessionFile
267		for _, f := range files {
268			h, err := readHeader(f)
269			if err != nil {
270				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
271				continue
272			}
273			if h == nil {
274				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
275			}
276			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
277		}
278		return out, nil
279	}

321		}

323			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(path, data); dErr != nil {

423		// root/<encoded-cwd>/. Deeper *.jsonl files are extension/subagent
424		// internals (observed: <proj>/<ts>_<uuid>/<hash>/run-0/session.jsonl) that
425		// the project-scoped APIs (SessionFilesInProject) can never resolve by id;
426		// indexing them would create rows sync/preview/resume cannot fetch.
427		wantDepth := 1
428		if flat {
429			wantDepth = 0
430		}
431		scan := func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
432			rel, relErr := filepath.Rel(root, path)
433			if relErr != nil || strings.Count(rel, string(filepath.Separator)) != wantDepth {
434				return nil, nil
435			}
436			s, sErr := scanPiSession(path)
437			if sErr != nil {
438				return nil, sErr
439			}
440			if s == nil {
441				return nil, nil // non-session file
442			}
443			return scanToGlobalRef(s, path), nil
444		}
445		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)
446	}
447	
448	// piSessionScan holds the metadata fields read from a session file for
449	// listing/reindex: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd +
450	// the latest user-set session name. The scan walks the SAME leaf path the full
451	// parse uses, so its Slug/Name always match what deriveSlug produces for the
452	// generated markdown (file order can differ from the active branch when the
453	// first prompt was re-edited). foundUser is false for sessions with no real
454	// user prompt; scanPiSession returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
455	type piSessionScan struct {
456		sessionID        string
457		timestamp        string
458		firstUserMessage string
459		sessionName      string
460		cwd              string
461		foundUser        bool
462	}
463	
464	// scanPiSession reads a pi session file's metadata for listing: the header
465	// (session id, timestamp, cwd), the first user message text on the active leaf
466	// path, and the latest session_info display name. Returns (scan, nil) for a
467	// real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session file or a session with no user
468	// message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse errors so
469	// ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
470	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
471		h, err := readHeader(path)
472		if err != nil {
473			return nil, err
474		}
475		if h == nil {
476			return nil, nil // not a pi session file
477		}
478		_, entries, err := readEntries(path)
479		if err != nil {
480			return nil, err
481		}
482		if len(entries) == 0 {
483			return nil, nil // header-only session; nothing to list
484		}
485		scan := &piSessionScan{sessionID: h.ID, timestamp: h.Timestamp, cwd: h.Cwd}
486		// pi resolves the display name from the LATEST session_info entry in file
487		// order (not the leaf path), and an empty name explicitly clears the title
488		// (session-manager.ts getSessionName) — mirror both rules.
489		for _, e := range entries {
490			if e.Type == entrySessionInfo {
491				scan.sessionName = strings.TrimSpace(e.Name)
492			}
493		}
494		for _, e := range leafPathEntries(entries) {
495			if scan.foundUser || e.Type != entryMessage {
496				continue
497			}
498			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
499				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
500				scan.foundUser = true
501			}
502		}
503		if !scan.foundUser {
504			return nil, nil // no user prompt; nothing worth listing
505		}
506		return scan, nil
507	}
508	
509	// scanName returns the display name for a scanned session: the user-set
510	// session_info name when present (pi lets users rename sessions), otherwise a
511	// readable name derived from the first user message like other providers.
512	func scanName(scan *piSessionScan) string {
513		if scan.sessionName != "" {
514			return scan.sessionName
515		}
516		return spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage)
517	}
518	
519	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
520	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
521	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
522		if !scan.foundUser {
523			return nil
524		}
525		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
526			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
527			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
528			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
529			Name:       scanName(scan),
530			NativePath: path,
531			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
532		}
533	}
534

1	package piagent

3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// Environment overrides pi documents in `pi --help` (config.ts ENV_AGENT_DIR /
11	// ENV_SESSION_DIR). PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR relocates the agent dir (sessions live
12	// under <dir>/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/). PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR points
13	// at a sessions directory used FLAT — pi writes session files directly into it
14	// with no per-cwd encoding, so project scoping must filter by header cwd.
15	const (
16		envAgentDir   = "PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR"
17		envSessionDir = "PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR"
18	)
19	
20	// piSessionsRoot returns the directory under which pi stores sessions and
21	// whether that directory uses the flat layout (files directly in the root)
22	// instead of the default per-cwd encoded subdirectories. Precedence mirrors
23	// pi's own resolution (main.ts): PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR >
24	// PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/sessions > ~/.pi/agent/sessions. pi's --session-dir flag
25	// and settings.json sessionDir are per-invocation and not visible here.
26	// It does not require the directory to exist.
27	func piSessionsRoot() (string, bool, error) {
28		if dir := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(envSessionDir)); dir != "" {
29			return expandTilde(dir), true, nil
30		}
31		if dir := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(envAgentDir)); dir != "" {
32			return filepath.Join(expandTilde(dir), "sessions"), false, nil
33		}
34		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
35		if err != nil {
36			return "", false, fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot resolve home dir: %w", err)
37		}
38		return filepath.Join(home, ".pi", "agent", "sessions"), false, nil
39	}
40	
41	// expandTilde expands a leading "~/" to the user's home directory, matching
42	// how pi itself expands its env overrides (expandTildePath).
43	func expandTilde(path string) string {
44		if strings.HasPrefix(path, "~/") {
45			home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
46			if err == nil {
47				return filepath.Join(home, path[2:])
48			}
49		}
50		return path
51	}
52	
53	// EncodeCwd maps a working directory to pi's session-subdirectory name,
54	// mirroring pi's own encoder exactly (session-manager.js:
55	// `--${resolvedCwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, "").replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-")}--`):
56	// one leading '/' or '\' is stripped, every remaining '/', '\', and ':' becomes
57	// '-', and the result is wrapped in '--'. E.g. "/Users/jane/proj" ->
58	// "--Users-jane-proj--". Replacing the full character class matters: a project
59	// path containing ':' (legal on macOS/Linux) would otherwise compute a
60	// directory name pi never writes, silently finding zero sessions.
61	func EncodeCwd(cwd string) string {
62		trimmed := cwd
63		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") || strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, `\`) {
64			trimmed = trimmed[1:]
65		}
66		encoded := strings.NewReplacer("/", "-", `\`, "-", ":", "-").Replace(trimmed)
67		return "--" + encoded + "--"
68	}
69	
70	// projectCandidates returns the working-directory forms a pi session for this
71	// project may have been recorded under: the absolute path as given and, when
72	// different, its symlink-resolved form. pi encodes the cwd as its own process
73	// saw it, which may be either form (e.g. /tmp/foo vs /private/tmp/foo on
74	// macOS), so callers must check both.
75	func projectCandidates(projectPath string) ([]string, error) {
76		cwd := strings.TrimSpace(projectPath)
77		if cwd == "" {
78			wd, err := os.Getwd()
79			if err != nil {
80				return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot get working dir: %w", err)
81			}
82			cwd = wd
83		}
84		abs, err := filepath.Abs(cwd)
85		if err != nil {
86			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: cannot resolve %s: %w", cwd, err)
87		}
88		candidates := []string{abs}
89		if real, rErr := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs); rErr == nil && real != abs {
90			candidates = append(candidates, real)
91		}
92		return candidates, nil
93	}
94	
95	// ProjectSessionDir returns the session directory pi would use for the given
96	// project (for display/diagnostics), WITHOUT requiring it to exist. In the
97	// flat PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR layout this is the override directory
98	// itself; otherwise it is the encoded per-cwd subdirectory for the project's
99	// absolute path.
100	func ProjectSessionDir(projectPath string) (string, error) {
101		root, flat, err := piSessionsRoot()
102		if err != nil {
103			return "", err
104		}
105		if flat {
106			return root, nil
107		}
108		candidates, err := projectCandidates(projectPath)
109		if err != nil {
110			return "", err
111		}
112		return filepath.Join(root, EncodeCwd(candidates[0])), nil
113	}
114	
115	// SessionFilesInProject lists the pi session files belonging to the given
116	// project. In the default layout it unions the encoded directories for each
117	// project-path candidate (raw and symlink-resolved). In the flat override
118	// layout it lists the root and keeps files whose header cwd matches the
119	// project, the same filtering pi applies to custom session dirs. Returns an
120	// empty slice (no error) if nothing exists yet.
121	func SessionFilesInProject(projectPath string) ([]string, error) {
122		root, flat, err := piSessionsRoot()
123		if err != nil {
124			return nil, err
125		}
126		candidates, err := projectCandidates(projectPath)
127		if err != nil {
128			return nil, err
129		}
130		if flat {
131			return flatSessionFiles(root, candidates)
132		}
133		var files []string
134		seen := make(map[string]bool)
135		for _, c := range candidates {
136			dir := filepath.Join(root, EncodeCwd(c))
137			dirFiles, dErr := jsonlFilesInDir(dir)
138			if dErr != nil {
139				return nil, dErr
140			}
141			for _, f := range dirFiles {
142				if !seen[f] {
143					seen[f] = true
144					files = append(files, f)
145				}
146			}
147		}
148		return files, nil
149	}
150	
151	// flatSessionFiles lists *.jsonl in a flat override sessions dir, keeping only
152	// files whose session header cwd matches one of the project candidates.
153	func flatSessionFiles(root string, candidates []string) ([]string, error) {
154		all, err := jsonlFilesInDir(root)
155		if err != nil {
156			return nil, err
157		}
158		var files []string
159		for _, f := range all {
160			h, hErr := readHeader(f)
161			if hErr != nil || h == nil {
162				continue // unreadable or not a pi session; skip in listing
163			}
164			for _, c := range candidates {
165				if h.Cwd == c {
166					files = append(files, f)
167					break
168				}
169			}
170		}
171		return files, nil
172	}
173	
174	// jsonlFilesInDir lists the *.jsonl files directly inside dir (no recursion).
175	// Returns an empty slice (no error) if the directory does not exist.
176	func jsonlFilesInDir(dir string) ([]string, error) {
177		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
178		if err != nil {
179			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
180				return nil, nil
181			}
182			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading session dir %s: %w", dir, err)
183		}
184		var files []string
185		for _, e := range entries {
186			if e.IsDir() {
187				continue
188			}
189			if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".jsonl") {
190				continue
191			}
192			files = append(files, filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
193		}
194		return files, nil
195	}

3	import (
4		"context"

9	
10		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
11		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/factory"
12	)
13	
14	// WatchAgents starts watchers for all registered providers concurrently.
15	// Convenience wrapper around WatchProviders that resolves the full provider registry.
16	func WatchAgents(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
17		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
18		providers := registry.GetAll()
19	
20		if len(providers) == 0 {
21			return fmt.Errorf("no providers registered")
22		}
23	
24		return WatchProviders(ctx, projectPath, providers, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
25	}
26	
27	// WatchProviders starts watchers for the given providers concurrently.
28	// Calls sessionCallback when any provider detects activity.
29	// Runs until context is cancelled or all watchers stop.
30	// Context cancellation (Ctrl+C) is treated as a clean exit, not an error.
31	//
32	// Parameters:
33	//   - ctx: Context for cancellation and timeout control
34	//   - projectPath: Agent's working directory to watch
35	//   - providers: map of provider ID to provider instance to watch
36	//   - debugRaw: whether to write debug raw data files
37	//   - sessionCallback: called with provider ID and AgentChatSession data on each update
38	//
39	// The callback includes the provider ID to help consumers route/filter sessions.
40	// The callback should not block as it may delay other provider notifications.
41	func WatchProviders(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, providers map[string]spi.Provider, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
42		slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting multi-provider watch", "projectPath", projectPath, "providerCount", len(providers), "debugRaw", debugRaw)
43	
44		// Track last-seen message count per session to suppress duplicate callbacks.
45		// Providers fire callbacks on every JSONL change, but not all changes produce
46		// new messages in the parsed SessionData. Messages are append-only, so a
47		// matching total count means nothing meaningful changed.
48		var mu sync.Mutex
49		lastMsgCount := make(map[string]int)
50	
51		var wg sync.WaitGroup
52		errChan := make(chan error, len(providers))
53	
54		for providerID, provider := range providers {
55			wg.Add(1)
56			go func() {
57				defer wg.Done()
58	
59				slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting watcher for provider", "providerID", providerID, "providerName", provider.Name())
60	
61				// Wrap the callback to deduplicate and include provider ID
62				wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
63					if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
64						return
65					}
66	
67					// Count total messages across all exchanges
68					totalMsgs := 0
69					for _, exchange := range session.SessionData.Exchanges {
70						totalMsgs += len(exchange.Messages)
71					}
72	
73					// Skip if message count hasn't changed for this session
74					mu.Lock()
75					prev, seen := lastMsgCount[session.SessionID]
76					if seen && prev == totalMsgs {
77						mu.Unlock()
78						slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
79							"providerID", providerID,
80							"sessionID", session.SessionID,
81							"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
82						return
83					}
84					lastMsgCount[session.SessionID] = totalMsgs
85					mu.Unlock()
86	
87					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
88						"providerID", providerID,
89						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
90						"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
91	
92					sessionCallback(providerID, session)
93				}
94	
95				err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
96				if err != nil {
97					// Context cancellation is expected when user presses Ctrl+C, not an error
98					if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
99						slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
100						errChan <- nil
101					} else {
102						slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
103						errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
104					}
105				} else {
106					errChan <- nil
107				}
108			}()
109		}
110	
111		// Wait for all watchers to complete (they run until Ctrl+C)
112		wg.Wait()
113	
114		// Individual watcher failures are already logged in the goroutines with
115		// full context and must not kill the surviving watchers' results. But when
116		// EVERY watcher failed (e.g. `specstory watch <provider>` on a provider
117		// whose watch is unsupported), returning nil would print the watching
118		// banner and then silently exit 0 — surface the failure instead.
119		var failures []error
120		for range len(providers) {
121			if err := <-errChan; err != nil {
122				failures = append(failures, err)
123			}
124		}
125		if len(providers) > 0 && len(failures) == len(providers) {
126			return errors.Join(failures...)
127		}
128	
129		return nil
130	}
131

19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// An entry with no type carries nothing the mapper can use; skip it so
91			// a stray malformed line cannot mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			// Unmigrated pi v1 files store a flat linear sequence with no id/parentId
97			// (pi's migrateV1ToV2 synthesizes them at load). Chain such entries to the
98			// previous one so the tree walk sees the same linear path pi would build.
99			if e.ID == "" {
100				e.ID = fmt.Sprintf("legacy-%d", len(entries)+1)
101				if len(entries) > 0 {
102					pid := entries[len(entries)-1].ID
103					e.ParentID = &pid
104				}
105			}
106			entries = append(entries, e)
107			return nil
108		})
109		if err != nil {
110			return nil, nil, err
111		}
112		return header, entries, nil
113	}
114	
115	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root
116	// and reverses to chronological order. Compaction entries on the path are NOT
117	// applied as truncation: pi's buildContextEntries drops pre-compaction entries
118	// only to fit the LLM context window, but SpecStory's job is preserving the
119	// full transcript, so every entry on the active branch is kept (the compaction
120	// summary itself is rendered as a marker by buildExchanges).
121	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
122		byID := indexByID(entries)
123		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
124		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
125		reverse(path)
126		return path
127	}
128	
129	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
130	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
131		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
132		for _, e := range entries {
133			m[e.ID] = e
134		}
135		return m
136	}
137	
138	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
139	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
140	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
141	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
142		var path []rawEntry
143		cur := leaf
144		visited := make(map[string]bool)
145		for !visited[cur.ID] {
146			visited[cur.ID] = true
147			path = append(path, cur)
148			if cur.ParentID == nil {
149				break
150			}
151			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
152			if !ok {
153				break
154			}
155			cur = parent
156		}
157		return path
158	}
159	
160	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
161	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
162		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
163			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
164		}
165	}
166
```

110	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL session file (v3 tree or unmigrated v1 linear)
111	// and maps its current leaf-path branch into the unified schema.SessionData.
112	// The FULL leaf path is kept: compaction only trims pi's LLM context window,
113	// not the transcript, so pre-compaction history is preserved and the
114	// compaction summary is rendered as a marker message.
115	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
116		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
117		if err != nil {

119		}
120		if header == nil {

122		}

124			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
125		}
126		if header.ID == "" {

190	func extractPathHints(input map[string]any, workspaceRoot string) []string {

227	// formatToolMarkdown builds the pre-formatted markdown (and optional summary)
228	// for the pi tools with a natural rendering: single-line bash commands become
229	// an inline-code summary, multi-line commands and file writes become fenced
230	// blocks, file tools show their path. Tools without a specific format return
231	// empty so the CLI's generic fallback (which renders input and output) is
232	// used instead. When a specific format is produced, the tool output is
233	// appended so the markdown stays self-contained.
234	func formatToolMarkdown(tool *schema.ToolInfo) (string, string) {
235		var summary string
236		var b strings.Builder
237		in := tool.Input
238		switch strings.ToLower(tool.Name) {
239		case "bash":
240			cmd, _ := in["command"].(string)
241			if cmd == "" {
242				return "", ""
243			}
244			if strings.Contains(cmd, "\n") {
245				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "```bash\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(cmd, "```", "\\```"))
246			} else {
247				summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, cmd)
248			}
249		case "read", "edit", "ls":
250			p, _ := in["path"].(string)
251			if p == "" {
252				return "", ""
253			}
254			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", p)
255		case "write":
256			p, _ := in["path"].(string)
257			if p == "" {
258				return "", ""
259			}
260			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`\n", p)
261			if content, _ := in["content"].(string); content != "" {
262				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n```\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(content, "```", "\\```"))
263			}
264		case "grep", "find":
265			pattern, _ := in["pattern"].(string)
266			if pattern == "" {
267				return "", ""
268			}
269			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", pattern)
270		default:
271			return "", ""
272		}
273		appendToolOutput(&b, tool)
274		return summary, strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
275	}

306	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
307		var exchanges []schema.Exchange

475			case schema.ContentTypeThinking:
476				if b.Thinking != "" {
477					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: b.Thinking})
478				}
479			case "toolCall":
480				messages = append(messages, buildToolMessage(e, b, am))
481			}
482		}
483		if len(parts) > 0 {
484			head := schema.Message{
485				ID:        e.ID,
486				Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
487				Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
488				Model:     am.Model,
489				Content:   parts,
490				Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
491			}
492			return append([]schema.Message{head}, messages...)
493		}
494		if len(messages) == 0 {
495			return buildErrorMessage(e, am)
496		}
497		// Tool-call-only assistant message: carry model+usage once on the first
498		// tool message so no metadata is lost and no schema-invalid empty message
499		// is emitted.
500		messages[0].Model = am.Model
501		if messages[0].Usage == nil {
502			messages[0].Usage = mapUsage(am.Usage)
503		}
504		return messages
505	}
506	
507	// buildToolMessage builds an agent Message wrapping a ToolInfo from a toolCall.
508	// The parent assistant message's model is passed through so tool messages carry
509	// the same model metadata as text/thinking messages. The Message ID is derived
510	// from the parent entry id + the toolCall id, so multiple toolCalls in one
511	// assistant message get distinct Message IDs (downstream provenance keys use
512	// msg.ID as a deterministic component).
513	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
514		return schema.Message{
515			ID:        toolMessageID(e.ID, b.ID),
516			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
517			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
518			Model:     am.Model,
519			Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{
520				Name:  b.Name,
521				Type:  classifyToolType(b.Name),
522				UseID: b.ID,
523				Input: b.Args,
524			},
525		}
526	}
527	
528	// toolMessageID builds a unique Message ID for a tool-call message from the
529	// parent entry id and the toolCall id. This avoids duplicate Message IDs when a
530	// single assistant entry contains multiple toolCall blocks.
531	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {
532		if callID != "" {
533			return entryID + ":" + callID
534		}
535		return entryID
536	}
537	
538	// buildToolOutput constructs the ToolInfo.Output map from a toolResult's
539	// content, error flag, and optional details blob. details (e.g. exitCode) is
540	// decoded into a generic value so downstream consumers (markdown rendering,
541	// cloud) can surface structured tool metadata without re-parsing raw JSON.
542	func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
543		out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
544		if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
545			var details any
546			if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {
547				out["details"] = details
548			}
549		}
550		return out
551	}
552	
553	// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map
554	// to InputTokens/OutputTokens; cacheRead/cacheWrite map to the Claude-style
555	// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics); reasoning maps to the same field
556	// codexcli uses so telemetry aggregates pi thinking tokens like other providers.
557	func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
558		if u == nil {
559			return nil
560		}
561		return &schema.Usage{
562			InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
563			OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
564			ReasoningOutputTokens:    int(u.Reasoning),
565			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
566			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
567		}
568	}
569	
570	// buildErrorMessage surfaces an assistant entry with stopReason=error and an
571	// empty content array (no text/thinking/toolCalls) as an agent text message so
572	// the error event is not dropped from the transcript (and compaction boundaries
573	// stay interpretable). Returns nil if there is no errorMessage to surface.
574	func buildErrorMessage(e rawEntry, am assistantMessage) []schema.Message {
575		if strings.TrimSpace(am.ErrorMessage) == "" {
576			return nil
577		}
578		return []schema.Message{{
579			ID:        e.ID,
580			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
581			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
582			Model:     am.Model,
583			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "[error] " + am.ErrorMessage}},
584			Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
585		}}
586	}
587	
588	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
589	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
590	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
591	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
592		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
593			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
594				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
595					continue
596				}
597				for _, part := range msg.Content {
598					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {
599						return spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(t)
600					}
601				}
602			}
603		}
604		return ""
605	}
606	
607	// classifyToolType maps pi tool names to the schema tool-type taxonomy.
608	func classifyToolType(name string) string {
609		switch strings.ToLower(name) {
610		case "read":
611			return schema.ToolTypeRead
612		case "edit", "write":
613			return schema.ToolTypeWrite
614		case "bash", "ls":
615			return schema.ToolTypeShell
616		case "grep", "find", "web_search", "fetch_content":
617			return schema.ToolTypeSearch
618		case "until_done_set", "until_done_plan", "until_done_task_update",
619			"until_done_progress", "until_done_complete", "until_done_block",
620			"until_done_replan", "until_done_distill":
621			return schema.ToolTypeTask
622		default:
623			return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
624		}
625	}
626	
627	// firstUserText extracts the first user message text from a message entry, if
628	// its role is "user". Returns "" for non-user messages or empty content.
629	func firstUserText(e rawEntry) string {
630		var m struct {
631			Role    string          `json:"role"`
632			Content json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
633		}
634		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m); err != nil {
635			return ""
636		}
637		if m.Role != roleUser {
638			return ""
639		}
640		return userContentString(m.Content)
641	}
642	
643	// userContentString extracts a plain string from a pi user message content
644	// field (either a string or an array of {type:text} blocks). The result is
645	// trimmed so the scan path produces the same Slug/Name as the full-parse path
646	// (deriveSlug trims too).
647	func userContentString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
648		if len(raw) == 0 {
649			return ""
650		}
651		var s string
652		if raw[0] == '"' {
653			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
654				return strings.TrimSpace(s)
655			}
656		}
657		var blocks []contentBlock
658		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
659			return ""
660		}
661		for _, b := range blocks {
662			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
663				return strings.TrimSpace(b.Text)
664			}
665		}
666		return ""
667	}
668

13	// writeDebugRaw writes numbered JSON files (one per non-header entry) plus the
14	// central session-data.json via the shared spi helper. This matches the
15	// --debug-raw contract used by every provider.
16	func writeDebugRaw(sessionPath string, data *schema.SessionData) error {
17		if err := spi.WriteDebugSessionData(data.SessionID, data); err != nil {
18			return err
19		}
20		dir := spi.GetDebugDir(data.SessionID)
21		entries, err := readRawEntries(sessionPath)
22		if err != nil {
23			return err
24		}
25		return writeNumberedEntries(dir, entries)
26	}
27	
28	// writeNumberedEntries writes each raw entry as 1.json, 2.json, ... in dir.
29	func writeNumberedEntries(dir string, entries []json.RawMessage) error {
30		for i, raw := range entries {
31			filePath := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", i+1))
32			payload, mErr := json.MarshalIndent(raw, "", "  ")
33			if mErr != nil {
34				continue
35			}
36			if wErr := os.WriteFile(filePath, payload, 0o644); wErr != nil {
37				return wErr
38			}
39		}
40		return nil
41	}
42	
43	// readRawEntries returns each non-header line of a session file as a raw JSON
44	// value, for debug-raw burst output. Uses bufio.Reader (via readLines) so
45	// arbitrarily large lines are captured without the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap.
46	func readRawEntries(path string) ([]json.RawMessage, error) {
47		var out []json.RawMessage
48		first := true
49		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
50			if first {
51				first = false // skip the session header line
52				return nil
53			}
54			out = append(out, json.RawMessage(line))
55			return nil
56		})
57		return out, err
58	}
59

64		longDesc := `Watch for coding agent activity in the current directory and auto-save markdown files.
65	
66	Unlike 'run', this command does not launch a coding agent - it only monitors for agent activity.
67	Use this when you want to run the agent separately, but still want auto-saved markdown files.
68	
69	By default, 'watch' is for activity from all registered agent providers. Specify a specific agent ID to watch for activity from only that agent.`
70		if providerList != "No providers registered" {
71			longDesc += "\n\nAvailable provider IDs: " + providerList + "."
72		}
73	
74		watchCmd := &cobra.Command{
75			Use:     "watch [provider-id]",
76			Aliases: []string{"w"},
77			Short:   "Watch for coding agent activity with auto-save",
78			Long:    longDesc,
79			Example: examples,
80			Args:    cobra.MaximumNArgs(1), // Accept 0 or 1 argument (provider ID)
81			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
82				config.EnsureDefaultProjectConfig()
83				slog.Info("Running in watch mode")
84	
85				registry := factory.GetRegistry()
86	
87				// Read flags from the command
88				debugRaw, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("debug-raw")
89				useLocalTimezone, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("local-time-zone")
90				useUTC := !useLocalTimezone
91				jsonOutput, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("json")
92				outputDir, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("output-dir")
93				flagDebugDir, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("debug-dir")
94				noCloudSync, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("no-cloud-sync")
95				onlyCloudSync, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("only-cloud-sync")
96				provenanceEnabled, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("provenance")
97				noTelemetryPrompts, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("no-telemetry-prompts")
98	
99				// Apply debug dir override from flag if provided
100				if flagDebugDir != "" {
101					spi.SetDebugBaseDir(flagDebugDir)
102				}
103	
104				// Setup output configuration
105				config, err := utils.SetupOutputConfig(outputDir, flagDebugDir)
106				if err != nil {
107					return err
108				}
109	
110				// Ensure history directory exists for watch mode
111				if err := utils.EnsureHistoryDirectoryExists(config); err != nil {
112					return err
113				}
114	
115				// Initialize project identity (needed for cloud sync)
116				cwd, err := os.Getwd()
117				if err != nil {
118					slog.Error("Failed to get current working directory", "error", err)
119					return err
120				}
121				if _, err := utils.NewProjectIdentityManager(cwd).EnsureProjectIdentity(); err != nil {
122					// Log error but don't fail the command
123					slog.Error("Failed to ensure project identity", "error", err)
124				}
125	
126				// Check authentication for cloud sync
127				CheckAndWarnAuthentication(noCloudSync)
128	
129				// Validate that --only-cloud-sync requires authentication
130				if onlyCloudSync && !cloud.IsAuthenticated() {
131					return utils.ValidationError{Message: "--only-cloud-sync requires authentication. Please run 'specstory login' first"}
132				}
133	
134				// Start provenance engine if enabled (used in later phases for event correlation)
135				provenanceEngine, provenanceCleanup, err := provenance.StartEngine(provenanceEnabled)
136				if err != nil {
137					return err
138				}
139				defer provenanceCleanup()
140	
141				providerIDs := registry.ListIDs()
142				if len(providerIDs) == 0 {
143					return fmt.Errorf("no providers registered")
144				}
145				if len(args) > 0 {
146					providerIDs = []string{args[0]}
147				}
148	
149				// Collect provider names for analytics
150				providers := make(map[string]spi.Provider)
151				for _, id := range providerIDs {
152					if provider, err := registry.Get(id); err == nil {
153						providers[id] = provider
154					} else {
155						return fmt.Errorf("no provider %s found", id)
156					}
157				}
158				var providerNames []string
159				// Get all provider names from the providers map
160				for _, provider := range providers {
161					providerNames = append(providerNames, provider.Name())
162				}
163				analytics.SetAgentProviders(providerNames)
164	
165				// Track watch command activation
166				analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventWatchActivated, nil)
167	
168				// Create context for graceful cancellation (Ctrl+C handling)
169				// This allows providers to clean up resources when user presses Ctrl+C
170				ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
171				defer cancel()
172	
173				// Start filesystem watcher for provenance correlation if enabled (uses signal context for Ctrl+C)
174				fsCleanup, err := provenance.StartFSWatcher(ctx, provenanceEngine, cwd)
175				if err != nil {
176					return err
177				}
178				defer fsCleanup()
179	
180				if !log.IsSilent() && !jsonOutput {
181					fmt.Println()
182					agentWord := "agents"
183					if len(providerNames) == 1 {
184						agentWord = "agent"
185					}
186					fmt.Println("👀 Watching for activity from " + agentWord + ": " + strings.Join(providerNames, ", "))
187					fmt.Println("   Press Ctrl+C to stop watching")
188					fmt.Println()
189				}
190	
191				// Keep sessions.db current in real time alongside the markdown writes (nil/no-op
192				// if the index can't be opened — never block the watcher on it).
193				liveIndex := NewLiveIndexer(cwd)
194				defer liveIndex.Close()
195	
196				// Track sessions we've seen to suppress initial-scan output.
197				// Existing sessions found at startup get their markdown refreshed
198				// but don't produce output — only new activity does.
199				var seenMu gosync.Mutex
200				seenSessions := make(map[string]bool)
201	
202				// Session callback for watch mode output
203				sessionCallback := func(providerID string, sess *spi.AgentChatSession) {
204					// Check if markdown file already exists to determine if this is an update or creation
205					fileFullPath := session.BuildSessionFilePath(sess, config.GetHistoryDir(), useUTC)
206					_, fileExistsErr := os.Stat(fileFullPath)
207					fileExists := fileExistsErr == nil
208	
209					// Process the session (write markdown and sync to cloud)
210					// Don't show output during watch mode
211					// This is autosave mode (true)
212					markdownSize, err := session.ProcessSingleSession(ctx, sess, config, session.ProcessingOptions{
213						OnlyCloudSync:      onlyCloudSync,
214						IsAutosave:         true,
215						DebugRaw:           debugRaw,
216						UseUTC:             useUTC,
217						NoTelemetryPrompts: noTelemetryPrompts,
218					})
219					if err != nil {
220						// Log error but continue - don't fail the whole watch
221						// In watch mode, we prioritize keeping the watcher running.
222						// Failed markdown writes or cloud syncs can be retried later via
223						// the sync command, so we just log and continue.
224						slog.Error("Failed to process session update",
225							"sessionId", sess.SessionID,
226							"provider", providerID,
227							"error", err)
228						return
229					}
230	
231					// Mirror the markdown write into the restore index in real time.
232					liveIndex.Record(providerID, sess)
233	
234					// Suppress output for existing sessions seen for the first time (initial scan).
235					// New sessions (!fileExists) always get output since they represent real activity.
236					seenMu.Lock()
237					firstSeen := !seenSessions[sess.SessionID]
238					seenSessions[sess.SessionID] = true
239					seenMu.Unlock()
240					if firstSeen && fileExists {
241						return
242					}
243	
244					// Output formatted line to stdout for watch mode
245					if !log.IsSilent() {
246						// Determine if this was an update or creation
247						action := "updated"
248						if !fileExists {
249							action = "created"
250						}
251	
252						// Get timestamps from session data
253						startTime := sess.CreatedAt
254						endTime := startTime
255						if sess.SessionData != nil && sess.SessionData.UpdatedAt != "" {
256							endTime = sess.SessionData.UpdatedAt
257						}
258	
259						// Count messages by role
260						userPrompts := 0
261						agentActivity := 0
262						if sess.SessionData != nil {
263							for _, exchange := range sess.SessionData.Exchanges {
264								for _, msg := range exchange.Messages {
265									if msg.Role == schema.RoleUser {
266										userPrompts++
267									} else {
268										agentActivity++
269									}
270								}
271							}
272						}
273	
274						// Output the formatted line
275						if jsonOutput {
276							record := map[string]interface{}{
277								"timestamp":          time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339),
278								"action":             action,
279								"session_id":         sess.SessionID,
280								"start_time":         startTime,
281								"end_time":           endTime,
282								"provider":           providerID,
283								"markdown_size":      markdownSize,
284								"total_user_prompts": userPrompts,
285								"agent_activity":     agentActivity,
286							}
287							if !onlyCloudSync {
288								record["markdown_file"] = fileFullPath
289							}
290							_ = json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(record)
291						} else {
292							emoji := "♻️"
293							if action == "created" {
294								emoji = "✨"
295							}
296							activityWord := "activities"
297							if agentActivity == 1 {
298								activityWord = "activity"
299							}
300							promptWord := "prompts"
301							if userPrompts == 1 {
302								promptWord = "prompt"
303							}
304							fmt.Printf("  %s  %s  %s · %s · %d %s · %d agent %s\n",
305								time.Now().Format("15:04:05"),
306								emoji,
307								providerID,
308								truncateSessionID(sess.SessionID),
309								userPrompts,
310								promptWord,
311								agentActivity,
312								activityWord)
313						}
314					}
315	
316					// Push agent events to provenance engine for correlation
317					provenance.ProcessEvents(ctx, provenanceEngine, sess)
318				}
319	
320				return utils.WatchProviders(ctx, cwd, providers, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
321			},
322		}
323	
324		// Watch-specific flags
325		watchCmd.Flags().Bool("json", false, "output session updates as JSON lines (one JSON object per line)")
326		watchCmd.Flags().String("output-dir", "", "custom output directory for markdown files (default: ./.specstory/history)")
327		watchCmd.Flags().String("debug-dir", debugDir, "custom output directory for debug data (default: ./.specstory/debug)")
328		watchCmd.Flags().Bool("only-cloud-sync", false, "skip local markdown file saves, only upload to cloud (requires authentication)")
329		watchCmd.Flags().Bool("no-cloud-sync", false, "disable cloud sync functionality")
330		watchCmd.Flags().Bool("debug-raw", false, "debug mode to output pretty-printed raw data files")
331		_ = watchCmd.Flags().MarkHidden("debug-raw") // Hidden flag
332		watchCmd.Flags().Bool("local-time-zone", localTimeZone, "use local timezone for file name and content timestamps (when not present: UTC)")
333		watchCmd.Flags().Bool("provenance", false, "enable AI provenance tracking (correlate file changes to agent activity)")
334		_ = watchCmd.Flags().MarkHidden("provenance") // Hidden flag
335		watchCmd.Flags().StringVar(cloudURL, "cloud-url", "", "override the default cloud API base URL")
336		_ = watchCmd.Flags().MarkHidden("cloud-url") // Hidden flag
337		watchCmd.Flags().String("telemetry-endpoint", "", "Open Telemetry Protocol (OTLP) gRPC collector endpoint (default is off, e.g., localhost:4317)")
338		watchCmd.Flags().String("telemetry-service-name", "", "override the default service name for telemetry, if telemetry is enabled")
339		watchCmd.Flags().Bool("no-telemetry-prompts", false, "exclude prompt text from telemetry spans, if telemetry is enabled")
340	
341		return watchCmd
342	}
343

// isSyntheticMessage checks if a message is synthetic/internal and should be skipped
// when looking for the first real user message (e.g. for the session title/slug).
// Filters warmup prompts, title-generation prompts, and slash-command noise (the
// command invocation, its local stdout/stderr, and the local-command caveat) — these
// are conversation scaffolding, not the user's actual prompt. Without this, a session
// that opens with a slash command gets an empty title and falls back to its UUID.
func isSyntheticMessage(content string) bool {
	// warmup and the <TEXTBLOCK> title-generation wrapper can be embedded anywhere
	// in the record, so match them with Contains.
	if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(content), "warmup") {
		return true
	}
	if strings.Contains(content, "<TEXTBLOCK>") {

// dirType determines the type of directory relative to sessionsRoot based on the
// YYYY/MM/DD structure. Returns "year", "month", "day", or "" if not a recognized type.
func dirType(path string, sessionsRoot string) string {
	rel, err := filepath.Rel(sessionsRoot, path)
	if err != nil || strings.HasPrefix(rel, "..") {
		return "" // Path is not under sessionsRoot
	}

	parts := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(rel), "/")
	switch len(parts) {
	case 1: // YYYY
		if len(parts[0]) == 4 {
			return "year"
		}
	case 2: // YYYY/MM
		if len(parts[0]) == 4 && len(parts[1]) == 2 {
			return "month"
		}
	case 3: // YYYY/MM/DD
		if len(parts[0]) == 4 && len(parts[1]) == 2 && len(parts[2]) == 2 {
			return "day"
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// startCodexSessionWatcher starts watching hierarchically for Codex sessions.
// Watches sessionsRoot/YYYY/MM/DD/ structure to handle date changes across days, months, and years.
// The initialDayDir is scanned immediately if it exists.
func startCodexSessionWatcher(projectPath string, sessionsRoot string, initialDayDir string) error {
	slog.Info("startCodexSessionWatcher: Creating hierarchical watcher",
		"sessionsRoot", sessionsRoot,
		"initialDayDir", initialDayDir)

	// Create a new watcher
	watcher, err := fsnotify.NewWatcher()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create file watcher: %v", err)
	}

	// Increment wait group before starting goroutine
	watcherWg.Add(1)

	// Start watching in a goroutine
	go func() {
		// Decrement wait group when done
		defer watcherWg.Done()

		// Log when goroutine starts
		slog.Info("startCodexSessionWatcher: Goroutine started")

		// Defer cleanup
		defer func() {
			slog.Info("startCodexSessionWatcher: Goroutine exiting, closing watcher")
```

224	// renderToolInfo renders tool use information
225	func renderToolInfo(tool *ToolInfo) string {
226		var markdown strings.Builder
227	
228		// Get the tool type for the data attribute
229		toolType := tool.Type
230		if toolType == "" {
231			toolType = "generic"
232		}
233	
234		// Open tool-use tag
235		fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, ToolUseOpenTag, toolType, tool.Name)
236		markdown.WriteString("\n")
237	
238		// Generate summary tag
239		if tool.Summary != nil && *tool.Summary != "" {
240			// Provider provided custom summary content
241			fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, "<summary>%s</summary>\n", *tool.Summary)
242		} else {
243			// Generate default summary
244			fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, "<summary>Tool use: **%s**</summary>\n", tool.Name)
245		}
246	
247		// Use pre-formatted markdown from provider if present
248		if tool.FormattedMarkdown != nil && *tool.FormattedMarkdown != "" {
249			markdown.WriteString(*tool.FormattedMarkdown)
250			// Ensure there's a newline before the closing tag
251			// Some providers include it, some don't - normalize here
252			if !strings.HasSuffix(*tool.FormattedMarkdown, "\n") {
253				markdown.WriteString("\n")
254			}
255		} else {
256			// Fallback to generic formatting
257			markdown.WriteString(renderGenericTool(tool))
258		}
259	
260		// Close tool-use tag
261		markdown.WriteString(ToolUseCloseTag)
262		markdown.WriteString("\n")
263	
264		return markdown.String()
265	}

267	// renderGenericTool renders a tool without provider-specific formatting
268	// Displays all available information as key-value pairs
269	// Note: The <summary> tag is already written by the caller (renderToolMessage)
270	func renderGenericTool(tool *ToolInfo) string {
271		var markdown strings.Builder
272		markdown.WriteString("\n")
273	
274		// Display input as key-value pairs if present
275		// Sort keys for deterministic output order
276		if len(tool.Input) > 0 {
277			markdown.WriteString("**Input:**\n\n")
278	
279			// Extract and sort keys for deterministic ordering
280			keys := make([]string, 0, len(tool.Input))
281			for key := range tool.Input {
282				// Skip internal fields like _cwd
283				if !strings.HasPrefix(key, "_") {
284					keys = append(keys, key)
285				}
286			}
287			sort.Strings(keys)
288	
289			for _, key := range keys {
290				fmt.Fprintf(&markdown, "- %s: `%v`\n", key, tool.Input[key])
291			}
292			markdown.WriteString("\n")
293		}
294	
295		// Display output if present
296		if tool.Output != nil {
297			if isError, ok := tool.Output["is_error"].(bool); ok && isError {
298				markdown.WriteString("**Error:**\n\n")
299			} else {
300				markdown.WriteString("**Result:**\n\n")
301			}
302	
303			if content, ok := tool.Output["content"].(string); ok {
304				markdown.WriteString("```\n")
305				markdown.WriteString(content)
306				markdown.WriteString("\n```\n")
307			}
308		}
309	
310		return markdown.String()
311	}

30	// Provider implements spi.Provider for the pi coding agent.

32	type Provider struct{}

34	// NewProvider returns a new pi provider instance.

40	// parsePiCommand splits a custom check/run command into binary + args,
41	// expanding a leading ~ like sibling providers (spi.SplitCommandLine handles
42	// quoting). Falls back to the default `pi` binary when no custom command is
43	// given.
44	func parsePiCommand(customCommand string) (string, []string) {
45		if strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != "" {
46			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
47			if len(parts) > 0 {
48				return expandTilde(parts[0]), parts[1:]
49			}
50		}
51		return defaultCmd, nil
52	}
53	
54	// classifyCheckError buckets a Check failure for messaging and analytics,
55	// matching the sibling providers' error taxonomy. errors.Is unwraps through
56	// exec.Error/os.PathError, covering both PATH lookups (exec.ErrNotFound) and
57	// explicit custom paths (os.ErrNotExist).
58	func classifyCheckError(err error) string {
59		switch {
60		case errors.Is(err, exec.ErrNotFound) || errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist):
61			return "not_found"
62		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
63			return "permission_denied"
64		default:
65			return "version_failed"
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// buildCheckErrorMessage renders the user-facing Check failure text. The
70	// custom-command branch avoids the misleading "not found on PATH" wording when
71	// the user pointed at an explicit path, and version-probe failures surface the
72	// probe's stderr so the underlying diagnostic is not lost.
73	func buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, command string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
74		var b strings.Builder
75		switch errorType {
76		case "not_found":
77			b.WriteString("The pi coding agent was not found.\n\n")
78			if isCustom {
79				b.WriteString("• Verify the custom command/path you provided exists and is executable.\n")
80				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Provided command: %s\n", command)
81			} else {
82				b.WriteString("• Install pi (see https://pi.dev) and ensure `pi` is on your PATH.\n")
83				b.WriteString("• Re-run `specstory check pi` after installation.\n")
84			}
85		case "permission_denied":
86			b.WriteString("SpecStory cannot execute the pi binary due to permissions.\n\n")
87			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Try: chmod +x %s\n", command)
88		default:
89			b.WriteString("`pi --version` failed.\n\n")
90			if stderr != "" {
91				b.WriteString("Error output:\n")
92				b.WriteString(stderr)
93				b.WriteString("\n\n")
94			}
95			b.WriteString("Run `pi --version` manually to diagnose, then retry.")
96		}
97		return b.String()
98	}
99	
100	// Check verifies the pi binary is available and reports its version.
101	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
102		isCustom := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != ""
103		cmdName, _ := parsePiCommand(customCommand)
104		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
105		if err != nil {
106			errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
107			slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
108			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "", errorType, err.Error())
109			return spi.CheckResult{
110				Success:      false,
111				ErrorMessage: buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, cmdName, isCustom, ""),
112			}
113		}
114		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
115		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
116		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
117		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
118		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
119			errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
120			stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
121			slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err, "stderr", stderrOutput)
122			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, stderrOutput, errorType, err.Error())
123			return spi.CheckResult{
124				Success:      false,
125				Location:     resolved,
126				ErrorMessage: buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, cmdName, isCustom, stderrOutput),
127			}
128		}
129		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
130		if version == "" {
131			version = "unknown"
132		}
133		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
134		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
135	}

137	// DetectAgent reports whether pi has created sessions for the given project.
138	// When helpOutput is true and nothing is found, it prints guidance like the
139	// sibling providers do — the CLI callers (sync/list) rely on the provider to
140	// explain a negative result instead of exiting silently.
141	func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
142		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
143		if err != nil {
144			slog.Debug("pi: DetectAgent error", "error", err)
145			return false
146		}
147		if len(files) > 0 {
148			return true
149		}
150		if helpOutput {
151			log.UserMessage("No pi sessions found for this project yet.\n")
152			if dir, dirErr := ProjectSessionDir(projectPath); dirErr == nil {
153				log.UserMessage("Expected session directory: %s\n", dir)
154			}
155			log.UserMessage("Run pi inside this project to create a session, then rerun `specstory sync pi`.\n")
156		}
157		return false
158	}

211	// sessionFile pairs a discovered pi session file with its header metadata.
212	type sessionFile struct {
213		Path   string
214		Header sessionHeader
215	}
216	
217	// findProjectSession locates the session file with the given ID within the
218	// project's pi session directory. Returns "" if not found.
219	func findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
220		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
221		if err != nil {
222			return "", err
223		}
224		for _, f := range files {
225			h, err := readHeader(f)
226			if err != nil || h == nil {
227				continue
228			}
229			if h.ID == sessionID {
230				return f, nil
231			}
232		}
233		return "", nil
234	}
235	
236	// readHeader parses only the first JSON value of a session file and returns it
237	// only if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty
238	// id). Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them. The read is
239	// capped at 1MB: a real pi header is a few hundred bytes, and the cap keeps a
240	// crafted file with a multi-GB first value from being buffered into memory.
241	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
242		f, err := os.Open(path)
243		if err != nil {
244			return nil, err
245		}
246		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
247		dec := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(f, 1*MB))
248		var h sessionHeader
249		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
250			return nil, nil
251		}
252		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
253			return nil, nil
254		}
255		return &h, nil
256	}
257	
258	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
259	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
260	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
261	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
262		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
263		if err != nil {
264			return nil, err
265		}
266		var out []sessionFile
267		for _, f := range files {
268			h, err := readHeader(f)
269			if err != nil {
270				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
271				continue
272			}
273			if h == nil {
274				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
275			}
276			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
277		}
278		return out, nil
279	}
280	
281	// GetAgentChatSession returns a single pi session by ID for the project.
282	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
283		path, err := findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID)
284		if err != nil {
285			return nil, err
286		}
287		if path == "" {
288			return nil, nil
289		}
290		return parseToAgentSession(path, debugRaw)
291	}

293	// GetAgentChatSessions returns all pi sessions for the project.
294	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
295		files, err := listProjectSessions(projectPath)
296		if err != nil {
297			return nil, err
298		}
299		total := len(files)
300		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
301		for i, sf := range files {
302			chat, pErr := parseToAgentSession(sf.Path, debugRaw)
303			if pErr != nil {
304				slog.Debug("pi: skipping session", "path", sf.Path, "error", pErr)
305			} else if chat != nil {
306				result = append(result, *chat)
307			}
308			if progress != nil {
309				progress(i+1, total)
310			}
311		}
312		return result, nil
313	}

315	// parseToAgentSession parses one session file into an AgentChatSession,
316	// writing debug-raw artifacts when debugRaw is true.
317	func parseToAgentSession(path string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
318		data, err := ParseSession(path)
319		if err != nil {
320			return nil, err
321		}
322		if debugRaw {
323			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(path, data); dErr != nil {
324				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
325			}
326		}
327		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
328		if err != nil {
329			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
330		}
331		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
332			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
333			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
334			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
335			SessionData: data,
336			RawData:     string(raw),
337		}, nil
338	}
339	
340	// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single pi session directly from its native
341	// file path, skipping the by-id discovery search. originCwd is the session's
342	// originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd), passed through
343	// as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
344	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath. Implements spi.PathSessionReader
345	// so `specstory reindex` uses the O(N) path-keyed fast path instead of the
346	// O(N²) by-id lookup.
347	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
348		data, err := ParseSession(nativePath)
349		if err != nil {
350			return nil, err
351		}
352		if data.WorkspaceRoot == "" && originCwd != "" {
353			data.WorkspaceRoot = originCwd
354		}
355		if debugRaw {
356			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(nativePath, data); dErr != nil {
357				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
358			}
359		}
360		raw, err := os.ReadFile(nativePath)
361		if err != nil {
362			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
363		}
364		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
365			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
366			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
367			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
368			SessionData: data,
369			RawData:     string(raw),
370		}, nil
371	}

373	// ListAgentChatSessions returns lightweight metadata for all project sessions,
374	// deriving Slug/Name from the leaf path's first user message (and the user-set
375	// session name when present) without decoding full message payloads.
376	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
377		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
378		if err != nil {
379			return nil, err
380		}
381		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
382		for _, f := range files {
383			scan, scanErr := scanPiSession(f)
384			if scanErr != nil {
385				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", scanErr)
386				continue
387			}
388			if scan == nil || !scan.foundUser {
389				continue
390			}
391			result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
392				SessionID: scan.sessionID,
393				CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
394				Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
395				Name:      scanName(scan),
396			})
397		}
398		return result, nil
399	}
