```text
401	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every pi session across all projects,
402	// each ref carrying its originating cwd (read from the session header).
403	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
404		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
405	}
406	
407	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all pi sessions with live scan
408	// progress, using the shared parallel scanner. Each ref carries Slug/Name
409	// derived from the first user message and the originating cwd from the header.
410	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
411		root, flat, err := piSessionsRoot()
412		if err != nil {
413			return nil, err
414		}
415		if _, statErr := os.Stat(root); statErr != nil {
416			if os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
417				return nil, nil
418			}
419			return nil, statErr
420		}
421		// ScanSessionsInParallel walks recursively, but pi session files live at a
422		// fixed depth: directly in the root for the flat override layout, else in
423		// root/<encoded-cwd>/. Deeper *.jsonl files are extension/subagent
424		// internals (observed: <proj>/<ts>_<uuid>/<hash>/run-0/session.jsonl) that
425		// the project-scoped APIs (SessionFilesInProject) can never resolve by id;
426		// indexing them would create rows sync/preview/resume cannot fetch.
427		wantDepth := 1
428		if flat {
429			wantDepth = 0
430		}
431		scan := func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
432			rel, relErr := filepath.Rel(root, path)
433			if relErr != nil || strings.Count(rel, string(filepath.Separator)) != wantDepth {
434				return nil, nil
435			}
436			s, sErr := scanPiSession(path)
437			if sErr != nil {
438				return nil, sErr
439			}
440			if s == nil {
441				return nil, nil // non-session file
442			}
443			return scanToGlobalRef(s, path), nil
444		}
445		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)
446	}
447	
448	// piSessionScan holds the metadata fields read from a session file for
449	// listing/reindex: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd +
450	// the latest user-set session name. The scan walks the SAME leaf path the full
451	// parse uses, so its Slug/Name always match what deriveSlug produces for the
452	// generated markdown (file order can differ from the active branch when the
453	// first prompt was re-edited). foundUser is false for sessions with no real
454	// user prompt; scanPiSession returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
455	type piSessionScan struct {
456		sessionID        string
457		timestamp        string
458		firstUserMessage string
459		sessionName      string
460		cwd              string
461		foundUser        bool
462	}
463	
464	// scanPiSession reads a pi session file's metadata for listing: the header
465	// (session id, timestamp, cwd), the first user message text on the active leaf
466	// path, and the latest session_info display name. Returns (scan, nil) for a
467	// real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session file or a session with no user
468	// message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse errors so
469	// ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
470	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
471		h, err := readHeader(path)
472		if err != nil {
473			return nil, err
474		}
475		if h == nil {
476			return nil, nil // not a pi session file
477		}
478		_, entries, err := readEntries(path)
479		if err != nil {
480			return nil, err
481		}
482		if len(entries) == 0 {
483			return nil, nil // header-only session; nothing to list
484		}
485		scan := &piSessionScan{sessionID: h.ID, timestamp: h.Timestamp, cwd: h.Cwd}
486		// pi resolves the display name from the LATEST session_info entry in file
487		// order (not the leaf path), and an empty name explicitly clears the title
488		// (session-manager.ts getSessionName) — mirror both rules.
489		for _, e := range entries {
490			if e.Type == entrySessionInfo {
491				scan.sessionName = strings.TrimSpace(e.Name)
492			}
493		}
494		for _, e := range leafPathEntries(entries) {
495			if scan.foundUser || e.Type != entryMessage {
496				continue
497			}
498			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
499				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
500				scan.foundUser = true
501			}
502		}
503		if !scan.foundUser {
504			return nil, nil // no user prompt; nothing worth listing
505		}
506		return scan, nil
507	}
508	
509	// scanName returns the display name for a scanned session: the user-set
510	// session_info name when present (pi lets users rename sessions), otherwise a
511	// readable name derived from the first user message like other providers.
512	func scanName(scan *piSessionScan) string {
513		if scan.sessionName != "" {
514			return scan.sessionName
515		}
516		return spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage)
517	}
518	
519	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
520	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
521	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
522		if !scan.foundUser {
523			return nil
524		}
525		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
526			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
527			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
528			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
529			Name:       scanName(scan),
530			NativePath: path,
531			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
532		}
533	}
```

```text
1	package piagent

3	import (
4		"bufio"

14	
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// An entry with no type carries nothing the mapper can use; skip it so
91			// a stray malformed line cannot mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			// Unmigrated pi v1 files store a flat linear sequence with no id/parentId
97			// (pi's migrateV1ToV2 synthesizes them at load). Chain such entries to the
98			// previous one so the tree walk sees the same linear path pi would build.
99			if e.ID == "" {
100				e.ID = fmt.Sprintf("legacy-%d", len(entries)+1)
101				if len(entries) > 0 {
102					pid := entries[len(entries)-1].ID
103					e.ParentID = &pid
104				}
105			}
106			entries = append(entries, e)
107			return nil
108		})
109		if err != nil {
110			return nil, nil, err
111		}
112		return header, entries, nil
113	}
114	
115	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root
116	// and reverses to chronological order. Compaction entries on the path are NOT
117	// applied as truncation: pi's buildContextEntries drops pre-compaction entries
118	// only to fit the LLM context window, but SpecStory's job is preserving the
119	// full transcript, so every entry on the active branch is kept (the compaction
120	// summary itself is rendered as a marker by buildExchanges).
121	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
122		byID := indexByID(entries)
123		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
124		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
125		reverse(path)
126		return path
127	}
128	
129	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
130	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
131		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
132		for _, e := range entries {
133			m[e.ID] = e
134		}
135		return m
136	}
137	
138	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
139	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
140	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
141	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
142		var path []rawEntry
143		cur := leaf
144		visited := make(map[string]bool)
145		for !visited[cur.ID] {
146			visited[cur.ID] = true
147			path = append(path, cur)
148			if cur.ParentID == nil {
149				break
150			}
151			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
152			if !ok {
153				break
154			}
155			cur = parent
156		}
157		return path
158	}
159	
160	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
161	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
162		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
163			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
164		}
165	}
```

```text
// NewProvider creates a new Factory Droid CLI provider instance.
func NewProvider() *Provider {
	return &Provider{}
}

func (p *Provider) Name() string {
	return "Factory Droid CLI"
}

// Check verifies that the Droid CLI is available and returns its resolved
// location and version information based on the provided custom command override.
func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
	cmdName, _ := parseDroidCommand(customCommand)
	isCustom := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != ""
	versionFlag := "--version"

	resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
	if err != nil {
		msg := buildCheckErrorMessage("not_found", cmdName, isCustom, "")
		trackCheckFailure("droid", isCustom, cmdName, "", versionFlag, "", "not_found", err.Error())
		return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, Location: "", ErrorMessage: msg}
	}

	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
		stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
		msg := buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, resolved, isCustom, stderrOutput)
		trackCheckFailure("droid", isCustom, cmdName, resolved, versionFlag, stderrOutput, errorType, err.Error())
		return spi.CheckResult{Success: false, Location: resolved, ErrorMessage: msg}
	}

	versionOutput := sanitizeDroidVersion(stdout.String())
	version := extractDroidVersion(versionOutput)
	if version == "" {
		version = strings.TrimSpace(versionOutput)
	}
	trackCheckSuccess("droid", isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version, versionFlag)
	return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
}
```

```text
package spi

import "strings"

// SplitCommandLine splits a command line string into arguments, respecting quoted strings.
//
// Supports both single and double quotes. Quotes can be escaped with backslash.
// This is used by providers to parse custom command strings that may contain paths
// or arguments with spaces.
//
// Examples:
//   - "claude --debug" -> ["claude", "--debug"]
//   - `claude --config "~/My Settings/config.json"` -> ["claude", "--config", "~/My Settings/config.json"]
//   - `claude --msg 'It'\”s working'` -> ["claude", "--msg", "It's working"]
//   - `claude --path "C:\\Users\\test"` -> ["claude", "--path", "C:\Users\test"]
//
// Behavior:
//   - Single and double quotes are treated equivalently
//   - Backslash escapes the next character (including quotes and backslashes)
//   - Whitespace (space, tab, newline) outside quotes separates arguments
//   - Empty quoted strings are ignored (e.g., `cmd "" --arg` -> ["cmd", "--arg"])
//   - Unclosed quotes consume to end of string
func SplitCommandLine(s string) []string {
	var args []string
	var current strings.Builder
	var inQuote rune // ' or " when inside quotes, 0 otherwise
	var escaped bool

	for _, r := range s {
		if escaped {
			// Previous character was backslash, add this character literally
			current.WriteRune(r)
			escaped = false
			continue
		}

		if r == '\\' {
			// Next character will be escaped
			escaped = true
			continue
		}

		if inQuote != 0 {
			// Inside quotes
			if r == inQuote {
				// End quote
				inQuote = 0
			} else {
				current.WriteRune(r)
			}
			continue
		}

		// Not inside quotes
		if r == '"' || r == '\'' {
			// Start quote
			inQuote = r
			continue
		}
```

```text
// sessions rather than raw files.
func (r *ScanReporter) Add(n int) {
	if r != nil {
		r.found.Add(int64(n))
	}
}

// Found returns the number of sessions found so far.
func (r *ScanReporter) Found() int64 {
	if r == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return r.found.Load()
}

// ProgressEnumerator is an OPTIONAL Provider capability: enumerate all sessions while reporting
// scan progress into r (which may be nil — ScanReporter is nil-safe, so report unconditionally).
// Providers that don't implement it are enumerated via ListAllAgentChatSessions with no live
// feedback. reindex uses this to render a per-agent "Scanning agents…" display.
type ProgressEnumerator interface {
	ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *ScanReporter) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
}

// ScanSessionsInParallel walks root for *.jsonl session files and scans each one concurrently
// with scan, returning the collected refs. It is the shared engine behind each provider's
// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress: providers differ only in where their sessions live (root)
// and how a single file's header maps to a GlobalSessionRef (scan).
//
// scan returns (ref, nil) to include a session, (nil, nil) to skip a non-session file
// (warmup-only / empty / sidechain-only), or (nil, err) to log-and-skip a malformed file.
// Files are independent and the per-file read+parse is CPU-bound, so scanning fans out across
// CPUs; output order is unspecified (reindex dedups and sorts later). r counts sessions found
// (not files scanned) and is nil-safe. label names the provider in scan-failure logs.
func ScanSessionsInParallel(root, label string, r *ScanReporter, scan func(path string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error)) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error) {
	// Phase 1: collect file paths (dirents only — no opens).
	var paths []string
	walkErr := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return nil // skip unreadable entries rather than abort the whole sweep
		}
		if d.IsDir() || filepath.Ext(path) != ".jsonl" {
			return nil
		}
		paths = append(paths, path)
		return nil
	})
	if walkErr != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("walking %s sessions: %w", label, walkErr)
	}

	// Phase 2: scan headers in parallel. min(NumCPU, 12) is always ≥ 1, so no lower-bound guard.
	workers := min(runtime.NumCPU(), 12)
	pathCh := make(chan string, workers)
	refs := make([]GlobalSessionRef, 0, len(paths))
	var mu sync.Mutex
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			for path := range pathCh {
				ref, scanErr := safeScan(scan, path)
				if scanErr != nil {
					slog.Warn("reindex: failed to scan session", "agent", label, "path", path, "error", scanErr)
					continue
				}
				if ref == nil {
					continue // not a session (warmup / empty / sidechain)
				}
				mu.Lock()
				refs = append(refs, *ref)
				mu.Unlock()
				r.Add(1) // count sessions found, not files scanned
			}
		}()
	}
	for _, path := range paths {
		pathCh <- path
	}
	close(pathCh)
	wg.Wait()
	return refs, nil
}

// safeScan runs scan(path), converting a panic into an error so one malformed session file is
// logged and skipped (via the caller's normal error path) rather than crashing the whole sweep.
func safeScan(scan func(string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error), path string) (ref *GlobalSessionRef, err error) {
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			ref, err = nil, fmt.Errorf("panic scanning session: %v", r)
		}
	}()
	return scan(path)
}
```

```text
166	// (foreground reindex); the background warm passes visible=false and stays silent.
167	func enumerateAll(registry *factory.Registry, visible bool) (ids []string, provs []spi.Provider, perProvider [][]spi.GlobalSessionRef) {
168		ids = registry.ListIDs()
169		perProvider = make([][]spi.GlobalSessionRef, len(ids))
170		provs = make([]spi.Provider, len(ids))
171	
172		var scan *scanProgress
173		if visible {
174			scan = newScanProgress(ids)
175			scan.begin()
176			defer scan.end()
177		}

180		for i, id := range ids {
181			prov, err := registry.Get(id)
182			if err != nil {
183				continue
184			}
185			provs[i] = prov
186			reporter := scan.reporterFor(id)
187			ewg.Add(1)
188			go func(i int, id string, prov spi.Provider, reporter *spi.ScanReporter) {
189				defer ewg.Done()
190				refs := enumerateOne(id, prov, reporter)
191				perProvider[i] = refs
192				scan.markDone(id, len(refs))
193			}(i, id, prov, reporter)
194		}
195		ewg.Wait()
196		return ids, provs, perProvider
197	}

200	// (Codex, the long pole, ticks the live line; the rest snap to their final count via markDone).
201	// A panic in a provider's enumeration (e.g. a malformed session tree) is recovered and logged so
202	// one bad provider degrades to "no sessions" rather than crashing the entire reindex/warm sweep.
203	func enumerateOne(id string, prov spi.Provider, reporter *spi.ScanReporter) (refs []spi.GlobalSessionRef) {
204		defer func() {
205			if r := recover(); r != nil {
206				slog.Error("reindex: provider enumeration panicked", "provider", id, "panic", r)

208			}
209		}()
210		var err error
211		if pe, ok := prov.(spi.ProgressEnumerator); ok {
212			refs, err = pe.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(reporter)
213		} else {
214			refs, err = prov.ListAllAgentChatSessions()
215		}
216		if err != nil {
217			slog.Warn("reindex: enumeration failed", "provider", id, "error", err)
218		}
219		return refs

222	// dedupRefs collapses enumerated refs by (agent, session_id), keeping the freshest file. A
223	// resumed session can span MULTIPLE native files sharing one id; they all map to one
224	// (agent, session_id) row, so without dedup the duplicates ping-pong — each run, one file's
225	// stat never matches the fingerprint the other file just stored, re-indexing both forever.
226	// Keeping the freshest by mtime makes the fingerprint stable. Sessions with no native id are
227	// dropped (unresumable, and would collide on the PK). order is first-seen order (deterministic
228	// processing); foundPerAgent is the distinct-session count per agent (for the "Found" line).
229	func dedupRefs(ids []string, provs []spi.Provider, perProvider [][]spi.GlobalSessionRef) (best map[string]reindexItem, order []string, foundPerAgent map[string]int) {
230		best = map[string]reindexItem{}
231		foundPerAgent = map[string]int{}
232		for i, id := range ids {
233			if provs[i] == nil {
234				continue
235			}
236			for _, ref := range perProvider[i] {
237				if strings.TrimSpace(ref.SessionID) == "" {
238					slog.Debug("reindex: skipping session with no id", "agent", id, "path", ref.NativePath)
239					continue
240				}
241				size, mtime := statNative(ref.NativePath)
242				item := reindexItem{agent: id, prov: provs[i], ref: ref, size: size, mtime: mtime}
243				key := sessionindex.FingerprintKey(id, ref.SessionID)
244				if cur, ok := best[key]; ok {
245					if mtime > cur.mtime {
246						best[key] = item
247					}
248					continue
249				}
250				best[key] = item
251				order = append(order, key)
252			}
253		}
254		for _, key := range order {
255			foundPerAgent[best[key].agent]++
256		}
257		return best, order, foundPerAgent
258	}
```

```text
30	// Provider implements spi.Provider for the pi coding agent.
31	// pi stores sessions as JSONL v3 trees under ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/.
32	type Provider struct{}
33	
34	// NewProvider returns a new pi provider instance.
35	func NewProvider() *Provider { return &Provider{} }
36	
37	// Name returns the human-readable provider name.
38	func (p *Provider) Name() string { return providerName }
39	
40	// parsePiCommand splits a custom check/run command into binary + args,
41	// expanding a leading ~ like sibling providers (spi.SplitCommandLine handles
42	// quoting). Falls back to the default `pi` binary when no custom command is
43	// given.
44	func parsePiCommand(customCommand string) (string, []string) {
45		if strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != "" {
46			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
47			if len(parts) > 0 {
48				return expandTilde(parts[0]), parts[1:]
49			}
50		}
51		return defaultCmd, nil
52	}
53	
54	// classifyCheckError buckets a Check failure for messaging and analytics,
55	// matching the sibling providers' error taxonomy. errors.Is unwraps through
56	// exec.Error/os.PathError, covering both PATH lookups (exec.ErrNotFound) and
57	// explicit custom paths (os.ErrNotExist).
58	func classifyCheckError(err error) string {
59		switch {
60		case errors.Is(err, exec.ErrNotFound) || errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist):
61			return "not_found"
62		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
63			return "permission_denied"
64		default:
65			return "version_failed"
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// buildCheckErrorMessage renders the user-facing Check failure text. The
70	// custom-command branch avoids the misleading "not found on PATH" wording when
71	// the user pointed at an explicit path, and version-probe failures surface the
72	// probe's stderr so the underlying diagnostic is not lost.
73	func buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, command string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
74		var b strings.Builder
75		switch errorType {
76		case "not_found":
77			b.WriteString("The pi coding agent was not found.\n\n")
78			if isCustom {
79				b.WriteString("• Verify the custom command/path you provided exists and is executable.\n")
80				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Provided command: %s\n", command)
81			} else {
82				b.WriteString("• Install pi (see https://pi.dev) and ensure `pi` is on your PATH.\n")
83				b.WriteString("• Re-run `specstory check pi` after installation.\n")
84			}
85		case "permission_denied":
86			b.WriteString("SpecStory cannot execute the pi binary due to permissions.\n\n")
87			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Try: chmod +x %s\n", command)
88		default:
89			b.WriteString("`pi --version` failed.\n\n")
90			if stderr != "" {
91				b.WriteString("Error output:\n")
92				b.WriteString(stderr)
93				b.WriteString("\n\n")
94			}
95			b.WriteString("Run `pi --version` manually to diagnose, then retry.")
96		}
97		return b.String()
98	}
99	
100	// Check verifies the pi binary is available and reports its version.
101	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
102		isCustom := strings.TrimSpace(customCommand) != ""
103		cmdName, _ := parsePiCommand(customCommand)
104		resolved, err := exec.LookPath(cmdName)
105		if err != nil {
106			errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
107			slog.Info("pi: Check binary not found", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
108			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, "", "", errorType, err.Error())
109			return spi.CheckResult{
110				Success:      false,
111				ErrorMessage: buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, cmdName, isCustom, ""),
112			}
113		}
114		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
115		cmd := exec.Command(resolved, versionFlag)
116		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
117		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
118		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
119			errorType := classifyCheckError(err)
120			stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
121			slog.Info("pi: Check version probe failed", "resolved", resolved, "error", err, "stderr", stderrOutput)
122			trackCheckFailure(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, stderrOutput, errorType, err.Error())
123			return spi.CheckResult{
124				Success:      false,
125				Location:     resolved,
126				ErrorMessage: buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, cmdName, isCustom, stderrOutput),
127			}
128		}
129		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
130		if version == "" {
131			version = "unknown"
132		}
133		trackCheckSuccess(isCustom, cmdName, resolved, version)
134		return spi.CheckResult{Success: true, Version: version, Location: resolved}
135	}
136	
137	// DetectAgent reports whether pi has created sessions for the given project.
138	// When helpOutput is true and nothing is found, it prints guidance like the
139	// sibling providers do — the CLI callers (sync/list) rely on the provider to
140	// explain a negative result instead of exiting silently.
141	func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
142		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
143		if err != nil {
144			slog.Debug("pi: DetectAgent error", "error", err)
145			return false
146		}
147		if len(files) > 0 {
148			return true
149		}
150		if helpOutput {
151			log.UserMessage("No pi sessions found for this project yet.\n")
152			if dir, dirErr := ProjectSessionDir(projectPath); dirErr == nil {
153				log.UserMessage("Expected session directory: %s\n", dir)
154			}
155			log.UserMessage("Run pi inside this project to create a session, then rerun `specstory sync pi`.\n")
156		}
157		return false
158	}

181	// matching the shape other providers use.
182	func trackCheckSuccess(custom bool, commandPath, resolvedPath, version string) {

211	// sessionFile pairs a discovered pi session file with its header metadata.
212	type sessionFile struct {
213		Path   string
214		Header sessionHeader
215	}
216	
217	// findProjectSession locates the session file with the given ID within the
218	// project's pi session directory. Returns "" if not found.
219	func findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID string) (string, error) {
220		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
221		if err != nil {
222			return "", err
223		}
224		for _, f := range files {
225			h, err := readHeader(f)
226			if err != nil || h == nil {
227				continue
228			}
229			if h.ID == sessionID {
230				return f, nil
231			}
232		}
233		return "", nil
234	}
235	
236	// readHeader parses only the first JSON value of a session file and returns it
237	// only if it is a valid pi session header (type=="session" with a non-empty
238	// id). Non-session files return (nil, nil) so callers skip them. The read is
239	// capped at 1MB: a real pi header is a few hundred bytes, and the cap keeps a
240	// crafted file with a multi-GB first value from being buffered into memory.
241	func readHeader(path string) (*sessionHeader, error) {
242		f, err := os.Open(path)
243		if err != nil {
244			return nil, err
245		}
246		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
247		dec := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(f, 1*MB))
248		var h sessionHeader
249		if err := dec.Decode(&h); err != nil {
250			return nil, nil
251		}
252		if h.Type != entrySession || h.ID == "" {
253			return nil, nil
254		}
255		return &h, nil
256	}
257	
258	// listProjectSessions returns all session files in the project's pi directory
259	// with their headers. Non-session files (readHeader returns nil,nil) are
260	// skipped silently; only a genuine read error is logged.
261	func listProjectSessions(projectPath string) ([]sessionFile, error) {
262		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
263		if err != nil {
264			return nil, err
265		}
266		var out []sessionFile
267		for _, f := range files {
268			h, err := readHeader(f)
269			if err != nil {
270				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", err)
271				continue
272			}
273			if h == nil {
274				continue // not a pi session file (bad header type/id)
275			}
276			out = append(out, sessionFile{Path: f, Header: *h})
277		}
278		return out, nil
279	}
280	
281	// GetAgentChatSession returns a single pi session by ID for the project.
282	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
283		path, err := findProjectSession(projectPath, sessionID)
284		if err != nil {
285			return nil, err
286		}
287		if path == "" {
288			return nil, nil
289		}
290		return parseToAgentSession(path, debugRaw)
291	}
292	
293	// GetAgentChatSessions returns all pi sessions for the project.
294	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
295		files, err := listProjectSessions(projectPath)
296		if err != nil {
297			return nil, err
298		}
299		total := len(files)
300		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
301		for i, sf := range files {
302			chat, pErr := parseToAgentSession(sf.Path, debugRaw)
303			if pErr != nil {
304				slog.Debug("pi: skipping session", "path", sf.Path, "error", pErr)
305			} else if chat != nil {
306				result = append(result, *chat)
307			}
308			if progress != nil {
309				progress(i+1, total)
310			}
311		}
312		return result, nil
313	}
314	
315	// parseToAgentSession parses one session file into an AgentChatSession,
316	// writing debug-raw artifacts when debugRaw is true.
317	func parseToAgentSession(path string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
318		data, err := ParseSession(path)
319		if err != nil {
320			return nil, err
321		}
322		if debugRaw {
323			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(path, data); dErr != nil {
324				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
325			}
326		}
327		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
328		if err != nil {
329			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
330		}
331		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
332			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
333			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
334			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
335			SessionData: data,
336			RawData:     string(raw),
337		}, nil
338	}
339	
340	// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single pi session directly from its native
341	// file path, skipping the by-id discovery search. originCwd is the session's
342	// originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd), passed through
343	// as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
344	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath. Implements spi.PathSessionReader
345	// so `specstory reindex` uses the O(N) path-keyed fast path instead of the
346	// O(N²) by-id lookup.
347	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
348		data, err := ParseSession(nativePath)
349		if err != nil {
350			return nil, err
351		}
352		if data.WorkspaceRoot == "" && originCwd != "" {
353			data.WorkspaceRoot = originCwd
354		}
355		if debugRaw {
356			if dErr := writeDebugRaw(nativePath, data); dErr != nil {
357				slog.Warn("pi: debug-raw write failed", "error", dErr)
358			}
359		}
360		raw, err := os.ReadFile(nativePath)
361		if err != nil {
362			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading raw session: %w", err)
363		}
364		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
365			SessionID:   data.SessionID,
366			CreatedAt:   data.CreatedAt,
367			Slug:        deriveSlug(data),
368			SessionData: data,
369			RawData:     string(raw),
370		}, nil
371	}
372	
373	// ListAgentChatSessions returns lightweight metadata for all project sessions,
374	// deriving Slug/Name from the leaf path's first user message (and the user-set
375	// session name when present) without decoding full message payloads.
376	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
377		files, err := SessionFilesInProject(projectPath)
378		if err != nil {
379			return nil, err
380		}
381		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
382		for _, f := range files {
383			scan, scanErr := scanPiSession(f)
384			if scanErr != nil {
385				slog.Debug("pi: skipping unreadable session file", "path", f, "error", scanErr)
386				continue
387			}
388			if scan == nil || !scan.foundUser {
389				continue
390			}
391			result = append(result, spi.SessionMetadata{
392				SessionID: scan.sessionID,
393				CreatedAt: scan.timestamp,
394				Slug:      spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
395				Name:      scanName(scan),
396			})
397		}
398		return result, nil
399	}

401	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every pi session across all projects,
402	// each ref carrying its originating cwd (read from the session header).
403	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
404		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
405	}
406	
407	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all pi sessions with live scan
408	// progress, using the shared parallel scanner. Each ref carries Slug/Name
409	// derived from the first user message and the originating cwd from the header.
410	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
411		root, flat, err := piSessionsRoot()
412		if err != nil {
413			return nil, err
414		}
415		if _, statErr := os.Stat(root); statErr != nil {
416			if os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
417				return nil, nil
418			}
419			return nil, statErr
420		}
421		// ScanSessionsInParallel walks recursively, but pi session files live at a
422		// fixed depth: directly in the root for the flat override layout, else in
423		// root/<encoded-cwd>/. Deeper *.jsonl files are extension/subagent
424		// internals (observed: <proj>/<ts>_<uuid>/<hash>/run-0/session.jsonl) that
425		// the project-scoped APIs (SessionFilesInProject) can never resolve by id;
426		// indexing them would create rows sync/preview/resume cannot fetch.
427		wantDepth := 1
428		if flat {
429			wantDepth = 0
430		}
431		scan := func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
432			rel, relErr := filepath.Rel(root, path)
433			if relErr != nil || strings.Count(rel, string(filepath.Separator)) != wantDepth {
434				return nil, nil
435			}
436			s, sErr := scanPiSession(path)
437			if sErr != nil {
438				return nil, sErr
439			}
440			if s == nil {
441				return nil, nil // non-session file
442			}
443			return scanToGlobalRef(s, path), nil
444		}
445		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(root, providerID, r, scan)
446	}
447	
448	// piSessionScan holds the metadata fields read from a session file for
449	// listing/reindex: identity + first-user-message metadata + originating cwd +
450	// the latest user-set session name. The scan walks the SAME leaf path the full
451	// parse uses, so its Slug/Name always match what deriveSlug produces for the
452	// generated markdown (file order can differ from the active branch when the
453	// first prompt was re-edited). foundUser is false for sessions with no real
454	// user prompt; scanPiSession returns (nil, nil) for those so callers skip them.
455	type piSessionScan struct {
456		sessionID        string
457		timestamp        string
458		firstUserMessage string
459		sessionName      string
460		cwd              string
461		foundUser        bool
462	}
463	
464	// scanPiSession reads a pi session file's metadata for listing: the header
465	// (session id, timestamp, cwd), the first user message text on the active leaf
466	// path, and the latest session_info display name. Returns (scan, nil) for a
467	// real session, (nil, nil) for a non-session file or a session with no user
468	// message, and (nil, err) for genuine read/parse errors so
469	// ScanSessionsInParallel logs them during reindex.
470	func scanPiSession(path string) (*piSessionScan, error) {
471		h, err := readHeader(path)
472		if err != nil {
473			return nil, err
474		}
475		if h == nil {
476			return nil, nil // not a pi session file
477		}
478		_, entries, err := readEntries(path)
479		if err != nil {
480			return nil, err
481		}
482		if len(entries) == 0 {
483			return nil, nil // header-only session; nothing to list
484		}
485		scan := &piSessionScan{sessionID: h.ID, timestamp: h.Timestamp, cwd: h.Cwd}
486		// pi resolves the display name from the LATEST session_info entry in file
487		// order (not the leaf path), and an empty name explicitly clears the title
488		// (session-manager.ts getSessionName) — mirror both rules.
489		for _, e := range entries {
490			if e.Type == entrySessionInfo {
491				scan.sessionName = strings.TrimSpace(e.Name)
492			}
493		}
494		for _, e := range leafPathEntries(entries) {
495			if scan.foundUser || e.Type != entryMessage {
496				continue
497			}
498			if msg := firstUserText(e); msg != "" {
499				scan.firstUserMessage = msg
500				scan.foundUser = true
501			}
502		}
503		if !scan.foundUser {
504			return nil, nil // no user prompt; nothing worth listing
505		}
506		return scan, nil
507	}
508	
509	// scanName returns the display name for a scanned session: the user-set
510	// session_info name when present (pi lets users rename sessions), otherwise a
511	// readable name derived from the first user message like other providers.
512	func scanName(scan *piSessionScan) string {
513		if scan.sessionName != "" {
514			return scan.sessionName
515		}
516		return spi.GenerateReadableName(scan.firstUserMessage)
517	}
518	
519	// scanToGlobalRef builds a GlobalSessionRef from a scan, deriving Slug/Name from
520	// the first user message. Returns nil for sessions with no user message.
521	func scanToGlobalRef(scan *piSessionScan, path string) *spi.GlobalSessionRef {
522		if !scan.foundUser {
523			return nil
524		}
525		return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
526			SessionID:  scan.sessionID,
527			CreatedAt:  scan.timestamp,
528			Slug:       spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(scan.firstUserMessage),
529			Name:       scanName(scan),
530			NativePath: path,
531			OriginCwd:  scan.cwd,
532		}
533	}
```

```text
588	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
589	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
590	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
591	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
592		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
593			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
594				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
595					continue
596				}
597				for _, part := range msg.Content {
598					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {
599						return spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(t)
600					}
601				}
602			}
603		}
604		return ""
605	}
```

```text
1	package piagent

3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"log/slog"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"strings"
13	)
14	
15	// Line-size sanity limits, mirroring claudecode/codex. bufio.Reader.ReadString
16	// has no line-size limit, so a 250MB cap guards against OOM from pathological or
17	// malicious files (a legitimate pi session line — a big tool result or base64
18	// image — can exceed the 16MB bufio.Scanner cap, so we do NOT use Scanner).
19	const (
20		KB                    = 1024
21		MB                    = 1024 * 1024
22		maxReasonableLineSize = 250 * MB
23	)
24	
25	// errStopRead is a sentinel a visit callback may return to stop iteration early
26	// (without error). readLines treats it as a clean stop.
27	var errStopRead = errors.New("stop reading")
28	
29	// readLines reads a pi session file line-by-line via bufio.Reader (unbounded
30	// line size, unlike bufio.Scanner) and calls visit for each non-empty trimmed
31	// line. Lines exceeding maxReasonableLineSize are refused with an error to
32	// prevent OOM. Returning errStopRead from visit stops iteration cleanly.
33	func readLines(path string, visit func(line string) error) error {
34		f, err := os.Open(path)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("pi: opening session %s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
39	
40		reader := bufio.NewReader(f)
41		lineNum := 0
42		for {
43			line, readErr := reader.ReadString('\n')
44			if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
45				return fmt.Errorf("pi: reading line %d of %s: %w", lineNum+1, path, readErr)
46			}
47			line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\n")
48			lineNum++
49			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
50			if trimmed != "" {
51				if len(trimmed) > maxReasonableLineSize {
52					slog.Warn("pi: line exceeds reasonable size limit",
53						"lineNumber", lineNum, "sizeMB", len(trimmed)/MB,
54						"limitMB", maxReasonableLineSize/MB, "file", filepath.Base(path))
55					return fmt.Errorf("pi: line %d of %s exceeds %dMB (refusing to process potentially malformed file)",
56						lineNum, path, maxReasonableLineSize/MB)
57				}
58				if vErr := visit(trimmed); vErr != nil {
59					if errors.Is(vErr, errStopRead) {
60						return nil
61					}
62					return vErr
63				}
64			}
65			if readErr == io.EOF {
66				return nil
67			}
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// readEntries parses every line of the session file into a header (line 1) and
72	// a list of message/control entries (the rest). Malformed lines are skipped
73	// rather than aborting the whole parse.
74	func readEntries(path string) (*sessionHeader, []rawEntry, error) {
75		var header *sessionHeader
76		var entries []rawEntry
77		err := readLines(path, func(line string) error {
78			if header == nil {
79				h := sessionHeader{}
80				if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &h); jErr != nil {
81					return fmt.Errorf("pi: parsing session header: %w", jErr)
82				}
83				header = &h
84				return nil
85			}
86			var e rawEntry
87			if jErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &e); jErr != nil {
88				return nil // skip malformed line, keep going
89			}
90			// An entry with no type carries nothing the mapper can use; skip it so
91			// a stray malformed line cannot mislead leaf selection.
92			if e.Type == "" {
93				slog.Debug("pi: skipping entry with empty type", "file", path)
94				return nil
95			}
96			// Unmigrated pi v1 files store a flat linear sequence with no id/parentId
97			// (pi's migrateV1ToV2 synthesizes them at load). Chain such entries to the
98			// previous one so the tree walk sees the same linear path pi would build.
99			if e.ID == "" {
100				e.ID = fmt.Sprintf("legacy-%d", len(entries)+1)
101				if len(entries) > 0 {
102					pid := entries[len(entries)-1].ID
103					e.ParentID = &pid
104				}
105			}
106			entries = append(entries, e)
107			return nil
108		})
109		if err != nil {
110			return nil, nil, err
111		}
112		return header, entries, nil
113	}
114	
115	// leafPathEntries walks from the leaf (last entry in file order) to the root
116	// and reverses to chronological order. Compaction entries on the path are NOT
117	// applied as truncation: pi's buildContextEntries drops pre-compaction entries
118	// only to fit the LLM context window, but SpecStory's job is preserving the
119	// full transcript, so every entry on the active branch is kept (the compaction
120	// summary itself is rendered as a marker by buildExchanges).
121	func leafPathEntries(entries []rawEntry) []rawEntry {
122		byID := indexByID(entries)
123		leaf := entries[len(entries)-1]
124		path := walkToRoot(leaf, byID)
125		reverse(path)
126		return path
127	}
128	
129	// indexByID builds an id -> entry lookup for the tree walk.
130	func indexByID(entries []rawEntry) map[string]rawEntry {
131		m := make(map[string]rawEntry, len(entries))
132		for _, e := range entries {
133			m[e.ID] = e
134		}
135		return m
136	}
137	
138	// walkToRoot collects entries from the given leaf up to the root (parentId
139	// null). A visited set guards against parentId cycles in corrupted sessions so
140	// the walk terminates instead of looping forever.
141	func walkToRoot(leaf rawEntry, byID map[string]rawEntry) []rawEntry {
142		var path []rawEntry
143		cur := leaf
144		visited := make(map[string]bool)
145		for !visited[cur.ID] {
146			visited[cur.ID] = true
147			path = append(path, cur)
148			if cur.ParentID == nil {
149				break
150			}
151			parent, ok := byID[*cur.ParentID]
152			if !ok {
153				break
154			}
155			cur = parent
156		}
157		return path
158	}
159	
160	// reverse reverses a slice of rawEntry in place.
161	func reverse(s []rawEntry) {
162		for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
163			s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
164		}
165	}
```

```text
43:func UserMessage(format string, args ...interface{}) {
---
package utils

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"sync"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/factory"
)

// WatchAgents starts watchers for all registered providers concurrently.
// Convenience wrapper around WatchProviders that resolves the full provider registry.
func WatchAgents(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	registry := factory.GetRegistry()
	providers := registry.GetAll()

	if len(providers) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("no providers registered")
	}

	return WatchProviders(ctx, projectPath, providers, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
}

// WatchProviders starts watchers for the given providers concurrently.
// Calls sessionCallback when any provider detects activity.
// Runs until context is cancelled or all watchers stop.
// Context cancellation (Ctrl+C) is treated as a clean exit, not an error.
//
// Parameters:
//   - ctx: Context for cancellation and timeout control
//   - projectPath: Agent's working directory to watch
//   - providers: map of provider ID to provider instance to watch
//   - debugRaw: whether to write debug raw data files
//   - sessionCallback: called with provider ID and AgentChatSession data on each update
//
// The callback includes the provider ID to help consumers route/filter sessions.
// The callback should not block as it may delay other provider notifications.
func WatchProviders(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, providers map[string]spi.Provider, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(providerID string, session *spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
	slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting multi-provider watch", "projectPath", projectPath, "providerCount", len(providers), "debugRaw", debugRaw)

	// Track last-seen message count per session to suppress duplicate callbacks.
	// Providers fire callbacks on every JSONL change, but not all changes produce
	// new messages in the parsed SessionData. Messages are append-only, so a
	// matching total count means nothing meaningful changed.
	var mu sync.Mutex
	lastMsgCount := make(map[string]int)

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	errChan := make(chan error, len(providers))

	for providerID, provider := range providers {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()

			slog.Info("WatchProviders: Starting watcher for provider", "providerID", providerID, "providerName", provider.Name())

			// Wrap the callback to deduplicate and include provider ID
			wrappedCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
				if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
					return
				}

				// Count total messages across all exchanges
				totalMsgs := 0
				for _, exchange := range session.SessionData.Exchanges {
					totalMsgs += len(exchange.Messages)
				}

				// Skip if message count hasn't changed for this session
				mu.Lock()
				prev, seen := lastMsgCount[session.SessionID]
				if seen && prev == totalMsgs {
					mu.Unlock()
					slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Skipping duplicate callback",
						"providerID", providerID,
						"sessionID", session.SessionID,
						"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)
					return
				}
				lastMsgCount[session.SessionID] = totalMsgs
				mu.Unlock()

				slog.Debug("WatchProviders: Provider callback fired",
					"providerID", providerID,
					"sessionID", session.SessionID,
					"totalMsgs", totalMsgs)

				sessionCallback(providerID, session)
			}

			err := provider.WatchAgent(ctx, projectPath, debugRaw, wrappedCallback)
			if err != nil {
				// Context cancellation is expected when user presses Ctrl+C, not an error
				if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
					slog.Info("WatchProviders: Provider watcher stopped", "provider", provider.Name())
					errChan <- nil
				} else {
					slog.Error("WatchProviders: Provider watcher failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
					errChan <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", provider.Name(), err)
				}
			} else {
				errChan <- nil
			}
		}()
	}

	// Wait for all watchers to complete (they run until Ctrl+C)
	wg.Wait()

	// Individual watcher failures are already logged in the goroutines with
	// full context and must not kill the surviving watchers' results. But when
	// EVERY watcher failed (e.g. `specstory watch <provider>` on a provider
	// whose watch is unsupported), returning nil would print the watching
	// banner and then silently exit 0 — surface the failure instead.
	var failures []error
	for range len(providers) {
		if err := <-errChan; err != nil {
			failures = append(failures, err)
		}
	}
	if len(providers) > 0 && len(failures) == len(providers) {
		return errors.Join(failures...)
	}

	return nil
}
```

```text
feat(cli): add Pi agent provider
## Summary

Adds support for the [pi coding agent](https://pi.dev) to specstory-cli via a new provider package `pkg/providers/piagent/`, registered under provider id `"pi"`. This enables `specstory sync`, `list`, `search`, and `reindex` to work with pi sessions stored at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-cwd>--/*.jsonl`.

| Agent | Provider | Data Format | Source Location |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Pi](https://pi.dev) | `piagent` | JSONL | `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` |

## How it works

pi stores sessions as **JSONL v3 trees** — each entry has `id`/`parentId`, and the active conversation is the current leaf-path branch. The parser:

1. Walks the leaf → root, reverses to chronological order, and honors compaction (entries before a compaction entry's `firstKeptEntryId` are dropped, mirroring pi's own `buildContextEntries`).
2. Maps entries into the unified `schema.SessionData`:
   - **session header** → `SessionID` / `CreatedAt` / `WorkspaceRoot` / `Provider`
   - **user message** (string *or* content array) → user `Message`
   - **assistant message** (text / thinking / toolCall blocks) → agent `Message` with content parts, plus one `Message` per `toolCall` carrying a `ToolInfo`
   - **toolResult** (a top-level entry in pi, unlike Claude Code where it's a user-message content block) → merged into the matching `ToolInfo.Output` keyed by `toolCallId`
   - **usage** → `schema.Usage` (input / output / cacheRead / cacheWrite)
3. Groups the ordered entries into `Exchange`s (a new user message starts an exchange; assistant + toolResult append).

## Scope

**In scope (v1):** `sync`, `list`, `search`, `reindex`, `check`, `detect`, `--debug-raw`.

**Out of scope (follow-up):** the methods below exist to satisfy the `spi.Provider` interface but return `ErrReconstructionUnsupported` / a descriptive "not yet supported" error:
- `specstory run pi` (`ExecAgentAndWatch` wrapper + file watcher)
- `specstory watch pi` (`WatchAgent` live watch)
- `ReconstructSession` / `NativeSessionPath` (native JSONL v3 serializer for cross-machine resume)



## Docs

- `README.md` — Pi row added to the agent support table
- `docs/PROVIDER-SPI.md` — Pi added to the provider table, package directory tree, and dependency flow

## Testing

TDD: a RED test (`parser_test.go`, 8 subtests asserting the full schema mapping) was written and confirmed failing (`undefined: ParseSession`) before any parser code.

```
go test -count=1 ./...   → all packages ok (incl. piagent), exit 0
golangci-lint run        → 0 issues, exit 0
```

Proven against a real pi session (not proxy signals):
- `Check()` found `pi 0.80.3`
- `DetectAgent()` → true
- `GetAgentChatSession()` parsed **11 exchanges** from a live session
- `--debug-raw` wrote **242 files** (241 numbered JSON + `session-data.json` with 11 exchanges, `providerId="pi"`)
- `ListAllAgentChatSessions()` enumerated **17 sessions** across all projects with originating cwd

## Follow-up work

1. `specstory run pi` — exec wrapper + fsnotify watcher on the session dir
2. `specstory watch pi` — live watch without executing pi
3. `ReconstructSession` — pi JSONL v3 serializer (uses `spi.FlattenSessionData` + `spi.PrepareTurns`)
4. Image content blocks in user/assistant messages are currently dropped
5. `bashExecution` / `custom` / `branchSummary` / `compactionSummary` roles are skipped from exchanges in v1
6. `ListAgentChatSessions` slug/name is currently empty (header-only); a lightweight first-user-message scan would populate it
```

```text
110	// ParseSession reads a pi JSONL session file (v3 tree or unmigrated v1 linear)
111	// and maps its current leaf-path branch into the unified schema.SessionData.
112	// The FULL leaf path is kept: compaction only trims pi's LLM context window,
113	// not the transcript, so pre-compaction history is preserved and the
114	// compaction summary is rendered as a marker message.
115	func ParseSession(path string) (*schema.SessionData, error) {
116		header, entries, err := readEntries(path)
117		if err != nil {
118			return nil, err
119		}
120		if header == nil {
121			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: no session header in %s", path)
122		}
123		if header.Type != entrySession {
124			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: %s is not a pi session (header type %q)", path, header.Type)
125		}
126		if header.ID == "" {
127			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session header in %s has no id", path)
128		}
129		if len(entries) == 0 {
130			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: session %s has no entries", header.ID)
131		}
132		ordered := leafPathEntries(entries)
133		return buildSessionData(header, ordered), nil
134	}
135	
136	// piProviderVersion derives the provider version string recorded on SessionData
137	// from the pi session header's format version (e.g. v3). Always non-empty so
138	// schema.Validate() does not warn about a missing provider.version.
139	func piProviderVersion(header *sessionHeader) string {
140		if header.Version > 0 {
141			return fmt.Sprintf("v%d", header.Version)
142		}
143		return "v1"
144	}
145	
146	// buildSessionData maps the ordered leaf-path entries into schema.SessionData.
147	func buildSessionData(header *sessionHeader, ordered []rawEntry) *schema.SessionData {
148		exchanges := buildExchanges(ordered)
149		enrichToolMessages(exchanges, header.Cwd)
150		return &schema.SessionData{
151			SchemaVersion: "1.0",
152			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{
153				ID:      providerID,
154				Name:    providerName,
155				Version: piProviderVersion(header),
156			},
157			SessionID:     header.ID,
158			CreatedAt:     header.Timestamp,
159			WorkspaceRoot: header.Cwd,
160			Exchanges:     exchanges,
161		}
162	}
163	
164	// enrichToolMessages populates PathHints and Summary/FormattedMarkdown on tool
165	// messages after tool results are merged, matching the sibling providers: path
166	// hints feed provenance extraction, and the formatted markdown lifts tool
167	// rendering out of the generic key/value fallback.
168	func enrichToolMessages(exchanges []schema.Exchange, workspaceRoot string) {
169		for i := range exchanges {
170			for j := range exchanges[i].Messages {
171				msg := &exchanges[i].Messages[j]
172				if msg.Tool == nil {
173					continue
174				}
175				msg.PathHints = extractPathHints(msg.Tool.Input, workspaceRoot)
176				summary, markdown := formatToolMarkdown(msg.Tool)
177				if summary != "" {
178					msg.Tool.Summary = &summary
179				}
180				if markdown != "" {
181					msg.Tool.FormattedMarkdown = &markdown
182				}
183			}
184		}
185	}

187	// extractPathHints collects file paths from a pi tool call's arguments (pi
188	// tools use "path"; the extra keys cover extension tools) plus paths mentioned
189	// in shell commands, normalized and deduped like the sibling providers.
190	func extractPathHints(input map[string]any, workspaceRoot string) []string {
191		if input == nil {
192			return nil
193		}
194		var hints []string
195		add := func(p string) {
196			if p == "" {
197				return
198			}
199			n := spi.NormalizePath(p, workspaceRoot)
200			for _, h := range hints {
201				if h == n {
202					return
203				}
204			}
205			hints = append(hints, n)
206		}
207		for _, field := range []string{"path", "file_path", "filePath", "dir", "directory", "target"} {
208			switch v := input[field].(type) {
209			case string:
210				add(v)
211			case []any:
212				for _, item := range v {
213					if s, ok := item.(string); ok {
214						add(s)
215					}
216				}
217			}
218		}
219		if command, _ := input["command"].(string); command != "" {
220			for _, sp := range spi.ExtractShellPathHints(command, workspaceRoot, workspaceRoot) {
221				add(sp)
222			}
223		}
224		return hints
225	}
226	
227	// formatToolMarkdown builds the pre-formatted markdown (and optional summary)
228	// for the pi tools with a natural rendering: single-line bash commands become
229	// an inline-code summary, multi-line commands and file writes become fenced
230	// blocks, file tools show their path. Tools without a specific format return
231	// empty so the CLI's generic fallback (which renders input and output) is
232	// used instead. When a specific format is produced, the tool output is
233	// appended so the markdown stays self-contained.
234	func formatToolMarkdown(tool *schema.ToolInfo) (string, string) {
235		var summary string
236		var b strings.Builder
237		in := tool.Input
238		switch strings.ToLower(tool.Name) {
239		case "bash":
240			cmd, _ := in["command"].(string)
241			if cmd == "" {
242				return "", ""
243			}
244			if strings.Contains(cmd, "\n") {
245				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "```bash\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(cmd, "```", "\\```"))
246			} else {
247				summary = fmt.Sprintf("Tool use: **%s** `%s`", tool.Name, cmd)
248			}
249		case "read", "edit", "ls":
250			p, _ := in["path"].(string)
251			if p == "" {
252				return "", ""
253			}
254			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", p)
255		case "write":
256			p, _ := in["path"].(string)
257			if p == "" {
258				return "", ""
259			}
260			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`\n", p)
261			if content, _ := in["content"].(string); content != "" {
262				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n```\n%s\n```", strings.ReplaceAll(content, "```", "\\```"))
263			}
264		case "grep", "find":
265			pattern, _ := in["pattern"].(string)
266			if pattern == "" {
267				return "", ""
268			}
269			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s`", pattern)
270		default:
271			return "", ""
272		}
273		appendToolOutput(&b, tool)
274		return summary, strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
275	}
276	
277	// appendToolOutput appends the merged toolResult content as a fenced block
278	// (truncated like codexcli) so formatted tools still show their result.
279	func appendToolOutput(b *strings.Builder, tool *schema.ToolInfo) {
280		if tool.Output == nil {
281			return
282		}
283		content, _ := tool.Output["content"].(string)
284		content = strings.TrimSpace(content)
285		if content == "" {
286			return
287		}
288		if len(content) > 5000 {
289			content = content[:5000] + "\n... (truncated)"
290		}
291		if b.Len() > 0 {
292			b.WriteString("\n\n")
293		}
294		if isErr, _ := tool.Output["is_error"].(bool); isErr {
295			b.WriteString("Error:\n")
296		}
297		b.WriteString("```\n" + content + "\n```")
298	}
299	
300	// buildExchanges groups ordered entries into schema exchanges. A new user
301	// message starts a new exchange; assistant messages append to the current
302	// exchange; toolResults merge into the matching ToolInfo; compaction entries
303	// become marker messages so trimmed-context sessions stay self-explanatory.
304	// Other control entries (model_change, custom, etc.) are skipped from the
305	// conversation body.
306	func buildExchanges(ordered []rawEntry) []schema.Exchange {
307		var exchanges []schema.Exchange
308		var current *schema.Exchange
309		commit := func() {
310			if current != nil && len(current.Messages) > 0 {
311				exchanges = append(exchanges, *current)
312			}
313		}
314		for _, e := range ordered {
315			if e.Type == entryCompaction {
316				current = appendCompaction(current, e)
317				continue
318			}
319			if e.Type != entryMessage {
320				continue
321			}
322			switch messageRole(e) {
323			case roleUser:
324				commit()
325				current = &schema.Exchange{
326					ExchangeID: e.ID,
327					StartTime:  e.Timestamp,
328					EndTime:    e.Timestamp,
329					Messages:   []schema.Message{buildUserMessage(e)},
330				}
331			case roleAssistant:
332				current = appendAssistant(current, e)
333			case roleToolResult:
334				mergeToolResult(current, e)
335			}
336		}
337		commit()
338		return exchanges
339	}
340	
341	// appendCompaction appends a compaction entry's summary to the current exchange
342	// as a marker agent message (creating an exchange if none exists yet). The
343	// summary is what pi replaced the pre-compaction context with; rendering it
344	// keeps the transcript self-explanatory without dropping any history.
345	func appendCompaction(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) *schema.Exchange {
346		if strings.TrimSpace(e.Summary) == "" {
347			return current
348		}
349		if current == nil {
350			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
351		}
352		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, schema.Message{
353			ID:        e.ID,
354			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
355			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
356			Content: []schema.ContentPart{{
357				Type: schema.ContentTypeText,
358				Text: "[Conversation compacted — summary of the earlier context]\n\n" + e.Summary,
359			}},
360		})
361		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
362		return current
363	}
364	
365	// appendAssistant appends an assistant message to the current exchange, creating
366	// one if none exists yet.
367	func appendAssistant(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) *schema.Exchange {
368		if current == nil {
369			current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: e.ID, StartTime: e.Timestamp}
370		}
371		current.Messages = append(current.Messages, buildAgentMessages(e)...)
372		current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
373		return current
374	}
375	
376	// messageRole extracts .message.role from a message entry.
377	func messageRole(e rawEntry) string {
378		var m struct {
379			Role string `json:"role"`
380		}
381		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m)
382		return m.Role
383	}
384	
385	// mergeToolResult folds a toolResult entry into the matching agent ToolInfo in
386	// the current exchange, keyed by toolCallId == ToolInfo.UseID. It also advances
387	// the exchange EndTime to the toolResult's timestamp so downstream stats that
388	// read the last exchange's EndTime report the real final-event time.
389	func mergeToolResult(current *schema.Exchange, e rawEntry) {
390		if current == nil {
391			return
392		}
393		var tr toolResultMessage
394		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &tr); err != nil {
395			return
396		}
397		content := toolResultContent(tr)
398		for i := range current.Messages {
399			msg := &current.Messages[i]
400			if msg.Tool != nil && msg.Tool.UseID == tr.ToolCallID {
401				msg.Tool.Output = buildToolOutput(content, tr)
402				msg.Timestamp = e.Timestamp
403				current.EndTime = e.Timestamp
404				return
405			}
406		}
407	}
408	
409	// toolResultContent joins the text blocks of a toolResult message.
410	func toolResultContent(tr toolResultMessage) string {
411		var parts []string
412		for _, b := range tr.Content {
413			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
414				parts = append(parts, b.Text)
415			}
416		}
417		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
418	}
419	
420	// buildUserMessage maps a pi user message entry to a schema user Message.
421	// pi user content is either a plain string or an array of {type:text|image}.
422	func buildUserMessage(e rawEntry) schema.Message {
423		var um userMessage
424		_ = json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &um)
425		parts := userContentParts(um.Content)
426		return schema.Message{
427			ID:        e.ID,
428			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
429			Role:      schema.RoleUser,
430			Content:   parts,
431		}
432	}
433	
434	// userContentParts decodes a pi user message's content (string or array) into
435	// schema ContentParts. Image blocks are dropped in v1 (recorded as a gap).
436	func userContentParts(raw json.RawMessage) []schema.ContentPart {
437		if len(raw) == 0 {
438			return nil
439		}
440		if raw[0] == '"' {
441			var s string
442			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &s); err == nil {
443				return []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: s}}
444			}
445		}
446		var blocks []contentBlock
447		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &blocks); err != nil {
448			return nil
449		}
450		var parts []schema.ContentPart
451		for _, b := range blocks {
452			if b.Type == schema.ContentTypeText && b.Text != "" {
453				parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
454			}
455		}
456		return parts
457	}
458	
459	// buildAgentMessages maps a pi assistant message entry to one or more schema
460	// Messages: one Message holds the text+thinking content parts; each toolCall
461	// block becomes its own agent Message carrying a ToolInfo.
462	func buildAgentMessages(e rawEntry) []schema.Message {
463		var am assistantMessage
464		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &am); err != nil {
465			return nil
466		}
467		var parts []schema.ContentPart
468		var messages []schema.Message
469		for _, b := range am.Content {
470			switch b.Type {
471			case schema.ContentTypeText:
472				if b.Text != "" {
473					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: b.Text})
474				}
475			case schema.ContentTypeThinking:
476				if b.Thinking != "" {
477					parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: b.Thinking})
478				}
479			case "toolCall":
480				messages = append(messages, buildToolMessage(e, b, am))
481			}
482		}
483		if len(parts) > 0 {
484			head := schema.Message{
485				ID:        e.ID,
486				Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
487				Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
488				Model:     am.Model,
489				Content:   parts,
490				Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
491			}
492			return append([]schema.Message{head}, messages...)
493		}
494		if len(messages) == 0 {
495			return buildErrorMessage(e, am)
496		}
497		// Tool-call-only assistant message: carry model+usage once on the first
498		// tool message so no metadata is lost and no schema-invalid empty message
499		// is emitted.
500		messages[0].Model = am.Model
501		if messages[0].Usage == nil {
502			messages[0].Usage = mapUsage(am.Usage)
503		}
504		return messages
505	}
506	
507	// buildToolMessage builds an agent Message wrapping a ToolInfo from a toolCall.
508	// The parent assistant message's model is passed through so tool messages carry
509	// the same model metadata as text/thinking messages. The Message ID is derived
510	// from the parent entry id + the toolCall id, so multiple toolCalls in one
511	// assistant message get distinct Message IDs (downstream provenance keys use
512	// msg.ID as a deterministic component).
513	func buildToolMessage(e rawEntry, b contentBlock, am assistantMessage) schema.Message {
514		return schema.Message{
515			ID:        toolMessageID(e.ID, b.ID),
516			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
517			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
518			Model:     am.Model,
519			Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{
520				Name:  b.Name,
521				Type:  classifyToolType(b.Name),
522				UseID: b.ID,
523				Input: b.Args,
524			},
525		}
526	}
527	
528	// toolMessageID builds a unique Message ID for a tool-call message from the
529	// parent entry id and the toolCall id. This avoids duplicate Message IDs when a
530	// single assistant entry contains multiple toolCall blocks.
531	func toolMessageID(entryID, callID string) string {
532		if callID != "" {
533			return entryID + ":" + callID
534		}
535		return entryID
536	}
537	
538	// buildToolOutput constructs the ToolInfo.Output map from a toolResult's
539	// content, error flag, and optional details blob. details (e.g. exitCode) is
540	// decoded into a generic value so downstream consumers (markdown rendering,
541	// cloud) can surface structured tool metadata without re-parsing raw JSON.
542	func buildToolOutput(content string, tr toolResultMessage) map[string]any {
543		out := map[string]any{"content": content, "is_error": tr.IsError}
544		if len(tr.Details) > 0 {
545			var details any
546			if err := json.Unmarshal(tr.Details, &details); err == nil {
547				out["details"] = details
548			}
549		}
550		return out
551	}
552	
553	// mapUsage converts a pi usage object to the schema Usage. pi's input/output map
554	// to InputTokens/OutputTokens; cacheRead/cacheWrite map to the Claude-style
555	// cache fields (pi uses the same semantics); reasoning maps to the same field
556	// codexcli uses so telemetry aggregates pi thinking tokens like other providers.
557	func mapUsage(u *piUsage) *schema.Usage {
558		if u == nil {
559			return nil
560		}
561		return &schema.Usage{
562			InputTokens:              int(u.Input),
563			OutputTokens:             int(u.Output),
564			ReasoningOutputTokens:    int(u.Reasoning),
565			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(u.CacheRead),
566			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(u.CacheWrite),
567		}
568	}
569	
570	// buildErrorMessage surfaces an assistant entry with stopReason=error and an
571	// empty content array (no text/thinking/toolCalls) as an agent text message so
572	// the error event is not dropped from the transcript (and compaction boundaries
573	// stay interpretable). Returns nil if there is no errorMessage to surface.
574	func buildErrorMessage(e rawEntry, am assistantMessage) []schema.Message {
575		if strings.TrimSpace(am.ErrorMessage) == "" {
576			return nil
577		}
578		return []schema.Message{{
579			ID:        e.ID,
580			Timestamp: e.Timestamp,
581			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
582			Model:     am.Model,
583			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "[error] " + am.ErrorMessage}},
584			Usage:     mapUsage(am.Usage),
585		}}
586	}

588	// deriveSlug returns a filename-safe slug from the first user message text.
589	// The trimmed text is passed to GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage so slugs do not
590	// differ only by leading/trailing whitespace.
591	func deriveSlug(data *schema.SessionData) string {
592		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
593			for _, msg := range ex.Messages {
594				if msg.Role != schema.RoleUser {
595					continue
596				}
597				for _, part := range msg.Content {
598					if t := strings.TrimSpace(part.Text); t != "" {
599						return spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(t)
600					}
601				}
602			}
603		}
604		return ""
605	}

607	// classifyToolType maps pi tool names to the schema tool-type taxonomy.
608	func classifyToolType(name string) string {
609		switch strings.ToLower(name) {
610		case "read":
611			return schema.ToolTypeRead
612		case "edit", "write":
613			return schema.ToolTypeWrite
614		case "bash", "ls":
615			return schema.ToolTypeShell
616		case "grep", "find", "web_search", "fetch_content":
617			return schema.ToolTypeSearch
618		case "until_done_set", "until_done_plan", "until_done_task_update",
619			"until_done_progress", "until_done_complete", "until_done_block",
620			"until_done_replan", "until_done_distill":
621			return schema.ToolTypeTask
622		default:
623			return schema.ToolTypeUnknown
624		}
625	}

627	// firstUserText extracts the first user message text from a message entry, if
628	// its role is "user". Returns "" for non-user messages or empty content.
629	func firstUserText(e rawEntry) string {
630		var m struct {
631			Role    string          `json:"role"`
632			Content json.RawMessage `json:"content"`
633		}
634		if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Message, &m); err != nil {
635			return ""
636		}
637		if m.Role != roleUser {
638			return ""

640		return userContentString(m.Content)
641	}
642	
643	// userContentString extracts a plain string from a pi user message content
644	// field (either a string or an array of {type:text} blocks). The result is
645	// trimmed so the scan path produces the same Slug/Name as the full-parse path

652		if raw[0] == '"' {

655			}
656		}
657		var blocks []contentBlock

661		for _, b := range blocks {
662			if b.Type == "text" && b.Text != "" {
663				return strings.TrimSpace(b.Text)
664			}
665		}
666		return ""
667	}
```

```text
// Validate checks the SessionData against schema constraints and logs warnings for any issues.
// Returns true if validation passed, false if there were any issues.
func (s *SessionData) Validate() bool {
	valid := true

	// Check schema version
	if s.SchemaVersion != "1.0" {
		slog.Warn("schema validation: schemaVersion must be '1.0'", "got", s.SchemaVersion)
		valid = false
	}

	// Check required root fields
	if s.Provider.ID == "" {
		slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.id is required")
		valid = false
	}
	if s.Provider.Name == "" {
		slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.name is required")
		valid = false
	}
	if s.Provider.Version == "" {
		slog.Warn("schema validation: provider.version is required")
		valid = false
	}
	if s.SessionID == "" {
		slog.Warn("schema validation: sessionId is required")
		valid = false
	}
	if s.CreatedAt == "" {
		slog.Warn("schema validation: createdAt is required")
		valid = false
	}
	if s.WorkspaceRoot == "" {
		slog.Warn("schema validation: workspaceRoot is required")
		valid = false
	}

	// Validate each exchange
	for i, exchange := range s.Exchanges {
		if exchange.ExchangeID == "" {
			slog.Warn("schema validation: exchange.exchangeId is required", "exchangeIndex", i)
			valid = false
		}

		// Validate each message in the exchange
		for j, msg := range exchange.Messages {
			if !msg.validate(i, j) {
				valid = false
			}
		}
	}

	return valid
}
```

```text
// Returns an empty slice (no error) if the directory does not exist.
func jsonlFilesInDir(dir string) ([]string, error) {
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return nil, nil
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("pi: reading session dir %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	var files []string
	for _, e := range entries {
		if e.IsDir() {
			continue
		}
		if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".jsonl") {
			continue
		}
		files = append(files, filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
	}
	return files, nil
}
```

```text
// DetectAgent reports whether the Factory Droid CLI agent is relevant for the given
// projectPath based on existing session files. When helpOutput is true, it may log
// warnings or print detection help to guide the user if detection fails.
func (p *Provider) DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool {
	files, err := listSessionFiles()
	if err != nil {
		if helpOutput {
			log.UserWarn("Factory Droid detection failed: %v", err)
		}
		return false
	}
	if len(files) == 0 {
		if helpOutput {
			printDetectionHelp()
		}
		return false
	}
	if projectPath == "" {
		return true
	}
	for _, file := range files {
		if sessionMentionsProject(file.Path, projectPath) {
			return true
		}
	}
	if helpOutput {
		printDetectionHelp()
	}
	return false
}
```

```text
3	import (
4		"fmt"
```
